Co-founders of Wellness Playground, retreat organizers and leaders, Laura and Anastasia have been teaching together for over 17 years! Both certified massage therapists, Thai therapists, aerialists, performers and instructors, they share a passion for playful movement practices. They also love to travel!  Leading their first wellness festival in Lake Tahoe in 2017, they decided to take it internationally, from Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama, Greece, Bali, Mexico, Spain, Thailand, Fiji and just recently, Dominican Republic. They have so much excitement for leading Wellness Playground Retreats and love bringing the community together in joyful movement in breathtaking locations.

La Generalitat Valenciana ha alçat el confinament i les restriccions de mobilitat a Gandia i a la majoria dels municipis afectats per les pluges.

🤝 Els campus continuaran oferint atenció personalitzada a les persones afectades que tinguen dificultats per a desplaçar-se.

📲 Seguiu les indicacions de les autoritats i consulteu únicament els canals oficials.

📲 Seguid las indicaciones de las autoridades y consultad solo los canales oficiales.

🩵 Gracias a toda la comunidad universitaria por su responsabilidad, colaboración y comprensión.

UPV | Medidas preventivas para el lunes 19 de octubre

El Gabinete de Emergencias Rectoral (GER), tras revisar las previsiones meteorológicas y los avisos oficiales, ha acordado las siguientes medidas:

APERTURA DE LOS CAMPUS

* València-Vera y Alcoy: abiertos en su horario habitual.
* Gandia: el campus abrirá a partir de las 10:00 horas.

CAMPUS DE GANDIA
* Todas las clases serán online durante toda la jornada.
* Se aplazan las pruebas de evaluación presenciales, que deberán reprogramarse.
* El personal cuyas funciones lo permitan podrá teletrabajar si las condiciones meteorológicas, su residencia o el trayecto aconsejan evitar desplazamientos, en coordinación con la persona responsable de su unidad.

CAMPUS DE VALÈNCIA-VERA
* Docencia y actividad laboral presenciales en sus horarios habituales.
* Se mantienen todas las pruebas de evaluación previstas.

CAMPUS DE ALCOY
* Docencia y actividad laboral presenciales en su horario habitual.
* Se aplazan las pruebas de evaluación presenciales, que deberán reprogramarse.

⚠️ Si resides en una zona afectada por el temporal o debes atravesarla y no puedes desplazarte con seguridad, evita el desplazamiento.

El estudiantado deberá comunicar y justificar esta circunstancia al profesorado. El personal deberá comunicarla a la persona responsable de su unidad; cuando sus funciones lo permitan, podrá autorizarse excepcionalmente el teletrabajo. Estas situaciones se atenderán con la flexibilidad necesaria.

RECOMENDACIONES GENERALES

- En los tres campus se recomienda extremar la precaución en los desplazamientos, evitar los innecesarios y consultar previamente el estado de las carreteras, los accesos y el transporte público.
- No se deben atravesar zonas inundadas o inundables, barrancos, ramblas ni pasos inferiores afectados. Deberán respetarse en todo momento los cortes de tráfico, las restricciones de movilidad y las instrucciones de las autoridades competentes.

Cualquier cambio se comunicará a través de los canales institucionales de la UPV.

biography: The longest running surf film festival in Australia screening over four nights in Torquay from Saturday 2nd- Tuesday 5th January 2027. Whew!!!

latestPosts.caption: The 16th Bells Beach Surf Film Festival will run from Saturday 2nd - Tuesday 5th January 2027. Three nights of amazing surf films from Australia and overseas PLUS a super special event night on Tuesday 5th!!!! The Festival Committee are currently finalising the programme. Tickets on sale first week of December. Stay tuned!📽️ 🎸 🏄‍♀️

The 2027 Bells Beach Surf Film Festival is just over four months away. Our festival committee have been working hard behind the scenes planning to bring you the best surf films from Australia and around the world. We have some big surprises planned for 2027... film submissions still welcome - email; bellsbeachsff@gmail.com ! 🌊🎬🍿

POINT BREAK turns 35 today. Kathryn Bigalow's film was a huge hit as Bodhi and his crazy surf mates hit banks in the water and banks out of the water. The final scene is a cracker.... set at Bells Beach (but filmed in Oregon) everyone at the Torquay screening erupted in laughter at the sight of the train station at 'Bells' and huge pine trees lining the cliff. Definitely one worth seeing ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Submissions are now open for the 2027 Bells Beach Surf Film Festival. We welcome innovative surf films with strong stories, great waves and awesome music. Please email or message us your films/trailers - bellsbeachsff@gmail.com Deadline 1st October. The festival will run during the first week of January 2027. 🎬🏄‍♀️📽️

On Saturday 30th January 2026 surfers and beach lovers came together at Cosy Corner Torquay to protest against plans for seismic blasting in the Otway Basin and Southern Ocean. The action was captured on video by festival committee members Ted Clark, Katey Shearer and John Foss and edited by Glen Hunwick. Our community have one more week to get submissions in (deadline Friday 20th February). Head to https://southernsea.givee.app/
Remember there are a number of stages to the submission process... first you CREATE a submission on the Southern Sea app...COPY your submission letter...next follow the link to the government webpage... PASTE your submission into the government page and finally SUBMIT. Here are the steps again - CREATE... COPY...PASTE... SUBMIT! https://youtube.com/shorts/qbQ0JezjLtw?si=0rt00egGpuXlBgVj

We are stoked to announce that Andrew Kaineder's film INNER MECHANICS has won BEST CINEMATOGRAPHY at this years surf film festival. Our festival committee recognised the beautiful photography and amazing angles through which Andrew and Russell told us about the thinking behind Russell Bierke's approach to those amazing waves. We know the festival has now given INNER MECHANICS the same award for cinematography that Kaineder and his team won last year for "The Outer Edge of Leisure" but we have to say both are outstanding examples of the craft of surf filmmaking. The committee especially loves the wonderful way Kaineder weaved the images of Russell's surfing into the interviews revealing how he is able to prepare and drop into those beautiful but intimidating slabs. 

We highly recommend that you check this film out on a big screen. It is awesome!

It is awards time and after much deliberation our festival committee chose to give SURFING WITH A PENGUIN the Best Short Film Award. The film screened to a highly appreciative audience who laughed and sighed with wonder at the way the penguin interacted with you and other surfers in South Africa. We all loved the way the telling was overlain with the ecological message of how we all need to value, respect and protect our ecosystems. A deserving winner!

Well that is a wrap for another year. We are still buzzing from Closing Night which featured a full house, filmmakers in the house (and a fascinating pre-recorded interview with Tim Bonython who was in Nazare), two World Premiere's and four amazing surf films including SWELL CHASING - MULLAGHMORE which was filmed two weeks ago and featured 30 foot plus bombs in huge cold Irish waves. Great vibes all night. A huge that's to our amazing festival committee - Katey, Ted, Glen, Bruce and John who work hard all year finding films and then presenting them in Torquay. Thanks also to Craig Baird and Pete Murphy at the Australian National Surfing Museum who looked after us each night. Thanks to our dedicated audiences who turn up each year and a massive shout out to the surf filmmakers around the world who create the surf films we get to enjoy on the big screen. 2026 was huge... a hard act to follow but we will be back with another surf films festival in January 2027! (photos courtesy Katey Shearer Photography)

Tonight is Closing Night of the 2026 Bells Beach Surf Film Festival. We are very excited tonight to have the World Premiere of Katey Shearer's latest surf film HOME. Filmed on the Surf Coast and combining Super 8mm footage with digital video HOME is a beautiful film exploring themes of country and coast. The festival will close with a BIG mystery film which we believe is also a theatrical World Premiere.... we can't tell to what it is but it is mind-blowing!!!! Another night of great surf films on the big screen... only at the Bells Beach Surf Film Festival.

We are still buzzing after a huge Opening Night at the festival last night. Great films, great crowd, great vibe... and we had cake for everyone to celebrate our 15th anniversary! No cake tonight but five amazing surf films with filmmakers in attendance. Another night of action on the big screen at the 2026 Bells Beach Surf Film Festival!

Tonight is Opening Night of the 2026 Bells Beach Surf Film Festival in Torquay. The festival is held at the Australian National Surfing Museum, 77 Beach Road, Torquay. We have also decided not to have beers this year... other liquid refreshments will be provided. Doors open at 7.30pm. Films start at 8.00pm!

If you’ve spent enough time around a Surfing NSW event, you probably know Fluro Phil.

You might not know his real name.

For more than 15 years, Phil Mansfield has kept NSW events running as a beach marshal, measuring boards, handing out event packs, making sure things run smoothly. 

Wondering where the nickname came from? Don’t look further than his outfits.

Long before the matching hats and event gear, Phil was the guy riding a nine foot longboard in the brightest fluorescent colour he could find.

The name stuck. 

It’s followed him ever since. At this year’s State Classic, the site crew turned up in matching orange fluro raincoats when the rain came in. Phil took one look, disappeared, and came back in yellow. Somehow still the brightest person on site.

Fluro has been a part of NSW longboarding for decades. Long enough to remember running BBQs just to scrape together judging fees, and long enough to watch that turn into fully computerised scoring. 

He might live north of Brisbane these days, but there’s one thing that hasn’t changed.

Phil’s loyalty to NSW.

“I’d love to enter competition again, but couldn’t on behalf of Qld because I’m a diehard NSW man.”

He’s NSW through and through.

And one of the familiar faces that makes NSW surfing what it is.

latestIgtvVideos.caption:
Looking back at our Meet the Maker series for last years festival with home.byholly (@hkrea) which celebrated local @craft.act members in our open studios program.

Here @ashcostelloagent visits @valerie_anne_kirk in her home studio.

Valerie Kirk studied art and design at Edinburgh College of Art, where she discovered woven tapestry. As a recent graduate she came to Australia and worked in the Victorian (now Australian) Tapestry Workshop and travelled the country to teach in communities and colleges, work as an artist-in-residence, exhibit and lead community tapestry projects. She is an artist and tapestry weaver, writer, teacher and public figure who has made a significant contribution internationally.

latestIgtvVideos.title: Meet the Maker | Bev Hogg
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
Spending lockdown looking back at our Meet the Maker series with @hkrea which celebrated local @craft.act members in our open studios program.

Here Jenny McReynolds visits @bev_hogg in her home studio.

Since graduating from ANU 30 years ago, Bev Hogg has worked from her studio, situated on the slopes of Mount Majura in Hackett. Her multi-faceted practice includes exhibiting sculptural ceramic and mixed media works nationally and internationally, creating public artworks as well as teaching. Hoggs’ figurative art works playfully explore the interconnectedness between people, animals and their shared environments and are held in public collections throughout Australia.

The 2026 @craftdesigncanberrafestival celebrates Canberra as a creative city of design and poses a big question: what can creativity change?

With Dissent as its 2026 theme, the festival explores how creative practice can challenge ideas, reshape our surroundings and spark new ways of thinking – from craftivism and sustainable design to accessibility, community connection and buying local.

And there’s plenty to do along the way: get hands-on in workshops, explore open studios, wander architecture and heritage tours, see public art and performances, join a Walk on Country, discover youth-led night walks, and shop more than 50 makers at the Undercurrent Design Market.

The festival takes over Canberra from 5–15 November, with more than 130 activations involving 500+ creatives – plus a month-long series of exhibitions.

Swipe through for a taste of what’s on, then head to craftanddesigncanberrafestival.org for the full program.

Create an embroidered soft circuit inspired by a memory of early digital technology. Combine stitching, copper tape and sound interaction to explore how personal stories can spark small, creative acts of dissent.⁠

In quiet dissent against a world that values speed over stillness, this workshop invites you to explore hand stitching techniques to slowly shape and adorn a talisman made from natural fibres and filled with flowers. Slow stitched talismans honour care, imperfection and the power of handmade objects as vessels of memory and protection.⁠

.⁠
Speakers include Alison Page @alison_joy_page, Tal Fitzpatrick @talfitzpatrick, Anna Madeleine Raupach @anna_madeleine, Rob Hopkins @robhopkins5085, Mammalian Diving Reflex @mammaliandivingreflex(Isabel Ahat + Fjoralba Qerimaj), Tamzin Nugent @tamzinnugent and Jodie Cunningham @jodiecunninghamart | Facilitated by Jenny Edwards⁠ @jenergy27⁠

Dissent by Design explores creativity as a form of Dissent: the way artists, designers, activists and storytellers use their practice to resist, imagine and rebuild. Across an afternoon of talks and conversation, it asks how the work of designing, building, making and imagining becomes a powerful response to climate pressure, social injustice and unsustainable systems, and how making itself can be an act of witness and resistance and a proposition for the world we want next. ⁠
.⁠
The afternoon brings together leading voices across craft, design, art, performance and dance and closes with the world premiere of a new dance film by Tamzin Nugent. ⁠
.⁠

Heartwood | Linda Fredheim - Myrtle Cabinets

Linda has been working with timber for over 30 years, completing a BFA (Design in Wood) at the University of Tasmania’s School of Art in 1992.  Her work has been exhibited nationally and internationally, and she has held teaching roles at the UTAS School of Art as well as the Sturt School for Wood in Mittagong, NSW.

Linda's Myrtle cabinets, showing in the Heartwood exhibition and part of the Design Tasmania Wood Collection,  reflect Linda’s interest in surface decoration and the process of labelling, cataloguing, and storage.  The motifs on the label and inside each drawer represent the real or imaginary imprint left by an object. The cabinets are small personal pieces of furniture, identical in shape, but different in their detailing. They are designed to be together but almost have their own separate personalities. 

Like many of Linda’s other cabinets, the attention to detailing means the viewer has to interact with and use the piece to fully appreciate it.  Link in bio to read more about Linda and her meticulous timber work.

Heartwood: Tasmanian Women in Timber runs at Design Tasmania until 8 February 2026, celebrating the creative leadership and enduring impact of women in timber.

OFFICIAL STATEMENT – Brisbane Street Art Festival 2026

After more than a decade of transforming Brisbane’s walls and public spaces into living art, we have some deeply disappointing news to share.

BSAF will not be taking place in 2026. This was not a decision we came to lightly. Over many months, our small and dedicated team explored every available avenue to secure the funding needed to present a festival worthy of this city. Despite that sustained effort, we were unable to proceed.

A free, large-scale public art festival of BSAF’s scope depends on meaningful investment from government and partners. That investment did not come together for 2026. We are continuing to engage with all levels of government and the arts sector to make the case for renewed support.

A Decade That Changed This City
Since 2016, BSAF has supported hundreds of artists to deliver more than 400 works of public art across Brisbane — from Northshore to Spring Hill, the Airport to the CBD. We’ve brought world-class artists to our streets: Rachael Sarra, Fintan Magee, Sofles, Guido van Helten, Adnate, Said Dokins, Sor Two, and many more. BSAF has not just displayed art. It has created artists, built careers, sparked conversations, and made the case that public space belongs to everyone.

Building The Path To 2027
This is a pause, not a full stop. We are forming a 2027 steering group, bringing together artists, cultural leaders, and community advocates, to build the foundations for BSAF’s return. We’ll be sharing updates on that work and our advocacy for the sustained public arts investment this city deserves.

If you believe in what BSAF represents, we need your voice now. Write to your local councillor. Share this statement. Tag us and tell your story. Every message sent is a vote for the kind of city Brisbane chooses to be.

To our artists, volunteers, partners, and audiences, you didn’t just attend this festival. You made it. 

The walls are still out there. The art is still standing. And so are we.

With love, gratitude and determination,
Lincoln Savage & Joelle Wong
Brisbane Street Art Festival

DM’s from strangers on the internet about my @bsafest mural 🌈 It’s always a mixed bag of interactions - some make me chuckle, then some are absolutely heartbreaking. 

The world is feeling so heavy and gross right now - the more time passes, the darker it becomes. This is where public art becomes so important - it goes beyond making a space look nice, art also has this incredible ability to connect with us and sometimes heal a little bit too. It’s a constant prayer of mine that people can walk away from my art feeling encouraged and uplifted 🥹🙏🏼

#publicart #murals #propheticart #bsafest

I had the privilege of travelling to Brisbane, Australia to take part in @bsafest, and is one of the most significant experiences of my artistic practice.
Australia gave me encounters with artists, communities and people of extraordinary generosity and talent, amazing people like @aletheabeetson , @shanifinch , @burgkaba , @jadescott_ , @thatlincoln , @qt_, @mitchsmegapixels, @lukesmitheram, @gothdayout, @simplebao, @grisone, @toksojophoto, @carlia_louise, @vanessasuzette_makeup , @nube_jaguar, @mstdesign, @itsamye, @emohbrien , @kittyonthemountain and so many others with whom I shared walls, conversations and that particular energy that only happens when so many creative people come together.
There I painted two murals under the concept Sleeping Languages in Queensland: a tribute to the Aboriginal cultures and languages of Queensland. It was deep work, built from listening to organisations like @digiyoutharts and shaped by the words that the people of Brisbane shared with me.
I remember that after months of paperwork like visas, permits, forms, I turned up to my first meeting with Digi Youth Arts with a boring slide presentation, very institutional, very formal. And Digi Youth simply introduced themselves with a beautiful song that gave me goosebumps. That moment reminded me that community, art and connection always come first, everything else is just admin.
Today BSAF shares some difficult news: the festival will not be going ahead in 2026 due to a lack of government funding. A festival that over a decade produced more than 400 murals and transformed the public identity of an entire city deserves every bit of support it can get.
The walls are still standing, the art is still there, and so are we. Public art is not a luxury, it’s a community right. 🙏🏽 @brisbanecitycouncil @artsqueensland help #BSAFEST

There I painted two murals under the concept Sleeping Languages in Queensland: a tribute to the Aboriginal cultures and languages of Queensland. It was deep work, built from listening to organisations like @digiyoutharts and shaped by the words that the people of Brisbane shared with me.

Last year went even better than expected, and I hope to see lots of people get involved again!
 
Paste up is arguably the most democratic form of art because it can be done by anyone with no need for qualifications or approval from the establishment, and the safer process also makes it more equitable. This is open to all - send in a photo, drawing, glueable sculpture, painting, print or collage!
 
All you have to do is mail your artwork (preferably on thin paper - this glues best) for arrival before 9 May to:

‼️MURAL ARTIST ‼️

Russell Fenn, better known as Sofles (@sofles), is an Australian graffiti artist originating from Brisbane. Self-taught, he has been honing his skills for over 20 years, exploring various mediums such as spray paint, acrylic, drawing and brush painting, as well as digital and illustration works.

Sofles’ large scale murals have taken him around the world ten times over and now grace many of the world’s largest cities, including Berlin, Copenhagen, Oslo, Las Vegas, and LA.  Clients he has worked with include Amazon Prime, Art Aid, Amity Affliction, Commonwealth Games Gold Coast, Culture Kings, ESPN, Ironlak, KSR Gallery, Juddy Roller, Lego, Marvel, Miami Art Basel, Mural Oasis, Quicksilver, Red Bull, Tennis Australia, Uber, Universal Studios, Westfield and many more. His bright graphics, strong colours, fine details and abstract elements have caught the attention of many art-lovers and those alike.

Sofles has a clear goal with his art; he aims to create strong images that evoke emotions in people. “I believe art should be an important part of the city landscape. I want to create public art for people to enjoy, to transform spaces”, he says. Drawing inspiration from nature, society, graffiti and traditional art, his work focuses on the ideas of time, dimensions, and an abstract mix of past experiences.

We look forward to sharing Russells’s art as the festival progresses.

🎨 Workshop: Slap Up Sticker Art🎨 

In this workshop, you’ll dive into the world of Slap Ups. 

Participants will explore a series of hands-on activities—from image making and manipulation to creating their own Slap Ups and posting them on our pop-up Graf wall. Slap Ups (also known as Sticker Art) have long been a vital part of street art culture, offering a space for cross-pollination between mediums and creative movements. 

Using techniques like collage and digital alteration, Slap Ups empower artists to craft striking, subversive visuals that push back against the dominance of mass media. It’s also a culture of exchange—artists frequently trade stickers to expand their reach, allowing their work to travel across cities, countries, and continents, often landing in places they’ve never been.

‼️MURAL ARTIST ‼️�

Fintan Magee (@fintan_magee) is a Sydney based social realist painter, specialising in large-scale murals. Born in 1985 in Lismore, New South Wales, to an architect mother and father who was a sculptor, he started drawing at a young age. His earlier large-scale paintings often inhabited the isolated, abandoned and broken corners of the city, and today are found all over the world including in London, Vienna, Los Angeles, Miami, Atlanta, Buenos Aires, Copenhagen, Kyiv, Rome, Jordan, and Dublin among others. 

Magee’s practice is informed by a profound interest in political murals, inspired by exposure at a young age to those of his father’s native Northern Ireland. This is reflected in the socialist nature of his public artworks, which combine journalistic elements with public art. Magee’s work is driven by his recognition of the power of murals to communicate political and social viewpoints and thus divide or unite communities. 

Drawing from personal experience and the mundane, his figurative paintings are deeply integrated with the urban environment and explore themes of diversity, migration and transition, waste and consumption, loss, and the environment. His works exude an inherent sentimentality and softness influenced by children’s books and the Low Brow art movement.  In recent years, Magee has solidified his position as one of Australia’s leading public artists and has traveled extensively, completing projects in countries across the world, including Belarus, India, Jordan, Spain, Tahiti, USA, among many others. His recent solo exhibitions are ‘Big Dry’ at Think Space in Los Angeles (2018), ‘Waves’ at Mathgoth Gallery in Paris (2017) and ‘Water World’ at Backwoods Gallery in Melbourne (2016).

We look forward to sharing their art as the festival progresses.

The art talk will discuss two topics related to the figure and work of Nunung WS. The first topic is the Nunung WS’ position under New Order’s gender politic, which discriminated against women, including in the art world. Nunung is a woman artist within Indonesia’s historical canon and art world that marginalizes women. The second topic is Nunung’s work which explores issues of spirituality that she has dealt with in-depth and, simultaneously, fluid because she is exposed to various spirituality. These two topics will be discussed simultaneously to mark the connection between the two.

Hilmy P. Soepadmo is a 2017 Fine Art Painting graduate from the Institute Technology of Bandung, Indonesia. Working with varied mediums from painting, prints, to perspex he is working into deconstructing consumerist culture by identifying visual stimulants that drive people’s behavior to consume. Hilmy’s artistic practice juxtaposes the elitism of art as luxury goods, by exposing factual labels that are printed and presented on a material associated with ready-made and fabricated mediums, such as perspex. The works are packaged to bring awareness of individuals buying values and habits.

🔴Still, To Draw Near — Solo presentation by Chintia Kirana (@see.in.tia)
📍 DGallerie (@dgalleriejakarta) Barito, Jakarta
📅 Until October 31, 2026

What remains when memory can no longer be fully recovered? How might we approach the past without attempting to restore it?

In Still, to Draw Near, Chintia Kirana explores memory, displacement, and belonging through ash, carbon, soil, photographic transfers, and surfaces transformed by fire. Informed by her family’s departure from Jakarta following the anti-Chinese violence of May 1998 and their subsequent resettlement in Alabama, USA, the exhibition approaches personal and collective histories through fragments rather than direct reconstruction.

Fire emerges as both a material process and a meditation on irreversible transformation. Photographs suspended on sheer fabric, paper perforated by heat, and residues drawn from ritual and domestic life create a delicate interplay of presence and absence. Ash, carbon, and soil bring distinct cultural and geographical histories into proximity, allowing connections to emerge without erasing their differences.

At its core, Still, to Draw Near considers how we remain connected to what has been lost. Rather than pursuing recovery or resolution, Kirana invites us to consider memory as something that persists through change, held in the traces and residues of what remains. Here, to draw near is not to reclaim the past, but to learn how to remain in relation to it.

D Gallerie is pleased to share installation views of “Still, To Draw Near”, a solo presentation by Chintia Kirana.

Kirana brings together works on paper, photographic fabric transfers, ash, carbon, soil, gold and silver leaf, and surfaces altered by heat. Across the exhibition, Kirana uses fire both as a material process and as a means of thinking through memory, distance, and transformation. These concerns emerge from her own history: her family left Jakarta following the anti-Chinese violence of May 1998 and subsequently settled in Alabama, USA. Rather than reconstructing this history directly, the exhibition approaches it through materials and images brought into close proximity.

“Still, To Draw Near” continues through October 31.

Cinthia Kirana (@see.in.tia) menelusuri pengalaman diaspora melalui api, abu, tanah, fotografi, dan abstraksi dalam pameran di D Gallerie (@dgalleriejakarta) yang dikuratori oleh Mitha Budhyarto (@mithabudhy).

Chintia adalah seniman multidisiplin, kurator, dan cultural organizer yang bekerja antara Montgomery, Alabama, dan Brooklyn, New York. Ia merupakan bagian dari diaspora Tionghoa-Indonesia yang keluarganya meninggalkan Jakarta pascareformasi Mei 1998 dan kemudian menetap di Amerika Serikat.

#DEWIseni [MAR]

D Gallerie is proud to present ‘Still, To Draw Near’, a solo presentation by Chintia Kirana.

We invite you to join us at the opening reception this Saturday, September 26 at 4PM.

—

Fire enters this exhibition not simply as an image, but as a force made visible through what it transforms.

Chintia Kirana approaches ash, carbon, soil, and burn marks as forms of material inheritance: materials and traces that arrive already shaped by ritual, labor, place, and consequence. Ritual ash appears alongside references to the anti-Chinese violence of May 1998 in Indonesia without equating devotional fire with political violence. Photographs of Kirana’s grandmother and childhood birthday celebrations, together with the repeated date in ‘Notation (1998)’, move between recognition and dissolution rather than toward resolution.

In her work, Kirana refers to a “conditional presence”: a state where visibility depends on light, distance, and duration rather than arriving all at once. Her recurring square holds these instabilities without containing them. Nothing here is fully disclosed. What persists is not the past restored, but its continuing pressure within the present.

—

𝗔𝘀 𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝗴𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘀 ponders the idea of protection. Sekarputi Sidhiawati presents the Otherhood series (2026), a row of ceramics set within black wooden frames and protected by plexiglass. The frames provide protection, preservation, and remembrance for pieces that combine everyday objects – cups, plates, and spoons – with tools of exposure – such as bottles and knives – alongside short, explicit texts. These portraits reflect a position often perceived as deviant or unusual: that of women who refuse to move in the same direction as dominant ways of thinking. The framing creates distance, resembling specimens in a cabinet of curiosity. In Otherhood, being “the other” is not a deficiency to conceal, but a perspective worthy of being seen and contemplated.

Embodied Memory

This time, we stepped beyond our usual book-club setting and into an art gallery, surrounded by powerful works by women artists — the perfect setting for this week’s theme: WOMEN AT THE HEART OF THE BOOK.

Divided into four groups, we brought different books to the table and explored what the women at the heart of these stories have in common: their character, values, power, struggles, and even the ways their stories end.

Surrounded by art, the discussion took on new energy, reminding us that sharing perspectives can reveal strikingly similar truths across very different stories.

Should we create more sessions like this one?

Do you love spreadsheets? Or publishing on real paper? Would you like to help create the fabulous WTF Guide and organize the Dust app? Last year we launched the Telegram channel "Blazing Swan Broadcasts" to help provide an alternative way for the community to get official announcements about the event.

The Telegram channel currently has a small userbase, but it's received positive feedback and we're continuing to use it for this year's event.

🌿WELLNESS COORDINATOR WANTED🌿

UPDATE - Thank you to everyone for their interest in this position, and thank you to those who applied. This position has now been filled. Please stay tuned to social media and the website for other volunteering opportunities.

----------------

Our Wellness Team looks after the event teams who build and packdown Blazing Swan, and we’re looking for someone to help lead the team and keep the whole thing running smoothly.

We’re looking for an organised, approachable human who’s good with people, can wrangle bookings and lead the volunteer team.

You’ll help coordinate the Wellness space, manage bookings and services, support and guide our volunteer crew and generally make sure things keep ticking along.

The role will focus on event setup and pack-down, with the first and last weeks of the event being the busiest. Hours will vary, with most Wellness services happening later in the day as you'll work around the crews' working hours.

You’ll have a 2IC and a team of Wellness volunteers to help make it happen.
Wellness experience is a bonus, but not essential. Being organised, friendly and good at making things happen is far more important.

latestIgtvVideos.title: What is Shakti? Awaken the life force energy in the feminine body
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
We caught up with Sarah-Jane Perman after her 'Awaken the Feminine Body' workshop at the 2019 BaliSpirit Festival to find out what shakti is. Sarah-Jane is a passionate and deeply authentic wisdom keeper, way shower and mother, in service to the rise of the feminine and our planet Gaia. Movement has always been Sarah-Jane's medicine and she has always been a dancer, moving the Spirit through her body. Spurred on an inner knowing that there was more to life, she dove into yoga, trying many lineages before finding her own unique style of Shakti flow. Sarah-Jane then opened herself to metaphysical realms and the ancient mystery streams. It was here Sarah-Jane acknowledged her greater mission of service is to anchor the light on earth and assist in the activation of others through her own embodiment process. It was her own experience of feeling disconnected with her feminine energy that lead her to walk the path of the priestess and remember the wisdom of her womb and yoni.

Many love Sarah-Jane for her authenticity as she shares her transmissions from her heart and she holds powerful sacred space and weaves alchemical journeys of yoga, dance, multidimensional energy and sound healing, breathwork, shamanic ritual, womb activation and sacred movement practices. Find out more about Sarah-Jane @sarahjaneperman 
#shakti #shaktiflow #BaliSpiritFest #bali #BaliSpiritFestival #BaliSpiritFest2020 #BaliSpiritFestival2020

latestIgtvVideos.title: #tbt 2017 at this epic cacao ceremony with Raio & friends!
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
There are so many heartfelt cacao ceremonies planned for BaliSpirit 2020. Cacao (the pure base of chocolate), known as “the elixir of the Gods”, is a powerful and sacred plant medicine that has been used ceremonially for thousands of years across Central and South America. BaliSpirit Festival pays respects to the ancient while creating a ritual form entirely our own, featuring beautiful live and DJ’d music and facilitated experiences to support us in rising together in love and gratitude. The ceremony will be guided by a collective of core BaliSpirit family members, but the power, grace, and joy of it will come from each and every individual. As the Quechua say: Ayllu Masikunapa! We are all one Family!

Join @r_a_i_o 💜 Monday night @theyogabarn for a Full Moon Cacao Ceremony. Its festival season ...YAY 🤗

latestIgtvVideos.title: What is a Vision Board?
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
Visions Boards are a tool to help you visualise your dreams and desires. It can help bring clarity to your ideas and is a great activity for the mind. When making a vision board you can use magazines and newspapers to find words and images that speak to you. It is then organised on a piece of paper or card. People often place their vision board on their alter or somewhere they will see it everyday to remind them of their dreams to keep them aligned and focused. No matter what you are dreaming of, creating a vision board is great for anyone. It is a fun and creative process that many describe as mediative.

latestIgtvVideos.title: What is Shamanic Yoga? A deeply connected stretching ceremony
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
We caught up with Levi Banner at the 2019 BaliSpirit Festival to talk about Shamanic Yoga 🧘‍♀️we are excied to announce he will be back in 2020 too.

With a warm smile, an energetic hug, and sly sense of humor, Levi Banner draws you into his world – teaching the spiritual sciences for healing and transformation. Yoga, Breathwork, and Astrology comprise his trinity of mystical knowledge. He creates a safe, peaceful classroom space where students can learn and grow to their fullest potential. Levi’s specialties are a strong, consistent vinyasa yoga practice; precious yet powerful pranayama practice; relaxing and healing restorative yoga, and divining deep astrological insights through the cosmic viewpoint.

Levi is also a Shamanic Breathwork Facilitator. Mystery, transformation, and healing magically combine as he leads intensive Shamanic Breathwork journeys, helping participants reconnect to their highest selves. By gifting students with personal empowerment and self-healing, he strives to create a community of open-hearted difference makers with world-changing potential.

Levi can be found teaching at The Yoga Barn in Ubud, Bali, or traveling the shamanic path as he conducts workshops and immersions around the globe. In Yoga, Levi is rated E-RYT 500, the highest level of Yoga Alliance certification. Enlightened techniques and ancient philosophies learned through his studies in India, Guatemala, Sedona, and Bali are transmitted into his practice, gracing students with an unusually well-rounded experience and profound lifetime benefits.

She successfully moves, touches and inspires many people around the world with her knowledge and passion for Masala Bhangra ® and Bollywood. Sarina’s energy is infectious and you will be feeling high and uplifted post session!

Get a taster of what to expect in this video from 2018 and be sure to check out the workshop line up, its filled with world renowned presenters from across the globe! (link in bio)

latestIgtvVideos.title: What is Shadow Work? - Uncover the ways that you sabotage yourself
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
We caught up with Deva Dwabha after her workshop at the 2019 BaliSpirit Festival to talk about shadow work. We are excited to announce that she will be back in 2020 to share her gifts with the BaliSpirit Festival community 🧡

Deva Dwabha is an international mystic, healer and teacher of spiritual wisdom. Using the ancient tool of Tarot and her workshops for the past 38 years, individually and in groups, she has helped thousands look into this magic mirror of their own souls and use the archetypal images as a powerful tool for spiritual growth and transformation. Her work can be used to deepen our self-awareness and call our attention to inner and outer work that needs to be done in problem solving to help us explore our options, make difficult choices, and find new directions for our lives.Her seminars on Healing Shadows are based on direct guidance from her enlightened Master's guidance for all women to achieve liberation. She is the recipient of the Spiritual Humanitarian Award, 2017 Bhakti Festival, Joshua Tree Ca., Divine Shakti Leadership Award, All India 2018, Rotary International THE ONE Giving the Most Award 2018. She is founder/director of Ramana's Garden Children's Home/Schools, Rishikesh, India. She generates most of the funding By Empowering Women around the globe. Dwabha lives in Rishikesh, India and has devoted her life to uplifting and empowering women and children from sexual abuse, forced labor, poverty and illiteracy.

Welcome to CAPTAIN COYOTE’S FROG BOG! 🐸 This year, Pickathon’s Coyote Neighborhood (@pickathoncoyote) family zone will transform into a bustling bog, where our youngest adventurers can play, create and explore.

Families will step into a world of imaginative play, with a stage decorated with glowing cattails and shimmering frog eggs, a tree stump info booth, lily pad balance platforms, a nurse log play structure, a spider web weaving project, and so much more.

Designed by resident artists @theodoreerratic @greenelbow & @livingthingsunion with support from @cedarwoodwaldorf. Drawings by Jason Greene; logo by @faerin.millington. Video, animations and music by @davewgulick.

The Coyote Stage features GRAMMY-winners Fyütch and 123 Andrés, GRAMMY-nominees Aaron Nigel Smith and Flor Bromley, and Portland favorites Red Yarn, Mo Phillips & the Spaghetti Pants Dance Band, and Sing with Teacher Brittany — plus a Family Square Dance, wilderness adventures with Trackers Earth, morning yoga, collaborative art, crafts, and more.

Full schedule to be announced soon! Visit pickathon.com for more details. 🫧

🌲 2027 PRESALE IS OPEN NOW!

Hey, Pickathon fam! Grab the lowest priced tickets we’ll offer all year and skip the lineup season rush. Lock in your spot, save some money, and start counting down to the best weekend of the year, back at Pendarvis Farm in Happy Valley, Oregon, August 4–8, 2027.

📢 Sign up for 📧 email alerts (pickathon.com) and our📱Text Club (laylo.com/pickathon) to receive early announcements, exclusive discounts and more!

🫶 Visit @creativeneighborhoods at creativeneighborhoods.com to learn more about our nonprofit partner who helps make the Pickathon magic happen while creating opportunities, empowering communities, and shaping a more sustainable future.

Raising little festival lovers in the best place possible. Pickathon 2026 had an amazing coyote cove (@pickathoncoyote) for the kids and families.

📷 @dylanvanweelden

It's hard to believe that a month has already passed since Pickathon and that summer is quickly drawing to a close. The music, laughter, and spirit of the weekend is still resounding through my heart, and I'm so honored to have had the chance to once again be a part of the magic and fun on the farm. I had such a ribbiting time hanging out in Captain Coyote's Frog Bog taking care of the Lily Pad Post Office and serving as typist and typewriter teacher alike, and I hope that all around the world the beautiful Lily Pad Postcards people created are finding their way to family, friends, and loved ones. It's such an incredible feeling to have the opportunity to be The Traveling Typist, to share that spark of typewriter joy with spirits both young and old, and I'll never tire of hearing  nimble fingers typing away and channeling their inner creativity. 

I want to give a huge thank you to everyone who stopped by the Lily Pad Post Office, both to create their own Lily Pad Postcard and to try out writing on a typewriter. For me being The Traveling Typist is about so much more than just writing, it's about cultivating that incredible sense of community, joy, and creativity that typewriters inspire. I also want to thank @pickathon and @pickathoncoyote for having me, @redyarnpdx for his amazing work in helping to plan and bring Frog Bog to life, and to everyone else at Pickathon who helped make the weekend magical.

I am obsessed with this gorgeous footage shot by @butterflyboycemedia during our Sunday morning set on the @pickathon Coyote Stage! It perfectly captures the joy, the heart, the creativity, the collaborations, the friendships & the family sweetness that make the @pickathoncoyote neighborhood so special. This year was my favorite Pickathon of the ten I’ve attended, all because of these impeccable community vibes. Performing on the family stage at the world’s greatest indie music fest, alongside my luminous wife @jgeiaf and my dear pals @oscarmurden, @johnnie_ballard75 & Mr. E, in communion with this lovely, loving audience, is pretty much the most ecstatic experience ever. Deep gratitude to everyone who helps make it happen! I can hardly wait for next year! ❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️

I’ve been stressed all week about the amount of work edits I’m constantly behind on. I can’t ever seem to get caught up and the shoots keep piling up. Then @pickathon comes along and this is supposed to be the “fun” one. 

Once I got done with my edit this year I felt a huge weight lift and that’s when I realized I put too much pressure on myself to get the best shots of the festival. I don’t know if I ever even realized it but I want to capture that one image that the NY Times or Billboard magazine picks up as the image that defines what #pickathon is. I’ve gotten those hits before and I guess it feels a bit expected now. 

Whenever I shoot Pickathon I walk away not sure if I got anything at all and this year was just that. Anyways, I digress. Here’s my top 20 from this year, hope you find something redeeming in some of them.

@benchapman @steveearle @builttospill @thewomacksisters @pickathoncoyote @elkhatmusic @meridianbrothers @hogslopstringband

What an absolute joy to perform for the liveliest crowd ever, with this stellar band of pals, on the @pickathon Coyote Stage on Sunday morning! This is “Sister Rabbit,” our new adaptation of the African American folksong “Mister Rabbit,” part of our upcoming musical, “Saturday Night at the Briar Patch.” This was my first-ever all-electric set, and they didn’t even boo me off the stage! Big thanks to my radiant singing partner @jgeiaf, my bandmates @oscarmurden @johnnie_ballard75 & Mr. E, and everyone in the @pickathoncoyote neighborhood for bringing the party! ❤️🎸🐰

Thank you @pickathoncoyote for having Making Earth Cool and the @350pdx and @xrpdxofficial giant puppets join you again this year! We had so much fun!! Shout out to @scrapportland for supplying us with all the rad craft supplies! The kids went wild with their creations 😍 And @unpresidentedbrassband503 for always being down to parade!!! Let’s make this our parade Fall!!! There is so much to parade about!!

latestIgtvVideos.caption:
Overseas countries are no longer accepting our recycling. ♻️ The way we have to recycle across Australia is changing and Yarra is changing with it.
 
Our new glass-only recycling bin is the first step. 💜 By separating the glass and recyclables at the source, we can avoid contamination and ensure both can be used again to make something new. 👍
 
📹Yarra Mayor Cr. Gabrielle de Vietri shares more details about these changes at the Australian Paper Recovery where our recycling is processed.
 
If you have any questions about your recycling, visit our website https://bit.ly/33tbR0i

🛑 When the flags are displayed at a children’s crossing, you must stop for pedestrians who are waiting to cross or who have started crossing

Yarra’s Biodiversity Blitz 2026 has wrapped up 🕸️🕷️

Throughout September, Yarra locals came together to discover, observe and record the incredible biodiversity living across our parks, waterways, streets and in our backyards.

Using the free iNaturalist app, residents recorded sightings of birds, frogs, insects, native plants, fungi and other wildlife to help build a valuable picture of Yarra’s local ecosystems. 

From backyard discoveries to wildlife spotted in our parks, every observation helped shine a light on the incredible species that call Yarra home 🕷️🦋🌱

A huge thank you to everyone who took part and helped make Biodiversity Blitz 2026 a celebration of our local environment.

Introducing the Burning Man 2027 theme 🔮 Spellbound.

Every year as Black Rock City draws to a close we say goodbye to what was, and hello to the future we build together. With this renewal comes the Burning Man 2027 theme ~ Spellbound.

The next 12 months invite you to plumb the mysteries of playa magic — from the serendipity of resonant coincidence to the gobsmacked awe of seeing things that cannot possibly be, and yet somehow are. It is an invitation to consider the nature of enchantment itself; to delve into the enigmatic depths of your own psyche, where belief and disbelief collide and the stories we are told bleed into the stories we tell ourselves, and in turn into the realities we construct for others.

Read the Burning Man 2027 theme announcement! Link in bio

Thanks to Cory and Catska Ench for the theme illustration, and to DA Tinio for collaborating on the concept.

Dystopia is compelling. What’s the opposite? Hope.

Xtina Chu and Corey Johnson talk in Black Rock City about all things interesting with our solar future happening now! They share how in an age of cynicism, optimism is the ultimate punk rock rebellion.

What started as a DIY experiment has evolved into a megawatt array gifting clean-energy to EV art cars and fuel-free theme camps. Meanwhile, back in California, they deploy rapid disaster-relief. They’re rewriting the rules of power, even large-scale event power. 

The future doesn’t stink. 
Moving away from individualism, they view "self-reliance" as a collective resilience network. They shine a light on the engineering — and cultural engineering — happening now and forever, more and more.

latestPosts.caption:
🎻 OMBLIGO EN ASALTO EN ÉPILA 2026 🎶

¡El viernes 23 de octubre tenemos una cita con la música en directo!

Este año, Asalto en Épila contará con Ombligo, un proyecto musical nacido en Madrid de la mano de Anika y Ángel Cáceres que nos propone un viaje sonoro sin fronteras.

Con el violín y la guitarra como protagonistas, su música mezcla ritmos balcánicos, swing, bolero, jazz y muchas otras influencias, dando forma a un universo propio, lleno de energía, virtuosismo y buen humor.

Una propuesta festiva, sorprendente y difícil de etiquetar, de esas que invitan a dejarse llevar, mover los pies y disfrutar de la música sin demasiadas explicaciones.

Porque en Asalto también nos gusta encontrarnos alrededor de la música, compartir un buen rato y celebrar la cultura en la calle.

📅 Viernes 23 de octubre
🕗 20:00 h
📍 Palacio del Conde de Aranda. Épila (Zaragoza)

¡Nos vemos allí!

#AsaltoEnÉpila #FestivalAsalto #Ombligo #Épila #MúsicaEnDirecto CulturaEnLaCalle

Harsa y Sara Marcos trabajan desde la ilustración, el diseño y la creación gráfica, desarrollando un lenguaje visual reconocible por el uso del color, las formas sintéticas y la construcción de imaginarios en los que naturaleza, arquitectura y escenas cotidianas conviven dentro de una misma composición.

En esta quinta edición de Asalto en Épila trasladarán ese universo gráfico al espacio público con “Épila: un recorrido ilustrado del territorio”, una intervención mural concebida como una especie de mapa vivo del municipio. 

El río Jalón, las viñas y los frutales, las cigüeñas, la arquitectura mudéjar, el Palacio de los Condes de Aranda, industrias, caminos, edificios y pequeños elementos de la vida cotidiana podrán aparecer conectados en una gran cartografía ilustrada que no pretende reproducir literalmente Épila, sino representar algunos de los elementos que construyen su identidad y su imaginario.

📍 Intervención: Calle del Cuartel, 2

Durante unos días aparecerá en Épila algo poco habitual: un estudio de pintura abierto al pueblo.

Isabel Garmon trasladará su práctica de retrato fuera del estudio para pintar directamente a cinco vecinos y vecinas de Épila.

Mientras tanto, se podrá observar cómo se construye una pintura, acompañar las sesiones, conversar con la artista o simplemente acercarse a mirar. 

Porque Épila al natural entiende el retrato no solo como la representación de una persona, sino como una situación de encuentro. 

Pintar a alguien requiere algo cada vez menos habitual: detenerse, mirar y compartir tiempo.

🎨 Estudio de artista: Palacio del Conde Aranda
📍 Ubicaciones de los retratos: por determinar.

¿Qué cosas merece la pena conservar de un lugar?

Una canción. Un refrán. Un juego de infancia. Una historia. Un remedio casero. Una expresión. Un consejo que alguien nos dio hace muchos años y todavía recordamos.

David Feroce llama a todo ello “recetas para la vida”: pequeños conocimientos, recuerdos y relatos que pasan de unas personas a otras y que también forman parte del patrimonio de una comunidad. 

Durante Asalto en Épila reuniremos a distintas generaciones para conversar y escucharse. Las personas más jóvenes se convertirán en entrevistadoras y las mayores compartirán historias, recuerdos y saberes.

Una selección de esas “recetas” se trasladará después a piezas cerámicas que aparecerán en diferentes rincones de Épila, construyendo poco a poco un archivo de memoria disperso por el municipio. El proceso incluirá además la creación colectiva de pequeños Recetarios para la vida mediante encuadernación artesanal. 

Porque el patrimonio de un lugar no está únicamente en sus edificios. También está en aquello que sabemos, recordamos y transmitimos a los demás.

📍 Ubicación por determinar

Una ventana tapiada suele hablarnos de cierre, abandono y de un lugar que ha dejado de habitarse.

¿Y si, en lugar de ladrillos, la cerrásemos con libros?

Elisa Terroba llega a Asalto en Épila con Barricada Cultural, una instalación site-specific que interviene los huecos de una vivienda utilizando libros usados.

El gesto pone en relación dos maneras de construir: el ladrillo construye físicamente nuestros espacios; el libro construye conocimiento, memoria y cultura. 

Para construir esta barricada necesitaremos también la participación de Épila.

📣Abrimos un llamamiento para que vecinos y vecinas puedan donar libros usados que pasarán literalmente a formar parte de la intervención. 📣

Libros que salen de las casas para ocupar otra casa.

📍 Ubicación por determinar según estudio previo

¿Quiénes forman hoy Épila? ¿Qué lugares sentimos como propios? ¿Qué recuerdos compartimos y cuáles estamos construyendo juntos?

Hugo Casanova propone una intervención mural que pone el foco en las personas, la convivencia y la diversidad que conforman actualmente el municipio. 

El proceso ha comenzado en el CEIP Gaspar Remiro, entendido como uno de los lugares de encuentro y socialización de Épila. A través de conversaciones con alumnado de 5.º y 6.º de Primaria, el artista irá reuniendo fotografías, historias, lugares y recuerdos que servirán como punto de partida para construir la obra. 

Familias arraigadas en Épila desde hace generaciones y otras llegadas desde distintos lugares forman parte hoy de una misma realidad social, agrícola e industrial.

Fotografías antiguas, fragmentos de paisaje y arquitectura, figuras humanas, objetos cotidianos y símbolos locales se irán superponiendo para construir un relato sobre la tierra que compartimos.

📍 Carretera Muel a Lumpiaque, esquina con Camino Los Huertos

¡Nueva edición de Asalto en Épila!

Cinco ediciones construyendo una relación entre creación contemporánea, espacio público y territorio. 

Este año damos un paso más: el mural sigue estando presente, pero el proyecto se abre a otros lenguajes y formas de intervenir.

Pintura, ilustración, retrato, instalación, cerámica, memoria oral y procesos participativos para acercarnos a Épila desde lugares diferentes. 

Cinco artistas y proyectos formarán parte de esta edición:

Harsa y Sara Marcos / @harsa_pati / @sara.marcos_ con Épila: un recorrido ilustrado del territorio.
 
Hugo Casanova / @hugo.elhugo, con La tierra que compartimos

David Feroce / @david.feroce, con Recetas para la vida

Isabel Garmon / @isigarmon, con Épila al natural.

Y Elisa Terroba / @elisa_terroba con Barricada Cultural.

Y además, música, paseo por las intervenciones y un vermú vecinal para encontrarnos y celebrar juntos esta quinta edición. 

¡Muy pronto os contamos mucho más!

#AsaltoEnÉpila #Épila #ArteContemporáneo #ArteUrbano #CulturaContemporánea

Para su intervención en Farlete, Nicolás ha desarrollado una recopilación de objetos conservados por los propios vecinos en sus casas. 

Lejos de buscar piezas excepcionales o de valor histórico monumental, Nicolás se interesó por aquellos elementos cotidianos que, con el paso del tiempo, han adquirido una carga emocional y simbólica para quienes los conservan. 

Esta forma de trabajar conecta con una parte fundamental de su trayectoria artística, centrada en la observación de los objetos, los símbolos populares y las huellas que las personas dejan en su entorno. 

El resultado es una gran naturaleza muerta contemporánea donde conviven piezas aparentemente inconexas que, al ser colocadas juntas, construyen un retrato colectivo del pueblo.

Formalmente, este mural combina la monumentalidad característica de sus murales con una composición cercana a la tradición clásica del bodegón. La intensidad cromática de la obra, dominada por el amarillo de fondo y los contrastes entre azules, verdes, rojos y negros, dota al mural de una presencia vibrante que destaca en el paisaje urbano. Al mismo tiempo, la composición mantiene una lectura cercana y accesible, permitiendo que cualquier vecino pueda reconocer en ella fragmentos de su propia historia.

Esta intervención forma parte del proyecto COMMUN: Community Murals Now – Urban Art for Social Change desarrollado por @b.murals financiado por el @culturagob

La intervención de Laura Merayo en Farlete se construye desde una mirada contemporánea hacia el mundo rural, alejada de la nostalgia y de los estereotipos. 

Laura toma como punto de partida una joven pastora caminando entre un rebaño de ovejas en los campos que rodean el municipio. Sin embargo, la obra trasciende la representación para convertirse en una reflexión sobre la identidad, la permanencia y el futuro de los territorios rurales.

La composición se organiza en dos lenguajes visuales complementarios. Una pintura figurativa de gran sensibilidad que se construye mediante pinceladas visibles, veladuras y una paleta cálida, frente a una estructura gráfica inspirada en los repertorios visuales tradicionales: retículas, tipografías de raíz histórica y una serie de símbolos que remiten a elementos fundamentales de la cultura local. 

Estos iconos funcionan como una suerte de heráldica popular, un inventario de aquello que constituye la memoria colectiva del lugar.

“Defiende el rural” se plantea como una invitación a reconocer el valor cultural, humano y medioambiental de los pueblos. La defensa del mundo rural no aparece aquí ligada únicamente a la conservación del pasado, sino también a la capacidad de imaginar futuros posibles desde el arraigo, el cuidado del territorio y la continuidad de sus comunidades.

La obra de Allan Halley se construye a partir de fotografías familiares aportadas por los propios vecinos de Farlete.

A través de una pintura delicada y fragmentaria, el artista reúne tres imágenes cargadas de simbolismo:

La figura central de la niña actúa como eje emocional de la composición. A su alrededor aparecen otras presencias familiares que parecen emerger y desvanecerse al mismo tiempo, como ocurre con los recuerdos que sobreviven al paso del tiempo. Junto a ella, las flores introducen una dimensión más poética y evocadora que, tratadas con una pincelada suelta y atmosférica, parecen surgir de la memoria más que de la observación directa. 

En el extremo izquierdo, una escena muestra a varias personas portando una imagen religiosa durante una celebración popular. Lejos de centrarse en el carácter devocional de la escena, Allan desplaza la atención hacia quienes sostienen el rito colectivo, lo que nos habla de la dimensión comunitaria de las tradiciones.

Con este trabajo, Allan Halley nos invita a reconocer que la identidad de una comunidad se compone tanto de los grandes acontecimientos como de los pequeños gestos, los afectos, las celebraciones y los recuerdos compartidos que se transmiten de generación en generación.

💫 Vuelve VITA URBIS, un festival cultural con el que nos acercamos a nuestro pasado.

💫 Este año, el artista @elmiguelperalta realizará un mural de gran formato inspirado en uno de los episodios más significativos del yacimiento La Cabañeta: la huida repentina de la población por un ataque a la ciudad.

🏺 En esta huida dejaron atrás objetos cotidianos como joyas, herramientas o enseres domésticos que hoy nos permiten reconstruir diferentes aspectos de la vida en la ciudad.

🏁 26 August 1967

On this day, Burt Munro recorded an average speed of 184.087 mph (296.259 km/h) at the Bonneville Salt Flats, setting a world record in the Class S-A 1000cc category aboard his modified 1920 Indian Scout.

It was the achievement of a lifelong pursuit and a moment that would forever connect Southland with the world of motorcycle racing.

Each year on 26 August, riders and motorsport fans pause to remember the day Burt's name was etched into the record books, not simply for the speed he achieved, but for what the achievement represents: the pursuit of a goal, no matter how ambitious.

As we mark this historic anniversary, we also look ahead to another milestone. In February 2027, the Burt Munro Challenge celebrates 20 years, bringing together the people, motorcycles, and stories that continue to keep Burt's legacy alive.

#20YearsOfBurtMunroChallenge #BurtMunro #Bonneville #Southland #MotorcycleHistory

🏍️ Did You Know?
Burt Munro didn't make just one trip to Bonneville.

Over the years, he returned to the famous Salt Flats again and again, continuously improving his machine in pursuit of more speed.

His legendary 1967 record was the result of decades of dedication, innovation and countless hours spent chasing a dream.

📸 Photo supplied by Garry Jamieson

🏍️ 20 Years of Burt

Teretonga Sprint Races at the very first Burt Munro Challenge in 2006.
Twenty years later, Teretonga remains one of the iconic stops on the Burt Munro Challenge calendar.

Do you recognise anyone in this photo? Tag them below!

📸 Archive photo – Burt Munro Challenge 2006

#20YearsOfBurtMunroChallenge

🏍️ Did You Know?

Burt Munro got faster... 37 years after he died.

His famous 1967 Bonneville run was originally recorded at 183.586 mph.

In 2014, that figure was corrected to 184.087 mph (296.3 km/h), confirming Burt had actually gone even faster than first recorded.

Nearly five decades after setting the record, history finally caught up with the man from Invercargill.

📸 Photo supplied by Garry Jamieson

De la calle al mundo. 🇷🇺🌎 ¿Qué pasa cuando distintas formas de vivir la cultura urbana se encuentran en un mismo lugar?

En KARDO conviven el graffiti, breaking, skate, BMX, rap, DJing, parkour y muchas otras expresiones que siguen creciendo alrededor del mundo.

El proyecto reunió a casi 80 mil participantes de 195 países, con una programación que abarcó 13 disciplinas de cultura urbana y deporte. Pero más allá de los números, hay algo que se repite en cada encuentro: gente que llega con algo propio, lo comparte y encuentra nuevas formas de seguir creciendo.

Desliza y conoce un poco más sobre KARDO. 🧡

Fantastic week last week! Big cheers to Te Waiponamu for putting on some epic crowds for the 10th ASFF 🤙 Next week we’re wrapping it all up in Whangarei, Auckland & Tauranga! Yeeha! 🌊🌊 Here’s a taste of one of the hit films from the tour. ‘Nancy’ by Anna Frances Pearson. ‘Nancy is in her 90s and lives a simple life by the sea in Sumner, gardening and hitting the surf on a board made by Christchurch’s legendary gumboot-manufacturing Skellerup factory. The surfboard – made in the 1970s – is a little worse for wear, but Nancy – made in the 1920s – exudes an infectious amount of joy riding the waves on her vintage piece of foam.’ 🤙🤙

This week the South Island tour is back!
Here’s a taster of ‘Tears of a Mountain ~  Ngā roimata ō te maunga’ by @beach_thurlow 🎥 
As Karioi lays dormant, she watches over Whāingaroa. The tears that flow down her body and into the sea, refracting the southerly swell around her feet, where chaotic energy bends into perfect waves. 
Tickets to see this and many more / ASFF.CO.NZ 🎟

Next week the South Island tour is on! 🎞
Here’s a taster of ‘Jonas Tawharu | Rusty Part’ by @oscarjohns & @jonastawharu 🎥 
The part is filmed over two years, mostly through winters in the deep south of New Zealand. Surfer Jonas Tawharu and filmmaker Oscar Johns teamed up again to document Jonas's ability in some of the best waves in the South Island. Pouring their own time, money and knowledge into this project and spending their free time travelling and filming in some of the harshest conditions in New Zealand.
Tickets to see this and many more / ASFF.CO.NZ
Coromandel 🌊🌊 Unreal to be back 💛 Come along to our screening tonight in Whitianga @ Monkey House Theatre kicking off at 7PM 🤙

Benefits of being on tour! Few gems from this morning 🌊
Gizzie we’re in your neck of the woods tonight! SOLD OUT show, kicking off at 7pm 🤙🤙

🎬🌊 The 2026 ASFF Programme is HERE
Once again, we’ve been blown away by the calibre of submissions. This year we received 50+ films from Aotearoa and around the world, making it no easy task to trim things down to a tight two-hour programme. Massive congrats to everyone who submitted — the creativity, storytelling, and surf stoke on display this year is next level.
The selected films span New Zealand and abroad, delivering spectacular surfing, innovative cinematography, and stories that dig a little deeper. We can’t wait to share this programme with audiences up and down the motu.

ASFF Film submissions are closing in one month! Get those final edits done people, as we’re about to get our 15th ASFF Tour programme together. For all submission info, hit the link in bio 🔗
Submissions close 22 Nov, 2026.

Video features flavours from this years tour thanks to @isaac_chaddy @dano.fletcher @wahinewaveriders_film @sinkorsurface @andydavisstudios

🌊🎥 Here we go whānau — 15 years of ASFF! Film submissions are OPEN!

Every year the films get bigger, bolder, and more local than ever. We’re frothing to see more Kiwi surf stories hitting the screen — a huge credit to you talented filmmakers bringing the stoke from Aotearoa’s coastlines to the masses.
Dust off the GoPro, dig into the archives, or round up the crew for that dream session. Whether you’re pro, amateur, or giving it a crack for the first time — we want your story. 
If it celebrates the art of wave-riding in all its wild and wonderful diversity, it belongs on the big screen.
👉 Submissions now open at asff.co.nz
🏄‍♀️ NZ & International submissions open ⏰ Entries close 22 November 2026
We’ll be announcing new prize categories, tour stops, and sponsors in the coming months. For now, good luck and big ups to all the filmmakers — can’t wait to see what you’ve been cooking up.
🤙 Mā te wā 🌊

Huge congrats to TOM GILBERTSON @gilb19 of Kaikōura ⛰️🐋, who has taken out the @verduresurf $2000 custom surfboard voucher prize 💥

A massive shoutout to Jack and the @verduresurf team for sponsoring the tour this year, legends of the NZ shaping game, doing some incredible mahi in moving the industry toward environmentally conscious surfboard production, while simultaneously creating high-performance designs.

Big ups legends! 🌴🌞

The ASFF 2026 finale was seriously special. A very cool vibe in that fine, fine theatre. A few highlight moments captured and collated by @jeanpi_g . Give us a 🙋 if you can glimpse yourself in the clip 🌞

Highlights of the night include:
• Having two of our film makers present for the evening, and watching their faces light up with joy at the way the everyone lapped up their films @dano.fletcher @sinkorsurface 
• Watching Ben Maurice @sinkorsurface receive Best Kiwi Film Award for “Bread & Butter”, and give a touching speech highlighting the amazing Pōneke surf scene.
• Witnessing the uber talented @georgevillanz start the night off with fan-favourite and unreleased material
• Seeing the pure stoke on everyone’s faces, and having amazing conversations with you all the whole night through.

A big thanks to you TĀMAKI MAKAURAU for an impeccable finale filled with ecstasy and stoke, and a memorable night for us involved in ASFF.

Stay tuned for full 2026 tour wrap up ❤️‍🔥

🌊🏆 Awards Time Our 14th year — and by far the biggest yet.
We wrapped things up in style last night at @hollywoodavondale with a sold-out crowd, epic films, and an all-time vibe. We’re stoked to announce this years film winners:
🎬 Best Kiwi Film Huge congrats to @sinkorsurface for ‘Bread & Butter’ — a standout South Coast story that hit home.
🎥 People’s Choice Award, Presented by @yeti_nzl @yeti_au Big ups to @wahinewaveriders_film @forgettingkirstymarshall @zyanya_jackson — voted by the people, for the people.
🌱Most Environmentally Conscious Film, Supported by @patagoniaaus : @haustumbuna by @matty_hannon & Nicki Wynnychuk

Special shoutout to all filmmakers for submitting into this years festival and to our incredible judging panel — we couldn’t do it without you. Thanks for your time, care, and sharp eyes: @photocpl @amberandfriendsphoto @gavinbisman @christyprior ✨

TĀMAKI MAKAURAU!! The 14th Aotearoa Surf Film Festival hits your neck of the woods, TONIGHT, for the nationwide finale… 💥

What a special couple of months on the road. Can’t wait to go absolutely all out tonight to bring it home to Tāmaki. Revel in a few beautiful images from previous years at Hollywood Avondale 🌞

Stoked to have the legendary @georgevillanz (pictured last slide) performing a solo set tonight too. An absolute weapon of a songwriter and sure to leave ya’s enthralled with his infectious spirit.

🌊💚 Sponsor Spotlight — Patagonia
We’re proud to have the kind humans @patagoniaaus back to the ASFF whānau for the fourth year running.
The good crew at Patagonia continue to back conscious storytelling in Aotearoa, supporting the Most Environmentally Conscious Film Award — recognising filmmakers who are using surf cinema to highlight sustainability, environmental protection, and meaningful action.
The award is open to filmmakers from New Zealand and Australia, celebrating authentic stories that shine a light on the people and ideas working to protect our oceans and coastlines.

🏆 The winning filmmaker receives: $1000 Patagonia voucher & $500 cash to donate toward an environmental cause or social enterprise highlighted in their film

Massive thanks to Patagonia for continuing to support filmmakers telling stories that matter! We’ll be announcing the Most Environmentally Conscious Film @ the Finale THIS FRI @hollywoodavondale 

P.S. Te Whanganui-a-Tara folks, did you also know Patagonia have opened up a new store? Open daily @ 13 Tory St. 🏠

🌊🎬 Final Week of the ASFF Tour!
What a ride it’s been. From the deep south in Riverton all the way to the far north in Kaitaia, Tour Manager @max_came has been charging the length of the motu sharing surf stories, good yarns, and packed houses along the way.
Now we’re rolling into the final week of shows — a few last chances to catch the programme on the big screen before we wrap things up for the year. 📍 Tonight — Aotea, Great Barrier Island @abc.aotea 
📍 Tues — Whangārei @oneonesixwhangarei  📍 Wed — Mangawhai  📍 Thurs — Matakana @matakanacinemas  📍 Fri — Grand Finale in Auckland @hollywoodavondale 
Massive thanks to everyone who’s come out so far — filmmakers, audiences, venues, and our partners who make the tour possible. Let’s finish strong 🤙
🎟 Last tickets → asff.co.nz

A reminder that we have an Easter Saturday show tonight in Kaitaia (@teahu_cinema ), and an Easter Monday show this coming Monday at Aotea, Great Barrier Island (@barriersocialclub ). Tickets still available for both shows!

Enjoy the Easter weekend. Hope you get plenty of time in the water 🦭

Last year’s murals are being removed as we prepare the boards for nine new murals at International Mural Fest 2026. It may look a little bare for now, but from 1-7 November, artists will bring this year’s theme, ‘Paint Me A Song’, to life.

We mourn the passing of one of Sheffield’s great mural artists, John Eathorne of West Tamar, Tasmania.

John left a lasting mark on our town, painting many beautiful murals and achieving recognition as a multi International Mural Fest Finalist. 

Across a career spanning more than four decades, John worked as a freelance commercial artist specialising in sign writing, murals, and fine art portraiture with projects commissioned throughout Australia and internationally. 

You will be greatly missed John, but your work and your legacy will remain part of Sheffield and the Kentish Municipality forever. ❤️

#desertmob2022

The Garma Festival is Australia's largest Indigenous gathering, a 4-day celebration of Yolngu life and culture in remote northeast Arnhem Land. 

Hosted by the Yothu Yindi Foundation, the event showcases traditional Yolngu miny'tji (art), manikay (song), bunggul (dance), and story-telling, and is an important meeting point for the clans and families of the region. 

Garma 2022 will take place from Friday 29 July - Monday 1 August, at Gulkula, a Gumatj ceremonial site about 40km from the township of Gove.

Follow @garma_festival_official to stay up to date with the festival activities!! 

Come together in the Top End this August for the world’s biggest week of events celebrating Australia’s First Nations peoples in Art, Music and Culture 🔗 #linkinbio

#NIFA2022 #indigenousfashionprojects #countrytocouture #darwinartfair #natsiaa #nima2022 #garma #garmafestival #garma2022 #yolngufestival #yolnguculture #yolngucountry

📸 Cover image: Toddler Joban Yunupingu stole the show at Garma 2019, looking up to his elders for guidance while performing bunggul (traditional dance) at the opening ceremony, Photo by Melanie Faith Dove. 
🎥 Video courtesy of Garma (Yothu Yindi Foundation).

Ever wanted to learn some kunwok (language)?

Join language teachers Kalidjan Janet Marawarr and Ngarridjdjan Raylene Bonson from Maningrida and get familiar with 20 Kuninjku words you should know!

Kuninjku is a dialect of Bininj Kunwok, a language belonging to people in Central/Western Arnhem Land.

This event will be hosted at Darwin’s freshest art space ‘The Laundry Gallery’ in Parap! Can’t wait to host you all there- bookings essential. #linkinbio☝🏾

Part 3: Our Art Centres 

“What is an art Centre?”

DAAF Foundation is a not-for-profit Indigenous organisation owned and governed by the Art Centres it represents.

But Art Centres are far more than governing bodies — they are the heart of community life. They are places where culture is maintained, stories are shared, artists are supported, and generations come together. Their role extends far beyond governance, not only for us, but for the communities they belong to. 

Image courtesy of Art Centres 

1. Papunya Tula Artists 
3. Hermannsburg Potters 
4. Bindi Mwerre Anthurre Artists 
5. Tjarlirli and kaltukatjara art 
7. Karungkarni Art and Culture

9. Papulankutja Artists

Revisiting some of the stunning works that sold during DAAF Online last month. A reminder that many of the Art Centres involved have online stores you can visit year-round.

This piece, ‘Yukuwa’, is by artist Djirrirra Wunuŋmurra from Buku-Larrŋgay Mulka.

Yukuwa is one of Djirrirra’s personal names and the subject of this work, with the motif described as almost a self-portrait and an expression of her personal identity.

Yukuwa is a yam whose annual reappearance is a metaphor for the increase and renewal of people and Country. The work also references Yirritja renewal ceremony and the kinship lines that connect groups together.

Yukuwa
Earth pigment on paper
56.5 × 30.2 cm
Buku-Larrŋgay Mulka

Can you guess how many sales were made at DAAF this year?? 🧐

No matter how much - we never take commission. 100% of sales return directly to First Nations Art Centres, artists, and their communities right across Australia. That's real impact.

Want to see how big this year's number is? Our full Impact Report is dropping soon! Stay tuned.

This linocut is by artist Bayalki Dhamarrandji from Buku-Larrŋgay Mulka.

“When I was little I would watch the older people preparing gunga (pandanus). Old people have been doing this for a long time. A few years ago I started making gunga. I enjoy it and I now teach my daughter.

The colours of this print are latju (beautiful), the blue makes me think of water, waves and rain. The pink is like the colours we use for dyeing gunga.”

Bayalki Dhamarrandji
Linocut

Buku-Larrŋgay Mulka

Marcus has been painting since 2017 and is known for his signature minimalist style of action painting. His distinctive grid-and-band compositions are guided by fluid formulae and mental mathematics, echoing sketches he creates on pieces of scrap paper and is said to have drawn since childhood.

🚨SCAM ALERT – PLEASE READ🚨

We've seen an increase in scams targeting our stallholder community, so we'd like to remind everyone how to identify genuine communications from our team.

Official emails will ONLY come from emails ending in the following:
• @marketlife.com.au
• @perthmakersmarket.com
• @perthupmarket.com.au

⚠️ Common scams we're seeing include:
• Comments or messages claiming there are stallholder spaces available and asking you to DM someone privately.
• Fake emails offering stallholder opportunities for events we don't run.
• People pretending to represent our markets in Facebook groups.
• Emails offering to sell our stallholder database.
• Fake commission requests.
• Requests for payment via PayPal.

Please remember:
❌ We will NEVER ask you to message a staff member's personal Facebook account.
❌ We will NEVER ask you to pay via PayPal.
❌ We will NEVER request payment or personal information from an unknown email address.
✅ All market applications are made through the MarketLife website.
✅ All successful applications are invoiced via email from events@marketlife.com.au
✅ If you see different stall prices from those listed on our website, it's a scam.

If you receive a suspicious email or message:
• Don't reply.
• Don't click any links.
• Don't provide personal information or make any payments.

If you're ever unsure, please contact us directly at events@marketlife.com.au, before taking any action. 

Thank you for helping keep our stallholder community safe. Please share this post with fellow makers and report any scam posts or accounts you come across.

latestIgtvVideos.title: The Byron Community Pantry
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
We want to extend a HUGE thank you to everyone who donated to the Byron Community Pantry!

Thanks to your generosity, we are able to deliver food boxes to Byron Shire locals in need who are unable to financially and physically shop.

We want to use this opportunity to share an update with you. In the last months, meals given out by the Byron Community Centre have doubled. Currently, we deliver 500 meals weekly through the Byron Community Pantry, and our friends at Liberation Larder Inc are giving out 400 weekly meals at the Centre.

The majority of people asking for help are international students who are unable to travel home and workers who are unable to access any government support. Most people now ask for vegetarian meals, but in the past, the request for meat meals was at 50%. We see that the Byron Community Pantry project will need to extend well beyond COVID-19 closedowns as we expect the impact in our community to last years. And we need your help to help the community!

If you can, please support the Byron community Panty with a financial donation. With your help, we will be able to purchase necessary items like fruit & veg; staples like muesli/tinned goods/pasta, etc. and personal care items. To donate today, visit https://byroncentre.com.au/donations/bcc/

Thank you very much for your support!

All donations are tax-deductible, 20% of every donation is used for admin costs.

#byroncommunitycentre #byroncommunitypantry
