Great stories need time, space and support to grow.

Byron Theatre Company is proud to launch 𝘚𝘵𝘰𝘳𝘺𝘵𝘦𝘭𝘭𝘦𝘳𝘴, a new development program supporting Northern Rivers artists to create and develop original Australian theatre right here in the region.

Four projects will be selected for a three-day Development Lab at Byron Theatre, with up to two progressing to a five-day Project Residency and work-in-progress showing.

Confirmed mentors include producer Jane Fuller and award-winning director Heather Fairbairn, with guest mentors including acclaimed actor and director Wayne Blair joining artists during the Residency stage.

Whether you’re developing a new play, devised work, physical theatre, contemporary performance or something that crosses disciplines, we want to hear what you’re creating.

Expressions of Interest are now open via the link in our bio.

Applications close Sunday 1 November at 6pm.

"Every classic play was once a new work." - Jane Fuller

And every new work needs the opportunity to grow.

That's the thinking behind Storytellers, Byron Theatre Company's new artist development program for Northern Rivers theatre-makers.

We're inviting creative teams to bring their original projects into a space where they can experiment, challenge ideas, take creative risks and discover what their work might become.

Experienced producer Jane Fuller and award-winning director Heather Fairbairn will lead the mentorship, with additional guest practitioners chosen to suit the needs of each project. Because every work is different, and the right creative support can make all the difference.

Four teams will be selected for a three-day Development Lab in January 2027, with up to two progressing to five-day residencies. Artist funding, professional mentorship and dedicated creative time are all part of the program.

Have a project you'd love to develop? We'd love to hear from you.

SUPPORTING THE PEOPLE WHO SUPPORT OUR COMMUNITY.

Behind some of the Northern Rivers' most important community services are dedicated people working every day to support others.

At @vitariatraining we believe being a local business should mean more than only operating in the Northern Rivers. It should mean contributing to the community around us.

Through our Community Partnership Program, we're proud to recognise our newest Community Partners - @fletcherstreet_cottage & @byroncommunitycentre!

Recently, @vitariatraining had the privilege of delivering hands-on CPR & Emergency Preparedness training to their staff and volunteers, sharing practical lifesaving skills, frontline specialist paramedic experience and the confidence to respond when it matters.

The work both @fletcherstreet_cottage & @byroncommunitycentre do for people experiencing homelessness, hardship and social isolation is incredibly important, particularly as housing pressures continue to rise across our region.

We were especially grateful for the feedback from Damian Farrell, Manager of Fletcher Street Cottage:

“Please consider supporting the training organisation that supports our community.”

For us, that captures exactly why we established this program and why @vitariatraining exists.

Our commitment is to use our specialist paramedic knowledge and frontline experience to support the organisations and people making a genuine difference across the Northern Rivers.

A sincere thank you to Damian and the teams at @fletcherstreet_cottage & @byroncommunitycentre for the important work you do.

We're proud to play a small part in supporting it.

Learn more about the ongoing challenges facing our region and what @fletcherstreet_cottage is doing here

Happy snaps recapping Flotsam's sold-out launch for A Living Ocean, an underwater deep dive curated by marine wildlife photographer @eviewilderness 

Captured moments from Gold Coast's world-renowned surf breaks, A Living Ocean showed an entirely different world exists just below the surface. Evie took the audience through the collection, including camera gear used, tips for underwater shooting, and the stories behind the images captured and diversity of life and beauty below

Loved Evie's prints? You're in luck -select images from the collection are now available, see @eviewilderness to shop her print store

A Living Ocean was supported by @nikonaustralia

📷@curious_luce

Dream Day by @andrewkidman 
Featuring: @lacurren @stephaniegilmore a pod of dolphins, and Kirra

A top finalist in this year's Flotsam Homegrown surf clip awards, this short film by Andrew Kidman features Lee-Ann Curren getting a dream tour of Kirra with Steph Gilmore and a cast of fine finned locals. Lee-Ann's vocals also feature on the soundtrack by Kidman's band Sunset & The Windy Hills 

Enjoy!

Dig the soundtrack? Sunset and the Windy Hills new LP - Dirty Power - is available to pre-order now on Bandcamp

Dale's Snapper vs Kirra fist raise ✊

Did you experience Flotsam's Focal Point in AR? One of the new additions to this year's Flotsam Festival was the use of augmented reality to bring surf images to life. 

By scanning the Focal Point outdoor photo installations, visitors unlocked stories, interviews and archival footage connected to the images on display - preserving not just iconic moments, faces and places, but the memories and voices behind them.

This installation paired an iconic image of Dale Richards from a momentous 2012 Kirra swell. Footage from @shaggamang of Dale at Snapper was superimposed over the photograph by @sweetocean to show Dale in motion - fists firmly raised in both captures

Once one of the region's finest up and comers, Dale rocked the surfing world when he won the Quiksilver Pro Trials in 2007 and in doing so, become one of the first aboriginal surfers to compete in a WCT event - paving the way for the current crop of standout indigenous talent putting their stamp on the lineup

Focal Point exhibition is Flotsam's interactive archive of Gold Coast surf culture, connecting generations through the stories that shape our coastline. Flotsam's Focal Point installations are packed away for another year, but the images live on. 

Surfer: @darkydale_2.0

Film: @shaggamang

Photo: @sweetocean

#FlotsamFestival #SurfCulture #AugmentedReality #GoldCoastSurfing

Flotsam Retrospect rolled out classic surf cinema at iconic Kirra Hill with filmmaker and founder of @surffilmarchive Jolyon Hoff hosting a panel of pioneering surf filmmakers and photographers, including Dick Hoole, David "Mex" Sumpter and @harveysurf 

The surf nostalgia deep dive included rare big screen screenings of Searching for Micheal Peterson and You Should Have Been Here Yesterday at Kirra's historic cultural centre overlooking the world famous break. 

Flotsam Retrospect brought together aficionados of the art of surf filmmaking for a candid evening with true legends of the lens.

Flotsam hosts event like Retrospect during the festival to archive the coast while it’s still evolving. Historic surf photography exhibitions, film retrospectives and photo walks connect the Gold Coast’s past to its emerging identity, and treat surf history as something worth coming together to share and preserve. Thanks to all who shared the night with us!

Flotsam Homegrown surf clip Youth Division is always hotly contested, with several age divisions throwing down their best waves. This year each division winner scored filming + coaching sessions with Zane and Brook Silvester at Bombora while vying for the overall prize of a new surfboard by @woodsurfboardslennox 

U/18 finalists @marley.orourke @natecorowa and @hemi.obrien had their big screen moment at Homegrown, with Hemi taking first place + scoring the @bombora.surf.school prize bundle. Congrats to all finalists! 

More age division clips + winners to come

Hemi footage 🎥: @gartner.films @charliecullenmedia

Surfer Dave Rastovich and filmmakers Chris Miyashiro and Milo Inglis took audiences on a journey of conservation and creativity at Flotsam Oceans, part of the Kirra Immerse Hub outdoor film program during the festival. 

Kicking off with a beach cleanup and info booth with @surfridergoldcoast audiences were treated to live music by @haydengoseek @breadnbutterphotobooth keepsake photos for all before evening skies lit up with films. @patagoniaaus brought their 'Sensing Home' film tour finale to Oceans, with filmmaker @milo_inglis and surfers Dave Rastovich and Chris Miyashiro on hand, plus the magical 'Aʻā' by @mystomiyashiro Ecofoam + more

See full event gallery over on the Flotsam Facebook page

INTRODUCING THE NEXT ACT FUND RECIPIENTS! 🎭

We're pleased to announce the latest recipients of the ARTRAGE Next Act Fund!

The fund is dedicated to supporting emerging artists and creative talent, providing opportunities to develop new ideas, explore creative possibilities and bring innovative projects to life.

Congratulations to this year's recipients! We're proud to support the next generation of artists and look forward to seeing their work.

From the ARTRAGE archives: ECLIPSE, 2 November 2002.

Picture this. It's a Saturday night in Northbridge. You've got $15 in your pocket, your best going-out outfit on and absolutely no idea what you're about to walk into.

Welcome to ECLIPSE, the official closing party of the 2002 ARTRAGE Festival.

Taking over Russell Square's Moon Garden, the night brought together German electronic music, circus performers, aerial acts, fashion installations and even an electric stunt violinist. Your ticket also got you into The Bakery for a set from German electronic act Funkstörung.

More than two decades later, ECLIPSE offers a glimpse into ARTRAGE’s history of transforming Perth's spaces into places for artistic experimentation, creative expression and unforgettable experiences.

Remember this one? We'd love to hear your memories in the comments. 🕺

CELEBRATING 15 YEARS OF ROOFTOP MOVIES 🎬

What began as an idea to transform a Northbridge car park into an open-air cinema has become one of Perth’s most loved summer traditions.

15 years later, Rooftop Movies continues to bring people together through film, entertainment and unique experiences in the heart of the city.

As we proudly celebrate this milestone and welcome another season, we’re looking back at the legacy of Rooftop Movies and the exciting journey that brought us here.

🔗 Read the full story via the link in bio.

Another summer, another season of @rooftopmovies🍿

It's officially back, and we couldn’t be more excited to welcome this new season of movie magic. Our team has been working hard behind the scenes to bring Rooftop Movies to life, with a programme packed full of cult classics and crowd favourites.

We can’t wait to see the space come alive again and share another season of unforgettable nights with you all.

Tickets on sale now! Discover more via the link in bio.

📸 @portia_gebauer_photographer

NO ART. NO FUTURE.

For over 40 years, ARTRAGE has believed in the power of creativity, bold ideas and giving artists the space to showcase something that matters.

Our latest article explores why art has always mattered, why it still does, and why a future without it isn’t much of a future at all.

🔗 Read the full article via the link in bio.

📸 @vidimage

From the ARTRAGE archives: SoCo Cargo, 2007.

Four shipping containers had landed on Roe Street. But instead of doing what shipping containers normally do, these ones had polished floorboards, Art Deco furniture, a stage, a bar and a seriously good sound system. Meet SoCo Cargo.

Fresh from popping up around Australia and overseas, the 300-person live music venue landed in Northbridge for ARTRAGE’s 2007 Alphabet City festival joining a collection of spaces that included an old ice-cream factory, a former luxury car showroom, The Bakery and a switchyard. Because apparently a normal venue was a little too… normal.

For a few weeks, this pocket of Northbridge became a playground for live music, performance, visual art and plenty of late nights, before it all came together for XYZ  a multi-venue, multi-artform precinct party to close out the festival.

Nearly 20 years later, a lot has changed.

But taking over unexpected corners of Perth, filling them with artists and giving people a very good reason to leave the house?

Sounds pretty familiar.

¡PRIMER LUGAR EN GRAFFITI! 🏆🇵🇪 COLORIZA ha sido reconocido como organización que promueve el graffiti a nivel internacional. Estuvimos en el podio junto a dos organizaciones rusas 🇷🇺 que hacen un gran trabajo: ZWS CREW @zws.crew y TIME FOR ART @time_for_art_rus , un gusto conocer a sus representantes y líderes.

Este reconocimiento en KARDO 2026 celebra el trabajo, la constancia y todo lo que venimos construyendo desde el graffiti y el arte urbano.

Un premio que nos llena de orgullo y que representa a todas las personas que han sido parte de este camino.  Gracias, KARDO, por reconocer el arte urbano y darle un espacio para seguir llegando más lejos.🌎🎉

biography: Annual Sydney zine fair that began in 2014 and continues to be community-run. 2026 table applications closed 15 April x 📧otherworldszinefair@gmail

latestIgtvVideos.caption: The seventh Other Worlds Zine fair will be held in person this May 29, 2022 back at our beloved Marrickville Town Hall. 🌹🌹🌹We are very happy to be back, albeit with a few changed rules, and in celebration this year there are no table fees! Follow the link in our bio to read more and register for your free table, applications close April 1!

latestPosts.caption:
Thank you to everyone who came to Other Worlds on Saturday. 

We hope you had a great time! We did :)

Keep tagging us or use #otherworldszinefair to share your zine haul. 

x Other Worlders
We are here! Open til 4, free as always, come on down to the Peter Forsyth Auditorium 📏

1 week to go 👀

Other Worlds 2026, 11-4pm
Saturday July 11
Peter Forsyth Auditorium in Glebe

💓

One month to go before Other Worlds 2026! 

Meet us at the Peter Forsyth Auditorium in Glebe, 11-4 on July 11th, admission free as always. Poster by Aphrodite D (School of Zines) and thanks to our friends at @glompress for the printing.

You have no doubt seen this year's OWZF poster by Aphrodite D (School of Zines) doing the rounds in the zinesphere, but here is a hearfelt thanks to Aphrodite, for creating this wonderful image, and for all their tireless work for the zine community ✨️

And will remain open until April 15! 🫲🫱

The link to apply is in our bio and on our website.

If you have any questions the best way to reach out to us is not! on here but via our email - otherworldszinefair @ gmail

Save the date! Other Worlds returns - but at a new time and place. Applications open mid March and will be open for 1 month - links updates and info will be posted here and on our new website, link in bio X

What a weekend we had (Sydney had)! It was so great to see the fair packed as ever even in the pouring rain and then of course to see hundreds of thousands turning out for Palestine the next day. We raised a totally incredible $696.75 from our donations box but looking at our bank account we decided the money could be better used going to @para.foundation this year, ty to everyone who pitched in, it’s really an incredible community.

Next year our beloved M’ville town hall will be closed for renos, so we will be moving to a new venue and (once again) perhaps to a slightly different time of year so keep your eyes peeled for our announcements! We always try to give an indication of what we’re doing around the time of the @sticky_institute Festival of the Photocopier in February. 

Big X 
OW
Down at the zine fair — it’s happening now!
It’s here, it’s here - it’s basically here! Bring your ☂️ and we’ll see you all tomorrow.

2 DAYS TO GO TILL THE ZINE FAIR! In the lead up, we are highlighting some of our fantastic stallholders in their own words and images. Give them all a follow! See previous posts for other zinemakers you may meet at the fair!

1) @glompress

Glom is a riso printer and press based in Naarm - we make hand-made books and prints, with a particular focus on comics. 

2) @leemitchell888 

Creates one of a kind, handcrafted zines from salvaged books/labels/capitalist detritus.

Explores contemporary themes, memes and collective dreams.

3) @cheylondevine.design

Hi I'm Cheylon, I make whimsical illustrated zines in a variety of mediums.

3 DAYS TO GO TILL THE ZINE FAIR! In the lead up, we are highlighting some of our fantastic stallholders in their own words and images! Give them all a follow and see the previous posts for information about some other zines and zinemakers you'll see at the fair on Saturday!

1) @refugeeartproject 

We support people of a refugee background through art workshops, exhibitions & zines in our studio @ Thirning Villa Ashfield on Gadigal land.

2) @artofpei 

Pause. The quiet rebellion is a zine inspired by all the simple, joyful moments in life that we often take for granted. An appreciation for slow living and a reminder to live in the moment. 

3) @betweeniaproject 

betweenia is a Naarm-based art book and zine project connecting Sinophone (Chinese-speaking & Chinese-ethnic) voices across the Asia-Pacific to publish, distribute, and imagine from the in-between.

4) @emilouwalsh

Emilie Walsh is launching a new zine 'Old C*nt' at OWZF! Freshly out of the press of her printmaking studio @c_o_u_l_e_u_r_

5) @ctyalcinkaya 

Can Yalcinkaya, who made the Other Worlds Zine Fair poster this year, is launching the first issues of his comics series, The Gurbet Fuzz, out from @glompress, along with a limited edition linocut print.

latestPosts.caption:
COMING FROM OVERSEAS TO REPCO BEACH HOP 2027? THIS ONE’S FOR YOU!

You travel from all corners of the world to join the party, and this year we’ve got something special for you,
our NEW International Visitors Pass!

Whether you’ve been coming for years or this is your first Beach Hop, we can’t wait to welcome you.

Your International Visitors Pack includes a special international swing tag, an exclusive Beach Hop gift, a festival programme and an invitation to our Friday international meet-up.

And here’s something to get excited about Friday night’s “Cruise with a Kiwi”! 

A chance to jump aboard a classic car or hot rod with some of our Kiwi Beach Hop entrants and experience a cruise lap for yourself!

Repco Beach Hop, 17–21 March 2027

Tag your mates coming from overseas and share this with them,
let’s make sure they’re part of it!

Get your International Visitors Pass here: https://beachhop.flicket.co.nz/events/d12454c9-9216-429b-b5b5-a8a7596fa91b/reservation?slug=7ab991a5&code=international%2520ticket

EXCITING NEWS FOR OUR RETRO CARAVANNERS!
The Retro Caravan Park has a bigger new home for Repco Beach Hop 2027 — Aicken Road Reserve.
Just a one-minute walk to New World and three minutes to Port Road, with access from Tuesday so you can settle in early.
We’ll have more powered sites, more non-powered sites and a very limited number of spaces for self-contained RVs. Plus an on-site bar, live music and the amazing Friday night light show!

Already purchased your Retro Caravan ticket?  Rest assured, there's nothing more you need to do - your booking carries over to our new location!

Tickets available https://beachhop.flicket.co.nz/

All enquiries, please email info@beachhop.co.nz

HOW FAR WOULD YOU TRAVEL FOR BEACH HOP?

The road trip starts long before you reach Whangamatā …and some of you have a BIG journey planned!

Our furthest hometown entered so far is DRUMMOND, SOUTHLAND!

That’s around 1,600 kilometres of driving EACH WAY, plus a Cook Strait ferry crossing. An estimated 3,200 kilometres return (minus the main street Beach Hop laps)!

Now THAT’S commitment! From the far North to Southland… you guys are getting your cars ready and the countdown is ON. Open roads, mates, great music and a massive five days of Repco Beach Hop waiting at the other end!

We can’t wait to have you back, meet those of you coming for the first time and of course see your cars cruising into town and get Whangamatā rocking again!

TELL US WHERE YOU’RE COMING FROM AND WHAT YOU’RE DRIVING!

Repco Beach Hop 2027, March Wednesday 17th - Sunday 21st

BRING ON THE ROAD TRIP!

DAY ONE OF ENTRIES & WHAT A RESPONSE!

Over 100 vehicles have already booked to come from the South Island! And there are entrants from the far North right down to the bottom of the South Island! 

The countdown to REPCO BEACH HOP 2027 is well and truly ON!

Here an insight into what’s leading the field on day one:

•⁠ ⁠Most popular car: Bel Air
•⁠ ⁠Most popular brand: Ford (only just!)
•⁠ ⁠Most popular year: 1968
•⁠ ⁠Most popular colour: Blue
•⁠ ⁠Oldest car: 1920 Ford (it will be 107 years old when it arrives at Beach Hop!)

From all of us who organise Beach Hop, thank you from the bottom of our hearts to our extended Beach Hop family of car entrants. We know the time, money and love you put into your cars, and the effort it takes to get here. We never take that for granted.

You are the heart of Beach Hop. Every car has a story, and every one of you helps make this festival special. Your support means the world to us, and we’re pouring that same passion into putting on a massive five days for you!

17–21 March 2027. BRING IT ON!

#beachhop

ULTIMATE PASSES ARE SOLD OUT!

What a start to Repco Beach Hop 2027 ticket sales!

Our Ultimate Passes have officially sold out, but as of right now, Standard Vehicle Passes are still available.

If you know someone who hasn’t got their Vehicle Pass yet, now’s the time to tag them, send them this post or give them a rev up. Once they’re sold out, they’re gone!

So far, it’s not just Kiwis coming, we have people visiting from Australia, South Africa, Singapore and USA to join us in Whangamatā!

We’ve got loads in store for Repco Beach Hop 2027, and it’s shaping up to be one for the books.

Get your Standard Vehicle Pass while you still can!

TICKET ENTRIES are LIVE for 2027 Repco Beach Hop!

We are ready to roll! Find the link in our bio, on our website or in the comments to go directly to purchase via our new ticketing partners, Flicket.

Look forward to seeing you in 2027!

This is a friendly reminder that we are 24 hours away from Repco Beach Hop 2027 ENTRIES OPENING

Register through the link in the comments to our NEW ticketing system powered by Flicket, to get an emailed updates for:

- Standard Vehicle Passes
- Ultimate Passes
- Motorbike Passes, &
- Retro Caravan Sites

All going LIVE on OCTOBER 1st

From 7AM on 1 October, you’ll go online and purchase your Beach Hop vehicle entry first. 
The new upgraded process is nice and simple. Once you’ve purchased your entry, you’ll receive an email with a link to log back in and complete your vehicle and entrant details.

*Our vehicle criteria are not changing. Beach Hop vehicle entries are for vehicles up to 1972, along with our existing eligible vehicle categories. Please do not purchase a vehicle entry if your vehicle does not meet the Beach Hop entry criteria.

Entries open in 24 hours, on OCTOBER 1st at 7AM NZT!

3 days out from Repco Beach Hop 2027 entries opening!

Register through the link in the comments to our NEW ticketing system powered by Flicket, to get an emailed updates for:

- Vehicle Passes
- Ultimate Passes
- Motorbike Passes, &
- Retro Caravan Sites

All going LIVE on OCTOBER 1st

From 7AM on 1 October, you’ll go online and purchase your Beach Hop vehicle entry first. 
The new upgraded process is nice and simple. Once you’ve purchased your entry, you’ll receive an email with a link to log back in and complete your vehicle and entrant details.

*Our vehicle criteria are not changing. Beach Hop vehicle entries are for vehicles up to 1972, along with our existing eligible vehicle categories. Please do not purchase a vehicle entry if your vehicle does not meet the Beach Hop entry criteria.

Entries open 7AM OCTOBER 1st - GET READY because we are!

ARE YOU REGISTERED FOR BEACH HOP 2027?

There’s 6 days to go before entries open!

Register through the link in our IG bio to our NEW ticketing system powered by Flicket, to get an emailed updates for Vehicle Passes, Ultimate Passes, Motorbike Passes, Retro Caravan Sites …….all going LIVE on OCTOBER 1st. 

The new upgraded process is nice and simple. From 7AM on 1 October, you’ll go online and purchase your Beach Hop vehicle entry first.
Once you’ve purchased your entry, you’ll receive an email with a link to log back in and complete your vehicle and entrant details.

Our vehicle criteria are not changing. Beach Hop vehicle entries are for vehicles up to 1972, along with our existing eligible vehicle categories. Please do not purchase a vehicle entry if your vehicle does not meet the Beach Hop entry criteria.

Entries open 7AM OCTOBER 1st - GET READY because we are!

BEACH HOP ENTRIES OPEN 7AM, 1 OCTOBER – NEW TICKETING SYSTEM!

This year Beach Hop is moving to a new ticketing system powered by Flicket.

Our old entry system has served us well for many years, but it’s time for an upgrade!

The new process will be nice and simple.

From 7AM on 1 October, you’ll go online and purchase your Beach Hop vehicle entry first.

Once you’ve purchased your entry, you’ll receive an email with a link to log back in and complete your vehicle and entrant details.

Our vehicle criteria are not changing. Beach Hop vehicle entries are for vehicles up to 1972, along with our existing eligible vehicle categories.

Please do not purchase a vehicle entry if your vehicle does not meet the Beach Hop entry criteria.

We’ll release clear, simple instructions before entries open so everyone knows exactly what to do.

7AM, 1 OCTOBER – GET READY!

And we’ve got another exciting announcement coming soon – our NEW Beach Hop Membership, available to vehicle entrants and the public!

More details coming soon!

THE 2027 BEACH HOP GIVEAWAY CAR IS HERE!

Meet our 1964 Chevrolet Impala four-door pillarless, a fresh California import and the start of one very cool Beach Hop build!

A massive thanks to long-time Beach Hop friends Graham & Debbie Dodd, who brought this beauty in from California and gave us the opportunity to make it our next giveaway car.

From there, BikeTranz picked it up and delivered it to Wellington, where Josh Trybula at All Fleet Services has worked his magic getting it through compliance. It’s passed — and now the transformation begins!

Next stop: PAINT! We’ve got some big plans for this Impala, and we’ll be taking you along for the ride as the build comes together.

Beach Hop 2027 vehicle entries open 1 OCTOBER, and this year we’re launching a brand-new entry system.

More information coming very soon, keep an eye on our socials!

Only 63 days to go! 
The countdown is on... Beach Hop 2027 vehicle registrations open on 1 October! 
So, what’s happening in your shed? What are you building? What are you bringing to Beach Hop 2027? We want to hear about it! 
And that’s not all... 
We’re getting very close to revealing the 2027 Beach Hop giveaway vehicle, and trust us, you’re going to want to see this one. More exciting news coming soon!
Get those projects finished, spread the word, and we’ll see you all on 1 October when registrations go live!

latestPosts.caption:
Four years of Tangi.

What started as a small idea has grown into a festival that brings artists, communities, friends, and new faces together through walls, workshops, music, and shared experiences.

Every year has brought something different. New places, new artists, new collaborations, new challenges, and a lot of good memories along the way.

This year, we spent a week in Glagalinggah, Kintamani, painting walls, meeting people, making things, dancing, laughing, and simply enjoying being together.

Looking back, it’s not only the walls that make us proud. It’s everything that happens around them.

Four years in, Tangi is still growing. And we’re very happy to see where it takes us next. 🌞

Thank you to all artists, partners, supporters, volunteers, team and everyone who has been part of the journey.

Tangi Street Art Festival 2026
📍 Glagalinggah, Kintamani
10–17 May 2026

Journey documentary produced by our talented friends @fajarmahendra_ and @es4satria ❤️

At Tangi, creating murals is only one part of the experience🌱

We believe that understanding the local culture and community is just as important as painting in a public space. That’s why we dedicated a day for our participating artists to slow down, learn, and connect with Bali beyond the walls.

The journey began at Gunung Kawi in Tampaksiring, an 11th century temple complex known for its monumental rock carved shrines and rich historical significance. Guided by our curator and cultural advisor @susantadwitanaya from @guratinstitute, the artists were introduced to stories, history, and cultural perspectives that offer a deeper understanding of the island 💫

We then visited the exhibition at @rad_ruangartaderau , where we were warmly welcomed by Bu Puti, Agung, and the team. The visit became an opportunity to exchange ideas, share experiences of making art in Bali, and have open conversations about artistic practice, culture, and everything in between.

For us, meaningful cultural exchange happens not only through murals, but also through listening, learning, and spending time together❤️

Video produced by @es4satria and @fajarmahendra_ 💥

#tangistreetartfestival #streetartbali #tangisaf2026

The final days of painting always bring a different kind of energy.

As deadlines get closer, the walls become busier, ideas become bolder, and something unexpected always happens. At Tangi, artists don’t simply finish their murals. They keep responding to the place around them.

Sometimes that means adding more details than originally planned. Sometimes it means starting spontaneous walls that weren’t part of the schedule at all. When inspiration comes, it’s hard to stop.

This is what we love most about the festival. Every wall grows through curiosity, conversations, and the atmosphere shared between artists, the village, and the people who pass by every day.

Not every mural was planned. Some simply happened because Bali inspired them ❤️💫💥

Video produced by @fajarmahendra_ and @es4satria 📹

#tangistreetartfestival #tangi2026 #streetartbali

Day 3 at Tangi Street Art Festival 2026 ⛰️🎨

This year’s artists are working FAST 😭🔥
By day 3, almost everyone is already close to finishing their walls, and the village keeps transforming every single day.

At this point, the people of Desa Kintamani are getting used to seeing us around 😆
Some locals even started offering more walls for the artists to paint, which honestly means a lot to us.

Slowly, the festival becomes part of the village atmosphere ❤️

Day 2 at Tangi Street Art Festival 2026 🌞⛰️

While the artists continued working across the village walls, we also spent the day at SDN 2 Kintamani together with @ikomangadiartha and @eviberryy for a series of workshops with the students.

Over the past few days, the kids have been watching the murals slowly appear around their village. From empty walls to sketches, colors, and details growing day by day. Yesterday, we finally got to visit their school, share stories, make art together, and spend time with them directly.

A lot of smiles, curiosity, and excitement filled the day ❤️

Star Resonance is a first Lisbon solo exhibition by German artist, @witoldriedel envisioned together with @ours_lisbon for @lisbondesignweek 2025. 
 
At its heart, Star Resonance is a meditation on connection. Riedel asks us to look beyond the surface of things, beyond forms, interventions, and the boundaries we draw between man and nature and to recognise the deeper unity that binds us all. Every material in this space, every object and organism, even the artist themselves, is part of a continuous flow of energy and matter. The idea of “resonance” with the stars becomes the cosmic matter running through the exhibition: an invitation to see ourselves not as separate, but as fundamentally intertwined with everything around us.
 
The show brings together objects, drawings, and living organisms, some created as vessels, some as pure expressions of art. 
 
The “grown drawing” (2025), is made with inks from diesel pollution collected from trucks in Delhi, combined with ink made of burned wood from Japan. The paper, made from cotton, is itself a product of sunlight, water, and air, transformed through photosynthesis. 
 
Several of the wood objects presented in the show are in various states of refinement or decay. Even now, the tree fragment continues to be the home to mosses, insects, and fungi, a living testament to the ongoing dance of life and decay.
 
The ceramic works, hand-crafted and fired in an electric kiln with energy from the sun. The clay comes from places significant to the artist, Silesia (Poland), Germany, and from a friend’s farm in Setubal. The clay is shaped, combined, and transformed through ancient and modern techniques. In some instances, the clays are combined and then carved in a process called “kurinuki”, Riedel learned the process from Japanese Raku Master Kyoshitsu Sasaki.  The artist embraces the transformation through this process, each firing is a collaboration with forces which are out of our control. 
 
In every aspect, “Star Resonance” invites viewers to contemplate the interconnectedness of all things. The materials are not inert, they are participants in a vast, ongoing exchange of energy and matter.

Stones & Circuits: Art, AI, and the More-Than-Human Commons 📖🪨🔌

Guest edited by V Barratt and Julianne Pierce of VNS Matrix (@vns_matrix ), Un Magazine (@un_projects ) brings together artists, writers, and thinkers considering how we live with, make use of, and imagine technology—particularly at a moment when AI is reshaping the ways we work, communicate, and create.

Moving between the speculative and the everyday, the issue considers dreaming, computation, AI, ecology, care, domesticity and the material worlds that underpin our digital lives. With contributions spanning essays, interviews, scores and artist pages, Stones & Circuits offers a broad and often unexpected collection of perspectives on technology, art and the more-than-human.

Contributors include Suzanne Kite, Francesca da Rimini, Xanthe Dobbie, Bianca Tainsh, OMSK Social Club, Amit German, Jemimah Widdicombe, Mara Schwerdtfeger, and more.

Garage Papers is now in the shop 🏛️📐👷🏻‍♀️

Recently we welcomed the Garage Press crew to the IMA as part of our ongoing series of architecture discussions, Off Grid, led by Andrew Wilson, (Senior Lecturer in Architecture, UQ) and Andrew Leach, (Professor of Architectural History, QUT).

The latest edition of the Melbourne-based independent quarterly features writing by Sally Farrah (@s_farrah_), Aaron Peters (Vokes & Peters) (@aaron_vokesandpeters) and Esteban Montecinos (@montecinosesteban), covering architect Enrico Taglietti, planometric projection, and childhood memories of doors and cereal boxes.

Edited by Kate Finning (@kfarchitect), Andrew Murray (@angrew87) and Jean-Marc Tang (@mrjeanmarctang) and designed by Chloe Papas (@__chloepapas).

Garage Papers 3 and 4 now available in store and online 🔗

We have just received copies of Jon Rafman’s MSM TV GUIDE VOL. 2 📺👁️🎬🧠🪫

Published by Farmers Publishing @farmersxdaughter alongside Sprüth Magers @spruethmagers , MSM TV GUIDE VOL. 2 is a cavernous 250-page hardcover proof-of-concept art book documenting the surreal cast of Rafman’s evolving ‘Main Stream Media Network’. Designed by Liam Denhamer and The Opioid Crisis Lookbook (Dustin Cauchi & Dasha Zaharova), the publication expands on Rafman’s strange and delirious world.

Currently on view as part of Jon Rafman: Memento Hikikomori, ‘Main Stream Media Network’ (2025-26) is an evolving, AI-visualised TV channel brimming with slop for the brainrot generation. An ambitious act of world-building, it features distinctive pop stars, 3D-animated cartoons with inscrutable narratives, and disturbing documentary short stories—as if we’ve tuned into an MTV broadcast from a parallel dimension.

Featuring contributions from Honor Levy, Jack Self, Norman M. Klein, Halycon Veil, Heavy Traffic Magazine, SEX IS DEATH, and many more.

Available in store and online, alongside Jon Rafman’s Nine Eyes. 🔗

Jon Rafman: Memento Hikikomori is on show until 27 September.

The 700+ page eponymous artist book accompanies technologist and artist Mindy Seu’s acclaimed performance-lecture, revealing the pervasive and perverted origins of digital tools. Gathering anecdotes, artworks, and historical artefacts, it is part history, part experiment in collective storytelling.

Introducing Blank Forms 📦

Blank Forms is a nonprofit organisation supporting emerging and historically significant artists who produce work across disciplines, often rooted in traditions of experimental and creative music.

They aim to establish new frameworks to preserve, nurture, and present these artist’s work, and to build platforms for practices underrepresented in art’s commercial, institutional, and historical fields.

Blank Forms collaborates with artists on commissions, exhibitions, publications as well as archival and estate projects within contemporary cultural ecosystems and in perpetuity.

In presenting and documenting this work, they seek to foster an artistic community founded upon engaged and equitable conversations across continents, media, and generations.

That’s a wrap on BLEACH Festival 2026 💜

11 days filled with incredible live music, dance, theatre, installations and art, featuring an exciting mix of local, national and international artists across the HOTA precinct.

There was so much to see, discover and be part of.

A huge thank you to everyone who joined us, contributed and helped bring this year’s festival to life. Here’s a look back at BLEACH Festival 2026! Until next time! 🫶

World Percussion Workshop🪘

Kombumerri Traditional Owner, Lann Levinge, and Turkish musician, Atman, gave us an immersive cross-cultural music workshop that blended didgeridoo practice with world percussion traditions.

Arkestra Choir 🎼

A deep listening and creative performance by Fletcher Babb (Cold Ghost), Daniele Constance and a community of passionate Gold Coast artists and musicians.

Spot yourself? 📸

There's more photos of YOU at @six60 and @subtribemusic on our Facebook Page @bleachfestivalgc. 🤩

Our biggest audience yet at HOTA!

A 3-tonne block of melting ice, suspended from a crane, over Evandale Lake at HOTA.

What a way to make a splash! 🪼✨

From the mesmerising illuminated jellyfish by Dead Puppet Society to the jaw-dropping stunts from Jetpack Entertainment & Events, the finale was one for the books. 

A massive THANK YOU to everyone who came along, lit up the festival and made it so unforgettable.

A huge thank you to our incredible sponsor family for championing the arts and helping bring BLEACH Festival to life.

We're deeply grateful to @goldcoastairport, @redemont.legal, @griffithuniversity  and Playking Foundation for their support of creativity, culture and community on the Gold Coast.

Your commitment to the arts helps create opportunities for artists, inspires audiences, and ensures stories, ideas and experiences can be shared and celebrated through BLEACH Festival.

And just like that, the tide rolls out on BLEACH Festival 2026! 

100 glowing jellyfish, live music, mesmerising illuminated puppets from the award-winning Dead Puppet Society, and a thrilling stunt performance from Jetpack Entertainment & Events. 

A magical celebration to wrap up an incredible festival. 💙🪼

Boom Festival 2027 tickets sold out in 2 hours. 40,000 tickets. 0 lineup announcements. 169 countries represented so far. A global community of love.✨

We’re happy, moved, and overflowing with gratitude for all your support.

To the whole worldwide Boomer community: muito obrigado, thank you!

To the entire Boom crew, artists, facilitators, speakers, partners and friends: this moment of recognition from the Boomers belongs to you too. Thank you.

We know how frustrating it is for everyone who didn’t manage to get a ticket, and we’re truly grateful for your interest in what we do. Boom has a limited capacity so we can keep the balance between people and nature. In 2027 we are selling 5% fewer tickets than in the previous edition.

We feel your love, and the responsibility that comes with this sold out. The plans for our 30th anniversary edition are amazing, the vibe is sky-high, and we’re giving it everything to bring you an epic edition.

Boom is built on independence: we are proudly free from corporate sponsorship. Boom thrives entirely thanks to you, our vibrant, diverse family of Boomers. Every ticket purchased is a direct contribution to keeping the spirit of the festival alive, to the regeneration of Boomland and the charity initiative Boom Karuna Project.

May this celebration of Boom culture cherish what makes us human: togetherness, celebration, respect for the Earth, and love.

From our hearts to yours, thank you ❤️

#BoomFestival2027 #BoomFestival30Years #OnlyLoveBringsLove

Boom turns 30 next July and we are gathering the community for an epic celebration under the moon and stars ✨

As we prepare to open online ticket sales tomorrow, 13 October, we would like to share a short note on how things will roll out.

Ticket sales will go ahead exactly as planned, at the scheduled time: 13 October, 09:00 Continental Portuguese time on the online ticket platform. 

The only change concerns the services. Here's what's shifting.

Given the growing number of requests we've received for accommodation and other services, we've decided to separate the service sales from the ticket release. 

This way, ticket sales can unfold calmly and smoothly, without the system having to carry everything at once. It also allows us to give each service request the care and attention it deserves.

There's another reason, too. We've learned that life can change in the months leading up to Boom. Plans shift, and people who have booked the Boom Bus and Accommodation (Tipi Camp, Lizard Camp and Cardboard Village) may find they no longer need the service they have purchased.

Giving services their own moment, a little later down the line, means you can make these decisions with a clearer picture of your festival travel and on-site accommodation needs.

We’d also like to assure you that kids aged 14 and under (born on or after 19 July 2012) can be registered at a later date. 

Services and Kids Registration will open on the full moon of March 2027. Stay tuned. 

We believe splitting the process into two stages will provide a better experience when purchasing both tickets and services. Thank you for your feedback and flexibility as we continue to make launch day the best it can be for our community.

Please remember that Boom 2027 tickets are limited to keep a balance between human presence and nature.

🎉🌿 50 YEARS IN THE MAKING… AND TOMORROW WE CELEBRATE! 🌿🎉

Here's a few quick shots from the start of today's set-up as we get ready for something truly special!

🥳 The Channon Craft Market is turning 50!

Things are starting to take shape, and the excitement is building as we prepare to celebrate five incredible decades of makers, bakers, growers, music, friendship and community.

❤️ 50 years of memories. 50 years of community. One very special celebration!

Tomorrow isn't just another market day. It's a chance to celebrate the people, stories and traditions that have made our little country market so special for half a century.

🎊 WE WANT YOU TO BE PART OF IT!

Bring your family, bring your friends, bring your memories and come help us make history!

Whether you've been coming for decades or you're visiting for the very first time, this celebration belongs to our whole community.

Let's make our 50th Anniversary a day to remember! 🎂🎶💜

📅 TOMORROW – Sunday 11 October 2026
⏰ 9am – 3pm
📍 The Channon

50 years only happens once. Don't miss it! 🎉

#TheChannonCraftMarket #50YearsOfTheChannon #TheChannon #NorthernRivers #VisitLismore #MakeItBakeItGrowIt

Remember we are a pet and alcohol free event

🎶 The program is here! 🎶

We’re getting very close to a pretty special Sunday — and now you can start planning your day at The Channon Craft Market’s 50th Celebrations.

From our Welcome to Country and Smoking Ceremony with Uncle Gilbert through to live music, stories, official speeches and a few familiar faces, we’ve got plenty happening throughout the day.

On the program you’ll find Lismore Flood Water Revival, Kevin Newton, Michelle Bell, Tobi and Friends, Monkey and the Fish and Luke Vassella.

And there’s more happening around the Market too: including the Chai Tent, decorations by Benny Zable, the Bubble Girls and RiverFest BioBlitz activities.

📅 Sunday 11 October 
📍 The Channon Craft Market, The Channon

Have a look through the program, pick out what you don’t want to miss, and come spend part (or all)of this very special market day with us.

And when the Market day wraps up, the celebrations don’t have to! You can keep the evening going at the Chai Tent and Drumming Circle, or if that’s more your style, head on down to The Channon Tavern and settle in for the rest of the evening.

50 years of people, art, music, craft and community. We reckon that’s worth celebrating. ❤️

Proudly supported by Lismore City Council.

Museum seeks expressions of interest from museum curators. 

Are you thinking about a change of pace, geography, or institutional culture? Comfortable making exhibitions with living artists, assessing acquisitions, or rethinking how a collection can be presented? Well, swipe right. 

There's no position description, no salary range, no start date. But there's a little more detail and our contact via link in bio.

A brief word on motives. Like the art in the museum, the library is a gradualist collection: an informal, frequently random, often serendipitous, learning-by-doing collection—about which David has said he decided why he was collecting after the fact. He also said, never ask someone about their motives because they’ll be the last to know.

Which is to say: here are some things that David and Mary are excited about putting out on display in Phrontisterion.

Images:
An inscribed copy of Charles Darwin's The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life, John Murray, London, 1872. The sixth edition, and the last to be published in Darwin's lifetime.

Ben Jonson's Workes: the first First Folio, the earliest published folio of an author’s own collected dramatic works in English, and a direct model for the First Folio of Shakespeare’s plays seven years later. Printed and published by Will Stansby, London, 1616.

Captain James Cook's Voyages and Life: published 1773–1788 in 11 volumes, with engravings, charts and maps, documenting his navigation of the Pacific, Atlantic and Southern oceans.

The largest, most expensive book published in the 17th century, by Willem Jansz. Blaeu and Joan Blaeu: Le Grand Atlas, ou Cosmographie Blaviane, en laquelle est exactement descritte la Terre, la Mer, et le Ciel (The Grand Atlas, or Blaeu’s Cosmography), published by Joan Blaeu, Amsterdam, 1663.

Isaac Asimov's PhD: ‘The Kinetics of the Reaction Inactivation of Tyrosinase during its Catalysis of the Aerobic Oxidation of Catechol’, Columbia University, New York, 1948, inscribed to a fellow doctoral candidate.

'Ruins, for me, are the beginning. With the debris, you can construct new ideas. They are symbols of a beginning.'
—Anselm Kiefer

Images:
View inside Elektra, 2025, by Anselm Kiefer, with his painting Die Lebenden und die Toten (The Living and the Dead), 2019, beyond
Shipping containers, cast concrete, steel, glass, plant materials, lead, terracotta, plaster, fabric, emulsion, razor wire, photographs, water, emulsion, oil, acrylic, shellac and wood on canvas

MONA Bangkok

'MONA Bangkok will take the creative spirit of Mona into a new context. Like the museum in Hobart, it will present work by leading international artists, while also creating opportunities for meaningful dialogue with Thai artists, audiences and cultural traditions.

The theme of light will be explored both as a physical phenomenon and as a metaphor. Light has long been a source of fascination, reflection and hope across cultures, and it feels especially resonant in Bangkok, with its rich cultural life and deep traditions.'
—Leigh Carmichael

Link in bio.

All right then, keep your five bucks. 

Locals no longer need to pay a deposit to visit Mona. Treat yourself. Or the kids—there’s a new children's library and school holiday menu on the lawns for the diminutive among us.

Never before have we gone to so much trouble to achieve so little.

出展者による招待制の出展形式を採用し、「Library Hotel」をコンセプトに掲げる芝パークホテルの空間を活かしながら、国内外のインディペンデント出版シーンや、参加者同士の交流をより活性化することを目指します。

TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR 2026 will take place over three days, from Friday 1 May to Sunday 3 May 2026, at Shiba Park Hotel.

TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR 2026 is a fair organised by TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR and built around networks in art book publishing. The second edition will take place over three days, from Friday 1 May to Sunday 3 May 2026, at Shiba Park Hotel. A total of 52 exhibitors, including artists, publishers, bookshops, and galleries from Japan and abroad, will gather, each developing their own activities through publications such as art books and zines.

The fair uses an invitation-based format, in which participating exhibitors invite other exhibitors to join. Making use of the setting of Shiba Park Hotel, known as a “Library Hotel,” the fair hopes to encourage exchanges among participants and bring more energy to the independent publishing scene in Japan and abroad.

We very much look forward to welcoming you.

TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR

TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR is a new fair launched in 2025 by TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR (TABF), structured around networks within art book publishing. Through a format distinct from conventional fairs and its compact scale, it aims to activate the independent publishing scene in Japan and internationally, as well as exchanges among participants.

The shift from “TOKYO” to “TOKIO” signals an intentional repositioning: not as an alternative to TABF, but as a parallel platform offering a different perspective. This subtly “bootleg-like” naming reframes TABF’s alternative potential while embracing the heterogeneous, cross-cultural nature of art book publishing.

Dylan Blackstone has been part of the Strawberry Fields story for 13 years, creating immersive installations that blur the lines between art, architecture and experience. 

Inspired by the patterns and forms found throughout the natural world, his work invites you to slow down, look closer and get lost in the details. Shapes repeat, colours shift and familiar forms transform as you move through them, revealing something new from every angle.

“I’ve been building for Strawberry Fields for 13 years, and for all of those years it has been one of the major highlights of my year. Strawberry was the first festival that truly trusted me in my creative process, half-finished drawings, bamboo skewer models, hand gestures paired with funny noises to try to explain what was happening inside my head. I’ve made some of my best friends, met my wife and even moved to a new country because of the experiences I’ve had and the relationships I’ve formed at Strawberry Fields. I’m forever grateful to my Strawberry family.”

We’re excited to see what Dylan dreams up for Strawberry this November 🍃

From conifers and camellias to azaleas and figs, discover up to 100 different bonsai trees, each one a living work of art. Search ‘bonsai house’ at the link in our bio to plan your visit. 

#Brisbane #ThingsToDoInBrisbane #Bonsai

Grab a paddle, gather your friends and get to your local courts for World Pickleball Day! 🎾 
 
There are plenty of ways to play, with purpose-built pickleball courts at more than 25 of our parks and classes running throughout the week as part of Move Well. Combining elements of tennis, badminton, and table tennis, pickleball is easy to pick up and suitable for all ages and skill levels. 
 
Search ‘pickleball’ at the link in our bio to find out more and get involved. #Brisbane #ThingsToDoInBrisbane #WorldPickleballDay #MoveWell

Textiles don’t belong in your recycling bin. 👕♻️ 

Clothing, shoes, towels, sheets and other textiles can’t be recycled in your yellow bin. If they end up there, they can damage machinery used in the recycling process. 

Before throwing textiles away, consider whether they can be: 
✅ Given a second life through resale or reuse 
✅ Donated to an op shop 
✅ Donated to local animal shelters, vets or other organisations (where suitable) 

If your textiles can’t be reused or donated, place them in your red-lid general waste bin. 

To learn more search ‘clothing and textile recycling’ at the link in our bio. #Brisbane

This Wednesday 5/13! 4-7 pm at Migration Brewing N Williams Ave @migrationbrewing 

I miss you and cannot wait to see everyone for a proper celebration of two decades of information and inspiration. 🫶🎉

In case you didn't click through to the story on the blog yesterday...

As you might have sensed, things have slowed down a lot on BikePortland lately. There are a lot of reasons for that, and I might share them in more detail some day. For now, I just want you to know that I need a bit of space from the daily grind. BikePortland has taken a lot out of me for 21 years, and I’ve finally taken time to think deeply about what that means for me, my family, and our community.

I’ve always been honest with you and I just want you to know where I’m coming from. This is me saying I need a reset and the community needs to reset their expectations of BikePortland. For now, at least.

I’m not sure yet exactly how things will be different going forward, just that I’m sure things will be different. I’ve come to realize that I can’t find the clarity and space I need to chart a different path forward until I get off the path I’m on.

- Jonathan ❤️🙏 @jonathan.maus 

Read more by swiping through or on the blog at www.bikeportland.org.

We shouldn’t accept crappy bike lanes that flood every single time it rains! These bike lanes on N Lombard flooded right after they were installed. Mixed w leaves that aren’t swept, these already inadequate bike lanes - and many others citywide - become nearly unusable for months. Bike riders are left w a lose-lose choice of riding through puddles and leaves, or sharing lanes with drivers. 

Do better bike lane builders! Figure out the engineering so bike lanes drain properly. Sorry to rant but we deserve better.

Couple weeks ago I was lucky enough to join @something_cycles and a crew of people to go overnight bikepacking on the Fire and Ice Cave Loop (made by @bikepackingcom ). 50 miles and 4,500 feet of elevation made it challenging but not grueling. 

Had so much fun meeting new people, testing out new gear and enjoying Mother Nature. I made my usual YouTube video (out now, link in bio/story) but also got asked to write about it for @bikeportland 😮 if you would like to read about it I highly encourage checking it out (link in bio/story)!!! The Bob Stacey Crossing is a bike and pedestrian bridge in the inner southeast Hosford-Abernethy neighborhood. The crossing helps community members get safely across the Union Pacific Railroad tracks as well as MAX Light Rail lines. This crossing opened in 2020, but is often closed due to vandalism that makes the elevators inoperable. 
 
Folks are forced to carry bikes and strollers up many stairs or use lengthy detours – or not cross at all! And the outages make the crossing inaccessible to those with physical disabilities. 
 
I’m proud to support this project with my office funds, along with @councilornovick and @councilorangelitamorillo, to get the crossing operable again! 
 
Thank you, @councilornovick, for your leadership on this, and even more, thank you to all the community members for bringing this to our attention through strong advocacy! I love how engaged District 3 is, and I love to say: We heard you, and we’re taking action! 
 
The improvements are expected to be completed by Fall 2026. 
 
 
Image ID: 
Quote by Councilor Koyama Lane: “I’m thrilled to dedicate some of my Council office funds to these repairs so that, very soon, community members won’t need AreTheElevatorsBroken.com! I want ‘Yes, they’re working’ to be the permanent answer for the Bob Stacey Crossing. Elevators are not just a convenience – they are a necessity for the ADA community, parents with strollers, cyclists and more!” Faded photo of Bob Stacey Crossing in background.

Let’s Celebrate Tomorrow.

For 20 years @bikeportland has been advocating for safer legislation, bike lanes, and everything in between for a better Portland Cycling Community.

Join us tomorrow at 3PM as we celebrate Jonathan and @bikeportland amazing accomplishment.

Hi everyone! As part of my hiatus-ing, I’ve been thinking a lot about the past. All the cool stories and people I’ve met doing this weird job for so long. The other day while hanging in the Shed, I looked at my stack of old notebooks and thought, “What if I just opened one and started reading?” Then I thought, “What if I shared that in a video and told some stories about what I found?”. So I did. 

I think this is a fun way to share some history and it helps my brain to recall these stories. 

As you watch this one (which touches on a few weeks of October-November 2009), keep in mind this is just a few weeks of stories. From a panel of Europeans visiting Portland, to farmers in Washington County, local businesses, and handmade bike builders — it really shows the wide editorial scope of BikePortland. That was part of what I loved about the job back in the day.

If folks like this, I could do tons more. This is just a few pages from one notebook... and I’ve got about 35 more on the shelf! It feels good to recall the past right now as I try to figure out my future. 

Thanks for all your support. Stay tuned and I’ll see you on the streets. 😎❤️💪🏻🙏🏻

New story up about the frustrating and persistent closure of the elevators at the Bob Stacey Crossing in Southeast Portland. Neighborhood advocates are pressing the issue with Mayor Wilson and PBOT says they've ordered security cameras to help thwart recurring vandalism and camping that has kept these two elevators closed.

Vandalism and faulty mechanics have plagued these elevators several times — and for many months — since these elevators first opened in 2020.

latestIgtvVideos.caption:
Early last week, we finally got what we had been waiting for. The @bellsbeach50yearstorm Invitational in memory of Shaun Brooks ran in some solid waves after years of waiting for the right conditions. It did not disappoint with the swell rising all day and some of Victoria's best big wave surfers going hard to raise awareness for mental health. Congratulations goes to @timstevenson for claiming top honours on the day and to @angelaaball for being awarded the big charger Johny Utah award. An absolutely incredible day for all which wouldn't have happened without the dedication from the @bellsbeach50yearstorm committee 🙏 and all of the sponsors that supported the day. If you would like to make a contribution to helping others with mental health struggles, please head to our beneficiaries @_oneinfive_ and @headspacegeelong

🎶 Bring your instrument and be part of the 2027 National!

Learn alongside Festival artists, meet fellow musicians and rehearse together in daily Festival Ensemble workshops. Then share the stage, living our 2027 theme: Participation – Making Culture Together. And this is only half of the options!

🪕 Festival Ukes with Ukastle Ukestra: Explore songs, riffs and rhythms each morning with these seasoned Festival favourites, with all experience levels welcome.

🎻 Festival Strings with San Miguel Fraser: Explore Castilian, American and Scottish fiddle traditions in a massed string ensemble for the Farewell Concert.

🪈 Flute Ensemble with Mélisande: Level up your skills and explore Québec’s traditional music with Alex de Grosbois-Garand, then join Mélisande and the band in concert.

🎸 Guitar Ensemble with Guanaco Trío: Discover new techniques and Argentine folkloric rhythms with Benjamín Aedo, then join Guanaco Trío on stage.

🎻 Restrung Ensemble with Mickey & Michelle: Join this unique Festival orchestra experience to rehearse new arrangements and perform alongside Australian and international artists.

🎶 Meet five voices joining our 2027 Festival to share songs of language, labour, place, memory and belonging.

🖤💛❤️ Gina Williams-Ghouse AM returns bringing her full five-piece band for the first time. Hear Noongar language songs and stories, and look out for a special collaboration still to be revealed.

🏭 Jennifer Reid (England) brings Lancashire work songs and Manchester street songs roaring out of the archives, with working-class stories, protest and women’s voices at their heart.

🌿 Lucy Wise returns to the Festival that inspired her as a young musician, launching her seventh album 'Salt'. Her beautifully delivered songs hold space for connection and reflection on the inner lives we carry.

🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 Kris Drever (Scotland) is an acclaimed solo artist and also known as one third of Lau. Kris brings his extraordinary voice, guitar playing and latest album 'Doing This For Love'.

🦘 Luke O’Shea turns Australian people, places and half-forgotten histories into songs about identity, belonging and community. The 17-time Golden Guitar winner calls it “singing up country” and delivers deeply moving performances.

And watching is only the beginning. Across the Festival you'll be able to learn Noongar with Gina, explore songwriting with Lucy, listen to Kris being interviewed, turn your own stories into songs with Luke, hear Jennifer discuss women and traditional music in a forum, and encounter all five through concerts, conversations and collaborations.

Got your tickets yet? Link in bio

The National Folk School is back in 2027!

Spend three days before the Festival learning directly from some of the world’s leading folk artists and tradition bearers. Go deeper than the one-hour workshop or Festival Ensemble: learn by ear, build your technique and repertoire, explore a tradition, and make music and dance with fellow folkies.

Your 2027 Folk School tutors are:
👞 Nic Gareiss (USA) — Percussive Dance
🎸 Jenn Butterworth (Scotland) — Traditional Guitar
🪗 Will Pound (England) — Harmonica & Melodeon
🎻 Sami Braman (USA) — Old-Time Fiddle
🪕 Allison de Groot (Canada) — Clawhammer Banjo
🎸 Quinn Bachand (Canada) — Guitar

And when the Folk School finishes, the music keeps going: all six tutors are also performing at the National Folk Festival in duo and trio combos. What you learn over those three days travels with you into the sessions, dances, ensembles and music-making of the Festival itself.

Returning after a long hiatus, the Folk School continues a National Folk Festival tradition stretching back more than 25 years, presented in partnership with the ANU School of Music.

Come early. Learn deeply. Then join in.

📅 23–25 March 2027
📍 ANU School of Music, Canberra
🎪 National Folk Festival: 25–29 March 2027
🎟️ Tickets on sale Monday 17 August at 9am AEST

We're delighted to welcome these exceptional Australian artists to our program in 2027. Know anyone who might be feeling a little bit lost or blue this Easter? Bring them along to the National Folk Festival! 

🎤 Karen Lee Andrews blends blues, soul, gospel and rock into a powerful live show, pairing an extraordinary voice with deeply personal songwriting inspired by her Polynesian heritage.

🎸 Lloyd Spiegel is one of Australia's most respected blues guitarists, renowned for his virtuosic fingerstyle playing, masterful storytelling and more than three decades of international touring.

🔥 Minnie Marks has built a devoted following with her explosive one-woman blues-rock performances, combining blistering guitar work, powerhouse vocals and her signature Foot Drum.

🥁 Festival favorite Carl Pannuzzo brings his band Checkerboard Lounge to the Festival, who have spent more than three decades at the forefront of Australian blues, delivering authentic Chicago-style blues, soulful grooves and world-class musicianship.

These folks will also feature in two special events: a soul-filled Blues Breakfast, and a long form, loose format, late-night Blues Jam, where blues artists plus surprise folky special guests will create spontaneous mayhem, wonder and joy late into the night. Who knows who'll show up on stage?

@nrmainsurance and Australian Red Cross are running workshops to help you get prepared for emergencies, and this weekend is Get Ready Weekend at your local Rural Fire Brigade.

Organisation must do! You can never be too prepared, especially for an emergency. 

I recently attended an @redcrossau EmergencyRedi workshop, supported by @nrmainsurance , and learnt all about why emergency planning is so important and how easy it is to get prepared. 

Here are a few simple ways I have gotten my family emergency ready - that are really easy (and satisfying) to do: 

1. Prepare an ICE Folder (in case of emergency folder) with important documents 
2. Pack an emergency essentials kit – batteries, torch, first aid kit etc 
3. Create kid’s calm cases – for emotional support (featuring craft, games and comfort toys)
4. Prep your pantry – non-perishable food, water and snacks in an easy to grab basket 

If you want to get yourself and family prepared in case an emergency strikes, I encourage you to attend a free Australian Red Cross Emergency Redi Workshop and create your own emergency Rediplan. Link in bio!

Surfing Australia is deeply saddened by the passing of Graham ‘Sid’ Cassidy, a pioneering figure whose vision, advocacy and passion helped shape the evolution of professional surfing.

A respected journalist, promoter and event director, Sid played a pivotal role in the growth of professional surfing throughout the 1970s and 1980s.

Sid helped establish the structures that underpin modern professional surfing, including the formation of the Association of Professional Surfing Athletes (APSA), before going on to lead the Association of Surfing Professionals (ASP), now the World Surf League, as Executive Director. 

His work helped shape the sport’s competitive pathways and the evolution of the world ranking system.

Beyond surfing, Sid made a significant contribution to Australian sport and public life, serving as Media Director for the Sydney 2000 Olympic and Paralympic Games and later as Director of City Engagement for the City of Sydney.

In 2025, Sid was inducted into the Australian Surfing Hall of Fame in recognition of his extraordinary contribution to the sport. His legacy lives on in the professional surfing landscape he helped build and the generations of athletes who have followed.

Our thoughts are with Sid’s family, friends and all those across the surfing community whose lives and careers were touched by his contribution.

Vale Graham ‘Sid’ Cassidy.

QUEM É QUE TE CONVIDOU? 
ESTÁS SEMPRE CONVIDADO ❤️‍🔥

Quatro dias. Cinco Palcos. Uma escola inteira para descobrir.

Houve uma orquestra a sério. Festa até doer as pernas. Música, breaking, performance, dança, cinema, conversas, futebol, instalações artísticas em salas de aula, convidados surpresa e tudo o que aconteceu nos corredores pelo meio do que estava programado.

Artistas, bairros, associações, crews, equipas, amigos e desconhecidos cruzaram-se aqui. Quem vinha para ver acabou a fazer parte.

Foi assim que celebrámos 10 anos de Iminente.

Uma década a juntar o que tantas vezes aparece separado. Quem está a começar com quem já anda nisto há décadas. O bairro com o palco. Portugal com o resto do mundo. E muita gente que provavelmente nunca se encontraria noutro sítio.

A festa dos 10 anos era nossa. Mas quem fez a festa foram vocês.❤️‍🔥

Obrigado a todos os artistas, comunidades, associações, parceiros, patrocinadores, equipas e a cada pessoa que atravessou estes portões e fez parte disto.

Foram 10 anos para chegar aqui. Agora queremos saber até onde podemos ir.

Durante quatro dias, a antiga Escola Afonso Domingues não foi apenas o lugar onde aconteceu o Iminente. Foi também matéria-prima.

Paredes, fachadas, janelas, estruturas e outros recantos deram origem a intervenções pensadas para este lugar; que partiram do espaço que encontraram, dialogaram com a sua arquitetura e história e passaram a fazer parte dele.

@camixvx, @3d_crew_, @43error + @pedritastudio + @furo_architecturestudio, @halfstudiosigns, @ml7_metro.lisboa, @obey_sktr, @pregos_shp, @ricardopassaporte,  @russo1003pv e @sepher.42 (com rvca_portugal).

Obras que desafiaram o olhar e mostraram que há sempre outras formas de habitar um lugar.

–

For four days, the former Escola Afonso Domingues wasn’t just the place where Iminente happened. It also became raw material.

Walls, façades, windows, structures and other corners of the School gave rise to interventions conceived specifically for this place; works that responded to the spaces they encountered, engaged with their architecture and history, and became part of them.

Contributions that challenged the way we see and showed us that there are always other ways to inhabit a place.

Important Update: For nearly 38 years, Tropical Fruits has been a volunteer-powered labour of love ~ a regional queer home built through a stubborn commitment to community, creativity and collective care.

Over the past few years we’ve weathered a lot.
Bushfires. COVID. And the devastating 2022 floods, which badly damaged our clubhouse and destroyed essential equipment and infrastructure.

Many of you will remember the $1.4 million rebuild grant we received after the floods. It helped get the bones of the building back in place ~ but the reality of rebuilding has been more complex than anyone anticipated. Construction inflation, revised engineering, and compliance issues have pushed costs far beyond the original scope.

Today the structure stands, but the fit-out remains incomplete. Walls, plastering, finishing details ~ the work that turns a shell back into a welcoming home.

Right now Tropical Fruits has no permanent base, our belongings remain in storage, and significant funding is still needed to complete the clubhouse rebuild and stabilise the organisation.

But the good news is this:

Our community is still here.
The care, creativity, volunteer spirit and queer brilliance that make Tropical Fruits what it is are absolutely flourishing.

So today we’re asking our community to help carry this next chapter.

Our Australian Cultural Fund fundraiser is now live. Donations are tax-deductible, and every contribution helps us complete the rebuild and protect the future of Tropical Fruits.

If Fruits has ever given you connection, joy, belonging, recovery, friendship, release ~ or simply the relief of being surrounded by people who get you ~ this is a moment to stand together.

Donate if you can.
Share widely if you can’t.  Consider becoming a financial member of our club thru our website - this gives you discounts on all Fruits events, inc 15% off NYE festival tix.

TATTOO EXPO BUENOS AIRES 2027
19, 20 y 21 de marzo | La Rural
¡Reservá tu stand y formá parte del evento más importante del tatuaje en Argentina y uno de los más grandes de Latinoamérica!
En 2027, Tattoo Expo Buenos Aires celebrará su edición número 23 con una novedad histórica: por primera vez la ciudad será sede del Campeonato Panamericano de Tatuaje, reuniendo a los mejores artistas de todo el continente en una competencia internacional que atraerá a miles de visitantes, profesionales y medios especializados.
Durante tres jornadas, La Rural se transformará en el punto de encuentro de la industria del tatuaje, el arte y la cultura urbana, con una convocatoria masiva y un público fiel que acompaña el evento desde hace más de dos décadas.
¿Por qué exponer en Tattoo Expo Buenos Aires?
Porque tu marca estará presente frente a miles de potenciales clientes en un entorno donde se generan ventas, contactos comerciales y posicionamiento de marca.
Atracciones destacadas de la edición 2027:
• Campeonato Panamericano de Tatuaje.
• Más de 700 artistas nacionales e internacionales.
• Concursos de tatuaje durante los tres días.
• Shows en vivo con bandas reconocidas.
• Ring de boxeo y exhibiciones deportivas.
• Pista y exhibiciones de skate.
• Galerías de arte y artistas en vivo.
• Cosplay y cultura alternativa.
• Gastronomía y espacios recreativos.
• Expositores de insumos, equipamiento, indumentaria y accesorios.
• Cobertura de medios, streamings y redes sociales.
• Miles de visitantes de todo el país y del exterior.
Una oportunidad única para tu empresa
✔ Presentar nuevos productos.
✔ Realizar ventas directas.
✔ Generar distribuidores y clientes mayoristas.
✔ Posicionar tu marca ante el público adecuado.
✔ Vincularte con referentes de toda América.
✔ Formar parte de un evento consolidado con 23 años de trayectoria.
Tattoo Expo Buenos Aires no es solamente una convención. Es una experiencia cultural, artística y comercial que año tras año reúne a la comunidad del tatuaje y a miles de personas que buscan descubrir las últimas tendencias, productos y marcas del mercado.
Los espacios son limita

Rainbow Disco Club 2026の翌週にWOMBで開催された「RDC 2026 After Party」。同パーティーで披露されたBen UFOによるAll Night Long Setのライヴレコーディングを公開します。

RDCは長年彼と多くの時間を共にしてきましたが、そのマインドセット、人間性、そして卓越した技術には常に魅了され続けています。今回の録音もまた、Ben UFOというDJの奥深さを存分に感じられる素晴らしい仕上がりとなっています。 ぜひ、お楽しみください。

The ‘RDC 2026 After Party’ took place at WOMB the weekend following the main festival. We are pleased to release the live recording of Ben UFO’s ‘All Night Long Set’, performed at the event.

RDC has spent many years working closely with him, and we remain constantly captivated by his mindset, character and exceptional skills. This recording is another superb piece of work that fully showcases Ben UFO’s depth as a DJ. Enjoy!

ロンドンのアンダーグラウンド・シーンを強烈な求心力で牽引する要塞クラブ「FOLD」と、日本を代表するダンスミュージックフェスティバル「Rainbow Disco Club」によるコラボレーション・イベントがWOMBで実現。ロンドンのインダストリアルな熱気と、RDCが培ってきた祝祭の要素が3つのフロアで激突・融合する。それぞれのフロアが全く異なるストーリーを描きながらも、一つのうねりとなって朝まで駆け抜ける、妥協なきキュレーションを体感してほしい。

2FではFOLDの熱気と日本のテクノ・シーンが共鳴する。ロンドンFOLDの狂騒をそのままパッケージしたかのような、ディープでエネルギッシュな空間となるだろう。FOLDのキーマンであるVoicedrone b2b James Newmarchがロンドンから直輸入のバウンシーかつインダストリアルなグルーヴを投下する。迎え撃つ日本勢は、本国のFOLDにも出演経験のあるストイックな探求でフロアを支配するHarukaと、国内外で躍進を続けトランシーかつ催眠的なセットで魅了するDJ Maria.だ。また、本公演でDJ Maria.は「Non Techno Set」と題したスペシャルなセットを披露する。

4Fでは深淵なるサイケデリックとオルタナティブの探求、音楽の深みへの没入体験がクラバーたちを待ち受ける。予測不能な異空間、ドロドロとした独自のサウンドスケープでフロアを底なしの沼へと引きずり込む悪魔の沼と、日本のオルタナティブ・ディスコ〜レフトフィールド・シーンの至宝Kenji Takimiが共演を果たす。妖しくも美しいコズミック・グルーヴと、サイケデリックな電子音が混ざり合う、中毒性の高い音楽体験がここにはある。

1Fはローカルの活気が溢れる豊潤なハウスやディスコで空間を暖かく彩るダンスフロアになるだろう。DJツアーと並行して果敢なプロデュースで世界に羽ばたいているMayurashkaと、安定感のある選曲でフロアに規律をもたらすCYKのNariがラインナップ。この2人を、RDCのレジデント Kikiorix が迎え撃つ。

国境を越え、ロンドンと日本のダンスミュージック・コミュニティが深く交じり合う特別なショーケース。この歴史的な交差点をお見逃しなく。

BEST004 - The Melting Hours - The Melting Hours EP

Out today on Beyond Space And Time: The Melting Hours, the debut EP by The Melting Hours, a live project by Wata Igarashi and Kuniyuki.

Available now on vinyl, digital, Bandcamp and all streaming platforms.

Written, Performed, Recorded and Mixed by Wata Igarashi & Kuniyuki Takahashi
Wata Igarashi - Guitars, Synthesizers and Electronics
Kuniyuki Takahashi - Synthesizers, Drum Machines, Percussions and Flute

Mastered by MaSpaventi @maspaventimastering 
Artwork by Kikiorix @kikigraphix 

It brings to mind the Rainbow Disco Club event back in 2026, where they wove their sounds amidst fresh greenery and surrounded by listeners under a clear blue sky. It felt as though the pulsating energy was spreading across the dance floor, guided by a session from The Melting Hours that seemed almost like a living creature. The organic breath one senses in this work not only evokes precisely that scene but also allows us to feel the unique, ephemeral nature inherent in this project—and, consequently, the boundless possibilities that stem from it.

来年で設立30周年を迎える、世界最高峰のレコードショップ／レーベル「Rush Hour」。その創設者であり、類稀なる審美眼と確かな技術で世界中のダンスフロアを魅了し続けるDJ、Antalを迎えた「Listening Session」を10月10日 (土) に1 Hotel Tokyoで開催します。

本セッションでは、「自身の人生に影響を与えた楽曲」や「Rush Hourの歩みを象徴する名曲」などをテーマに、Antal自身が厳選したレコードを聴きながら、彼の音楽的ルーツや哲学をインタビューとともに紐解いていきます。

サウンドシステムは英国のダンスミュージックシーンにルーツを持ち、国産木材を用いた卓越した造形で知られるスピーカーブランド「Higo Beat」。そして、最高峰の音響性能を誇るハイエンド・ロータリーミキサー「Cometa M2」。この特別な環境で味わう、美しく響く極上の音楽体験を1 Hotel Tokyo でご堪能ください。50枚限定の前売券発売開始 🎫

To celebrate the upcoming 30th anniversary next year of Rush Hour, one of the world's most acclaimed record shops and labels, we are proud to host a special Listening Session featuring its founder, Antal, a DJ renowned worldwide for his exceptional curation and technical prowess.

During this session, Antal will play a selection of personal vinyl records that have  influenced his life and career, as well as defining releases from Rush Hour’s history. Through these vinyl records and an intimate interview, we will delve into his musical roots and underlying musical philosophy.

The sound system features Higo Beat - a custom speaker brand rooted in British dance music culture and hand-crafted with domestic Japanese timber - paired with the Cometa M2 - a top-tier rotary DJ mixer celebrated for its exceptional audio fidelity and sleek design. Join us for an extraordinary listening experience set within a truly refined soundscape at 1 Hotel Tokyo.

latestPosts.caption:
Sauna Fest 2027 📍 Lake Tikitapu - May 14-16

Sauna Fest exists to grow and celebrate sauna culture in Aotearoa.

Each year in Rotorua, we create a weekend that feels truly unique, a festival fuelled by wood-fired saunas. 

This coming year, we’re leaning even further into the creative expression of the festival. From live performances to the NZ Aufguss Championship, we want to create an experience that leaves you feeling so high and amazed you won’t want to come down 🤩

Saunas are powerful and have stood the test of time across many cultures. We believe we’re only at the beginning of integrating sauna into our culture here in Aotearoa. So come join us on the shores of Lake Tikitapu as we make sauna culture history. 🙌🏼🔥❄️

The space is open to everyone.

Motorbeach Peru Día 1 … está pasando !!!

Arrancamos de Cuzco después de pasar un par de días aclimatando para evitar el mal de altura que aún así a unos cuantos nos afectó. 

Salimos rumbo hacia el Valle Rojo y la Montaña de Siete colores , una de las maravillas naturales de Peru para recorrer en moto con paisajes que parecen de otro planeta. 

Párte del grupo, los más motivados y físicamente más fuertes ascendieron caminando hasta los 5045 metros de altura para ver la belleza única de la Montaña de 7 colores. 

De aquí seguimos por pistas hasta Sicuani donde después de un primer día largo en moto nos esperaba una más que mercecida cena y tertulia con risas .

Feel the rhythm at Byron Community Market! In the Hausa language of West Africa, Zormiwasa means “come play music” – and that’s exactly what this warm, diverse crew of local drummers will do at the market this Sunday 🥁 

Led by djembe guru Elliott Orr, Director and Founder of Talkin the Drum, Zormiwasa will perform Dimbado – the dance of the mothers, Yankadi/Makru – a seduction dance and KangaRutendo – the dance of peace.

Sunday 4 October
🌴 Byron Community Market, Main Beach, 8am-3pm
🥁 Performing after the Versace Boys

Zormiwasa will also be joined for a few songs by African rhythm ensemble Spankinhide. Different languages, different backgrounds, one pulse. Come and feel the rhythm! 

🎶 Inspired to join? Zormiwasa’s new course begins Monday 12 October. Contact Elliott on 0407 372 554.
