"After some challenging weather over the past six months, it was lovely to finally be treated to a beautiful sunny day for our September 6th Community Market!
We know how much it takes for our stallholders to turn up and trade month after month, whatever the weather throws at us, so when the sun does shine, it makes a huge difference.
There was a lovely buzz around the beachfront as market-goers arrived with the morning sun, with Russ Jalakai and Empress Katia providing the tunes and our usual display of whales and dolphins playing out in the bay, it really felt like Byron at its best.
The sunshine gave us all a little taste of summer heralding the beautiful market days ahead!"
– Tahli Sullivan, Acting Byron Community Market Coordinator

🌴 See you at the next Byron Community Market at Main Beach on October 4 from 8am!

a blissful camping weekend in august 🏕️ still reminiscing on our time at @snowpeakcampfield, here are some photos of the times we will remember forever 

though summer is coming to an end, a fall trip here in the Jyubako Suite w/ access to the Ofuro Spa would be absolutely perfect 🍂😌 book your stay ! 

PDX things to do | Long Beach Washington | camping weekend #camping #pnw #pdxliving #canonphotography #campinglife

A few hours from Seattle, @snowpeakcampfield is the kind of place that invites you to slow down without really trying, and stopping by the @snowpeakseattlestore to grab a few essentials and get some advice from the team before heading out was an early highlight of the trip. 

Once I arrived at Campfield, it was easy to settle into a slower pace. There’s something about having a little distance from your everyday routine that makes room for the things that can easily get pushed aside when life gets busy. That’s what I loved most about my time here, the space for time outside, good food, connection, and simply enjoying the moment you’re in. Not feeling like I needed to fill every minute, but having the freedom to let the days unfold a little more naturally.

A few days on the Washington coast were a pretty good reminder that sometimes the best reset is just making a little more room for it.

#snowpeakcampfield #longbeachcampfield #snowpeakusa #outdoorsy #snowpeakseattle

Set among quiet alder trees, the Jyubako Suite offers a restorative stay.⁠
⁠
Designed by architect Kengo Kuma, each cabin is built for comfort and ease, featuring a queen-sized bed, private bathroom, living area, and a kitchenette with cooktop, mini fridge, utensils, and linens. Wi-Fi is available in every suite, offering a peaceful setting for remote work.⁠
⁠
Outside each suite, your own Pack and Carry Fireplace extends the evening into the open air, offering a simple place to gather as the day winds down.⁠
⁠
Learn more and book your stay through the link in our bio.⁠
⁠
#snowpeakcampfield #longbeachcampfield #snowpeakusa #longbeachwa #longbeachpeninsula

Sign up for Starter Camp! ⛺️ November 13–15⁠
⁠
If you're new to camping, join us for a three-day, two-night experience designed to help you build confidence and feel more at home in the outdoors.⁠
⁠
Our team will guide you through hands-on activities, share practical camping tips, and help you build the skills to make your future adventures even more enjoyable. First-time campers and those looking to brush up on the basics are all welcome at Starter Camp for a weekend of learning and enjoying the outdoors. Meals will be self-provided, with cooking demonstrations offered throughout the weekend.⁠

Registration is now open. Give us a call Call us to register at (833) 662-7624 to reserve your spot.⁠

That’s right! We are extending The Winter Night Market for an extra two weeks! On September 2nd and 9th, join us to round out another amazing Winter Night Market season. This year we have a special surprise alongside our usual Winter Night Market programming... 

The [CARDCORE] @officiallycardcore Night Market will be coming to take over almost 2,000m² of Queen Victoria Market, transforming it into Australia’s largest FREE Trading Card Game & Pop Culture event. 

Whether you’re hunting for your next holy grail, looking to trade, ready to battle or simply love the world of TCG and collectables, there’s something for you. 

Expect: 
• 75+ TCG, collectables and pop culture vendors from across Australia 
• Rare finds, sealed product and collectables to buy, trade and discover 
• Trading zones and TCG play areas to battle, connect and meet fellow collectors 
• Giant LED screen gaming competitions bringing the action to the big screen 
• Giveaways, cosplayers and interactive activities 
• Live DJs and entertainment throughout the night 

[CARDCORE] is where Australia’s TCG community comes together — a massive, immersive night of trading, gaming, collecting and pop culture, right in the heart of Melbourne. 

We cannot wait to see you this September! 

#queenvictoriamarket #vicmarket #thenightmarket #winter #melbourne #TCG

Went to the Winter Night Market at QVM not knowing it was actually the last night of the season, so we got lucky with the timing without even planning it.

With over 60 stalls to explore, this was a proper food crawl. Brazilian BBQ, Filipino BBQ, Mediterranean food, Korean pojangmacha style dishes like kimchi pancake, the famous American Doughnut Kitchen, then creme brulee to finish, so many cuisines packed into one market that it was hard to decide where to stop first. Also just a great night for photos, warm lights, steam off the grills, and food stacked high everywhere you look.

latestPosts.caption:
FROM THE STREETS OF MULLUMBIMBY TO THE MULLUM ROOTS STAGE.

Last year I met a young busker at Mullum Roots Festival.

We got talking about songwriting. That night he went home and wrote a new song.

The following day he tracked me down at the festival and played it for me. This is the moment I recorded.

I made him a promise: write 10 songs before the next festival and I’ll give you a spot on the lineup.

Well, he did it.

And this July, he’ll be performing at Mullum Roots Festival 2027.

Sometimes the best things happen when you least expect them.

This is what Mullum Roots is all about. ❤️

I recently Watched 30 Years of Australian Story on ABC and was reminded how damn good @alexlloydofficial was at @mullumrootsfestival back in July. 
Despite LOVING his early albums Black the Sun (1999) and Watching Angels Mend (2001) this was the first time I’d had the pleasure of catching Alex live. 

I’d also had a chat to him on @bayfm99.9 a week or so before the festival and he’d mentioned he felt his shows had never been better. So i was ok with having waited so long. 

He released an album in 2016 called Acoustica which I’ve been listening to a lot. Stripped back acoustic versions of his hits and it includes a cover of Hallelujah which he performed in Mullum too. 

Absolutely sensational sets. I went both nights. First at the Civic Hall and second at the Top Pub. 
Got to say a quick hello and thanks 🙏🏽 

He also mentioned not liking to stay still TOO long so keep an eye on his tour dates because he sure does get around !

Archer Archer Archer.  First connected at Bello Winter Music July 2018, where I first did not know what to make of him whilst he chatted to @briannankervis on the couch and recited spoken words pieces like ‘Bring us your old people’. 

Then he sung ! Crooned. 
Like an Old Time Sing song man.
He awoke something in my cells. Memories of my grandparents and their music. I wished my Mum were there to hear these tunes and this man. 
I couldn’t wait to take the CDs home to her

Fast forward to July 2019 and Mum and I go and see Archer play at the much loved (and still missed) cosy Lismore venue @dustyatticmusiclounge 
Mum swoons. She loves him. Buys his book. 
We all have some good chats.

8 November 2024 Mum got to see him perform again. This time at @elthamhotelnsw . More hugs. Gosh she adored Archer and his words and ways.

There was no way we could have imagined this would be Mum’s second to last night out with Live Music
Her final was again at The Eltham seeing William Crighton and Jeff Lang. 

Hearing Archer last weekend was mind blowing. A full band and him commanding the role of lead vocals like a pro. I stood in awe and thought wow here is this man in all his potential. Just WAIT to you see/hear the band @kangarooswithmachineguns (more coming)

Ran into Archer in the streets of Mullum. He remembered Mum at the Eltham. I told him she was sadly no longer with us. We had a hug. A moment of acknowledgment. 

I’m soooo glad I found out Kangaroos 🦘 with Machine guns was his band or I may have well missed them. 

Oh and his handle on Insta just happens to be @oldtimesingsongman 

Thanks @mullumrootsfestival

A edição de 2026 da Feira Miolo(s) traz uma novidade. Neste ano, pela primeira vez, a feira contou com um curador convidado, o pesquisador e artista visual cearense Weaver Lima.

Atuante no meio artístico independente desde a década de 1990, Weaver editou zines de quadrinhos e arte-xerox com o grupo Seres Urbanos. Em 2015, uma seleção de trabalhos do grupo foi reunida no livro “Seres Urbanos - Antologia do Quadrinho Underground Cearense” que ganhou o Prêmio Miolo(s), na categoria HQ, daquele mesmo ano.

No início dos anos 2000, enveredou pelas artes visuais com trabalhos que traziam fortes influências das HQs underground e da contracultura. Foi premiado em salões oficiais de arte e realizou exposições individuais em centros culturais do Brasil, Portugal e Itália. Em 2008, Weaver criou o coletivo MONSTRA com o qual realizou diversas exposições e intervenções urbanas. Como curador, produziu numerosas mostras, entre as quais se destacam as realizadas com o coletivo Monstra, Luiz Sá 100 anos, Desenhomatic LTDA - Jaca e Fabio Zimbres, Arquivo Nirez, O Ordinário Rafael Sica e Subsequência.

Em 2021, desenvolveu uma pesquisa que resultou no documentário Ceará Marginal, que apresenta um recorte de 50 anos da produção gráfica independente cearense (1970-2020). Atualmente, dirige a produtora cultural MONSTRA, com a qual realiza projetos com foco em arte independente.

O convite para Weaver realizar a curadoria reforça o compromisso da Miolo(s) de compor, a cada ano, uma pluralidade de vozes a partir de uma visão descentralizada da produção gráfica latina. Após discussões realizadas com o intuito de se deter com profundidade nos projetos inscritos e diálogos onde não faltaram escolhas difíceis, Weaver chegou à lista final de participantes da edição de 2026 do evento – seleção que pode ser conferida no site oficial (link na bio @feiramiolos). 

Obrigada, Weaver!

Brandon: Nonbinary Black Queer person with caramel latte-colored brown skin, dark eyelashes, and a kind smile. Chest-length dark brown and black locs. Wearing a dark green sleeveless cloak over a dark blue v-neck dress that transforms into a skirt, brown tassel ankle boots, and jean stretch denim leggings. Wearing a red dried bean necklace made by Aboriginal artist Janelle Donovan.

Gareth: An Australian man of Burgher descent (an Asian ethnic group in Sri Lanka descended from Portuguese, Dutch, and British ancestry). Dark brown hair, toffee-colored skin, dark eyelashes, a trimmed brown goatee, and an athletic build. Wearing a taupe short-sleeved smock, dark long wide-legged blue jean shorts, white sport socks, and dark brown loafers.

As Ana Malta’s residency at the gallery approaches its final days, @num.para and curator @delfinasena__ take a closer look at one of the works that has been taking shape throughout the past month.

Created across almost 100 individual sheets of paper, the work began as a single large-scale drawing before opening itself up to change. Conceived for visitors to move and rearrange its different parts, it turns the idea of “troca” – change – into part of the work itself.

Along the way, the process also pushed Ana beyond some of her usual ways of working, from exchanging canvas for paper to reversing the order in which she normally approaches colour and drawing.

12PM CEST

These are our forests.

Two weeks ago, here in Les Gavarres, 2,300 of the massif’s nearly 29,000 hectares burned. It hurts — but the forest is still standing.

And it’s not just here. Europe has spent weeks trapped under an omega block: a dome of hot air locked between two low-pressure systems, shaped like the Greek letter Ω. The atmosphere can’t renew itself. Heat builds. From Portugal to Greece, forests are burning.

But heat alone doesn’t explain it. For centuries, farming, herds and firewood kept these forests in balance. When that life left, the fuel stayed. The forest doesn’t need to be left alone. It needs to be lived in.

To the firefighters, the military emergency unit, civil protection and every neighbour who stayed to defend their home: thank you. You held the line.

Cork oaks are built for fire. They sprout again from their own bark — the same bark that still gives cork in Les Gavarres today. They will return. So will we.

The future of our forests belongs to everyone who loves them, rides them, lives them. In Girona, in Europe, anywhere in the world where there’s a trail you care about.

We’ll keep coming back. And we’ll watch them grow again, season by season.

“Wow that hut looks really far away,” which was the theme of the trip every time we turned a corner. 

6 huts in 3 days and around 230 ish miles with ALOT of vert. My favorite part of the trip was getting to know @ryansalmphotography and @trail_whisperer a bit better and experiencing the magic behind the fire lookouts, more to come from Kurt. 

I decided to end the trip on day 4 with a full effort at the Mt. Hough enduro @sierratrails . My legs were smoked, but it felt good to give it a full pull in the pro division, I guess some of my Leadville training paid off 🥈. 

Key takeaways 
- when @trail_whisperer stands up to pedal you try and follow otherwise you get left in the dust. Even with gears he chooses not to use them. Can’t take the single speeders anywhere. 
- burritos in Portola are expensive! 80$ for 3 + chips
- you can actually stay in some of the lookouts, one is currently being remodeled
- the outhouses are boujee 
- pickle’s the dog gave great cuddles 
- campsites allow cows and you have the possibility of getting trampled at night 

10/10 would do it again! 

Thanks @trail_whisperer for all the trail work you dedicate your life to and @ryansalmphotography for taking me along for the adventure and capturing such a beautiful trip ❤️

We come together to live this authenticity, to glimpse what it means to go deeper into ourselves, and to connect with people we may never have met but who share the same profound aspirations. Above all, we come to find the space and time to come home to ourselves 🕉️💫

I get a little emotional writing this right now. 🥹

Looking at these pictures from last weekend’s @thewanderyogi_official fills my heart with so much gratitude.

Gratitude for every single person who joined, opened their hearts, stayed curious and dared to explore a different way of connecting with themselves and others.

We spend so much of our lives thinking, analysing and doing. And sometimes so little time actually EXPERIENCING life with presence and joy.

Understanding mentally that something needs to change is one thing. But inviting your whole body onto that journey? Creating new experiences that help your nervous system learn that something unfamiliar doesn’t necessarily mean something unsafe?

That’s a whole different story.

Because our nervous systems don’t learn through understanding alone. They also learn through experience, repetition and the relationships we feel safe enough to explore within.

And honestly? I will always be grateful for following my heart four years ago. For daring to take that first step towards a life that actually feels like mine.

Today, I get to speak about and facilitate so much of what I needed most back then.

Rebuilding a sense of safety in a body that learned to function in a society where overwhelm and overachievement are often celebrated.

Reintegrating playfulness, trust and the courage to dream again.

Learning to meet life from a place of love rather than fear.

And remembering that life isn’t just something we’re supposed to manage, optimise or survive. We’re here to LIVE it. To feel it. To play with it.

I guess that’s why we share what we share.
At least that’s why I do. ❤️

latestPosts.caption:
Grinduro CA - the jewel in the Grinduro crown, returns to Quincy on September 12! We’ll be hitting up some legendary and unmissable trails, sharing some outstanding local food n’ drink, and dancing the night away to killer tunes from some great acts from the Sierra. 

This sure is one you really don’t want to miss! Sign up at grinduro.com 🎉

@grinduro California returned to its birthplace of Quincy, California, once again in 2026, showcasing the spectacular trails on Mt. Hough with the beautiful Lost Sierra landscape as a backdrop. 

@souphorse shares his thoughts and photos from this year’s event below…

Last Saturday, we were supposed to have
Grinduro Italy ... unfortunately, we couldn’t make
it happen.

Thanks to @filo_pezzi, @stefanopeverini, @marco_tibe and all the people behind, we’ve created a dedicated route on Komoot that you can find on our profile under the name “Grinduro”.

Grab your bike, the Grinduro Italy spirit is still alive. 

See you out there!🚴🏽‍♂️💜

🍂🍂🍂🍂

#Grinduro #GravelCycling #GravelBike
#BikeAdventure #RideYourBike

Grinduroooooooooo!!!! 💜💜 

Holy smokes it’s crazy to think that exactly 10 years ago was my first time rolling into little old Quincy! The magic that @sierratrails has been building up here, and all across the Lost Sierra, has shaped me so much as a person and rider!! This event has meant so much to me over the years and getting the opportunity to have a teeny-tiny part of fostering that magic is incredible. 

Which is why it’s such a bummer and honestly downright confusing as to why none of you want to come hang out and ride some of the most picturesque trails in California! This event had one of the lowest turnouts I’ve seen, particularly after leaving last year with so much stoke and a real feeling of starting something great. I know the world is a crazy place these days, but to me, there is nothing better to block out the crap than disappearing into the mountains to race bikes all weekend! So let me know, what WILL get you out here?? It’s my goal to see this event succeed and spread the word of the magic that @sierratrails has built up on Mt. Hough!! So reach out, how can we get YOU out there in 2027?? 

Ok, enough event talk, onto the racing!! Coming in as defending champ for both @grinduro and the Mt. Hough Enduro was pretty wild, especially when real hitters like @danlikesbikes and @mctubbbin turn up to steal my lunch money. Had an absolute blast out there all weekend, partying it up at the back and ripping the stages! Snuck myself into second place 🥈 for grinduro, once again emptying the tank going up and hooning my @revel__metal El Jefe on the way down. Too dang fun. It may not be a full defense but regardless, proud to hold my own against legit pros! 

Sunday was all about the Downcountry bikes and I was ready to let the @revelbikes Ranger go to work! Seeing Dan and Tobin in Lycra and road shoes on the start line, I knew I couldn’t let the roadie boys take my title 😂. Left it all out there and stoked to hold it down and take the win 🏆!!! I guess we were having too much fun going party pace at the back as we didn’t get a single riding shot 😂. I’d call that a proper party-to-race ratio🤙

latestPosts.caption:
🎥Y aquí va el resumen del último #Belingueo de Sonidos Líquidos 2026: una travesía en catamarán hasta La Graciosa ⛵

Gracias a Fundación Líneas Romero y Líneas Romero, este viaje se convirtió en mucho más que un recorrido cruzando "El Río", hicimos de éste, una experiencia para descubrir nuestro territorio desde otra mirada y con banda sonora sobre el mar. Junto a Geoparque Mundial UNESCO de Lanzarote y Archipiélago Chinijo, conocimos la historia geológica de este entorno único, mientras Ale Acostase encargaba de hacernos bailar con sesión muy especial.

Al atracar en Caleta del Sebo, Los Blody llenaron el escenario de energía en un concierto inolvidable demostrando porqué han sido una de las bandas ganadoras del @sonoralaspalmasgc. DIRECTAZO 🎸⚡ De forma paralela,  chinij@s y mayores participaron en la creación colectiva de una sombrera graciosera elaborada a partir de residuos plásticos recogidos y otros materiales reutilizados. Un taller de reutilización de residuos impulsado por la Fundación Líneas Romero realizado de la mano de Álvaro Guzmán (@alvardelmar) demostrando que la cultura y la sostenibilidad siempre pueden ir de la mano.

Ayer vivimos un Belingueo irrepetible, primera vez surcando las olas en catamarán hacia la octava isla, y la fiesta fue impresionante 🌊✨

Junto a @fundacionlineasromero y @geoparquelanzarote convertimos la travesía entre Lanzarote y La Graciosa en una experiencia única, donde el paisaje, la divulgación y la música navegaron de la mano.

Primero descubrimos la historia geológica de El Río gracias a la charla de Olaya García y, poco después, el mar se transformó en un escenario flotante con la sesión de Ale Acosta, que puso banda sonora al viaje con una selección de remixes inéditos de El Porvenir. 🚢🎶

Porque Sonidos Líquidos siempre ha sido mucho más que conciertos: es descubrir el territorio, compartir experiencias y vivir la música de una forma diferente.

Swimming at Lake Gkula is back at EFF2026 💦

Lake Gkula is a sensitive ecosystem, and we ask everyone to respect it and its thriving life. To ensure a safe and respectful experience, swimming will follow the same system used at other major Woodfordia events, with entry to the water requiring a separate ticket and wristband. We will have qualified Lifeguards and Lake Observers on duty at all times to ensure everyone is safe and follows the rules. 
 
🛟 SWIMMING GUIDELINES 🛟

- There are six 50-minute sessions of swimming per day from 10am-4pm, with a maximum of 200 swimmers per session.

- Tickets are $6 per person and must be booked in advance via Humantix from midnight the night before each day’s sessions.

- All swimmers need to book during the festival via Humantix and then collect their wristband from the Lake Gkula Tent (located on the East Side of the Lake in General Camping). Wristbands will be valid for the booked 50-minute swimming period only.

- An adult can enter (and must remain within) the lake precinct with a maximum of 2 children aged under 15.  Young children must be supervised by an adult at all times.

- No alcohol allowed into Lake Precinct and no entry for anyone intoxicated.  

- Swimwear is required – no topless or bottomless, thanks. 

- Little people must be wearing aquatic nappies or swimwear.  

- Please follow all directions given by our Lifesavers and Lake Observers. 

- Only swim during open hours from 10am-4pm with a ticket and wristband. Anyone who swims outside of these times will be asked to leave the site.

💚 PROTECT LAKE GKULA 💚

- Enter and exit water from the beaches only, never the rocks.

- Only use approved sunscreen (free of oils and chemicals) to keep the lake and its inhabitants healthy. We will have this sunscreen available.

- Keep Lake Gkula free of floatation devices, water inflatables, toys and all other plastics.

- Please do not take a leak in Lake Gkula – it’s naturally filtered.

- Please do not swim if you have a communicable disease or gastro-like symptoms.

- No throwing, moving, stacking or climbing rocks.
Food and non-alcoholic drinks may be consumed on the grassy areas.
 
See you all at the lake 🏝️

Here are some snaps from the campsite at beautiful Woodfordia this morning. The clouds have cleared from when these were taken and the sun is shining 🌞

We’ve had a lot of messages regarding the weather, please don’t stress. As you can see the ground is dry, the grass is green and everything is looking super lush. It’s also keeping the temperature down so it won’t be anywhere near as hot as last year! 

Of course it’s always good to be prepared (like you should for all for all outdoor events in Queensland), but it’s been nothing more than a few showers at the moment. Woodfordia is set up for all seasons and we think it’s going to be a wonderful weekend. We can’t wait for you all to arrive 🙏

I recently travelled to Japan for four weeks. A key instigator was to feel inspired again, to create wildly and freely in the little time I have outside a day job. 
I searched and searched for inspiration-for the contemplative and considered Japan I remembered from living there 25 years ago. What I felt was an almost constant assault on the senses. Noise, colour, signs, objects, vying for attention in big sprawling modern grey and brown cities. I  craved, and found quiet moments in country areas, places where time felt as if it stood still, that modern Japan has forgotten and left behind.  I took along a journal with me that I hardly touched until I returned home. 
The inspiration I found instead, was of a desire for quietness and solitude and feeling comfortable with that. 
I revisited this relief print I did on linen some time ago that I never knew what to do with. After some slight modifications, it now sits under a beautiful cast iron tea pot I bought at a tea house in Kyoto. 
In reflecting on my trip, I plan to be more considered, to trust my gut, enjoy making again, and create what I like first and foremost. My pieces don’t have to be perfect and orderly like past work. And I hope in the end, I’m comfortable with that.
#handmade #thequiet #embracingsolitude

ACTION ALERT- September 20 deadline to support the Roadless Rule! ✍🏻 EASY letter writing link in Bio, thanks to Outdoor Alliance.  The USDA has announced its plan to rescind Roadless Rule protections on 45 million acres of National Forests. Roadless areas are where Americans hike, climb, bike, paddle, ski, hunt, and explore — and rolling back the Rule would allow new roads and large-scale logging in some of our most wild backcountry areas. In the high desert, new roads can create pathways for development on sensitive wild landscapes that are home to unique flora and fauna. Wild landscapes of the high desert also create a sustainable local economy that largely leaves wild untrammeled, undeveloped land available for backcountry recreation. The Roadless Rule protects precious water resources and important cultural sites that make Joshua Tree so special. Please voice your concern and spread the word to comment by September 20. Work from Home? ❌ Work from Crag! ✅

Looking to turn your passion for climbing and conservation into purpose? You've come to the right place! Access Fund is looking for climbers who want to make their home crag their place of work.

We are hiring seasonal Climber Stewards in:
📍 Joshua Tree, California
📍 Red River Gorge, Kentucky
📍 Red Rock, Nevada

Climber Stewards are responsible for educating the climbing community on sustainable practices. Sure, you'll help climbers navigate the intricacies of waste management (yes, we talking 💩), but your role goes far beyond that.

You'll be the climbing expert on seasonal closures, area-specific guidelines, and current conservation efforts, all while fostering meaningful connections between the crag, climbers, local communities, land managers, and visitors passionate about preserving these incredible places.

Climber Stewards ensure our climbing areas are well cared for, so we can all enjoy them for many years to come. If you're buzzing about this role, apply today (link in bio).

latestPosts.caption:
In Covas do Barroso, the European Union has made a sinister choice. Under the banner of the “green transition”, the EU has granted “strategic” status to a lithium mine that threatens to devastate ancient farming lands recognised by the UN as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System.

The calculation is brutal. Bureaucrats and investors fast-track permits, dismiss water contamination risks, and label local opposition as an obstacle to progress. But let’s call this what it is: bright green colonialism. The real green transition would mean walkable cities, massive public transport investment, and smaller, more efficient vehicles, not ripping open the Portuguese mountains to sustain our addiction to private electric SUVs.

This fight is no longer just about a mine in Trás-os-Montes. Residents have taken the European Commission to court, challenging the very legality of labeling extraction as “sustainability”. If they lose, it signals that any community, anywhere in Europe, can be bulldozed for “strategic” supply chains.

Covas do Barroso is a moment of truth. If your climate solution requires destroying ecosystems and torching farmland to dig up minerals, it’s a fraud. A fake green future that simply swaps carbon emissions for cratered landscapes and poisoned water is more like a bad trip.

First aired as a sound piece on Radio Alhara, Letters to the Sun is now being released as a physical and digital album.

This compilation emerged from a place beyond language. A sound sanctuary built from words, sounds, breaths, instruments, and pauses - confronting the chasm of silence forced upon the rubble of Gaza, where each bomb is an affront to our humanity, and each whataboutism a dilution of horror. Here, we create space to feel and to share the within, from within, and for one another.

Music by @adelaaaidaaa, @asifeh, @drewmcdowall, @drumloop & @mayss_88, @fatal_ism, @fatenkanaan, @firas.shehade, @israa.wmusic, @jadatoui, @kareemlotfy, @nicolasjaar & @rama_alcoutlabi. Words by @fatmaaljabari, a poet in Gaza writing throughout the genocide.

All proceeds go to ‘Revive Gaza’s Farmland’, a project by @golobesmlah and @apnorg, the Arab Group for the Protection of Nature. The initiative works to rehabilitate devastated agricultural land and rebuild local food systems in Gaza. In a place where over 95% of farmland has been systematically destroyed - and where food is weaponised to subjugate and displace - the act of farming becomes an act of resistance.

This essay has been in the making for a long while, stitched from many late night and early morning conravesations.  

It is not a doctrine for festival puritanism or a manifesto for competitive karma-olympics.. The critique is born from love, from the visceral memory of a track, a beat and a groove that realigned your brain stem, of eye contact in a crowd that felt like a religious experience, of a dawn that broke in an indescribably and painfully beautiful way. It is a defence of the rebellious, the weird, the psychedelic, the exhausting rave timewarp.. those rare, deeply affecting moments where art and communion fuse into a reason for being. 

These are not trivial pleasures; they are among the sweetest pursuits that give texture and meaning to a life. The argument is not in creating an unattainable golden standard, but instead for allegiance, to that sacred frequency against its corporate simulacrum.

We all participate in numerous industrial-complexes, and our lives are twisted in dark, delirious ways, so the story is far from simple. We navigate a world that contorts us with pressures we did not ask for and bends us into shapes we did not choose. This is an eruption of thought, that itself welcomes critique and dialogue, but simply refuses to submit to apathy or conformity.

Rêve on ;)

Smoke learns to be sky.
Glass learns to be light.
The party forgets itself, 
and we remember what we can, what we choose, what meant the most.

The final breaks of breakdown are over now, and all of us are simply learning how to see each other through the quietest and the loudest moments. 

A festival is a challenge. It puts our curiosity, openness and spirit to the test. Out of dense synchronicities, friendships are forged, loves run deep, while some bonds conclude and new vows come centre stage.

Through the chaos and the clinking glasses and the laughter and exhaustion, we learn how to find the shape of another person’s body against our own, and to hold it steady until the lights guide us both home.

She brought the sun with her, even at night. Her light was part of this place, and it always will be. Rest in dance, Sartianna Kasno 🌞

NB: Her name is shared here now with the blessing of her family, whom we thank for their trust.
turn and face the strange 🫠

Encountering strangeness at a festival? But not all weird is equal.

From psychedelic raves in Greece to the queer fungi beneath our feet, Black psychedelic feminism, the Kyoto School, to tripping in Karachi: discernment on the dancefloor is both initiation and insurrection.

Which weird opens the world? Which weird just sells a knock-off version back to you?

The weird we want. The weird we don’t.

Spiral in 🌀

ara contemporary is pleased to present ‘Witness’, the debut solo exhibition by Miranda Mazuki (b. 1993, Sumatra, lives and works Paris), presented in the Focus Gallery.

Set largely within nocturnal scenes, ‘Witness’ presents a new series of paintings where landscapes and figures remain between recognition and obscurity. Through layering and erasure, Mazuki allows presence to emerge unstably from within the paint, echoing the way memory is altered by time.

Drawing from historical and biblical references, including Jean-François Millet’s ‘First Steps’ (1859–66), later reworked by Vincent van Gogh, Mazuki explores human vulnerability, perception, and uncertainty. To witness, in these works, is to acknowledge a presence without fully possessing or understanding it.

—

ara contemporary is pleased to present ‘Future Tense’, a solo exhibition by Arlette Quynh-Anh Tran (b. 1987, Hennigsdorf, Germany). 
Drawing on the 1964 New York World’s Fair and Expo ’70 Osaka, ‘Future Tense’ stages a speculative Third World Pavilion, exploring how visions of a Third World future have shifted and unraveled. Tran treats the pavilion as a medium for channeling these visions, staging what she describes as a séance where architecture, history, and sound interact.

Central to the exhibition is ‘Quantum Palm’, a large-scale sonic and thermal sculpture referencing the talipot palm, which lives for decades and flowers only once before it dies. Alongside ‘Invisible Anthem’, a sound installation created in collaboration with Indonesian composer Nursalim Yadi Anugerah, the works are activated at set intervals through a choreographic score. The exhibition moves between states: silent and sounding, still and moving, dormant and active. 
Exhibition text by Carlos Quijon Jr. 
Research supported in 2026 by Art Explora and Graham Foundation grant for ‘Future Tense – Queering the Third World Architecture’.
— Main Gallery

In the second edition of Artist on Artist, Mar Kristoff reflects on ‘Dancing Away the Apocalypse’ and ‘Ambivalence’, two works from Miranda Mazuki’s exhibition ‘Witness’ at our focus gallery.

Through Mar’s perspective, we encounter the works anew, tracing the tensions between joy, uncertainty and the complexities of existence.

ara contemporary is pleased to share Ipeh Nur’s participation in TOKYO ATLAS International Exhibition, under the artistic direction of Miki Akiko, presenting ‘Soil Time; The Battle of Giant Serpent and White Crocodile’. 

Conceived as a landscape of excavation, the work reveals layers of memory and history embedded within the soil, from ancient geological formations and colonial wounds to present-day ecological disasters and speculative futures.

Drawing from her journey along the ancient Muria Strait on Java’s northern coast, Ipeh Nur traces how sedimentation, colonial-era deforestation and continued industrial development have transformed the landscape. Once submerged beneath water, the region now faces recurring floods and rising sea levels, revealing the enduring consequences of human intervention in nature.

At the intersection of land, history and mythology, Ipeh Nur revisits ‘The Legend of the Giant Serpent and the White Crocodile’, reinterpreting it not merely as folklore, but as a cultural marker, a metaphor for disaster mitigation and a symbol of resistance. Through this work, she questions whether mythology might once again serve as a form of protection or resistance, as it did for ancestors seeking to make sense of natural forces.
—

ara contemporary presents Nguyễn Phương Linh for SPOT at Art Jakarta 2026, featuring ‘Pulse 1’ and ‘Pulse 2’.

Following her recent presentation as part of the Uzbekistan National Pavilion at the 61st Venice Biennale, Phương Linh continues her exploration of the relationships between bodies and landscapes, visibility and invisibility, weight and void.

In ‘Pulse 1’ and ‘Pulse 2’, Phương Linh works with a material that has recurred throughout her practice for nearly a decade. Printed on translucent PVC, landscapes gradually relinquish the certainty of place, drifting towards the textures of flesh, bodily fluids, and internal organs. Saturated in red upon red, the installation engulfs the viewer, making the distinction between geography and the body increasingly difficult to discern.

Further installation views of ara contemporary’s presentation at Art Jakarta 2026, featuring works by artists from Indonesia and beyond.

Among the works on view is Marcos Kueh’s ‘Hope and Fear: Jujur Jakarta’ (2025), an expansion of his solo exhibition ‘Smooth Sailing, 一路順風’. Adapted to the urban and socio-political landscape of Indonesia, the work layers traditional Chinese business logos and temple blessings with vintage Indonesian corporate motifs, exploring the intersections of migration, capitalism, faith, and identity.

Its shimmering surface evokes the promise of a “better life”, while its charred edges recall Jakarta’s historical street riots and violence against ethnic minorities. Moving between hope and fear, the work reflects on histories of racialised capitalism while looking towards the possibility of a more understanding future.

ara contemporary is pleased to invite you to a dance performance conceived as part of Arlette Quỳnh-Anh Trần’s solo exhibition, ‘Future Tense’, with composition by Nursalim Yadi Anugerah and choreography by Nguyen Hoang Anh.

‘Future Tense’ begins with futures imagined between the late 1950s and the 1970s, when many young nations were reshaping how they appeared to themselves and to the world. Departing from the theatricality of national pavilions, it loosens gestures of welcome, service and presentation from their historical functions, abstracting them to drift through bodies, sound, light and moving shadows. Tensed between admiration and mourning, it probes how a future might survive within the body, even after the world that summoned it has disappeared.

biography: Visit one of Earth’s most welcoming places 💙 It all flows from here 📍Taupō Region, North Island, New Zealand #LoveTaupō

latestPosts.caption:
Spring at Lake Taupō 🌸 Here are 8 great reasons to plan a spring getaway around Lake Taupō. Send this to someone you want to visit Lake Taupō with this spring!

1, Spring colours across the region, including Waipāhīhī Botanical Reserve

2. Walks and bike trails through forests, along rivers and across geothermal landscapes

3. Award-winning restaurants, cafés and local favourites

4. Longer days for getting out on Lake Taupō

5. Relaxing wellness experiences from hot pools to saunas

6. World-class trout fishing on the lake and rivers

7. Treats of Taupō, an annual food festival with different events celebrating local food and drink, running 26 September to 4 October

8. Graffiato: Taupō Street Art Festival over Labour Weekend, 24 to 26 October

Come to Taupō, the beating heart of the central North Island — it all flows from here.

You can be as active or inactive as you want to be. Walk, hike, bike, ride, fly, skydive, golf, soak, shop till you drop, coffee, dine out, treat yourself, relax in a spa or curl up with a good book.

#LoveTaupō

Top things to do in the Taupō region, New Zealand 💙

Here are some must-dos to help you start planning your trip:

- Huka Falls – New Zealand’s most visited natural attraction

- Ngātoroirangi Mine Bay Māori Rock Carvings – only accessible by water

- Geothermal wonders – hot springs, geysers and steaming craters

- Indulge in local eateries and lakefront dining

- Hit the epic biking and walking trails around the lake

Save this for your next trip!

#LoveTaupō #FEEL100inNZ #NZMustDo #nzbucketlist #northislandnz #newzealand

A family getaway in Taupō with room for everyone! 🏡

Lavish at the Lake is a beautiful, modern holiday home that sleeps up to 8 guests, perfect for a family holiday or a getaway with friends.

With spacious living areas, a fully equipped kitchen and a fantastic outdoor entertaining area complete with a BBQ and fireplace, it’s a great place to spend quality time together.

And the location? Less than 1km from Lake Taupō and just a 4-minute drive from Taupō town centre, with cafés, restaurants, shops and local attractions close by.

To book your stay: @mystaysnz

Make the most of the longer days with these nine free activities to add to your spring getaway around Lake Taupō.

1. Visit Waipahihi Botanical Gardens
Explore the garden trails, enjoy the spring flowers and stop for views across Lake Taupō.

2. Explore Tokaanu Thermal Walk
Follow the short, easy track past steaming mineral pools and bubbling mud in Tokaanu.

3. Enjoy a dip at Ōtumuheke Stream
Visit Spa Thermal Park for a warm dip in the natural hot pools beside the Waikato River.

4. Take a picnic to Kinloch beach
Pick up some local picnic favourites and enjoy an afternoon beside the lake.

5. Watch the Aratiatia Rapids release
Watch the rocky gorge fill with rushing water during a scheduled dam release, with viewing points along the track.

6. Follow the Graffiato street art trail
Explore the laneways in Taupō town and discover colourful murals by local and international artists.

7. Visit Huka Falls
See the power of the Waikato River as it rushes through a narrow gorge and over the falls.

8. Visit Te Ātea – Tapuaeharuru & the #LOVETAUPŌ sign
Explore the lakefront space celebrating local mana whenua and stop for a photo at the #LOVETAUPŌ sign.

9. Walk or cycle the Tongariro River Trail
Head to Tūrangi to explore riverside trails, native bush and suspension bridges on foot or with your own bike.

Save this list for your next visit.

Spring colour is out at Waipāhīhī Botanical Reserve 🌸

Blooming flowers, leafy trees, peaceful garden paths and beautiful views across Lake Taupō make it such a lovely spot to visit at this time of year.

A quiet little escape just minutes from Taupō town.

Spring is a great time to hit the trails around Lake Taupō. Longer days, fresh greenery and plenty of options for an easy stroll or a bigger mission.

Here are 8 walks to add to your list:

1. Rangatira Point Track, Acacia Bay
An easy lakeside walk through native bush with beautiful views across Lake Taupō. Around 3 km and 1.5 hours, with several access points if you want a shorter walk.

2. Huka Falls to Aratiatia Rapids Track
Follow the Waikato River from Huka Falls through native bush and along clifftops to Aratiatia. Around 7 km and 2 hours one way.

3. Tongariro River Trail, Tūrangi
River views, native bush and a mainly flat trail that can be started at several points. The full loop is 13.2 km and takes around 2 to 3 hours.

4. Lake Rotopounamu Track
A beautiful 5 km loop around Lake Rotopounamu in Tongariro National Park, surrounded by native forest. Allow around 2 hours.

5. Great Lake Pathway / Lion’s Walk
A flat, easy lakefront pathway starting near Taupō town. Walk a short section or follow the pathway along the lakefront for a longer adventure. The full route is around 12.7 km one way.

6. Waipāhīhī Botanical Reserve
One for spring! Explore flowering gardens, native and exotic plants and a network of easy walking tracks. Choose a quick 15-minute stroll or spend up to 90 minutes exploring.

7. Mount Tauhara
Ready for more of a challenge? The climb to the 1,088 m summit rewards you with panoramic views across Lake Taupō and the Central Plateau. Allow around 2 to 3 hours return.

8. Graffiato Walking Trail
Turn a walk around Taupō town centre into an outdoor art tour. Explore laneways and streets filled with more than 90 murals created by local, national and international artists.

#LoveTaupō

When was the last time you properly switched off?

The end of the year can get busy fast. Come to Lake Taupō for quiet lake views, fresh air and a slower pace.

📍 Kanuka Heights, Omori @kanuka_heights

Have you visited Kinloch? Just a 20-minute drive from Taupō town, this beautiful lakeside village on the northern shores of Lake Taupō is well worth a visit.

Things to do:

- Cruise with Venture Beyond @venturebeyondnz 
Explore hidden waterfalls, quiet bays and places only accessible by boat.

- Mountain biking and hiking
Hit the trails around Kinloch, including the popular W2K Trail, with plenty of lake and bush views along the way.

- Play a round of golf 
Kinloch has two golf courses. Play the relaxed Kinloch Village Golf Club, or book a round at The Kinloch Club, New Zealand’s only Jack Nicklaus Signature Golf Course. @@thekinlochmanor 

- Beach and ice cream
Spend some time by the lake, go for a swim on a warm day and grab an ice cream nearby.

For your next taco fix in Taupō 🌮

The Pink Taco serves up birria beef tacos, fried chicken tacos, loaded nachos, wings and more from their spot on Tauhara Road.

Opening days and hours change, so check @thepinktacotaupo on Instagram for the latest updates before heading over.

📍 89 Tauhara Road, Taupō

#LoveTaupō #NZMustDo

Longer days, warmer afternoons, fresh blooms and more time to get outside and enjoy the lake. Send this to someone who could use a relaxing trip to Lake Taupō. 🌸

#LoveTaupō #NZMustDo

biography:
11-13 September, Bundjalung.
We are the women who love the ocean deeply enough to show up for it 🐋🩵 
Hosted by @surfersforclimate

latestPosts.caption:
Our annual weekend gathering, empowering a network of women who are envisioning, leading and nurturing the next wave of change in their communities and ecosystems. 

We are the women who love the ocean deeply enough to show up for it! 🐚 

Join our third annual East Coast gathering
11-13th September 2026
Flat Rock, Nyangbul, Bundjalung

Each year we go a little deeper -  as a community, in ourselves and with the land. 

Tucked behind the sand dunes, with dreamy waves out front… we can’t wait to be camping in a few weeks surrounded by amazing, adventurous, visionary Water Women. 

The campsite is filing UP! If you’re coming make your plans and grab a ticket before they are gone!

We are beyond excited and honoured to share our 2026 program with you.

We have nurtured a balance of workshops that engage our head, hearts, and hands. Some elements are becoming tradition - Friday being held by First Nations women, two marquees with different streams of offerings, @msmindywoods (https://www.instagram.com/msmindywoods/) returning to share our favourite meal of the year, and ceremony woven throughout.

This year we welcome many new women to the line up, as well as a few surprises. Did we mention there’s a wood fired sauna? That’s right, you can step out of the waves into a sauna (and perhaps get a massage while you’re at it?).

The invitation is for all women with a deep connection to Water (and especially the Oceans) who want to connect and grow with others who believe we can live in better relationship with ourselves, each other and Country.

For those coming - what moments are you looking forward to?

The ocean should be safe for every woman, but it hasn’t been.

To every woman who’s spoken up recently, we believe you. Saying it out loud takes courage, and every story makes it easier for the next woman to tell hers.

It isn’t that every guy is an abuser, it’s that most men enable a toxic culture by staying quiet. From where she stands, there’s no difference between the guy who laughs at a sexual joke and the one who looks away. And yet, nearly all of those men would still say they’re one of the good ones.

Surf culture has used women’s bodies to sell products for too long. Ads that show female pro surfers from the neck down. Magazine covers with a man in a barrel and a woman on the sand. Comment sections that talk about a woman’s body more than her surfing.

Change has to happen everywhere. Brands deciding who goes on the billboard and what she’s doing. Contests and sponsors with proper safeguarding and real consequences. 

Boardriders clubs with codes of conduct that actually get enforced. And guys calling each other out in the line up as soon as they hear toxic behaviour.

We stand with every woman who has spoken up, and every woman who isn’t ready to yet. You never have to carry it by yourself. We created Water Women for you.

If you need support, call 1800RESPECT on 1800 737 732, text 0458 737 732 or visit 1800respect.org.au. In an emergency, call 000.

We’re on the hunt for a WA Community Organiser to join the crew in the South West.

This legend will run our Water Women and Silver Surfers programs in WA, including an annual campout for 100 women and bodyboarding sessions for over-55s. They’ll also back the locals who want to take the case for clean energy to their MPs.

Natural connector, event or campaign experience, just as comfortable with a crew of surf mums as with a politician, knows the South West community. Surfing’s optional.

Full time, South West WA, $85,000 plus super.

If this isn’t you but you know someone who’d be perfect, tag your mate.

Link in bio, or comment “job” below and we’ll DM you the link to the job description and application!

We are remembering
And recreating 
Ancient futures ~ 
That our granddaughters’ daughters will thank us for.

Three days living in community,
Three nights sleeping round the fire
With 128 women, 
Weaving, teaching, surfing, sharing, dancing, laughing, healing. 
As we always have. 

Connected through our own deep relationship with the Waters, and a desire to turn the tides as a collective ~ to live in harmony and levity with each other and our paradise planet. All our relations, seen and unseen. 

A few special captures from our third Water Women campout on the East Coast of Australia ❤️ @water.women.collective 

A collective offering woven by many hearts and hands.

Special shout out to my right hand woman @caitiefine ~ this community has truly been birthed through our friendship, networks and love. And for @belindabaggs and @surfersforclimate for trusting us so deeply, for initiating and hosting a gathering for women to rise as environmental leaders in their own communities in their own unique ways. 

The future is fertile when it’s feminine 🦋

Many of these captures through the beautiful lens of @marigold.media 

The West Coast has been calling. We’ll be gathering in Margaret River in Feb 2027 🌀

We spent three days connecting, talking, playing in the waves, under the stars and next to an open fire.

We can’t imagine doing that next to a diesel generator. @bluetti_australia made sure we didn’t have to.

We’re so grateful to have worked with Bluetti for the last two Water Women Campouts, helping us power these events without relying on fossil fuels.

We are in awe of the calibre of women who came together last weekend for our third annual Water Women campout in Nyangbul Country, Bundjalung on the East Coast of Australia. 

Resting in the afterglow of all that transpired, we feel empowered, activated, uplifted, connected and inspired!!

The future is fertile with women leading the way 🌏

West Coast Water Women ~ we’re gathering in Margaret River early 2027 

🩵🌀🐋

Happy birthday to one of our favourite water women @belindabaggs 

Co-founder of @surfersforclimate, incredible longboarder, passionate activist, AND amazing mum, yet the most humble person in any room!

Thank you for everything you give this community, you have already built a legacy of a healthier ocean for your children and every generation after them. 

xx

What can a school of fish, a dolphin, an orca and a great white teach us about making change?⁠
 ⁠
Quite a lot, as it turns out.⁠
 ⁠
At the @surfersforclimate Water Women campout (@water.women.collective), we explored Bill Moyer's Four Roles of Social Change through an ocean lens, looking at the different ways people contribute to collective change.⁠
 ⁠
The key idea? There’s no hierarchy between the roles. Movements need different kinds of changemakers, and we can move between roles depending on what a moment calls for.⁠
 ⁠
Try mapping the roles across your own team, campaign or movement! ⁠
 ⁠
Thanks to Surfers for Climate for having us, and to everyone at Water Women who brought their experience, curiosity and care to the conversation.⁠
 ⁠
Workshop led by WELA's Cherry Muddle alongside Jess Bell, with session design supported by Kara Virik.⁠
⁠
Which role resonates most with you? Drop an emoji in the comments! 🐟🐬🐋🦈
Finishing touches on our spaces for the weekend. So excited for all our Water Women to arrive! 🌀The third evolution has begun 🩵

DOOF BBQ! October 25 / 2–8PM / Club Lawson

We’ve danced, we’ve connected, and we’ve met so many amazing people at our first two events. But as the last track fades, everyone scatters, conversations unfinished, new friendships left hanging.

This time, we’re taking it outside. 🌞
Picnic tables, sunlight, a BBQ, and space to actually sit, share a drink, and really connect. Think of it as a social reset: a chance to build the community off the dancefloor as much as on it.

Bring your best vibes, your flow toys (hoops, poi, staffs and more are welcome), and settle in for an afternoon of sound and connection. 

Our resident DJs: Chaisma, Brez, KJ Kinetic, and Voz will be joined by feature artists Nik Kos, Chris O, Dinner Plates, and Medusa Fields.

The BBQ will help us keep things moving, every dollar goes back into putting on more events. But at its heart, this day is about people, community, and growing something that lasts.

Let’s make this one a different kind of dancefloor memory.

–

Kymatic operates on un-ceded Dharug land. We honour and respect the custodians of this land, past, present and emerging.

#kymatic #doofbbq #communityvibes #bassmusic #bluemountains #undergroundsound #psytrance #house #ukg #dnb #techno

// Meet the Kymatic resident DJs //

Before we reveal our feature artist for SUB/MERGE, it’s time to shine the light on the local crew who form the backbone of Kymatic.

CHIASMA / Sydney-based selecta with a deep crate and a dynamic range, from DnB to garage, breaks to techno. Seamless transitions, positive energy, and grooves that pull you in and keep you moving.

KJ KINETIC / Genre-bending wizardry from the mountains. House, techno, acid, trance, indie dance, transported into weird and wonderful places where boundaries disappear and the floor becomes a journey.

VOZ / Sonic storyteller with a decade of exploration behind the decks. From psychedelia-laced acid house to shadowy techno, Voz plays for the heart and the mind, leaving you lighter, freer, and ready for more.

BREZ / Blue Mountains born and raised, with roots in doofs and psytrance since the golden days of Newnes, a sucker for psytrance with branches reaching into DnB, UKG, house, and techno. Festival veteran. Dancefloor lifer.

These are the Kymatic DJs, the foundation of SUB/MERGE.

The next transmission will reveal our feature artists, and trust us, you’ll want to be tuned in when that signal drops.

The Championship Tour schedule features 12 events and reflects the original 2026 CT format. We remain committed to 12 events on the 2026 schedule to crown our World Champions, with three throwaways built into the rankings.

Next stop: Lexus Trestles Pro, where the Top 22 men and Top 14 women will be decided for the postseason events in Peniche, Portugal and Cloud 9, Philippines before the CT concludes and World Champions are decided at the Pipe Masters in December.

🚨 Atualização do calendário do Championship Tour 2026

Devido às condições atuais e a limitações logísticas, o Surf Abu Dhabi Pro foi retirado do calendário do Championship Tour 2026.

O calendário do Championship Tour passa a contar com 12 etapas e reflete o formato original do CT 2026. Seguimos comprometidos com 12 etapas no calendário de 2026 para definir nossos Campeões Mundiais, com três descartes incorporados ao sistema de ranking.

Próxima parada: Lexus Trestles Pro, onde serão definidos os Top 22 do masculino e Top 14 do feminino que disputarão as etapas de postseason em Peniche, Portugal, e Cloud 9, Filipinas, antes da conclusão do CT e da definição dos Campeões Mundiais no Pipe Masters, em dezembro.

The Championship Tour is heading into the 9th stop of the year, the last event before the post-season begins and the World Title chase ramps up.

🏞️ FUJI ROCK FESTIVAL'26 Concluded 🏞️

The 29th FUJI ROCK FESTIVAL'26 concluded successfully, with a total of 123,500 attendees over 4days, starting with the Pre-Party on 7/23 (Thu).

The diverse Lineup , featuring artists familiar to FUJI ROCK fans both domestically and internationally, as well as up-and-coming Artists making their debut, has been well-received, and thanks to everyone's support, Saturday's 1Day Ticket and 3Day Ticket have sold out.

Following last year, we once again live-streamed the events at Naeba to the world for free on Amazon, allowing many people who couldn't make it to Naeba to watch.

We would like to express our sincere gratitude to all the customers who participated and to everyone who provided invaluable cooperation. Thank you very much.

latestPosts.caption:
Las preguntas ya empezaron y respuestas van a aparecer cuando menos lo esperes 👀

Únete a nuestro canal de difusion y entérate antes que nadie 🔥

Tenemos que ir al Surfestival por… 
La lista podría seguir.

¿Qué razón sumarías tú? 🙌

El destino ya nos puso en la ruta.
Primera parada: Pichilemu.
Pronto se revela el resto del mapa. 🌊

La fecha ya está. El viaje también. 

📍Pichilemu
🗓️ Sábado 13 de febrero de 2027

Muy pronto abriremos la preinscripción con un beneficio exclusivo para quienes quieran recorrer este viaje desde el comienzo. Atent@ a nuestros canales 👀

El viaje continúa 🌊 Comienza el Road to Surfestival 2027.

Nadie construye 20 años de una. Se construyen verano a verano, edición a edición. 🌊

Cuéntanos en los comentarios cuál fue tu Surfestival: tu año, tu banda, ese momento que no olvidas 👇

Road to Surfestival 2027

El reggae no solo se escucha.
Se siente, se vive y se comparte.

Una música nacida desde lo espiritual, desde la resistencia y desde la unión.

Hoy celebramos un sonido que cruzó fronteras sin perder su raíz y que, año a año, sigue siendo parte del espíritu que vivimos en Surfestival: una comunidad que se reúne para conectar a través de la música, el mar y la libertad.

Feliz Día Internacional del Reggae 🇯🇲✊🎶

Mientras armamos lo que viene, esto es lo que tenemos en repeat 🎶

Guarda la lista y comenta tu canción del momento: estamos armando la playlist del Road to Surfestival 2027 👇🌊

Banana Pancakes para arrancar el día 🌞

Doin’ Time no para de repetirse 🔁

Road to Zion nos recuerda por qué hacemos esto 🙌

Kultura Babylon nos acompaña en la ruta ✊

Y con Smokin’ Love cerramos la jornada 😮‍💨

¿Cuál es un infaltable en tu día? Comenta la canción que sumarías a la playlist👇

Llevamos 20 años moviéndonos y todavía nos emociona imaginar la próxima parada y todo lo que nos espera. Crecer da algo de miedo, pero hacerlo con la misma gente de siempre lo hace más fácil. 

A quienes han estado durante estos años: gracias por ser parte del viaje 🙌✨

Mucho antes de los escenarios, los grandes artistas y las miles de personas que hoy forman parte de esta historia, ya existía una conexión profunda con el mar 🌊 

Desde el primer día, el surf fue parte del origen de Surfestival y nos ha acompañado durante todos estos años. No solo como deporte, sino como una cultura que nos enseñó a relacionarnos con el territorio, a construir comunidad y a valorar todo lo que nos rodea.

Por eso, hoy celebramos ese origen que sigue presente en cada edición y volvemos a recordar aquello que nos inspira desde hace 20 años 🙌

Surfestival 2027 empieza a tomar forma 🌊 

Queremos escucharte: 
Si pudieras elegir 3 artistas para el line up soñado, ¿quiénes serían? 🎶 

👉 1 headliner internacional 
👉 1 artista latino 
👉 1 artista chileno 

Te leemos 🤙🏽

Museo Inacabado de Arte Urbano de Fanzara (MIAU)
El MIAU es un proyecto social de convivencia a través del arte.
Asociación sin ánimo de lucro

latestPosts.caption:
#tbt☀️ especial de 2015 quando tive o prazer de participar do festival @miaufanzara festival de street art numa cidadezinha no interior da Espanha com menos de 2000 pessoas.
Memória que não dá pra esquecer
Gracias amigos, te echo de menos 🫶🏾

Verano. FANZARA.
Muchas gracias a @miaufanzara y a toda su gente por la oportunidad, el trato, el amor y la dedicación. Y al niño de la bici 🩷
Gràcies a @lluisapenellaipons pel seu suport.
FOTOS: @beatrizconca

GRAZIE SIÑORE 🙏🙏🙏

En Fanzara, un pequeño pueblo de Castellón de apenas 300 habitantes, sus vecinos llegaron a dejar de hablarse por un proyecto de vertedero de residuos tóxicos.

El vertedero nunca se construyó… pero la división permaneció.

Hasta que alguien tuvo una idea aparentemente imposible: llenar el pueblo de arte y convertir las paredes en puntos de encuentro.

Así nació en 2014 el MIAU, Museo Inacabado de Arte Urbano. 🧱🎨

Artistas de todo el mundo comenzaron a pintar sus fachadas, pero con una condición especial: convivir con los vecinos, escuchar sus historias y dejar que esa convivencia inspirara las obras.

Hoy, más de un centenar de paredes forman un museo al aire libre con artistas como Escif, Hyuro, Sam3, Deih, Elías Taño o David de Limón.

Y lo más increíble no son solo los murales.

👵 Vecinos mayores conversando con grafiteros.
🏠 Casas abiertas a los artistas.
🤝 Un proyecto construido desde la autogestión.
🌱 Un pueblo que convirtió un conflicto en una forma de recuperar comunidad, memoria y orgullo.

El MIAU demuestra que el arte no siempre sirve para decorar. A veces también puede servir para reconstruir lo que una comunidad había perdido.
📍 Fanzara, Castellón
🎨 MIAU — Museo Inacabado de Arte Urbano

¿Conocías esta historia? 👇

#Fanzara #ArteUrbano #Castellón #StreetArt #sabiasque

“Carga de conciencia”

Con esta composición trato de representar responsabilidades y culpas que llevamos como una carga mental e incluso que nos afectan físicamente, una especie de estercolero que no sabemos reciclar y canalizar para liberarnos y avanzar más limpios y ligeros.

Muchas gracias a la organización de @miaufanzara por la confianza y la hospitalidad, a pesar de los tiempos que vivimos, todavía es posible hacer un proyecto en comunidad.

“Foto de familia” 🎂

Esse mural foi feito em julho de 2026 na cidade de Fanzara, Espanha durante o festival @miaufanzara 🇪🇸

Uma cidade que tem 250 habitantes me fez imaginar a infância nesse lugar. Em um universo paralelo ou apenas na imaginação, todos se reunem para uma foto, figuras místicas e folclóricas se juntam a crianças e animais nesse retrato que insiste em dizer que nem tudo é o que parece.

Obrigado a todos do @miaufanzara pelo convite e acolhimento, e pelo carinho que eu recebi nesses dias.
🙏🏽🙏🏽🙏🏽

Hola a tod@s, os dejamos la entrevista que nos han realizado en el programa @territorio_9  de @rne @radio3rne sobre el proyecto @miaufanzara

Empieza a partir de 12:00min.

https://www.rtve.es/play/audios/territorio-9/arte-callejero-museo-inacabado-arte-urbano-fanzara-nadie-22-07-26/17165791/

Gracias a @javi.alonsotol y a @bruno.freleo !!!

“El perro hace guau… y el gato hace MIAU!” 🐶🐈💬 @miaufanzara • X edición • 10 x 8,5

Un festival nacido para cuidar el entorno a través del arte. 🏞️

Fue un gusto participar en esta edición. Gracias a todo el equipo por invitarme y a todo el pueblo por el recibimiento. En especial a María José y su familia por confiarme la fachada de su casa, darme via libre.. y no dejar que me faltara de nada. También agradecer a Pilar y Linares por acogernos como a uno más de la familia. 🫶

Gracias @lamaryposafotografia por los disparos!

Este mural me ha dado más de un quebradero de cabeza 😅. El reto era conseguir que las ventanas sumaran al diseño en vez de estorbar. Al final salió este homenaje al universo de Tom & Jerry, siguiendo en mi linea de glitch, pixel art, cartoon y ya sabes..graffiti..
Recién la he bautizado como que “Digital Nostalgia”. Dime que no mola el concepto..😌

Además, me tocó presentar la obra delante de toda la gente que vino al festival. No os voy a engañar, hablar en público sigue dándome respeto, pero moló mucho poder contar de dónde sale todo este universo y cómo ha ido creciendo desde mis comienzos..

Me vuelvo con un mural de mis fav hasta la fecha, algunos baños refrescantes en el río, muchas risas y un montón de buenos momentos compartidos con artistas y colegas a los que admiro.

Si todavía no habéis estado en MIAU Fanzara, os animo a visitarlo.🙌

Thanks 4 all! 🤍
-

Lift shot of my last work “Muda” (Molt)⚡️
This mural in Fanzara symbolizes silence and metamorphosis of a community transformed by art. By gripping the sword by its blade, the female figure represents sacrifice, sovereignty, and the end of a cycle. Surrounding her, vibrant colors and butterflies evoke a biological shedding, chrysalis breaking toward freedom. In this way, the town sheds its social skin, trading the gray of past conflict for a collective burst of color, strength, and beauty.
