Nimbin MardiGrass is a cannabis law reform rally & celebration in the tiny village of Nimbin in Northern NSW, Australia.

latestPosts.caption:
HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #729 | 15 OCTOBER 2026

High Headliners!

...Changing cultural practices is a slow process, but there is no doubt it is happening. Research consistently shows that people who use cannabis decrease their alcohol use and in many cases stop it altogether. When Americans are surveyed, the majority believe cannabis is a much healthier option than alcohol. We seem a long way behind that here.

In the Western Australian Parliament, Dr Brian Walker argued this week that grog poses a greater societal danger than pot and asked the Government to investigate a regulatory framework that treats each according to the evidence and harm. Way too rational for them I suspect.

There was yet another disappointing television show about the dangers of legal weed being unapproved and too high in THC, this time by SBS. Stories from people who have little experience, it sounds like, and doctors who pull out the same closed-minded nonsense. 

Their blindness in only allowing indoor, mostly hydroponic pot to be legal (and then it must be irradiated, but most importantly so little is organic), is a big part of the problem. Powerful chemical fertilisers are growing most of our food as well and I just know it’s not healthy.

Basically the authorities can’t handle that the horse has bolted, when they opened up Telehealth during the pandemic. Has anyone died from cannabis yet? No. Are thousands more getting huge pain relief from it? Yes. Will it lessen the stigma? Yes. They still don’t comprehend we have an Endocannabinoid System, each one of us.

Easily the highlight of my week was reading Lucy Haslam’s freshly penned story of her discovery of cannabis via her son Dan’s cancer treatments. And it’s not over yet, she’s still in the trenches, arguing for us all, trying to get heard by the rule-makers, as determined as ever. The book is available through print on demand via Lucy’s website (https://authorlucyhaslam.com/). It’s an inspiring story, also available on Amazon. A great read.

Love to everyone.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #728 | 8 OCTOBER 2026

High Headliners!

I was hanging out in Colombo at the ancient Buddhist Temple and got to know an old monk who spoke good English. I was telling him how magic mushrooms changed my life and he said, “Do you want to see how Buddha got enlightened?”.
It was an experience to remember.

He led me down into the bowels of the Temple, pulled an ancient key out from under his robe and opened an equally ancient cupboard with it. He pulled out an old book, the pages looking very handmade, which told the story of Buddha’s journey. There were simple drawings in the book, which was helpful, because I couldn’t read any Sanskrit.

He found the page and read it to me. Buddha had reached the end of his search for Truth and sat down under the Bodhi Tree and fasted for thirty days. He was determined to sit there until he attained awakening. Figs were falling from the tree and lay scattered around him on the ground. Birds were eating the fermented ones and getting drunk, falling over and so on. Buddha ate some and was enlightened and that was it! When I think about it, after fasting for so long, the alcoholic figs would have done the job. However, not all Buddhist’s I tell that story to like it! 

Four Corners on the ABC wasted a show this week, I thought, on a few companies ripping off the DVA by prescribing huge amounts of weed to Veterans, just like the NDIS rip offs. The real story for me is doctors who have no cannabis experience, being the prescribers. They’re so fortunate no one can die from using cannabis as they have no idea about it, a lot of them, and everybody is different. Experience is the real teacher.

I like that PlantMed wont prescribe THC without CBD as well. Just imagine if they let the hippies, who’ve used weed for decades, sell medicine from dispensaries, as well as cuttings of cultivars, suited to your needs, that you could grow at home. That’s the dream and I’m sticking to it! 

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #727 | 1 OCTOBER 2026
I’ve been visiting the massive brand new Tweed Hospital nearby, built in the middle of prime farmland. My old mate James Kingsbury, otherwise known to many of you as Heathen Lovechild, is who I’m visiting, and he’s very sick. As is Jim Moylan, who is going through an experimental new chemo trial, while choofing as much as he can which the doctors are of course fascinated by.

The Legalise Cannabis Party would not exist without the years of work put in by those two, so this mention is in deep appreciation. Some of the road trip campaigns I’ve been on with Jim are legendary while hermit Heathen kept the HEMP Party running from a little tin shed in the middle of the bush for years.

As a result of their decades of work, NSW MP Jeremy Buckingham was in parliament this week questioning when will we honestly tackle the current gang wars in Sydney, fighting over the massive profits to be made from coke and meth. Prohibition doesn’t work—drug use is a health issue—humans have always used drugs—they like them! The message is no different to thirty years ago, but meanwhile, thousands of lives are being trashed each week by the unwinnable drug war. It has to end sometime.

This year marks the 25th anniversary of Portugal decriminalising personal possession of all drugs. They’ve developed an integrated system of health and social services without making abstinence a precondition for getting help. Simply treat drugs as a health issue as we’ve been saying for years.

Alcohol is so popular in Australia and ingrained in our lifestyle and culture with mainstream advertising and promotions everywhere. Still, more and more people are discovering and loving cannabis, and hence drinking less. It’ll make us smarter and healthier, I reckon. A huge percentage of daily cannabis users I know don’t drink alcohol at all. It’s a significant change. Think don’t just drink!

Michael Balderstone
HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #726 | 24 SEPTEMBER 2026

RDT rules finally passed for NSW but I keep reading misunderstandings about it. As I see it, there will be no change to the testing roadside, just different punishments. If you have a prescription and register you should no longer get into trouble, so long as you are not impaired and no alcohol or other drugs! 

Pathetic really, but never forget this is war and we’re negotiating peace and this is just the first step. Finally you can consume your medical cannabis and drive and no longer be a criminal. You still might have to leave your car for 24 hours, nothing has changed there, but otherwise it’s a win for a lot of people who are happy getting their legal weed in the mail. A big thank you to Legalise Cannabis’ Jeremy Buckingham.

Hopefully now he can focus on the real job at hand which is allowing us to grow our own medicine and how to begin winding back the whole disastrous drug war… I virtually never do edibles, as they call it in weed world. A cookie can take a couple of hours to take full affect and then it can be too much or too little. That’s why the majority of us cannabis users smoke, we can feel when we’ve had enough. The effect is quickly into our bloodstream, then our brain.

It was half-time in the weekly Friday Hemp Hour on NIM-FM and I hadn’t eaten all day and got tempted by a chocolate ‘cookie’. As soon as I tasted it I knew it was strong, but down the hatch and I soon forgot about it. A couple of hours later it hit me like a freight train...

Smoking is in fact the way to self titrate your medical cannabis dose, but it is also the one that activates your saliva for RDT. As the police have said in the past, if you smoke we’ll catch you, if you eat a cookie, maybe we will, but if you swallow a capsule, we can’t detect it. This has encouraged many to not smoke but ingest in other ways which can be less safe, unless you know exactly the amount you need and the strength of the buds.

Love to everyone and keep your sense of humour handy if you can.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #725 | 17 SEPTEMBER 2026
High Headliners! 
I had a win in court on Monday with my old mate and legal wiz John Weller convincing the Magistrate to allow me to keep driving, albeit with a two year good behaviour clause. Coincidentally, the new RDT bill* will hopefully pass in NSW Parliament today, finally getting over the numerous road blocks. It’s a small but significant change I maintain, with no more automatic loss of licence, if you register with transport etcetera. 

This Headlines is full of great stories from Portugal, Switzerland, Holland, South Africa, India and more. The legendary Ed Rosenthal has turned his cannabis law reform radar on India which was forced to join everyone else and make their sacred ganja illegal in 1961. Did I forget they were given 25 years to “clean up their act” so in fact ganja didn’t really became illegal there until 1986. 

So my decade of going back and forth to the land of the Hindus, smoking copious chillums (pipes) with sadhus (spiritual disciples), was all legal times. We certainly never got in any trouble and I remember you could buy legal government grown ganja in some states. It didn't compare to the hash which was coming in from Afghanistan, Pakistan and northern India, by the tonne. 

How’s the AFP Police Commissioner trotting out that same old line blaming drug users for the gang shootings in Sydney? Now if everybody would stop using cocaine and meth all this violence would stop. I feel for the cops who are just going backwards in every way fighting this unwinnable drug war. Their morale is low and their numbers are down, understandably. We’re asking the impossible of the police. Time to start seriously questioning the drug war.
Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #724 | 10 SEPTEMBER 2026

If you’d like to donate to Nepal, Helen Simpson goes back and forth regularly, between working in the Nimbin Hospital. She’s a beauty and we trust she will spend any money donated wisely (see below).

There was a story in last week’s Headlines about how Albo promised $600 million to help Pacific nations stop international drug trafficking. I guess the profits are so massive even if only a percentage of the craft get through there’s still a fortune to be made. By the time it gets to Nimbin, after being cut any number of times, coke is $300 a gram. Every day there’s a gangland shooting in Sydney, fighting over the profits. 

Most of the coke is from Colombia and the meth from Mexico. The question is when does this end? They will never stop the illegal drug trade, they admit that, yet there is no discussion about ending the war creating it. How about we regulate these drugs with quality control and prescriptions through a doctor like they’ve done with cannabis?

NSW police have been at it again with their RAID, ‘Remove All Impaired Drivers’, last weekend. They conducted 6,420 drug tests with 774 positive. They don’t tell us how many were for cannabis but I bet the majority are and those people will most likely pay the $704 fine when it arrives in the mail, unaware it’s an admission of guilt and a week or two later they’ll get a letter saying they've lost their licence for three months. 

It’s sickening the way they keep saying these numbers represent “potential lives saved”. The same old propaganda cut and pasted over and over again. No wonder they’re struggling to get new recruits. Respect for the force is at an all time low and bad laws are a big part of it. Why do they refuse to accept presence does not mean impairment? Are they just bullies, or is this about money, like most things?

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #723 | 3 SEPTEMBER 2026
High Headliners!

I’m picking oranges every morning for juice and we just had a week of glorious sunshine, which makes heaven even more obvious. No doubt it’ll be hot soon enough and I read that it was the mildest winter in 150 years, so look out for a hot, hot summer. Speaking of climate change, Nepal changed my life fifty odd years ago.

It was the lifestyle of the people and their laughter. I’m six months out of the London stockbroker suit and wandering through the mountains out of Pokhara. I slept and ate with the locals in the villages and wondered at how happy these people were. The women would head off in the morning together, chatting and laughing to collect huge bundles of sticks they’d carry home on their backs.

The men worked together building or planting, or whatever, as they did everything themselves. The villages and countryside were beatifically maintained, with little whitewashed huts dotted amongst the gardens, it looked like paradise to me. Hashish was legal then and sold everywhere, cheap as chips, from plants growing wild alongside hillsides of rhododendrons. 

That was 1973, just before America and the UN pressured Nepal to make weed illegal, which totally disrupted their economy. I was in Nepal eight years ago and it was extremely hard to find hash. I was told by locals the King said it was bad and his word is gospel.

I love the story analysing the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics covering 20 million people between 1990 and 2025. In States that decriminalised mediweed (which only started in 1996 in California, remember) health related work absences dropped by about 7%. Health services saw a 32% drop, manual workers 39%. These are huge figures related to treating chronic pain, muscle conditions and mental stress. Interestingly, the largest absenteeism reductions, at 36%, were amongst the less educated and experienced.

Love to everyone!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #722 | 27 AUGUST 2026
High Headliners!
It was like the old days, protesting outside Parliament House in Brisbane on Tuesday about RDT. A great crowd of about a hundred people and lots of faces I haven't seen in years. True blue campaigners who’ve been at it for decades. Lots of women, mothers with children who were helped by weed. Life changing weed! Just imagine having a child with hundreds of seizures every day then with a tiny bit of cannabis they stop overnight. 

The fact that it took stopping epileptic children’s seizures to make the bastards accept that maybe it does have some medical value is disgusting. However, it shows how hard it is to change peoples minds and get them to actually question stuff and think for themselves. Not these mothers who risk their children being taken off them for using illegal plant medicine, they’re genuine heroes.

Former magistrate, David Heilpern, who spoke at the Rally is another hero. He had to quit his job because it literally sickened him having to repeatedly take away driving licences from innocent people for the mere presence of THC. He can’t believe the Queensland Government is now talking about jail for repeat drug driving offenders, and the proposed fines have skyrocketed to thousands of dollars that no poor people can ever pay.

The Australian Institute of Health and Welfare’s National Drug Strategy household survey found 3% of Australians had used cannabis for medical purposes in the last year, equating to about 700,000 people. You could safely treble that, I reckon. Not sure about you, but when I’m asked if I’m a criminal, I don’t really feel inclined to tick the yes box on that one.

Canada shipped 20 tonnes less weed to Oz last year, down to about 50. While Thailand went from one tonne to 21, a quarter of the total! Germany in comparison imported over 200 tonnes. We grew, in Oz, 55 tonnes of legal and exported seven. I just want to grow my own, and it still feels as far away as ever.

Good luck to Dr Craig Buchanan running in the Secret Harbour By-election in WA this weekend. He says pre-poll has been overrun by an orange tsunami!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #721 | 20 AUGUST 2026
I’ve been thinking about the story from New York in last week’s Headlines about the all-in-one permit that allows a small operator to cultivate, manufacture and sell weed at Farmers Markets and the like. “Small craft cannabis cultivators”, sounds like the dream to me.

In most of the world if you don’t work you don’t eat. Family becomes huge just to look after each other. Survival isn’t an issue here, there is always food somewhere. I can vouch for the skips behind the supermarkets in affluent Canberra. 

Wandering the planet showed me how little money has to do with happiness and how hard in fact it is to be rich, with so many choices like we have here. We would grow tired of rice and dahl every night, but for most, so long as the bowl is full, they are happy and grateful. Happier than us, generally, I think.

So I come back to cannabis and how many people would just love it if they could earn a living from growing their favourite vegetable, instead of letting Big Cannabis take over the market.

“Regulated cannabis has proven to be an economic engine for New York”, they’re saying and it could be the same here, I reckon. Thousands of Aussie tokers would love a small licence, say between 20-50 square metres, or even much smaller. It could just be your six home grown plants, but you could sell them at the market. 

Thousands of people would go off the dole or the pension. Thousands would love their job, many of whom have been learning it covertly for decades. Thousands would have a meaningful and purposeful life, which is not easy to find in this world right now. I'll keep dreaming.

Meanwhile it’s encouraging to read that global cannabis use is up forty percent as we follow, “a continuum of gradual normalisation towards cannabis use”. There’s hope for us yet!

Love to all!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #720 | 13 AUGUST 2026
High Headliners!
There have been some terrific speeches in Victoria’s parliament by our Legalise Cannabis MP’s in the last week or so. Tall David and Rachel are absolutely giving their all down there as the curtain draws closer on their term batting for us all. 

The rules changed there this week with the Government and Opposition voting out the Group Voting Tickets (GVTs), which pretty much spells the end of any chance of minor parties getting elected again in Victoria. It sounds like it will be Labor, Liberals, One Nation and Greens and no one else after 28 November. You need 16.7 % of the vote to get a spot in the Upper House, making it extremely hard, without a lot of backing.

Rachel and David had one shot left and called for a non binding plebiscite on legalising personal use, which in no time got voted down 27 to 8, despite their own parliamentary inquiry recommending it. Interestingly the polls in the papers are showing around 80% of people would support it, but the politicians clearly know better, they reckon!

I watched the debate in the New South Wales Legislative Council last week on the RDT Bill, which passed the Lower House. Jeremy has bent over backwards to try and get the smallest of changes, and it was extremely painful to watch one after another Coalition opponent use up their twenty minute time allocation, until there was no time for a vote. A filibuster it’s called! Now we wait for another month, before we can pick up the threads again, with not much time left in NSW before they shut down for the March 2027 Election.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #719 | 6 AUGUST 2026
High Headliners!
I’ve been on the road for the last week, just loving the natural Aussie bush, native trees with very few weeds. Anxious cannabis users driving around outback Queensland, tensing up every time we see a cop car, a cop shop. Where do we smoke a joint? In the middle of nowhere. We met a good country woman in an op shop who had the shakes, early Parkinson’s. “Have you thought about trying cannabis?”, I asked. “I hear it’s a problem driving”.

Shame on the bullies running the State... blindly doubling the punishment for drug driving offences in Queensland, including mandatory imprisonment for repeat offenders! A new war against cannabis users. Please spread the word about the 25 August RDT Protest at Parliament House in Brisbane (see details below). I’m looking for a lift so I don’t have to drive, like everyone else!

South of the border in New South Wales the new Bill to let medical cannabis patients drive passed the Legislative Assembly. The Bill now goes to the Upper House for debate. The Transport Minister assured parliament info they want from us will not link to automatic number plate recognition. One thing we importantly need is for anyone’s saliva who is tested to be given the results and interstate drivers with a prescription have an escape clause. Jeremy will be trying to pass amendments but the new system is a solid step forward. We’ll have to work on it when they review it. It will be a big relief to be able to drive knowing they can test me twice and I can have any amount of nanograms of pot in my saliva and not lose my licence. 

Sometimes I want to put a sign on the outskirts of the village… “Welcome to Nimbin—May contain traces of nuts”... We try hard to deal with any mental health episodes ourselves rather than call police so I was really happy to see the announcement NSW is getting a new statewide mental health emergency response model, which will see more appropriate people attending those incidents rather than police, unless they’re really necessary. It’s been shaped by the English, ‘Right Care Right Person’ Program, which makes good sense.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #718 | 30 JULY 2026
High Headliners!
I’m still so naive, I’m shocked by dishonesty. Prohibition has been good at teaching people to lie, but some just do it as part of their job, it seems. I mean, we all care about road safety I imagine, so why not be transparent about the saliva testing results, as we all try and work out if and how it can work? Why not be honest and open?

It is because they’re using road safety as an arm of the drug war, Dr Michael White from the University of Adelaide tells us. And there’s been nothing as effective as RDT in stopping cannabis use. Just the fact we’re not told our saliva test results is a problem for a start. If we were, it would quickly become apparent the results are all over the place and hold little relevance to safety on the roads. My saliva tested at 1200ng and the copper agreed I didn't look impaired, and I wasn’t.

Now I read how they did trials at Swinburne, five years ago and buried the results because they clearly showed how hopeless the spit tests are at detecting THC. The unpublished experiment involved 40 subjects who used their normal dose of THC medicine and were tested 1, 2, 4 and 6 hours after use. The non-detection rate was 40% after 1 hour; 65% after 2 hours: 70% after 4 hours and 77% after 6 hours. Police say they will, “inevitably catch cannabis use in drivers for up to 24 hours after use”. Bald-face lying they can justify, to themselves at least, because this is a war.

Drug use is not bad, we’ve just been told that. It’s actually awesome and important, if you do it right which is not so easy, with a war going on against you. It’s almost forgotten that it’s been a normal part of human behaviour forever until a hundred years ago, when the ‘Reefer Madness’ propaganda campaign began.

The truth will set us free, we just need to be open to it, in this fast changing, exciting and amazing time on Earth.

Love to everyone!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

【協賛企業紹介⑤】
JSFはたくさんの協賛企業様からご協賛をいただいております。
以下にて企業様をご紹介させていただきます。

・日研フード株式会社（五感で味わう青みかん）
捨てられてしまう「青みかん」をアップサイクルし、独自技術で原料化。おいしく飲めて体に良い粉末飲料として提供しています。当日は青みかんドリンクの試飲ブースと、青みかん香るサウナを出展します。

・フォージバンド株式会社
人事・組織コンサルティングとSES事業を展開。採用・育成・定着や組織づくりなど、企業ごとに異なる人事・組織課題の解決を支援しています。

・株式会社グレイスヴィジョン

川崎市高津区にあるデジタルサイネージ会社。サイネージ選びから施工、コンテンツ制作、導入後のメンテナンスまでワンストップでサポート。可動式LEDサイネージのレンタルも行っています。

・ひかり味噌株式会社
@hikarimiso 
1936年創業、長野県発の味噌メーカー。「自然の恵み、いただきます。」をコンセプトに、無添加味噌やオーガニック味噌、即席みそ汁、スープ、塩こうじ、甘酒などを展開。当日は甘酒「晴れのち糀」のサンプリング出店を行います。

・株式会社Kooga（SAUNA NAYA）
@sauna_naya 
茨城県古河市を拠点に、映像・写真制作、SNS運用、Web制作、イベント企画運営などを手がけるクリエイティブカンパニー。「JAPAN TEA EXPO」の企画運営やサウナ施設「SAUNA NAYA」も運営しています。当日は世界一に選ばれたお茶サウナ「SAUNA NAYA」を出展します。

・BUGGY STORY（バギーストーリー）
@buggystory 
千葉・勝浦の森と海を舞台に、絵本の主人公になって冒険するアトラクション型サウナ「BUGGY STORY」。森でハーブを摘み、香りを楽しむサウナや、バギーで森を駆け抜けて海へ向かう体験など、物語とリアルを融合したネイチャーファンタジー体験を提供します。当日はコラボテントサウナの出展に加え、物語の絵本も紹介します。

Entre máquinas inestables, dibujos microscópicos y personajes que rozan lo absurdo, Ricardo Lanzarini reconstruye aquí el hilo vital de su obra. La entrevista recorre los núcleos conceptuales de su exposición y libro "Electrocardiograma escultórico", y se abre a un relato donde la ironía y la experimentación, la escucha atenta de los espacios y un imaginario tan íntimo como indócil sostienen una práctica en permanente transformación.

Amid unstable machines, microscopic drawings, and characters that verge on the absurd, Ricardo Lanzarini traces the vital thread of his practice. The interview follows the conceptual cores of his exhibition and book “Sculptural Electrocardiogram”, opening onto a narrative where irony and experimentation, an attentive listening to space, and an imagination as intimate as it is unruly sustain a practice in constant transformation.

A edição mais especial de sempre já está no ar. Os bilhetes também!

Depois de meses de preparação, chegou finalmente o momento de revelar a programação da #15.ª edição do Portuguese Surf Film Festival.

De 17 a 31 de julho, a Ericeira volta a receber o melhor cinema de surf do mundo, com 34 filmes que nos levam dos maiores palcos do surf a comunidades remotas, de histórias de superação a aventuras inesquecíveis, da conservação dos oceanos à cultura que une surfistas em todos os continentes.

São quinze anos de histórias, encontros, emoções e inspiração. Quinze anos a celebrar o surf através do cinema.

Agora é a tua vez de fazer parte desta edição.

Still taking in what it meant to be part of the @savethewavescoalition Film Festival in Ericeira✨

Having our film screened at an event of this caliber, and seeing our short film travel around the world, means so much to me. Not only because of the incredible films and names we had the privilege of standing alongside, but especially because of everything Save The Waves stands for and the work they do to protect our oceans and coastlines.

Sitting there in Ericeira, I found myself thinking back to when I first started filming on the beach in Jacó, Costa Rica. Just a camera, the ocean, and a passion for telling stories.

Many thanks to @save_azores_waves for giving us the opportunity to share this video with the world.

A big thank you to @miguelbaratadealmeida and the whole team for putting together such a special event, and for the opportunity to present our film and share the stage with @_miguelblanco_ 

It was also so good to see some unexpected familiar faces, to watch our film on a screen in a place like this, and to see how passion projects and genuine stories can bring people together.

And above all, thank you @peterhealion. For opening the doors of your home to me, for sharing your story, and for believing in this idea from the very beginning.

Grateful for every part of the journey 🌊

latestPosts.caption:
Este não foi o meu primeiro ano como criativa no Portuguese Surf Film Festival (já ando por aqui desde 2020), mas esta edição foi particularmente especial: 15 anos de Festival!

Comecei por pensar num conceito que ligasse os 15 anos à Ericeira e ao surf: uma linha, a linha que conta os anos de histórias. E a partir dessa linha fui construindo toda a identidade visual desta edição.

Azul, vermelho, ondas, cinema, Ericeira.
Uma identidade que acabou por sair do papel e ocupar a Casa da Cultura, o festival e toda a comunicação.

E claro… não coloquei aqui tudo, senão tínhamos um Reel de 10 minutos. 😂

Ficaram de fora a identidade da Ocean Art, todo o merchandising, todas as peças digitais, social media, materiais de comunicação… enfim, muita coisa.

Também não consegui filmar toda a equipa e todo o processo (desculpem lá, não dá para estar sempre com o telemóvel na mão).

Mas não podia deixar de falar da minha enorme admiração pela @susana.metzger e pela @fezandavalli , as principais responsáveis por tornar este magnífico evento possível. É um privilégio fazer parte disto.

Um enorme obrigada à @camara_municipal_mafra pelo apoio, à @imagemplana pelo profissionalismo na montagem de toda a decoração do espaço, em tão pouco tempo (vocês são os maiores) e a todos os parceiros e patrocinadores que fizeram parte desta edição.

E obrigada ao Surf Film por me deixar continuar a contar estas histórias, à minha maneira. 

See you next year!

#graphicdesign #designer #ericeira #surffilmfestival #design

いよいよ明日から始まります。
ご来場前に、以下の通りいくつかの注意事項とお願いがあります。

●ステージの動画撮影禁止
スマートフォンを高く掲げて動画を撮影する行為は、イベントそのものや周囲の人々に対して非常に迷惑です。特に夜間は、明るいスマートフォンの画面が周囲の雰囲気を台無しにしてしまいます。見かけた場合は主催者やスタッフ、セキュリティから制止させて頂きます。

●駐車券
車で来場される方は、必ずZAIKOで駐車券を購入してください。当日、現金で駐車券を購入することはできません。まだ購入していない方は、是非本日中に購入してください。

●受付場所
すべての来場者のチェックインは、宝台樹スキー場の駐車場で行います。Google Mapやカーナビで目的地を設定する際は「群馬みなかみほうだいぎスキー場」を指定してください。キャンプ場へ直接車で向かわないよう、お願いいたします。また、受付後、オートキャンプ、場内駐車場のお客様はシャトルバスの専用ルートを通れないため迂回して会場に向かって頂きます。

●会場内でのお支払い
ダンスフロアにあるメインバーではキャッシュレス決済が利用できますが、フードマーケットでは現金が必要になる店舗もございます。必ず現金もご用意ください。

●天候・防寒対策
天気予報では素晴らしい晴天が見込まれていますが、夜間はかなり冷え込むことがあります。暖かい服装を必ずご用意ください。

●ゴミ・キャンプチェア
夜間、ゴミやキャンプチェアを会場内に放置しないでください。翌日も気持ちよくイベントをスタートできるよう、各自で自分のスペースをきれいに片付けましょう。

〜最後に〜
いよいよ、皆さんと一緒に過ごせる特別な週末がやってきました！ お会いできることを、心から楽しみにしています。

—

A few notes before you arrive:

* NO VIDEO OF THE STAGE. NO PHONES UP IN THE AIR. Holding a bright phone up in the air to take video is obnoxious and disrespectful towards the event and everyone around you, especially at night. Every person on the dancefloor behind you is forced to look at your device, but nobody wants to look at your phone. We have zero patience for this kind of space and light pollution and will ask you to stop immediately. 

 * Everyone coming by car needs to buy a parking ticket at Zaiko. We don’t accept cash on the day for parking tickets. 

* All check-ins take place at the ski resort parking lot. When setting your destination in your car navigation system, select “Gunma Minakami Hodaigi Ski Resort.” Do not attempt to drive into the campground directly. If you are at the autocamp site or the on-site parking lot, you cannot follow the shuttle bus’s designated route and will need to take the detour.

* The main bar accepts digital payments but bring cash for the food market. 

* The weather is absolutely brilliant sun, but such clear skies during the day can lead to cold nights. Be prepared with warm clothes (fleece, jacket, etc).

* Please do not leave trash or camping chairs on the floor at night. Clean up your space so we can begin the next day with a clean space.

We look forward to seeing all of you again. Our weekend together has arrived and the gods appear to be smiling.

この夏、東京では8月27日から10月2日まで、37日連続で雨が続き、観測市場最長だっだようです。
そして今週の天気予報は晴れ続き！ようやく光が戻って来ました。
今年のフライヤーのイメージのような色鮮やかな3日間になりそうです。
ただし、ご存じのように山の天気は変わりやすく、何が起こるかわかりません。
また会場は標高約1000mで夜は冷え込みます。
備えあれば憂いなし。防寒対策、雨対策、十分にお忘れなく。
それでは今週末、宝台樹の美しい森でお会いしましょう！

—

Tokyo saw an insane record-breaking streak of 37 consecutive days of rain this summer, from August 27 to October 2.

Now it’s time to see the light.

The weather forecast looks gorgeous with sunny days all week! This should be a brilliant Labyrinth—like the flyer design.

But keep in mind things can always change up in the mountains so please come prepared and be sure to bring warm clothes at night: layers, fleece, and jacket. Hodaigi is 1000 meters and it can get cold at night up there in October.

And bring sunglasses and a hat:)

Southern Cross University is a founding partner of Byron Writers Festival and their support has been integral to the success of the festival for 25 years. Together we have a shared passion for deep thinking and conversations about how we can create a better tomorrow.  Enjoy this wonderful video from Byron Writers Festival 2022  that captures our special partnership. 

@southerncrossuni

Tune into @booktopiabooks podcast ‘Tell me what to Read’ featuring our very own Artistic Director Zoe Pollock and Byron Writers Festival 2022 guest @hannahkentwrites, who together share their top picks for this year’s festival. #byronwf2022 #radicalhope

*LAST CHANCE TO BOOK* Our 'Writing Family' online workshop with Sara El Sayed kicks off next Wednesday.

We all have a story to tell when it comes to the family we know. But how can we pen a story of our own family in a way that is both ethical and compelling? What story should, or can, we tell? And what can we learn from writers who have attempted to capture their families on the page?

This two-part online workshop will guide participants through planning, researching and writing family stories.

Book now via workshops link in bio ✍️

Mick Fanning was met with a sold-out crowd at Lennox Head Cultural Centre last Wednesday as he shared his memoir All Heart.⁠
⁠
From local surf groms to literary lovers, the audience was treated with plenty of laughs, personal anecdotes, and a few tears too. ⁠
⁠
Mick was joined in conversation with Turia Pitt, divulging what life as a one of Australia's best-loved pro-surfers is really like.⁠
⁠
Mick Fanning's tell-all memoir All Heart is now available everywhere.

Credit @youllseephotography

Leading expert and US and Australian politics insider Bruce Wolpe reveals the many ways in which Australia has already been damaged by Donald Trump.⁠
⁠
Seeping into Australia from above and below, Trumpism has contaminated public debate, emboldened local political and religious extremists, diminished Australia's economy and international relations—and much more.⁠
⁠
Join Bruce Wolpe in conversation with David Heilpern on Wednesday 28 October at Brunswick Picture House from 6.00pm.⁠
⁠
Tickets are on sale now at byronwritersfestival.com

Listen in to Big Ideas on ABC Radio National with Natasha Mitchell at 8pm this evening to hear the Art & AI session from this year's Byron Writers Festival!⁠
⁠
Featuring authors Steve Toltz, Evelyn Araluen and Kirra Pendergast, hosted by Natasha Mitchell, this conversation traverses all things creativity and staying human in a world ruled by AI.⁠
⁠
Listen in via radio, or stream using the ABC Listen app.

Last chance to see Mick Fanning in conversation with Turia Pitt tomorrow night!⁠
⁠
Join three time world champion surfer Mick Fanning as he brings his tell-all memoir All Heart to the Lennox Cultural Centre tomorrow evening.⁠
⁠
Final tickets available at byronwritersfestival.com

Last chance to get tickets for Kate Grenville in conversation tonight at A&I Hall in Bangalow!⁠
⁠
Grenville will be joined by Mick O'Regan to discuss her latest book The Country School Master: A Mystery in 88 Letters ⁠
⁠
Get your tickets now at byronwriterfestival.com

Next week join three-time surfing World Champion Mick Fanning in Lennox Head for the launch of his memoir All Heart.⁠
⁠
All Heart is about growing up in a loud, loving family. It’s about chasing a dream and experiencing the highest of highs. It’s about being broken into pieces by unimaginable loss; about three brothers and a father dying too soon. It’s about doing whatever it takes, and learning whatever you can, to find your way again. ⁠
‍⁠
Mick will be in conversation with bestselling author and athlete Turia Pitt.⁠
⁠
Bar and food (Pocket Curries) available from 5pm. ⁠
⁠
Books will be available for purchase and signing at the event thanks to The Book Room.⁠
⁠
🗓️ Wednesday 14 October, 6:30pm⁠
📍 Lennox Head Cultural Centre⁠
🎟️ Tickets selling fast! Book now at byronwritersfestival.com

Final call! Make 2026 the year you wrote your novel.⁠
⁠
Join Miles Franklin Award-winning author Sofie Laguna for an eight-week novel masterclass starting this Saturday. This series is presented online, so you can participate from wherever you are in the world.⁠
⁠
Through discussion, writing exercises and text-analysis, Sofie will guide you in novel-writing through the lens of a character’s voice. Immersion in voice is liberating, rewarding — and will help you complete your story.⁠
⁠
Sofie Laguna’s Novel-Writing Masterclass starts Saturday 10 October via Zoom.⁠
⁠
Full details and booking info at byronwritersfestival.com

Join Pip Williams, bestselling author of global phenomenon The Dictionary of Lost Words and The Bookbinder of Jericho, in conversation with Naima Brown about her highly anticipated new book The German Ward. ⁠
⁠
The German Ward is the love story of the year: love between enemies behind the lines of WWI, and the Australian artist who captures their secret.⁠
⁠
Pip will be signing books, thanks to our friends at The Book Room.⁠
⁠
Thursday 8 October.

An evening with Kate Grenville in Bangalow this October.⁠
⁠
Join the author of The Secret River and Unsettled as she brings her latest novel to the Northern Rivers.⁠
⁠
Kate Grenville is one of Australia's most celebrated writers, and will be joined in conversation with Mick O'Regan.⁠
⁠
Tickets are now on sale at byronwritersfestival.com

Claudia Heredia es la creadora detrás del proyecto Para un roto y un descosido, una firma dedicada a la belleza del diseño natural y la decoración botánica. 
En esta edición de BROCANTE, impartirá el taller práctico “Crea tu centro con flores preservadas”. En esta experiencia de desconexión, diseñada para crear sin prisas y sin necesidad de experiencia previa, los participantes aprenderán a mirar el arte floral desde una nueva perspectiva. 
A través del juego con diferentes volúmenes, texturas y tonalidades, cada asistente descubrirá cómo conectar con la materia vegetal y plasmar su huella personal en el diseño, llevándose a casa un centro floral único, duradero y lleno de vida listo para conservar.
El taller es gratuito, pero se paga un pequeño importe de 15€ para cubrir los materiales.
📅 Fechas: 17 y 18 de octubre
📍 Lugar: Brocante by Mercado de Motores (Museo del Ferrocarril)
🔗 Descubre su trabajo: @paraunrotoyundescosido

𝗟𝗜𝗦𝗕𝗢𝗡 𝗗𝗘𝗦𝗜𝗚𝗡 𝗪𝗘𝗘𝗞 𝗥𝗘𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗡𝗦  𝗜 𝟭𝟵–𝟮𝟲 𝗠𝗔𝗬 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟳 – 𝗦𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲

Over the past four editions, Lisbon Design Week has grown from an ambitious idea into an internationally recognised platform celebrating Portuguese design, craftsmanship and contemporary creativity.

In 2027, we celebrate our 𝟱𝘁𝗵 𝗮𝗻𝗻𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗮𝗿𝘆, an important milestone and the beginning of a new chapter for LDW.

For this special edition, we are preparing an ambitious programme of exhibitions, commissions, encounters and collaborations across Lisbon, bringing together the creative community that has shaped LDW while welcoming new voices, opening fresh conversations, fostering connections between Portuguese and international designers and bringing different perspectives for the future. An opportunity to think bigger!

𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗔𝗳𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗛𝗼𝘂𝗿𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗼𝗻 𝗮𝘁 @hamrei’s. An evening of conversations, music, food, and good company, surrounded by Hamrei’s work and the atmosphere of his studio.

After Hours has always been about creating a space for honest conversations, new connections and the exchange of ideas. Bringing together people who are building, questioning, experimenting and shaping Lisbon’s creative community of emerging talent.

For our final gathering of the last season, we came together at @dam.lisbon, @hamrei’s studio, just before the opening of LDW26. A nice way to close a season filled with inspiring people, thoughtful conversations, and plenty of good energy.

A big thank you to @dam.lisbon and @hamrei for hosting us and opening the studio to the After Hours community.

Maybe evolution isn’t always about becoming something new.
Sometimes it’s about remembering how to be together.

To move together.
To breathe together.
To dance with people who were strangers yesterday and somehow don’t feel like strangers anymore.

That’s what stayed with me from this year’s Yoga del Mar Spirit Festival.

My second year here, reconnecting with beautiful people from last year, meeting new souls and artists, and experiencing again something quite rare: there is almost no line between artist and attendee.

We practice together, eat together, dance together, celebrate together. Everyone becomes part of the experience.

And maybe that is its own kind of evolution, when the individual becomes part of something collective, without losing who they are.

Very grateful for the music, the movement, the conversations, the familiar faces and the new ones.

But mostly, for the human connection behind all of it.

Thank you, Yoga del Mar family. 🤍
Until next time.

Thank you @yogadelmarspiritfestival for having me and capturing these beautiful moments. It was an honor to open the festival space…we began the weekend with a lunar eclipse and full moon in pisces with the theme: our dreams need a regulated body to land into. This is where we use a deep journey into sound to harmonize our biology and be receptive to the frequency and altitude of our highest selves. Pisces is the poet of the cosmos…a weekend where the stars remind us to step into the knowing of our inner eye and remember that collectively, we have no boundaries. We are one! Where instead of escaping into our dreams, we become enchanted by them and become the river to rush them into reality. 

We practice together so that our body, our container, is strong, rested and aligned to receive all of the magic and blessings that are continually on their way to us ✨🙏🏻 With this, the mantra that kept returning was one to cultivate our discernment between the real and the unreal … asatoma sad gamaya. 

If you’ve made it this far in my caption in the vast instagram world (hi, welcome, I am so glad you are here!), I invite you to close your eyes and chant this beautiful Pavamana Mantra. Chant when you are at a threshold, when you may be standing between what’s real and what’s illusion, when you may be beginning something new and when you may need to find your way back to clarity.

Om Asato Ma Sadgamaya
Tamaso Ma Jyotirgamaya
Mrityorma Amritam Gamaya
Om Shaanti, Shaanti, Shaanti
✨
Lead me from the unreal to the real
Move from illusion and untruth to eternal truth.
Lead me from darkness to light
Move from the ignorance of darkness to the light of wisdom.
Lead me from death to immortality
Move from mortal fear to the realization of the immortal self.
Om peace, peace, peace
Invoke ultimate peace within, around, and beyond.

Thank you to @meinlsonicenergy for the healing tools to create this experience for our community!

Hello BBSF community,
I hope you’re all well out there and getting some
waves in between all the other life happenings. Myself and the team want to share with you the news that unfortunately we won’t be holding the Byron Bay Surf Festival in 2025. This was a tough decision to make. We are currently in the midst of a creative reset including new ideas, direction, and staff. All of this needs a little extra time & space to be executed as best and as smooth as possible. I’m now in my 15th year as Founder and Creative Director of BBSF, and while I’m not going anywhere, I am super stoked to be welcoming on an epic new team for the August 2026 Festival. Together, we’ve started planting some new seeds for next year with our same strong focus on community, creativity, environmental initiatives, and of course all of the awesome and cool things in surf culture that are at the core of BBSF, including some brand new jazzy events, resurfacing some older ones, and a coupla bigger exciting things into the future…Stay tuned and updated via our IG page here or subscribe for news, views and tubes via link in bio 

Thankyou for riding long and high with us ✌🏽

See you all in there & out there, 
James

SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS…In 2024 BBSF made huge progress towards reducing our carbon footprint (using less of everything…energy, fuel, waste etc) to produce the festival. In comparison to 2023 our total emissions dropped by 63%, from 26.89 tons to 9.996 tons. Major reductions were seen in accommodation (van life, camping, accomm pooling..?) and transport (more crew walking/biking) with accommodation emissions cut by 64% and transport emissions reduced by 68%. Waste and water use also decreased sharply too. These changes reflect our commitment to sustainable business, and also the communities effort to lower their environmental impact. Basically this all equates to a decrease of around 33% of emissions per person that attended. So ThankYOU all and Thankyou @ecovantage for all stats and info 
👌🏽🌎
.
BBSF is the first Surf Event In Australia to be certified Carbon Neutral. We hope this psyches others to aim for same

latestPosts.caption:
We’re incredibly proud to present the results from the 35th Noosa Festival of Surfing 🚀✨

From local jobs and businesses to visitors travelling from around the world, this event keeps growing in all the right ways.

• $6M+ into the local economy 
• 39,000+ of you showing up (11% increase from last year)
• 50+ events, packed across 10 days 

Thanks to everyone who’s part of it — competitors, locals, partners, crew, photographers, videographers, local stores, spectators and everyone in between. 

We can’t wait to do it all again next year ☀️🕺

A HUGE shoutout to everyone who made the 35th Noosa Festival of Surfing what it was! It was an incredible 10 days of world class surfing, insane entertainment thanks to @brixtonanz, dog surfing, sponsor activations, @gageroadsbrewco beers and everything in between ☀️ 

We welcomed hundreds of competitors, from 8-80, with a large percentage of them from overseas, to share Noosa’s iconic right hand point break. We crowned winners, saw an incredibly talented calibre of surfers including pooches, and we danced all night long at the famous Beach Bar 🕺🪩

We can’t wait to do it all again next year! Mark your calendars 🗓️ 26 FEB - 7 MARCH 2027!! 

A massive shoutout to our awesome content team that somehow gets better and better every year:

🎥 @pangaproductions @physicalglobe 
📸 @melissahphoto @davidbowdler @framedbyerin @juliedelmarphoto @martinlills @sacha_canonier @unatalpenelope 
📲 and @brandid.media for pulling it all together!

If you didn’t witness the insane lineup of entertainment brought to you by @brixtonanz this March at the Beach Bar, you would’ve had a serious case of fomo… 

📸 @melissahphoto @sacha_canonier @unatalpenelope

Not every surf event feels like this.

For ten days each year, Noosa slows things down a little. Longboards glide across the points, music drifts up the beach and the line between competition and good times gets pleasantly blurry.

The Noosa Festival of Surfing has built a reputation around style, flow and community  where world champs, first-timers and everyone in between somehow end up sharing the same lineup.

Less pressure. Less noise.

From beach bars and live music to Old Mal divisions, nose riding and late-afternoon hangs on the sand, this one feels bigger than a surf comp.

Read the full feature in Roam Aus Magazine.

#roamausmagazine #surfculture #noosafestivalofsurfing

The @goldenbreedsurf Noserider Invitational brought together the worlds best noseriders to Noosa’s First Point to go head to head (or nose to nose) for the title 🏆

We even saw the father and son duo @jive and @surfcreativearmy have a little bet happening with Josh taking out the win
Who will we see in this division next year? 👀

🎥 @physicalglobe @pangaproductions 📸 @sacha_canonier @melissahphoto

The Art of Trim Old Mal division is one of the most iconic divisions of the festival.

With a Mixed and Masters division, we see a wide variety of old school board collections on show at First Point. This year, we saw @thewaxhead himself, take out the win riding a 1966 Jackson - made by Bobby Brown

Check out the recent feature of Matt in @pacificlongboardermagazine and a couple more in the works 👀

📸 @melissahphoto @martinlills @juliedelmarphoto

feeling very blessed for all the support from the last event, we honestly couldn’t do it without you all 🫶🏼

I can’t wait to share what we’ve got planned next for you guys! 

my full set from vol. 3 is now live on soundcloud (including some unreleased stuff) 👀 

hope you enjoy <3

link in bio 😈

Shoutout to the legends at @shadforthcivil for keeping our festival team and judges protected against the elements all festival long.

From make shift esky-chairs, to live stream set ups by @pangaproductions, insane drone angles with @physicalglobe, absolute legends doing everything behind the scenes, guest appearances on the commentating booth and knock off beers, it was all happening in the Judges Tower, thanks to @shadforthcivil 

📸 @melissahphoto @framedbyerin @juliedelmanrphoto

The first ever Noosa Night Glide went off with a bang ⚡️ 

Should we do night surfing again?

📸 @juliedelmarphoto

Single Fin moments @ Australias only Beach Bar thanks to @gageroadsbrewco 🍻

As soon as it hits 12pm every day during the Noosa Festival of Surfing, punters line up at the gates of the Beach Bar, waiting to order that first bevvy, enjoy the uninterrupted views of the action and kick off the dance floor 🕺

Are we going to turn it up a notch next year?… absolutely

latestPosts.caption:
The walls are waiting. 

Expressions of interest for artists are officially open for the 2027 Benalla Street Art Festival.

We are seeking submissions from artists around Australia (and the world!)

Link in bio!

Take a close look at Vero Coya's mural and you'll find the rhythms of the natural world woven into every element.

Vero Coya | Interwoven
📍5-9 Bridge Street East, Benalla, rear wall

Vero Coya’s mural creates a powerful dialogue between the organic world and the built environment, scaling microscopic rhythms of sun and rain into a striking, wall‑sized meditation on connection. By dissolving the boundary between individual and ecosystem, she invites viewers to see themselves as active threads within a larger, interwoven whole. Through rich texture and flowing forms, the work becomes a call for stewardship - a reminder that we are inseparable from the cycles that sustain us, and responsible for the future we help shape.

Read more: https://benallastreetartfestival.com.au/walls/vero-coya/

Benalla, See the art in everything.

📅 Save the Date: Benalla Street Art Festival 2027 | 2-4 April 2027 | Benalla, Victoria

Photos credit: James Bugg

Hand-painted lines, a trade skill, and a simple message: be kind.

Mattie Davo | Be Kind, It's Gangster
📍87 Nunn Street, Benalla (Laneway through to Denny Street Carpark)

Mattie Davo brings his signwriting craft to the festival with a mural that bridges trade skill and fine art, proving that precision and personality can coexist. Every hand‑painted line carries the heritage of his practice, transforming a functional surface into a bold visual statement. Anchored by the ironic phrase Be Kind, its Gangster , the work plays with cultural expectations, suggesting that choosing kindness is the most rebellious act of all. It’s a powerful reminder of the authority and authenticity found in work shaped by the human hand.

Read more: https://benallastreetartfestival.com.au/walls/mattie-davo/

Benalla, See the art in everything.

📅 Save the Date: Benalla Street Art Festival 2027 | 2-4 April 2027 | Benalla, Victoria

Photos credit: James Bugg

When art becomes a bridge between generations, something deadly happens. 

Anganya Artists and Uncle Chris Thorne
📍Tomorrow Today Foundation 66 Nunn Street, Benalla

Uncle Chris Thorne is a Benalla-region Aboriginal artist whose work tells Dreamtime stories passed down by his Elders. Since 2024, he has mentored young Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students through Tomorrow Today Foundations's Anganya program, and this mural brought that relationship to life.

Read more: https://benallastreetartfestival.com.au/walls/anganya-artists-and-uncle-chris-thorne/

Benalla, See the art in everything.

📅 Save the Date: Benalla Street Art Festival 2027 | 2-4 April 2027 | Benalla, Victoria

 Photos credit: James Bugg

Western Australian roots, Victorian landscape, and a burst of colour that stops you mid-step.

Sarsar | Field Notes
📍107 Bridge Street East, Benalla

Sarah McCloskey (SARSAR) shifts from her intricate realism to a bolder, more painterly approach for her mural, Field Notes, using the textured brick surface as a space for experimentation. Framed like an open sketchbook, the work features Eucalyptus preissiana and Hakea laurina - native species that connect her Western Australian roots to the Victorian landscape. With an amplified colour palette and a radiant neon orange backdrop, she transforms a quiet side street into a vibrant moment of discovery, inviting passersby to pause and appreciate the often‑overlooked beauty of their own local flora.

Read more: https://benallastreetartfestival.com.au/walls/sarsar/

Benalla, See the art in everything.

📅 Save the Date: Benalla Street Art Festival 2027 | 2-4 April 2027 | Benalla, Victoria

Photos credit: James Bugg

Krimsone has taken something personal and made it universal.

Krimsone | Peaches
📍37-41 Bridge Street East, Benalla

Krimsone’s mural explores the inner landscape of anxiety through a deeply personal lens, using fellow artist Peaches as the central subject. By grounding abstraction in a familiar face, he makes the intangible weight of nervous tension physically visible. The quiet intensity of Peaches’ gaze anchors the work, revealing vulnerability through Krimsone’s signature colour and form. It’s a raw, empathetic study of human connection, turning private struggle into a shared moment of honesty.

Read more: https://benallastreetartfestival.com.au/walls/krimsone/

Benalla, See the art in everything.

📅 Save the Date: Benalla Street Art Festival 2027 | 2-4 April 2027 | Benalla, Victoria

Photos credit: James Bugg

Discover art that carries generations of story, strength, and memory.

MadWings | unnamned artwork
📍103-105 Bridge Street East, Benalla 

MadWings - the creative partnership of Maddison Gibbs (Barkindji) and Jason Wing (Biripi/Cantonese) - brings a powerful fusion of ancestral memory and contemporary activism to Benalla. Their mural transforms public space into a platform for First Nations storytelling, cultural visibility and social justice. By blending Wing’s street‑art and political practice with Gibbs’ intuitive, intergenerational narratives, the duo creates work that reshapes the landscape and amplifies community strength.

Read more: https://benallastreetartfestival.com.au/walls/madwings/

Benalla, See the art in everything.

📅 Save the Date: Benalla Street Art Festival 2027 | 2-4 April 2027 | Benalla, Victoria

Photos credit: James Bugg

Dreamlike and deeply personal, Kitsune Jolene's work stops you in your tracks.

Kitsune Jolene | unnamed artwork
📍The Shed, 126-128 Bridge Street East Benalla

Kitsune Jolene brings her bold, emotive colour palettes and flowing compositions to Benalla, creating a dreamlike mural that explores transformation, intimacy and human connection. Her work invites quiet reflection while holding a strong presence in public space, blending surreal figurative forms with a deep care for mental health and the natural world. Through this piece, she encourages viewers to pause, feel and reconnect with the landscapes and inner worlds that shape us.

Read more: https://benallastreetartfestival.com.au/walls/kitsune-jolene/

Benalla, See the art in everything.

📅 Save the Date: Benalla Street Art Festival 2027 | 2-4 April 2027 | Benalla, Victoria

Photos credit: James Bugg

Across 84 square metres of brick, Juzpop captured intimate human emotion you can feel from the street.

Juzpop | Open your eyes
📍44 Bridge Street East, Benalla (Laneway through to Fawckner Drive)

JUZPOP’s mural stretches across 6×14 metres, pushing the boundaries of scale and intimacy through her signature double‑exposure technique. By merging the likeness of the MSWIM vocalist with the shifting intensity of the sky, she creates a single emotive landscape that moves from darkness toward light. The collision of textures and narratives brings raw vulnerability to the surface, transforming photographic process into paint to articulate profound human emotion.etched across an entire wall. Intimate and infinite at once.

Read more: https://benallastreetartfestival.com.au/walls/juzpop/

Benalla, See the art in everything.

📅 Save the Date: Benalla Street Art Festival 2027 | 2-4 April 2027 | Benalla, Victoria

Photos credit: James Bugg

Flowers, gold stars, and a sharp sense of humour, all at a an epic scale.

Jasmine Crisp | Tell me I'm pretty, tell me I'm good.
📍22 Carrier Street, Benalla

Jasmine Crisp’s mural, Tell me I’m pretty, tell me I’m good , delivers a witty critique of decorative public art, pairing lush floral imagery with a cascade of gold stars to parody our hunger for validation. Beneath the humour sits a celebration of her love for painting shiny things and the quiet joy she finds in nature. Created at a massive scale under a tight deadline, the work showcases her technical rigour and determination, transforming a challenging wall into a bold, self‑aware statement about beauty, originality and artistic confidence.

Close your eyes and you can almost feel the cool water on your skin.

Gus Eagleton | In Your Backyard
📍 19 Bridge Street East, Benalla, rear carpark

Brisbane artist Gus Eagleton brings a moment of quiet immersion to Benalla, drawing on the shimmering light and stillness of one of his favourite local swimming holes. His masterful handling of reflection transforms shifting sunlight into something vivid and tangible, transporting viewers straight to the water’s edge. The result is a sensory experience that blurs memory and presence, inviting the audience to feel the warmth, calm and gentle movement of the landscape as if they were standing there themselves.

Who knew a level crossing signal could inspire so much creativity?

Mur0ne | New Scenario
📍 31 Carrier Street, Benalla

Iker Muro’s mural draws inspiration from the level crossing signals he first noticed on the outskirts of Benalla, transforming their bold red‑and‑white stripes into striking geometric forms that echo the regional landscape. His energetic broom‑swept squiggles bring movement and contrast, grounding the structured poles in a more tactile, expressive gesture. By pairing these site‑specific elements with spontaneous mark‑making, Muro elevates everyday infrastructure into a fresh visual dialogue that encourages viewers to rediscover the hidden beauty in the objects we pass by each day.

SPEND FOUR HOURS UP CLOSE AND PERSONAL WITH BENJAMIN LAW AT THE BLUE MOUNTAINS SAUNA
If you’ve ever wanted to know more about the craft and economics of writing, Benjamin – who has written books, journalism, stage plays, TV screenplays, columns, documentaries and essays for over 20 years – is here to help, by answering all your questions in this no-holds barred, minimal-clothing* workshop at Blue Mountains Sauna!,

*Don’t worry: we’re not going all-out Scandinavian and naked, so bring your favourite swimsuit!

BOOK HERE: www.bluemountainswritersfestival.com.au/workshops/benjamin-law-workshop 

Participants will share a two-hour sauna session with Benjamin, where he’ll answer every question imaginable, in an environment conducive to openness and honesty. What makes for a good interview? How do you handle rejection? What does a good daily writing practice look like? How do you get an agent? How do I finish this damn manuscript? 

You'll have exclusive access to both saunas, including the Savu, the Southern Hemisphere's first public wood-fired smoke sauna, along with two cold plunges and three fireside rest areas. You’ll draw inspiration from a guided Aufguss with a trained Sauna Masters. Water infused with organic essential oils is poured over the stones, and the steam is moved through the room with choreographed towel work, set to music. It is immersive, physical and deeply grounding, and it is best experienced exactly as sauna is meant to be: together.

Then, after a short break, you’ll enter a relaxing workshop space, where you’ll use the experience of the sauna to inspire your work, participating in writing exercises and reflection under Benjamin’s guidance.

Blue Mountains Sauna opened in Leura in 2022 as Australia's first dedicated European-style public sauna, and has been championing authentic sauna culture ever since, performing Australia's first public Aufguss in 2023.

BOOK HERE: www.bluemountainswritersfestival.com.au/workshops/benjamin-law-workshop

latestPosts.caption:
Summer is coming. The countdown is on.

This December, more than 80 projects by nearly 100 artists from 35 countries will be in Melbourne for one incredible free exhibition.

NGV Triennial opens 13 December – 11 April 2027.

Click the link in our bio to discover the artists and plan your visit.

Kawita Vatanajyankur, Lady Papaya, 2023 (still) © Courtesy the artist and Nova Contemporary @kawitavv

#NGV #NGVTriennial #NGVTriennial2026

Passage: The Art of Atong Atem opens this month at NGV Australia.

This first-ever major solo exhibition of celebrated South Sudanese contemporary artist presents more than 65 works from her career to date, telling stories of culture and resilience, memory and imagination.

See world-premiere works alongside @atongatem’s richly layered and vibrant self-portraits that connect beauty and design with a lineage of African studio photography, feminist aesthetics and diasporic narratives.

Passage: The Art of Atong Atem opens 30 October 2026 – 14 June 2027 at The Ian Potter Centre: NGV Australia, @fed.square – free.

The sweet smell of spring is in the air…

And at NGV Australia, flowers are blooming in the Gallery as we put the final touches on our Margaret Preston exhibition.

Come and see them in full colour when you visit Margaret Preston – opening this Friday 4 September. Only at NGV.

💐 Which one of these is your pick of the bunch?

Make your next plan a work of art. 

Whether it’s a catch-up with friends, a date with a difference or some time for yourself, make your next day out a little more extraordinary with a Best of NGV Experience.

Guided by an NGV expert, you’ll see the Gallery in a whole new way, learning the secrets and stories behind some of the world’s greatest artworks.

❤️ Tag your friend that loves art.

Then, choose your experience via the link in our bio.

Consider this your sign: NGV Triennial is coming 👀

From a sea of inflatable penguins to a giant game of chess, a 100-metre-long mural to a monumental pink tree planted in the heart of the Gallery – step into a larger-than-life exhibition that mirrors the complexities of the world we live in, revealing the important stories of our time.

NGV Triennial opens on 13 December 2026 – 11 April 2027.

🐧 Tap the link in our bio to start planning your summer.

A yellow dress. A bouquet. A series of portraits that reframe art history.

With these five images, @AtongAtem draws on the visual language of classical Western painting to challenge the idealisation of whiteness.

Draped in vivid yellow cloth and delicate veils, Atem references the traditions of classical portraiture, while her use of blue, lilac and red face paint symbolises alienation – manifesting as an act of defiance against cultural invisibility.

Staring down the barrel of her camera, Atem reminds us that photography can do much more than just capture a moment. It can be a powerful tool for reclaiming agency and reframing history.

💛 See ‘A yellow dress, a bouquet’ in Passage: The Art of Atong Atem – opening 30 October at NGV Australia, free.

There’s always something new to see in Wurrdha Marra.

An ever-evolving exhibition space, Wurrdha Marra is a celebration of the richness of First Nations art and design from across Country – where no two visits are ever quite the same.

Stop by NGV Australia today to see these incredible moments by Emily Kam Kngwarray, @warrabaweatherall, @joelbraydance,  @karla_dickens, Malaluba Gumana, Guruwuy Murrinyina, Djurrayun Murrinyina, Philomena Yeatman, Glenda Nicholls, and many more.

❤️ Wurrdha Marra is open daily at NGV Australia – free, all year round.

A little dusting goes a long way. ✨

Come behind the scenes with NGV Senior Conservator of Frames and Furniture, Holly McGowan-Jackson, as she shows us some of the care that goes into preserving historic furniture in the NGV Collection.

Every friend group has its secrets 👀

There’s nothing quite like the feeling of finding some of art history’s ‘easter eggs’.

A signature disguised in the shadows. A tiny clue engraved on a paint brush. A blink-and-you’ll-miss-it detail that tells an entire story.

Some of art’s most fascinating stories are hiding in plain sight…

See what else you can spot when you visit Jacopo Amigoni’s Farinelli and Friends on Level 2 of NGV International – free.

One last polka with the Dancing Pumpkin 🖤 💛

After stealing the spotlight (and our hearts) at NGV International, Yayoi Kusama’s Dancing Pumpkin has taken its final bow (for now…) as we make way for NGV Triennial.

Here’s to one last dance (or glance) as it waltzes away for a while.

Thanks for the memories @decobroad @samy___baby @wild_hardt @smallfishchan @photographer_shankar @ro___zana and @raylsketches

👀 What do you think is coming next?

This work, now part of the NGV Collection, is generously supported by the Loti and Victor Smorgon Fund 💛

Step into the wild and wonderful world of @taisnaith 🌿 This holiday season, MECCA and the @NGVMelbourne present Australian artist and author Tai Snaith, whose fantastical worlds blur the lines between people, place, flora and fauna – and invite us to embrace the wild within.

Her marvellous cast of characters will bring every MECCA gift – and window! – to life with colour, curiosity and creativity.

As part of MECCA’s ongoing commitment to uplifting women in the arts through @MECCAMPOWER, our movement for gender equality, we’re contributing to the acquisition of work from Snaith’s ‘Wild weed tea’ series for the NGV’s permanent collection. The work will be unveiled at the much-anticipated NGV Triennial, opening 13 December at NGV International in Melbourne.

Colour, craft and complexity. 

Our Margaret Preston exhibition at NGV Australia brings the work of one of Australia's great modernists to life, while painting a nuanced portrait of her legacy.

NGV Director, Tony Ellwood AM, alongside NGV Senior Curator of Australian Art, Beckett Rozentals and exhibition co-curator Michael Gentle share what to look forward to when you visit.

💐 Book your tickets today via the link in our bio.

Perth Design Week is getting ready for its fifth edition – 11 to 18 March 2027.

Eight days. One city. A whole lot of design.

We are delighted to confirm the first of our Major Sponsors for PDW 2027.

The financial and in-kind support of our sponsors and partners is vital for the festival to continue to exist and deliver on its primary mission to elevate the creative and design sector here in WA. 
 
More sponsor and partner announcements to come in the months ahead. Follow along as we build toward March 2027.

ACT Natimuk in partnership with Gariwerd Wimmera Reconciliation Network and Regional Arts Victoria (VicHealth grant) are proud to present a Reconciliation Week 2026 event. The theme this is year is 'All in On Reconciliation' and our event 'Storytelling through Film' is an evening of conversation and connection. It connects a lot of what ACT Natimuk does in the space of arts, combining storytelling, film and circus alongside its support for First Peoples, providing a welcoming and safe space for all community to come and learn, reflect and enjoy powerful storytelling through film.

The event features a screening and conversation with Dylan Singh around The Story of Becoming Nala, a short film based on Alan Murphy and Chrissie Secombes book Becoming Nala, exploring Alan's journey of reconnecting with Country, culture, and identity.

#nationalreconciliationweek2026 #allinforreconciliation #becomingnala #actnatimuk #natimuk #horshamvictoria 

Alan and Chrissie were recipients of ACT Natimuk’s inaugural First Nations Creative Lab grant in 2023/24, and Dylan is the 2024/25 recipient. This work continues to develop through a project that ACT Natimuk are delivering in partnership with Regional Arts Victoria as part of VicHealth’s 'Shifting the Playbook initiative'.

The evening also includes 'The Colleano Heart', a powerful documentary examining Aboriginal identity through the story of Australia’s famous Colleano circus family. This connects beautifully with Dylan’s background as a second-generation circus performer and ACT Natimuk's own programming with its monthly Circus Jam sessions.

Please join us – the event is free, no booking required, and we will have refreshments during a short intermission break.

DAVE JONES BUSHFIRE RECOVERY FUND

Dave Jones has a long history as an artist in the Wimmera region and was a founding member of ACT Natimuk (formerly known as Arapiles Community Theatre Inc.) He has created works across the region and state, has advocated for the arts and brought joy and amazement to all who see his work.

He suffered devastating losses to his studio, equipment and art in the January 9 2026 Natimuk fire. We are running a fundraiser to help support Dave continue in his practice and work. Have a watch of the video and please consider making a donation.

www.givenow.com.au/dave-jones-bushfirerecovery

NATI FRINJ FESTIVAL DIRECTOR 2026/27

With the Nati Frinj 2025 all now done and dusted, it’s time to plan for the 2027 festival. And with that comes the role of the Festival Director. ACT Natimuk is now taking applications for the position.

We are seeking a visionary and dynamic Nati Frinj Biennale Director (2026–27) to lead the next chapter of one of regional Australia’s most exciting arts festivals. This is a unique opportunity to shape a bold, community-connected program that brings together contemporary performance, visual arts, and experimental practice in the heart of Natimuk.

As always, we’re looking for an inspiring leader with strong artistic vision, excellent collaboration skills, and a passion for regional arts. If you’re ready to create an unforgettable festival that celebrates creativity, place, and community—we’d love to hear from you. 
Previous applicants are welcome to apply.

For the full PD description and submission details follow the link here:

#natifrinj #natifrinjbiennale #festivaldirector #actnatimuk #natifrinj2027

ACT Natimuk/Nati Frinj Biennale has a long history within the township of Natimuk and the surrounding areas, and we are devastated, along with the entire community, by the impacts of the bushfire on Friday 9 January. While we are deeply thankful that no human lives were lost, many lives have been changed forever through the loss of homes, property, and the deep connections that come with them.

Although it is still very early days, Natimuk, as the resilient community it is, has already moved into support mode, caring for those most directly impacted. Our heartfelt thoughts are with everyone who is still reeling from these losses, and we hope that in the near future we can offer support and space in the ways we know best.

We cannot thank emergency services enough, both during the fire itself and throughout the ongoing aftermath. Firefighters, along with community members who stayed to defend properties, are the reason much of the township still stands. Essential services—including power, water and communications—were largely reinstated by Sunday evening, no small feat given the number of power poles destroyed. And community members who have stepped up to guide people towards support options ad offer help.

Thank you to all who have reached out with messages of care and understanding—both personally and as fellow arts organisations and supporters. Kind words at a time like this truly matter - there is a long road ahead for the community.

What an incredible experience was Journey of the Karen. Created by members of the Karen communities in Horsham and Nhill, in collaboration with Black Hole Theatre, this immersive multi-media production brought together traditional storytelling and contemporary performance in the most powerful way.

Told by performers across generations and cultures – with giant glowing puppets, original music, and evocative video – the work spoke not only to the Karen experience, but to the journeys of so many migrants: stories of persecution, resistance, escape, and survival. It was a moving testament to community strength and the importance of sharing stories that too often go untold.

All script, sets, video, music, props, and puppets were created by community members under the guidance of Black Hole Theatre’s brilliant creative team.  Images: Suzanne Phoenix

La III Bienal Mundial del Arroz de Cullera ha reunido durante cuatro días a grandes profesionales de la gastronomía, restauradores, visitantes y amantes de la cultura del arroz.

Una cita que ha puesto en valor nuestra tradición arrocera, el talento gastronómico y la estrecha relación de Cullera con uno de los productos más representativos de nuestra identidad.

🎤 Durante la Bienal hemos querido conocer la opinión y secretos de algunos de sus protagonistas.

Diferentes perspectivas, experiencias y formas de entender una misma pasión: el arroz🌾 

💛 Porque en Cullera, el arroz es mucho más que gastronomía. Es cultura, territorio y tradición.

#VisitCullera #Cullera #BienalMundialDelArroz #CulleraSabeAArroz #ArtesanosDelArroz

Un día de calderes d'Oliva a la Bienal de Cullera...Dos ciutats unides per l'arròs

🏆 Cullera, Premi Levante-EMV 2026 en la categoria d’Oci per l’esforç en l’estratègia que combina música, grans esdeveniments i turisme. Una programació que converteix l’oci en un element de promoció turística i que permet projectar una imatge de Cullera associada també a la celebració, la diversitat i la cultura contemporània,

Ahir, recollirem aquest premi al Palau de la Música per la gran quantitat de propostes públiques i privades que celebrem:

🪼Medusa.
🦓Zevra.
🏳️‍🌈Cullera Beach Pride.
🎙️LaDemo.

🎶Certamen Nacional de Bandes de Música ‘Ciutat de Cullera’.
🎞️Certamen Nacional de Bandes de Música de Cine ‘Memorial Rafael Talens Pelló’. 
🔊Les Festes Majors.
...i un llarg etcètera d’esdeveniments musicals que ocórren a Cullera.

❤️ Gràcies Levante-EMV per aquest reconeixement!

🌾 Arranca la III 𝐁𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐌𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐝𝐞 𝐥’𝐀𝐫𝐫𝐨̀𝐬 𝐝𝐞 𝐂𝐮𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐫𝐚

🥘 Fins al 18 d’octubre, Cullera es convertix en l’epicentre de la gastronomia arrossera amb quatre dies plens d’activitats, cultura, tradició, innovació, fira, demostracions, degustacions i música, amb l’arròs com a gran protagonista. 

👩‍🍳 L’obertura d’aquesta tercera edició ha comptat amb un showcooking en el qual han participan la xef Begoña Rodrigo, cap de cuina de La Salita, @artesanosdelarroz , i l’alcalde de Cullera, Jordi Mayor.
 
🍚 Cullera és capital gastronòmica de l’arròs per tradició, per cultura, per la qualitat del seu producte i per comptar amb un teixit empresarial i hostaler de referència.

🙌 Gràcies a totes les persones, professionals i entitats que feu possible aquesta gran celebració!

🥘 La III Biennal Mundial de l’Arròs de Cullera tindrà molts moments que no et pots perdre. Ací et contem alguns perquè disfrutes d’aquest festival gastronòmic i pugues viure una experiència especial en Cullera.
🔗 Pots consultar la programació completa a l’enllaç de la BIO.
📆 Del 15 al 18 d’octubre.

¡Así hemos vivido el puente de octubre en Cullera! 🏰✨

Cuatro días llenos de historia, tradición, cultura y muchos planes para disfrutar de nuestra ciudad.

🎉 Celebramos el 9 d'Octubre con música, bailes populares, muixeranga y la espectacular recreación histórica de la entrada de Jaume I en Cullera.

🏰 Viajamos al pasado con el Mercado Medieval, que llenó nuestras calles de artesanía, talleres, gastronomía y ambiente festivo.

🎭 Disfrutamos de la cultura con «Seis, el musical», dentro de la Mostra de Teatre Cullera a Escena.

🌿 Y tampoco faltaron las rutas guiadas, las actividades patrimoniales y las fiestas del Mareny de Sant Llorenç.

💙 Un puente para disfrutar, compartir y seguir descubriendo Cullera.

#VisitCullera #Cullera #9dOctubre #PuenteDeOctubre #ComunitatValenciana #CulleraTodoElAño
❤️ Un 9 d’Octubre d’orígens, d’història, d’arrels. De la nostra cultura. De la nostra identitat.

🥘✨ ¡Ya tenemos el programa completo de la III Bienal Mundial del Arroz de Cullera!

Del 15 al 18 de octubre, Cullera se convierte en el punto de encuentro de la gastronomía y la cultura del arroz🌾

Cuatro días para descubrir, degustar y disfrutar de un producto que forma parte de nuestra historia, nuestro paisaje y nuestra identidad. Y lo mejor… ¡hay planes para todos los gustos! 👇

👨‍🍳 ALTA COCINA Y SHOWCOOKINGS
Grandes referentes de la gastronomía como Begoña Rodrigo, Kiko Moya, Carolina Álvarez, José Manuel Miguel, Jorge Lengua o Bernd Knöller, junto a cocineros locales y profesionales de diferentes territorios, compartirán sus técnicas, conocimientos y nuevas formas de interpretar el arroz.

🍚 DEGUSTACIONES PARA TODOS LOS PALADARES
🍴 15, 16 y 17 de octubre: degustación de tapas de la Asociación de Hostelería de Cullera, de 18:00 a 23:50 h.

🥘 17 y 18 de octubre: degustación de arroces del Club de Producto Artesanos del Arroz, de 12:00 a 16:00 h.

🍷 CATAS, TALLERES Y EXPERIENCIAS
Catas de vino, aceite y productos locales, talleres gastronómicos, actividades artesanales y propuestas para conocer el arroz desde nuevas perspectivas.

🎶 MÚSICA, HUMOR Y TRADICIÓN
Conciertos de Pep Gimeno Botifarra, Los Roper y Yambu, monólogo de Óscar Tramoyeres, sesiones de DJ, muixeranga, bailes tradicionales y mucho más.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 ACTIVIDADES PARA TODA LA FAMILIA
El Juego de la Paella, rutas cicloturísticas entre arrozales, recreaciones teatralizadas, talleres y animación para pequeños y mayores.

🛍️ Además, disfruta de la feria de productos artesanales, la exposición de maquinaria agrícola y el concurso Jóvenes Talentos.

📅Del 15 al 18 de octubre de 2026
📍Centro urbano de Cullera: Jardines del Mercado, Plaza de la Virgen y Paseo Dr. Alemany, entre otros espacios.
