latestIgtvVideos.caption: On Sunday 13 October @katchafireofficial the boys from NZ stopped by Bali for an unforgettable performance during sunset at world famous Uluwatu destination Single Fin Bali. A large number of fans from all over the world stopped by to enjoy the reggae roots show. Watch how it all came together, from a pool to a dance stage filled in Rasta colours and @taibuddha showing the boys from the band the famous Uluwatu surf break. Combining two strong cultures and showcasing the music you all love to hear, watch how our Single Fin Sunday’s came together. #singlefinbali #singlefinsundays

latestIgtvVideos.title: Uluwatu Single Fin Classic 2019
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
In a magnificent climax to the second annual Uluwatu Single Fin Classic, Australia’s Ozzie Wright had the honor of hoisting the perpetual championship trophy, joined by his fellow finalists and the cheers of the thousands of spectators, friends and competitors that gathered for this unique and vibrant event in celebration of single fin surfing. “This is my most favorite place in the whole world…I really didn’t care about winning, just being out there with all the guys, good kinship, and being able to express myself, the froth that I feel for life, is what it’s all about really” said Ozzy before jumping on stage. 
The grand prize for the event champion was an air ticket to join the 2020 Burleigh Single Fin Festival, now a sister event to the Uluwatu Single Fin Classic, but seeing how Ozzie is already in Australia, Tai Graham and Made Kasim decided to give air tickets to the finalists @agusblackysetiawan  and Dex Scoot for their amazing performances in the event.

Fotos primer día del festival día 30 en la Autoridad Portuaria de Palma. Gracias por hacerlo posible 💙@mallorcalivemusic @portsdebalears @begudespuig.1927 @estrelladammmallorca @autovidal @trueworldorg @surferrulemag @bazanlab @balearacustic @imatgeievents @lomusic.es @bilbotex @goodkarmaprojects @surfriderespana @garazisanchez @neuscortes @ib3 @diariodemallorca @uhmallorca @gocactusboys @robertsherwoodfilms @daidabacktotheoceanfilm @vincentkardasik Amazing pics by @swen_exposure 📸💙
Momentos WIPEOUT ‘26

Algunos robamos de esta edición 🌊📸😜

@ajuntamentdecalvia @visitcalvia

Como dice nuestro querido Kepa Acero: “El mar me ha enseñado a fluir.” 🌊

Y fluir también significa entender que las condiciones no siempre son favorables. Que hay veces que toca adaptarse, aceptar los contratiempos y cambiar el plan, pero que lo verdaderamente importante se queda con nosotros.

El diluvio del sábado dejó inutilizados todos nuestros equipos eléctricos y nos obligó a parar antes de tiempo. Pero nos quedamos con los abrazos bajo la lluvia y, sobre todo, con una certeza: WIPEOUT no son solo luces, pantallas o amplificadores. WIPEOUT es su gente.

De parte de todo el equipo, solo podemos decir GRACIAS. Por cada mensaje de APOYO, por estar ahí, incluso bajo la lluvia… y por las ganas inmensas de que este proyecto que nos acerca al mar siga creciendo entre todo. 

Esta 5ª edición iba camino de ser inolvidable… y, de alguna manera, lo ha sido… pero nos quedamos con más ilusión y más ganas para la siguiente! Ojalá podamos seguir🙏🏽💪🎬🎶💙 Nos vemos en la próxima ola! 🌊

Gracias @martaruiz.m por colaborar 📸

@ajuntamentdecalvia @visitcalvia

Next year marks 100 years since Buick assembly began in New Zealand. To celebrate, these remarkable cars will have pride of place in the Art Deco Festival Napier - Vintage Car Parade in 2027!

Surveillance cameras with facial recognition, motion detectors, GPS receivers, thermal sensors,... Day, night, when you are at home or in public space, in the toilet, in the car or in the elevator. We know where you are and what you do there.
Do you doubt it? Open your eyes! You've been living in 1984. You're not the character in a science fiction novel, and you can't wake up from a nightmare. This is your reality, the miserable real life of each and every wasp on planet earth.
Be alert with the silly face you put on, you don’t know who will be recording you right now. Everything is moving so fast that the invisible network has wrapped you up without you even realizing it. And the most tragic thing is that it was your agreement and your irresponsible consent that legitimized your enslavement.
Proudly, you carry your handcuffs and spend your fortunes on the cutting-edge technology that gives you the most control. Laziness, a feeling of helplessness, the utmost stupidity, madness for consumption all the time, ... no matter what your case: you’ve allowed it! You have lived resigned and conformist.
And now you're scared, you want the freedoms that have been taken away from you, but you're late, very late. A trickle of cold sweat drips down your neck. And I can read what goes around your cerebral cortex: dissent, run away, go back to the woods. You are scared!

Cruïlla 2026 Barcelona Pintant mural al costat de l’artista @irenelopezleon Representant a @gargarfestival  Aquest mural explora la relació entre la creativitat, la natura i l’ecosistema digital contemporani. Al centre, l’altaveu simbolitza l’origen de la música i l’expressió artística, envoltat de flors exuberants que representen el talent, la diversitat i la vitalitat dels músics. A la part superior, unes abelles convertides en càmeres de vigilància observen l’escena.
La composició planteja una reflexió sobre els equilibris de valor dins l’entorn digital: mentre la música floreix i alimenta tot l’ecosistema, altres agents en recullen, gestionen i distribueixen els fruits. La presència dels elements de vigilància suggereix també com les plataformes no només intermedien l’accés a la música, sinó que condicionen i registren els hàbits d’escolta, configurant progressivament les nostres preferències culturals.
El contrast entre els elements orgànics i els tecnològics evidencia una tensió entre creació, consum i control, convidant l’espectador a qüestionar-se qui genera realment el valor, qui en determina la visibilitat i com es construeixen les nostres experiències musicals en l’era digital.

GarGar 2026
Penelles
No deixis que la tecnologia t’esclafi
Aquest mural de gran format és una peça de conscienciació que connecta dues problemàtiques
actuals: la desaparició de les abelles i la creixent desconnexió de l’ésser humà amb la natura
a causa de l’excés de tecnologia i l’ús de tòxics.
L’obra es una metàfora visual basada en el contrast entre dos mons. D’una banda, el món digital,
fred i artificial, on el fons està format per un codi binari (0 i 1) que simbolitza les pantalles,
les dades i la substitució de la realitat per una experiència virtual. De l’altra, el món natural, ple
de vida, on el fons està compost per hexàgons que evoquen l’estructura dels ruscs d’abella i
l’equilibri dels ecosistemes.
Les abelles simbolitzen la biodiversitat i la dolçor essencial de la vida: sense abelles no hi ha
mel, i sense mel la vida perd equilibri i harmonia.
El mural mostra la tensió entre aquests dos mons, però també deixa oberta una escletxa d’esperança:
la natura encara resisteix i ens recorda que sempre som a temps de reconnectar amb
el món real abans que només en quedi una còpia artificial.

“Símbols desfasats”
El ritme accelerat del progrés tecnològic ens porta a dependre constantment de nous sistemes i dispositius. El wifi, avui imprescindible, demà serà substituït per una altra tecnologia. El mercat ens empeny a comprar l’últim model sense preguntar-nos si és realment necessari o segur, generant residus tecnològics i una insatisfacció permanent.
El gran símbol del wifi, tan reconegut i buscat, acabarà convertint-se —com tants altres— en una simple relíquia del passat.

Pol·linitzant Gualta
homenatge a les abelles, pol·linitzadores essencials per a la vida, especialment en una zona com l’Empordà, rica en flors i arbres fruiters.
L’obra integra visualment l’escala del pati, mimetitzant-la amb el mural per crear un conjunt artístic i orgànic.
El projecte vol fer valdre el paper vital de les abelles en la biodiversitat i alertar sobre el seu perill d’extinció, provocat sobretot per l’ús de productes tòxics en l’agricultura.

“Ne passez pas à côté du miel de la vie” és un mural que neix amb l’objectiu de conscienciar sobre dues problemàtiques actuals: la desaparició de les abelles i la desconnexió creixent de l’ésser humà amb la natura a causa de la tecnologia. La idea va sorgir en veure que, a l’entorn de StreetArtCity, es produeix una mel boníssima, cosa que contrasta amb la tendència global d’allunyament del món natural.
El mural és una metàfora visual que mostra com, en substituir la vida natural per pantalles i connexions digitals, estem perdent l’essència mateixa de la vida. Sense abelles no hi ha mel, i sense mel, la vida perd la seva dolçor i el seu equilibri.

UNINHIBITED

Expressing yourself freely and naturally, without self-consciousness, restraint, or fear of judgement.

This moment was captured on the dance floor at @wellfestnz in February. @sarah.menlove and I were offering a Somatic Dance, Shakti was in full flow!

No choreography.
No performance.
No right or wrong way to move.

Just humans fully alive in their bodies.

This is what keeps calling me back to the dance floor again and again. Freedom to move, feel, express, and remember who we are beneath the layers.

Queenstown, I’m excited to be back with you tomorrow night!

Join me for a dance journey at 7pm in the Church. An opportunity to remember the truth of your own divinity. 

🎟 Tickets via Humanitix — link in the comments.

#EcstaticDance #Queenstown #ConsciousDance #SomaticDance #DanceMedicine

Someone came up to us after this dance and said they felt healed.

After one dance.

Healing doesn’t always have to be heavy.
Sometimes healing happens on the dance floor.

In a room full of strangers and friends.
Bare feet on the earth.
Bodies moving to the beat.

When we drop out of our heads and into our bodies…
something shifts.

We move.
We breathe.
We let the music move through us.

The creative pulse.
Shakti.
Life force.

After this particular dance at @wellfestnz a woman shared that when @sarah.menlove guided everyone to drop awareness down to the base of the spine, she felt a huge energetic blockage release in her lower body.

Our bodies hold so much.

Tension. 
Old stories. 
Limiting beliefs.

And sometimes when we surrender to the rhythm and let the body lead…those patterns begin to soften.

New movement.
New space.
New pathways.

Healing doesn’t always look like sitting in a therapy room.
Sometimes it looks like dancing. ✨

If you feel the call to move with us, we have two upcoming spaces:

#somaticdance #movementismedicine #dunedinNZ #autumequinox #devotioninmotion

Still reminiscing Wellfest ✨

The deep conversations, the love that filled the space, and the beautiful friends we made along the way. Feeling so grateful to have shared such special moments with incredible humans. 💛

How do you return to normal life after five days of magic?

Wellfest. WOWfest.

Five days of ceremony, music and connection.
Daily cacao. Saunas. Kirtan. Dancing.

Barefoot on the earth.
Living, breathing, singing and moving in community.

I was so immersed in the experience that I barely took any photos to capture the magic.

Huge gratitude to @natamakare @wellfestnz and the whole crew for the incredible mahi that made this gathering possible. What a gift to be part of it.

And now… integration.
How do we return to everyday life when something inside us has shifted?

Especially when there is so much chaos in the world outside.

Maybe the practice is simply this:

Keep showing up.
With love. With kindness. With presence.

Community feels more important than ever.

If you’re in Ōtepoti, I’m excited to be hosting two upcoming community gatherings:

✨ Devotion in Motion: Autumn Equinox
21 March | Kirtan + Somatic Dance

✨ Mauri Flow
11 April | Cacao Activation + Somatic Dance

Spaces to reconnect, move and drop back into the heart. ♥️

Curious — how do you integrate after a big transformational experience?

Maybe that’s the whole point…

that we came here to dance 🫶

We’re still dancing in our minds. ✨🌙

As the sun set, the whole landscape of Wellfest transformed.

The trees and earth began to glow.Fires were lit.Costumes got wilder.The music turned up just a little louder… and the dancing never stopped.

The Magic Nursery became a glowing beacon in the night — alive with interactive music games, UV painting, and co-created DJ sets that blurred the line between artist and audience.The late-night rave cave pulsed underground.Fire spinners lit up the darkness.Performers moved like living art against the flames.

Around the fires, smaller circles gathered — singing, drumming, sharing stories, locking eyes in conversations that felt timeless.The saunas carried on into the night, heat and laughter spilling out under the stars.

It was the kind of place where time dissolved.Where you were so deep in connection, rhythm, and presence that you didn’t even think to check the hour…Until you finally glanced at your watch and realised it was 3am.

Wellfest by night was wild and tender all at once.Electric. Elemental. Unforgettable.

There was something about Wellfest by day that’s hard to put into words… but we’ll try. ✨

First and foremost — it was the human connection.
People arrived exactly as they were. No masks. No performances. Just open hearts.
There was that feeling of being seen, heard, and loved in your wholeness — and offering that same presence to someone else.

By day, Wellfest felt expansive.
The workshops inspired growth, stretched minds, and opened up new perspectives across a wide range of beautiful modalities.

There was yoga beneath open skies.
Breathwork that moved emotion through the body.
Sauna sessions that grounded and reset.
Dance that shook us free.
Singing that opened hearts.
Fire circles that drew us closer.
Bare feet on the earth.
Art unfolding in real time.
Moments of co-creation that reminded us we’re not meant to do this alone.

It was nature. It was the elements. It was depth and play woven together.

There was a special energy in the air all day — something alive, intentional, and deeply human.
A kind of magic that couldn’t quite be matched… only experienced.

In-Between: Rest in Yogyakarta 01 was a dreamy, sticky zine-making workshop at @ykartbookfair in May. 

A workshop for 8 that made room for 11 under a huge ficus tree. A overworked printer with @toskecil and @adamasu__ . The rest of us sitting in a circle folding pages of our collective zine, two hour past the end time, bonding over the universal thing of teaching each other swear words in all the languages we know.

Yang dapat dihitung dengan angka adalah 3 hari penyelenggaraan, 6 bulan persiapan, 30 orang komite penyelenggara, 35 orang kru panitia, 43 exhibitor, 45 buku di open table, 30 program dan aktivasi ruang, 65 pihak partner dan 2800++ pengunjung. 

Namun yang tidak dapat dihitung adalah kepercayaan, rasa penasaran, kekecewaan, pembelajaran, kebingungan, harapan, dorongan berkarya, dan segala di antaranya. 

Terima kasih banyak kami ucapkan untuk segala yang bisa dihitung maupun tidak. Sampai jumpa di YKABF27!

#YKABF #booound

@ykartbookfair 2026 resmi berakhir. Tapi mungkin, yang paling tertinggal bukan hanya karya-karya yang dipamerkan, melainkan percakapan, pertemuan, dan rasa terhubung yang muncul di dalamnya.

Selama tiga hari, Yogyakarta Art Book Fair mempertemukan pekerja kreatif, seniman, penerbit independen, hingga komunitas lintas negara dalam satu ruang yang dipenuhi artbook, zine, workshop, diskusi, dan pertukaran ide. Di tengah industri kreatif yang semakin cepat dan individual, ruang seperti ini terasa semakin penting karena kreativitas tidak hanya tumbuh dari kemampuan untuk terus terlihat, tetapi juga dari kemampuan untuk saling terhubung.

Melalui praktik penerbitan independen, YKABF menunjukkan bahwa karya tidak selalu hadir sebagai produk akhir semata. Ia juga bisa menjadi medium sosial: membuka percakapan, mempertemukan pengalaman, dan membangun solidaritas lintas komunitas maupun lintas negara.

Dan mungkin, itu yang membuat ruang seperti YKABF terus dibutuhkan oleh kita. 

Terima kasih untuk @ykartbookfair dan semua pihak yang sudah merawat ruang ini bersama-sama. ✨

Dalam program Special Showcase, YKABF 2026 menghandirkan Ika Vantiani beserta jurnal-jurnal miliknya. Dipajang berderet, serta dipersilakan untuk bisa membolak-balik untuk melihat setiap halamannya. Pameran Junk-to-Journals: Between Undoing and Rewriting Ephemera berangkat dari praktik junk journaling yang dijalankan Ika Vantiani selama beberapa tahun terakhir. Praktik Junk Journal milik Ika Vantiani membawa kita pada kerja menelusuri hubungan antara menemukan, menyusun, dan menata apa yang kita pikirkan. Nasib suatu benda atau objek, agaknya dapat dihentikan, diputus ditengah oleh praktik Junk Journal. Lalu sang pembuat, seperti memberikan nasib yang lebih layak dan bernilai. 

Ada beberapa bagian yang memang tidak diperkenankan untuk didokumentasikan. Yaitu adalah catatan-catatan personal milik Ika Vantiani. Tentu ini perihal menghargai momen dan sekitarnya. Sama seperti bagaimana seluruh jurnal ini dibuat. Walau kita bisa pandang sangat serius, sebagai bentuk pengarsipan, namun kerja seperti ini kami rasa didominasi pada yang lebih manusiawi. Dimana kita punya ruang untuk menghargai secara penuh yang tak terduga, bahkan membaca ulang jurnal yang sudah kita buat pun adalah berkah yang tak terduga. 

Menurut kami, unsur paling menyenangkan dalam kerja-kerja Junk Journal adalah ketidakpastian dan kebaruan yang terus menerus ada. Sekian penelurusan, sekian temuan, juga sekian halaman akan membawa kita kesinambungan yang agaknya absurd. Mungkin tak banyak maksud untuk menyatukan suatu hal, namun akhirnya, kita punya suatu sensasi didalamnya. Coba saja amati bagaimana kombinasi gambar, bentuk, dan material dalam banyak jurnal Ika Vantiani. Memamerkan deretan jurnal ini, adalah langkah yang mengesankan. Agenda ini membuka refleksi kami pada material disekitar, perihal bagaimana budaya konsumsi kita, atau cara kita memperlakukan mereka. Kemungkinan menjadi pusat utama dalam praktik ini, yaitu digunakan kembali, baik secara fungsi maupun narasi. Praktik mengarsipkan pengalaman sehari hari melalui material bekas menunjukkan bahwa ingatan, keterikatan emosional, dan pengalaman hidup dapat hadir melalui medium sederhana. Pada akhirnya, nilai sesuatu bukanlah perihal-

⚪ ¡Llamado abierto!

En noviembre celebraremos la 16ª edición del Mes del Diseño Chile.
Invitamos a espacios culturales, instituciones, colectivos y agentes del diseño de todo el país a sumarse a nuestro Programa Abierto.

Pueden postular encuentros, festivales, ferias, exposiciones y actividades de formación vinculadas al diseño.

➜ ¿Cómo postular? Inscribe tu actividad en www.mesdeldiseno.cl
📅 Proceso abierto hasta el 4 de octubre.

El Mes del Diseño de Chile lo hacemos todas y todos, ¡súmate!

#mesdeldiseño #mdd #chile #diseño

Invitamos a la diseñadora de ambientes @sol_echevarria a contarnos sobre algún objeto cotidiano cuyo diseño haya sido significativo en su vida. 

En la 16a edición del Mes del Diseño volvemos la mirada hacia los objetos cotidianos para reconocer cómo, desde su utilidad, materialidad y permanencia, forman parte de nuestra memoria e identidad. 

Y tú, ¿qué objeto elegirías?

Chile y México: Unidos en el arte, el diseño y la solidaridad 🇨🇱🤝🇲🇽

¿Sabías que México acudió en ayuda de Chile tras los terremotos de Chillán (1939) y Valdivia? ¿Y que ese apoyo quedó inmortalizado en obras de arte y arquitectura que se pueden encontrar en Santiago y Concepción? De estas acciones y sus alcances expuso el Dr. Rodrigo Vera Manríquez @veramanriquez , en su visita a  la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, UNAM, el pasado 6 de octubre.

El director del Instituto de Historia y Patrimonio del Depto. de Diseño de la Facultad de Arquitectura y Urbanismo de la Universidad de Chile se presentó en el Aula Enrique del Moral de la Facultad de Arquitectura UNAM. Allí, dictó la conferencia “El Plan chileno-mexicano de cooperación fraternal (1960-1964): arquitectura, arte y diseño para la fraternidad de dos pueblos”, en la hizo una revisión histórica y estética de las donaciones y aportes artísticos y culturales brindados por México a Chile, durante la reconstrucción del país tras los terremotos de Chillán y Valdivia. 

¿Qué obras surgieron en estos períodos?

📍 “Presencia de América Latina” de Jorge González Camarena, ubicado en la Casa del Arte de la U. de Concepción, Concepción. (Foto 1)
📍 “De México a Chile” de Xavier Guerrero, mural en la Escuela República de México. (Foto 5). 
📍 “Muerte al Invasor” de David Alfaro Siqueiros, mural en la Biblioteca Pedro Aguirre Cerda, Santiago. ( Foto 8)
📍 “Fraternidad de dos pueblos indoamericanos”. Diseña por Juan O’Gorman y ejecutada por María Martner. Emplazada en el cerro San Cristóbal, Santiago.
📍El Club México de boxeo de Santiago.
📍El Club México de Boxeo de Osorno: con murales del artista mexicano Tomás Parra y la participación de artistas chilenos como María Martner y Nemesio Antúnez.

La conferencia, organizada por el Laboratorio Editorial de Arquitectura UNAM, fue parte de las actividades de Chile en México, realizadas con el apoyo del Área de Diseño del Ministerio de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio de Chile, que incluyeron la inauguración de la exposición Visión y Tradición, en el marco de @designweekmex 

📸 por @feliz__dia

Cinco años conectando ideas, impulsando talentos y demostrando que el diseño también transforma territorios.

𝐇𝐚𝐛𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐫 𝐞𝐥 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐞ñ𝐨: En su 16a edición, el Mes del Diseño invita a observar los objetos cotidianos y reconocer cómo, desde su utilidad, materialidad y permanencia, forman parte de nuestra memoria e identidad. Desde una taza de loza Futura, a las copas de Cristal Yungay o los jarros esmaltados de Fanaloza, los objetos nos acompañan para facilitarnos el quehacer y, de paso, permitirnos escribir nuestra historia. 

Y en tu caso, ¿qué objeto ha marcado tu vida?
¡Te leemos! 

*Imágenes del archivo digital del @museoartesdecorativas

Chile en México 🇨🇱 🇲🇽
Felicitamos y aplaudimos a cada una y uno de los diseñadores participantes en la exposición Visión y Tradición, en el Museo Nacional de Antropología de México: Paula Corrales @paulacorrales.studio, Rodrigo Bravo @rodrigobravo, Raúl H. Tralma @rautralma,  Camilo Huinca @onlyjoke, Catalina Zarhi @catazarhiceramista 👏👏👏

La muestra, que se realiza en el marco de @designweekmex 2026, y se extiende desde el 7 de octubre al 1 de noviembre, se compone de las piezas creadas por las y los diseñadores nacionales en colaboración con cinco artesanos de diversos estados mexicanos, durante el programa de residencias Visión y Tradición 2026.

La participación de Chile como país invitado en esta instancia única es fruto del trabajo articulado desde la Mesa de Internacionalización del Diseño, instancia que integran el Ministerio de las Culturas, DIRAC, ProChile, Imagen de Chile, y la Embajada de Chile en México.

The 2026 Metropolitan winner of the Whittles Body Corporate Management Services Venue Award is: @SouthHenleyNewsagencyAndPO!

The judges found that the South Henley Newsagency & Post Office completely embodied what this award is about in their support of artist Felicity Steer. From putting away their own stock to ensure that her artwork could breathe & present well, to getting so completely behind the spirit of her work, charging no commission on sales that they readily facilitated, and much more that was a delight to read in their nomination.

The 2026 Regional Winner of the Whittles Body Corporate Management Services Venue Award is: @Mallee_Spirit_Distillery!

The judges were impressed at the variety of ways that Mallee Spirit Distillery supported their artists. From free accommodation, words of encouragement, and the creation of opportunities for the artists to engage with visitors, through to the dedicated promotion of the event within and beyond the district of Lameroo, and accompanying events to encourage regional tourism and engagement with the work of these artists in an exciting way. New audiences ranged from school students to interstate travellers, ultimately building connections for these artists across a range of networks.

The 2026 winner of the SALA in Lights Award is: @SallyParnis!

The judges were impressed by the style of Sally’s work, which is a form of digital painting. They found that the works held an inviting atmosphere and felt that this work is the perfect choice to expand onto a larger canvas in 2027 and bring to audiences across the state. This award is sponsored by @Foodlandsa & @novatechcet.

The winner of the inaugural @Carclew Early-Career Artist Studio Award is: Chin Ton Naomi Tang!

The judges were taken by conceptual strength of Chin Ton Naomi’s work, and the perfect timing of this opportunity in sustaining their ongoing creative practice. They look forward to Chin Ton Naomi joining the Carclew community for a studio residency early next year.

The 2026 winner of the @Guildhouse_au Artist's Choice Award is: @Zoe.Crichton_art!

Guildhouse invited artists of any medium, age, or skill level to vote for the SALA Award finalist whose artwork impressed them the most in the 2026 SALA Festival. The prize includes $1,500 cash + 12 Month Guildhouse Accredited membership.

A record-breaking total of 507 votes were cast, with an overwhelming number of voters delighting in Zoe's work. Voters remarked on the vibrant colours and sense of movement in her work, and ultimately appreciated the nostalgic quality that transported them to their own childhood memories.

The 2026 winner of the @CityofUnley Active Ageing Award is: @AntheaJonesArtist!

The judges recognised that Anthea has introduced an intensely personal narrative and storytelling into her latest body of work which has resulted in a richer and rewarding engagement in the work for both herself and the viewer.

This particular artwork displayed both a brilliant execution of technique and detailed artistic content to awake the curious viewer.

The 2026 winner of the @CityofAdelaide Award is: Stephen Soeffky! @soeffky 

The judges decided that the actively engaging process of Stephen’s work, and his simultaneous practice of sustainability and skilled invention, sitting alongside place-bound nostalgia, humour and an impressive work ethic best spoke to the spirit and life of the City of Adelaide.

The rigorous site-specificity of Stephen’s project connected his father’s CBD-based coffee bean business (dating back to the 1970s) with another Adelaide institution, Floating Goose Studios, reimagining the latter through the satirical lens of commerce and workplace relations.”

“The work straddled the worlds of installation, furniture design, performance art, and relational aesthetics with wit and aplomb.”

latestPosts.caption:
As you plan for the year ahead, we want to share an update about On This Rock. The event has been moved from Fall 2026 to Spring 2027 for two reasons: 
🧗‍♂️🧗‍♂️🧗‍♀️
1) Supporting the local climbing community: The first weekend of October this year is going to be the inaugural Smith Rock Climbing Festival, a grassroots event led by our local climb shop, RedPoint (check them out!) 
🧗‍♂️🧗‍♂️🧗‍♀️
Common Ground is excited to support this festival in several ways, and moving OTR allows both events to thrive without overlap. If you love climbing and the PNW climbing community, mark your calendars on October 2-4, 2026 for this first-ever festival!
🧗‍♂️🧗‍♂️🧗‍♀️
2) Fine-tuning On This Rock: Our planning team is using this extra time to assess OTR and dial it in even more toward it’s mission—improving accessibility, experiencing belonging, and considering Jesus in the climbing space. Please keep our team in prayer, reach out to us with any ideas you have for OTR’s future, and block out May 21–23, 2027 for the next OTR!

We gather in different homes, carry different stories, and see from different perspectives. All while exploring and growing in the direction of each other and Jesus,  together. And you’re invited!
This is what Common Ground is all about!

#Spirituality #community #homechurch #faith #lifetogether

We’re absolutely thrilled to have @mac_pad from @crosswalk_portland come over the mountains and through the woods to share a message with us for our upcoming Gathers this Saturday at 5pm at the Historic Skyliners Lodge. Expect a time of fellowship and worship as well as a provided dinner! You won’t want to miss it. See ya there!
Our favorite time of the week is when we get to see everyone at our House Churches!

Starting this weekend, we will be diving into the first of a series of conversations that will lead us as house churches to reflect together and look ahead at how we want to continue to grow in embodying the identity of a local community of Jesus followers. Hope to see you there! Please DM us for addresses.

Last weekend 12 of the Common Ground family embarked on a 4-day backpacking retreat through the Mt. Jefferson Wilderness. With the theme of the trip being “Presence,” they learned and grew together in how to be intentionally present with others, with nature, and with God. Here’s a quick video that captures some moments from along the way!

Here’s a first look at the backpacking trip around Mt. Jefferson that Common Ground hosted with @randysroute as our guide! Beautiful terrains, incredible conversations, freezing alpine lake dips, and ibuprofen were all on the menu for our group of 12. We lucked out with weather and was overall a breath of fresh air to be among the trees and disconnected from our regular day-to-day lives.

We had an absolute blast welcoming in our fellowship and worship together at our home churches this past weekend. Special shoutout to the Saturday Evening fam—our newest CG home church that meets weekly from 5 to 7pm on Saturday’s. Interested in joining in and seeing what a church at a home is all about? Give us a holler!

CG is excited to share that the group laying the groundwork for our third house-church has identified September 12 as its first gathering! They’ll be gathering around a meal and focusing on growing an intergenerational family of faith that can extend grace and support to each other in life and in a shared pursuit of Jesus.
🌲🏔️🌲
This new house church will begin meeting Saturday, September 12, from 5:00–7:00 PM. Whether you’ve been part of Common Ground for years, are just beginning to explore faith, or are simply looking for a community to do life with, you’re welcome to join us!
🌲🏔️🌲
If you or anyone you know might be interested in this group, send us a message and pass the word along! We invite everyone to set a reminder to pray for this brand new initiative!
🌲🏔️🌲
Why a new LifeGroup? This approach is rooted in the picture we see in Acts 2:42–47, where followers of Jesus shared life together in homes, around tables, and throughout their communities. It’s relational rather than program-driven, simple and sustainable, and designed to multiply healthy Jesus-centered communities.

We’re in the midst of the beautiful teachings of what it ideally looks like to live in and through Community. As a central practice of Jesus, we hope you join us as we dive into Week 3 of the Community Practice by @practicingtheway 
•••
Friday at 6:30pm at Rachel, Trevor, and Ashley’s home. Please DM us for exact address. 
•••
Saturday at 10:00am at the Mack’s home!
For the next few weeks, we invite you to join our family of LifeGroups as we embark on learning about the Community Practice by @practicingtheway

→ Mitch Cairns: Artist’s Mouth

Next Saturday 24 October, the IMA hosts a talk by Australian photography historian and Oxford Professor Emeritus Geoffrey Batchen, presented in partnership with UQ School of Communication and Arts.

Since the introduction of hand-held cameras, people have been captured blinking. Though mid-blink images are often deleted, an online trend has seen celebrities posting photos with their eyes closed in manufactured candids. 

Unpacking this phenomenon, Batchen will consider how the desire to be viewed as ‘unseeing’ can be placed in a history of photography, while reflecting on the generative relationship between sight and blindness in photography from 1839 to now. 

Geoffrey Batchen: Eyes Wide Shut - A History of Photography
Saturday 24 October, 2pm
Free, all welcome
Registration essential

Image: 
Claude Brevet ‘François, a teacher in Neuville-les-Dames [with eyes closed]’ 1847.

Free Range sounds, sunny side up. Our final Thursday night sound club for the year is a big fry-up. 

Clocked Out (@clockedout.music) is a duo of restless sonic explorers, Vanessa Tomlinson and Erik Griswold. Working across composition and improvisation, they draw on experimental sound, jazz, and minimalism, often creating site-specific work. 

Scott Tinkler is a trumpeter extraordinaire, poly rhythmic maestro, diminished substitution practitioner, and sharp-edged pointillist. 

Local Painter brings together Kahl Monticone, Eric Liao, and Liam Eaton. Monticone’s usual delicate and understated guitar work is rewired into a noisy conversation with twin guitars and drums. 

Peyo (@p.appadopoulous) performs solo on the piano in a burning energy flow, hypnotic clusters of notes cascading into solid tone blocks. 

Thursday 29 October, 6pm

What if the ways we create knowledge also shape the worlds we can imagine? 

Drawing on feminist thinkers and writers, Janina Gosseye janina.gosseye (Professor of Architecture and the Built Environment, Delft University of Technology) asks who gets access to knowledge—and what might become possible when we move beyond familiar ways of producing it. 

Off Grid 7 explores how architecture and the built environment might be understood differently through new forms of writing, storytelling, and creative practice. 

Gosseye will share examples of experimental writing by feminist scholars, alongside work from her TUDelft seminar, ‘Building Stories’—where masters students use creative methods to question established ideas and imagine alternative ways of understanding our world.

Off Grid 7: Building Stories with Janina Gosseye
Wednesday 21 October, 6pm 

Free, all welcome. 
🔗 Ticket link in bio. 

Gosseye’s visit is supported by the Queensland Architecture research group at QUT.

Off Grid is a series of architecture discussions led by Andrew Wilson, Senior Lecturer in Architecture at University of Queensland, and Andrew Leach, Professor of Architectural History at Queensland University of Technology. 

Image: Max Loeschke, Eva Vlasblom and Lara Walter, 2024.

Container @container_bfs and the IMA present Big Cinema: a program of recent experimental 3D films by Johann Lurf, Victor Van Rossem, and Blake Williams. 

Join us for the screening at New Farm Cinemas @newfarmcinemas 7pm, Tuesday 27 October.

Join exhibition designer and curator Holly Riding for Essay Club No. 9 at the IMA, unpacking Sylvia Sadzinki’s ‘Discomfort, Disruption, Disgust: Queer Feminist Curating and the Affective’ (2026). Sadzinski’s text examines how queer feminist curating operates through affect, emphasising discomfort, disruption, and disgust as politically productive forces.

Holly works at the intersection of public art and purpose-led digital technology to create accessible cultural experiences. They navigate the symbiotic interplay of exhibition design, spatial planning, and inclusive practices as critical drivers of cultural engagement. In this live panel discussion from the @ncca_darwin as part of the @darwinstreetartfestival 10-year celebration, I sit down with the founder David Collins @uncooldaybed and a lineup of artists @george_rose @calebdude.art and Ris Pikala. @tom_gerrard_ hears different perspectives from established muralists to first-timers.

This conversation will inspire you.

We hear from David about the bold moment he pitched a local-run festival to the government, George about being part of four Darwin festivals, Caleb about growing up with the festival since high school and Ris about painting her first public mural.

The real story here: art isn’t just about the finished piece. It’s about the dreams it gives people. It’s about inspiration. It’s about a whole city saying “yes, this matters.”

@rissyrat_ for DSAF2026 💜

Created for the @charlesdarwinuniversity Casuarina Campus bus stop on Orange 1, as part of the new CDU art trail - this mural responds directly to its environment through the use of vibrant orange tones and complementary colours. 

“I wanted the work to bring a sense of energy, warmth and joy to a space that many people move through every day.

My creative process often begins with colour. From there, I explore pattern, rhythm and the relationships that emerge between shapes, lines and spaces. I’m interested in how colours interact with one another, how patterns create movement, and how the spaces between elements become just as important as the elements themselves.

Rather than telling a single story, this mural invites viewers to find their own meanings and connections. The forms can be interpreted in many ways, allowing each person to bring their own experiences, memories and imagination to the work. For me, the mural is a celebration of colour, pattern, place and the different ways we see and make meaning in the world.”

📍 CDU Casuarina Bus Stop

Not many has had a bigger year than Dean Turnley.

‘Actin Tough’ went global, his name travelled with it, and now we play host to one of the city’s biggest homecoming sets.  This will be massive. 🍰

Golden skies. Dancing shadows.

Daylight isn’t the only thing disappearing fast. Get your tickets now via link in bio. 🍰

New music? Yes please! A dig through some of the latest coming from the LTEC lineup. Six recent releases spanning house, techno, electro and a few places in between.

🎶 Slides 

1. DJ PGZ, Lady Shaka, Dolorres, Zaila - Sweat
2. Anetha, Lacchesi - No Pasaràn 
3. Soul Wun - In My Mind
4. William Kiss - Make It Bounce 
5. Jennifer Loveless - Felt That
6. Boys Noize, ZEP - 1+1+1

Bringing together Gunai/Kurnai and Yorta Yorta artist DJPGZ, UK producer KarmaKid, Italian-Australian artist DoloRRes and Brazilia’s Zaila, this is a true global affair. 

Verses ricochet between languages, cultures and continents before Lady Shaka steps in with a commanding rap that raises the stakes. 

Flashing like a wall of paparazzi lights, this is proper club electro.

🎥 YT @ladyshaka

Anetha walks the line between psychedelic and techno with the expertise of a tightrope walker. 

On this collaboration with fellow Parisian Lacchesi, she leans 5 degrees more to the psychedelic side, with sounds tumbling from the speakers in fascinating forms. 

Proper dancefloor fuel.

@anetha 
@mama_told_ya

Take your pick, all three tracks from his recent EP are fire. 

Here, ‘Make It Bounce’ sits somewhere between contemporary tech and old-school house, with enough punch to do damage in both camps. 

Released on Peggy Gou’s Gudu Records, expect this to do serious damage across the upcoming Australian summer dancefloors.

@williamkiss 
@gudurecords

On his debut LP, Kaleidoscope, Soul Win spins vintage deep house and dreamy 90’s trip-hop that’s hard to resist - an affecting listen to say the least. 

Taken from the album, the playful ‘In My Mind’ is Summer-drenched vocal house that could easily bloom from carefree afternoons hanging with friends at Edinburgh Gardens.

@soulwun 
@galleryrecs

If Gerd Janson’s Running Back label wants your record, you’re probably onto something. 

And this is… Nostalgic bliss? Unrequited love? A little whimsical beauty? 

Whatever Jennifer felt was bottled beautifully into this woozy slice of ethereal house. Another singular outing from a singular artist.

@jenniferrloveless 
@runningbackrecords

Fresh from his work with Nine Inch Nails, the German producer returns

That warm, hazy part when everyone’s tuned to the same frequency.   Dial it in. 

LTEC NYD. 🍰

Culture shaping? Trend setting? Era defining? Definitely.

Relevant? Always.

Boys Noize has been dominating dancefloors for two decades - and right now he might be more vital than ever.  
This is big: Legend incoming at LTEC NYD 2027. 👀

latestPosts.caption:
We realized something early…
this was never just about skateboarding.

Since 2015, THE SKATESIDE has worked with over 10,000+ kids across Los Angeles, not just teaching tricks, but helping kids build confidence, resilience, and life skills that carry far beyond the skatepark.

Because what we really care about is
the shy kid finding their voice
the moment they fall and choose to get back up
the friendships that form without trying
the confidence that shows up at school, at home, and in life

That’s what THE SKATESIDE is about.

Over the years, we’ve built programs that meet kids and families where they are
Afterschool programs in partnership with schools and cities
Weekend classes for consistent growth and progression
Seasonal camps during spring, summer, and school breaks
Private lessons for more personalized support and an annual festival @skatesidefest 

And beyond the skatepark, we’ve expanded into storytelling and creativity through our children’s book and brand, @gromlinuniverse , created to inspire imagination, character, and confidence in kids in a whole new way.

But one of the most powerful parts of this journey

We’re now seeing students come full circle
Kids who once stepped on a board for the first time with us
now coming back to help, mentor, and inspire the next generation

That’s bigger than skating
That’s legacy

🗣️ “Skateboarding gave me confidence when I didn’t have it anywhere else. THE SKATESIDE is about giving that same feeling to every kid.” — Lemar

🗣️ “We built this for families to create a space where kids feel supported, safe, and proud of who they’re becoming.” — Elena

We’re not just teaching skateboarding
We’re building people

More kids skating. More confidence. More community.

El Muay Thai de BAUM Fest ha sido protagonista en Mundo Deportivo, que se hace eco de lo vivido este fin de semana en Barcelona.

🥊 “El muay thai se impone al mal tiempo en el BAUM Fest de Barcelona y los espectadores disfrutan del espectáculo.”

A pesar de una edición marcada por la lluvia, cientos de personas se acercaron a la zona de Muay Thai para vivir los combates, las finales y el torneo infantil de Waikhru. Un fin de semana intenso junto a @internacionalgym_official que volvió a demostrar la fuerza que tiene esta disciplina dentro de BAUM Fest.

Gracias a tatuadores, artistas, expositores, marcas, colaboradores, equipos, profesionales y público, por vuestra comprensión y por seguir adelante con nosotros.

Hablaré sobre tatuajes, escarificaciones, piercings, deformaciones y otras formas de transformar el cuerpo, pero también sobre lo que hay detrás de ellas: identidad, pertenencia, estatus, espiritualidad, belleza y memoria.

latestPosts.caption:
The Gliding Award 🤍

@minnierobberds is heading to @glidingbarnacles in Portugal in September 2026.

For over 10 years, The Mingle has shared a special connection with the Gliding Barnacles Festival in Portugal. They’ve become like family – a brother / sister festival to us. So much of our community flows between these two events, and it’s something we’re incredibly proud of.

This year brought one of the most special surprises yet. Before The Mingle, GB founder @euricogoncalves reached out with an idea – to award one SFM surfer a trip to Gliding Barnacles this September. We spoke about how to choose, and landed on something simple: let the surfers decide.

During the event, our surfers were (unknowingly) asked to vote for the person who best embodied the spirit of The Mingle. The prize wasn’t revealed until this moment at Sunday’s prize giving, when Minnie was announced as the recipient of the Gliding Award – chosen by her peers.

Minnie is a Sumner local – a surfer, musician, and all-round beautiful human. She performed at the Friday night street party, competed on Saturday, and spent the weekend commentating. She truly embodies the spirit of these festivals, and we couldn’t be more stoked to see her take this one out.

Thank you @glidingbarnacles ❤️‍🔥

🎥 @williamahunt

Day 3. The Single Fin Mingle 2026 

The finals day that delivered! Kia ora to everyone that made our 12th edition of The Mingle so special and one we will remember for a very long time. LOVESICK has really filled our hearts and we can’t wait to continue to share all the amazing memories from this weekend to keep your hearts swelling until 2027… 

Captured by @williamahunt 

❤️‍🔥

These days, your algorithm is bound to keep serving you more of the same, but @melbfringe goes beyond the black box. This October, the festival is returning with a stacked lineup that re-embraces the weird, wonderful and unexpected.

This year's Curated Program is marked by the tenth edition of Deadly Fringe, featuring a major new participatory installation at Fed Square by Wiradjuri dance artist @joelbraydance, drawing on the campfire as a place of gathering, storytelling and ritual.

✍️ @molly.england 
📸 @alexisalexis1968 
🎨 @rlymcdnld

We are excited to congratulate Georgia Boseley (Central and Eastern Arrernte) for winning the award for Best Emerging Indigenous Artist at Melbourne Fringe for their solo show, ‘Weaving the Everywhen’, currently on show here at KHT!

Georgia’s sculptural work asks audiences to reflect on their relationship with their natural environment and consider a future shaped by Indigenous systems of reciprocity, relation and care for Country. Unsettling our linear understandings of time, the work draws on Indigenous deep history in order to imagine an Indigenous deep future. 

KHT is proud to host this deeply resonant exhibition in the Birraung Building. Come and experience this award-winning exhibition before it closes on 22 November.

—

Installation view of Georgia Boseley (Central and Eastern Arrernte), ‘Weaving the Everywhen’, Koorie Heritage Trust, 29 September – 22 November 2026. Image courtesy of Koorie Heritage Trust. Photo by Christian Capurro, 2026.

The fun hasn't quite finished. Fringe continues with a Ballarat encore 22-25 Oct. These Crowd Pleasers have gotten the audience's tick of approval. Don't take our word for it, take theirs! If you missed them in Melbourne, you've got a second chance to catch them in Ballarat.

Secure your tickets to these Fringe Encore: Ballarat events now.

@visitballarat @visitmelbourne 

Image descriptions in alt text

Incredibly exciting to have won Best Emerging Indigenous Artist at the @melbfringe festival for my exhibition Weaving the Everywhen. The show is open until 22nd November 26. 

Artwork featured: Harakeke Seed Pod (2026) made with @keaneceramics Dark Matter Clay. Image courtesy of Koorie Heritage Trust. Photo by Christian Capurro 2026.

The Melbourne Fringe Living Legend Award is presented to someone who sets a benchmark for excellence in their craft. Those whose artistry continues to inspire the Fringe community.

This year’s Living Legend Award is presented to none other than Laura Milke Garner, an award-winning producer with over 29 years’ experience developing, producing, and touring live performance across comedy, theatre, and cabaret both nationally and internationally. For the past 12 years, she’s also run the MILKE Emerging Producer Award at both Melbourne Fringe and Adelaide Fringe, supporting the next generation of producers. 

Congratulations, and thank you.

Thank you to the supporters who make these awards possible.

京都には、長い時間をかけて受け継がれてきた文化や技術があり、出版や表現に関わるさまざまな人や場所が、それぞれの活動を続けながら独自の文化を育んできました。KABFでは、そうした京都固有の環境とアートブックフェアという場を交差させることで、ここでしか生まれない出会いや交流のあり方を探っていきます。

In May 2027, a new art book fair, the KYOTO ART BOOK FAIR (KABF), will take place in Kyoto.

kyotoartbookfair.com

Since the NY Art Book Fair began in 2006, art book fairs have spread to cities around the world, growing into cultural spaces where makers and readers meet through books.
Kyoto is home to culture and craft passed down over a long span of time, and to diverse people and places involved in publishing and creative expression, each continuing its own work while nurturing a culture of its own. KABF will bring this environment, particular to Kyoto, together with the art book fair, exploring forms of encounter and exchange that can only emerge here.
With each edition, KABF aims to shape a character of its own from the time accumulated in Kyoto and the relationships among its people, and to become a book fair that could only exist in this place.

BETWEEN Spread and Gathering — Singapore

Today is the final day of the first stop of our relay in Singapore. A little belatedly, we’d like to share some scenes from the exhibition at Temporary Unit.

The exhibition brings together 40 books—20 selected in Japan and 20 in Singapore—alongside posters by Singapore-based gideon-jamie, who interpreted the Japanese selection and translated it into a new graphic form.

Throughout the exhibition, many people have spent time with the books, talked around them, and shared their thoughts. We hope to carry these encounters and conversations with us as part of the ongoing record of the project.

The books passed from Japan to Singapore have been joined by new books, words, graphics, and encounters here, and BETWEEN will now continue its journey to the next location.

A huge thank you to Gideon & Jamie, Atelier HOKO, Renée Ting, and Catherine Hu for making this project possible in Singapore, as well as to all the publishers and artists who contributed their books, and everyone who came to visit the exhibition. Thank you for being part of the first stop of BETWEEN!

Today, 19 September, is the final day. Posters by gideon-jamie are also available for purchase at Temporary Unit. If you’re in Singapore, please stop by!

-—

シンガポールでの最初のリレーも、本日が最終日。少し遅くなりましたが、Temporary Unitでの展示の様子をご紹介します。

会場では、日本とシンガポールでそれぞれ選ばれた20冊、計40冊の本と、シンガポールを拠点に活動するgideon-jamieが日本チームの選書を読み解き、ポスターへと翻訳した作品を展示しています。

会期中、たくさんの方が本を手に取り、本を囲んで話し、時間を過ごしてくださいました。こうした本を介した出会いや対話も含めて、このプロジェクトの記録として残していけたらと思います。

日本からシンガポールへ手渡された本に、シンガポールで新たな本や言葉、グラフィック、そして出会いが加わり、BETWEENは次の土地へと旅を続けます。

本日9月19日が最終日です。会場では、gideon-jamieによるポスターも販売しています。お近くの方はぜひTemporary Unitへ！

BETWEEN Spread and Gathering
A Relay Project Across Asian Art Book Fairs

本企画は、現在進行形で育まれているアジアの出版実践の記録を目的に、アジア各地のアートブックフェアを巡回するリレープロジェクトです。選者はアジアのブックデザインを切り口に20冊の本を選び、次の土地へ手渡していきます。選書は「ベスト・オブ」を決めるためのものではなく、その時点での選者の本棚や関心を反映した個人的な視点から行います。

前の土地から受け取った本は、現地のデザイナーが選書を読み解き、ポスターへと翻訳し、現地チームによる新たな選書とともにブックフェアの開催時期にあわせて展示され、さらに次の土地へと旅を続けます。約1年間の巡回を通して、本、言葉、グラフィック、人々の対話が重なり、2027年刊行予定の記録集へと結実していきます。

アートブックフェアは、本プロジェクトの会場であると同時に、その方法（Method）でもあります。単なる展示や販売の場ではなく、本づくりをともに行うための場と捉え、出会い、対話し、翻訳し、手渡していくプロセスそのものを共有し、ともに育てていくことを目指しています。

Episode 1 Singapore

BETWEENの最初の巡回地はシンガポールです 🇸🇬

本日8月30日には、Singapore Art Book Fair（inSGABF）のラジオプログラム「Radio Radio Radio」にて、BETWEENのプロジェクトと、日本・シンガポールで行われた選書についてお話しします。

そしてSGABF翌日の8月31日からは、移転後オープンしたばかりのTemporary Unitにて展覧会を開催します。

会場では、日本とシンガポールでそれぞれ選ばれた20冊、計40冊のアートブックと、シンガポールを拠点に活動するgideon-jamieが日本チームの選書を読み解き、ポスターへと翻訳した作品を展示します。

日本からシンガポールへ本が手渡され、そこで新しい本とグラフィックが加わり、次の土地へと旅を続けていきます。

本をきっかけに、さまざまな出会いや開かれた対話が生まれる機会となれば嬉しいです。

最後にSGABF直前にも関わらず協力してくれたシンガポールの友人たちに心から感謝します。ありがとう。

New exhibition!

@between__spread_and_gathering is a relay project travelling across art book fairs in Asia, documenting publishing practices as they continue to evolve across the region. Through the lens of book design, selectors in each location would choose twenty books from their bookshelves and pass them on to the next location. The selection is not intended to represent each place or define a “best of,” but rather reflects the selectors’ personal perspectives — the books on their shelves and their interests at that particular moment.Books received from the previous location are interpreted by local designers and translated into posters, then exhibited alongside a new selection made by the local team before continuing their journey to the next location. Over the course of this year-long relay, books, words, graphics, and conversations accumulate and intersect, with the process ultimately documented in a publication scheduled for 2027.The first stop of the relay is Singapore. The exhibition at 
Temporary Unit brings together forty art books — twenty selected in Japan and twenty in Singapore — alongside a poster created by gideon-jamie in response to the Japanese selection. We hope the books will become starting points for new encounters and open conversations.This project is organised and initiated by Naoko Higashi (@tokyoartbookfair), Daisuke Kano, Toshiaki Koga, and Yuma Wada, with Atelier HOKO, Catherine Hu, gideon-jamie, and Renée Ting (@singaporeartbookfair) joining for the first stop in Singapore.

TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR（TABF）は、シンガポールで開催されるSingapore Art Book Fair（SGABF）に参加します。

TABFのブースでは、TABFが制作した出版物に加え、TABFゆかりの出展者の皆さんによる本をご紹介します。

Thing Booksが主催するSGABFには、初回を含めこれまで3回参加してきました。毎回、素晴らしい出展者の方々やアートブック、ZINEとの出会いがあり、ウェルカムな雰囲気も心地よく、さまざまなチャレンジからいつもたくさんの刺激をもらっています。

今年はAtelier HOKOをアートディレクターとして迎え、初の「smaller edition」を開催。どのようなアートブックフェア体験になるのか、今から期待しています。毎日“席替え”もあるそうなので、いろいろな出展者の方たちと交流できるのも嬉しいところです。

シンガポールにいらっしゃる方は、ぜひこの実験的なフェアを目撃しに遊びにいらしてください！皆さんとお会いできることを楽しみにしています。

また、8月31日からはTemporary Unitにて、TABFの新しいリレープロジェクト「BETWEEN Spread and Gathering」の展示も開催します。アジア各地のアートブックフェアを巡りながら、本、デザイン、人をつないでいくプロジェクトです。こちらもあわせて、ぜひお越しいただけると嬉しいです！

BOOK?
Atelier HOKO（アトリエ・ホコ）は、2002年に設立されたインディペンデントのリサーチユニットで、現在はシンガポールを拠点に活動しています。本展では、デジタルメディアが広がり、私たちと物理的な世界との関わり方が変化しつつある今、本を読む行為にまつわる人間のふるまいや感覚について、さまざまな「問い」を来場者に投げかけます。本のサイズや形状、紙の質感は、読書体験にどのような影響を与えているのでしょうか。見慣れたソフトカバーの雑誌が、もし豪華なハードカバーだったら？ あるいは、本がページを閉じることを拒んだとしたら？ 素朴な疑問や想像から着想を得た多様なアプローチを通して、本展は「本」という存在をあらためて多角的に見つめ直す機会をひらきます。それは懐古主義ではなく、私たちが「読む」という行為の本質へ立ち返るための試みです。

Congratulations once again to @unbidden_tongues  Thank you for your generous support, @neutral_colors_magazine @new_cover_bookshop 

TABF2025では、新たな才能の発掘と支援を目的に掲げ、全出展者を対象とするアワード「𝙏𝘼𝘽𝙁 𝙏𝙖𝙡𝙚𝙣𝙩 𝘼𝙬𝙖𝙧𝙙」を開催しました。6組の選者が「最も推したい出展者」を1組選出し、それぞれの受賞者には、アーティスト長谷川有里によるTABF特製トロフィーと、選者からの副賞が贈られました。

WEEK 2の選者、NEUTRAL COLORSの加藤直徳さん、加納大輔さんは会場をじっくり見て、オランダの出版社Unbidden Tonguesを選出しました。

「これらは歴史的記念碑でもなければコレクターズアイテムでもない。報告書や婦人科の記録、忘れ去られた視覚詩など、これまで注目されることのなかった言葉の数々を、彼らは拾い上げる。1色のみで印刷された安価な出版物は、広く届けることを可能にし、「招かれざる舌」はあらゆる場所に忍び込む。薄くささやかな冊子に空けられた二つの穴が、この先に重なる厚みを予感させる」加納大輔

「一見すると地味な白い紙が並ぶブース構成に違和感を感じた。穴の位置もおかしい。またか、、、難解なコンセプトを提示されるのかと身構えてしまったからだ。しかしだんだんと意味がわかってくるにつれて、薄い紙たちが束ねられアートブックが現出する。しかもシンプルかつ明快なアートブックとして。これが並んでいることこそが可能性だ。たとえ資金が潤沢でなかったとしても、世界に声を行き渡らせることができる」加藤直徳

そして副賞として、NEUTRAL COLORSの書店NEW COVERでのフィーチャーが決定し、現在Unbidden Tanguesのメインプロジェクトである10冊をご覧いただけます。

TABFの雑踏の中でも、静かに、しかし確かな強さをもって響いていたUnbidden Tongues。
NEW COVERでは、その声が丁寧にすくい上げられ、紹介されています。

TABFでゆっくり見られなかった方、興味を持たれた方、ぜひこの機会にじっくりとご覧ください！

What an unforgettable afternoon at Adore Chef’s Table with Gareth Whitton from Tarts Anon during Ubud Food Festival 2026.

More than 60 pastry chefs, bakers, chocolatiers, and F&B professionals gathered to experience something truly special: three beautiful Tarts Anon-style tarts crafted using Adore Cacao, alongside the official launch of our Bali Single Origin chocolate.

Chef Gareth showcased his creativity by incorporating beautiful Indonesian ingredients into each tart, creating flavors that felt both familiar and exciting. Every bite told a story of craftsmanship, terroir, and thoughtful ingredient selection, making it a truly memorable experience for everyone in the room.

But this event was about more than just delicious desserts.

Throughout the tasting, we also shared something that sits at the heart of Adore: the importance of sustaining Indonesia’s cacao and vanilla farms.

At Adore, our mission goes beyond delivering premium quality chocolate and vanilla. We believe great ingredients begin with healthy farms, empowered farmers, and respect for the environment. Every product we make carries the hard work of many hands behind the scenes: from farm to chef’s table.

We know meaningful impact doesn’t happen overnight, but we believe in taking small steps, consistently.

Because in the end, true quality is not only about flavor, it is also about people, purpose, and sustainability.

Introducing ARUMA. 

Redefining performance through feeling. Engineered to sense every foothold, enabling precise smearing and edging. Soft, responsive, and adaptive, where control and comfort come together.

For @alexandermegos , Siurana is more than just a climbing destination. It’s a place where he has grown as a climber, returning throughout his career to take on some of its most iconic and demanding routes. Over the years, his story has become part of the area’s climbing history and community. 
In 2013, Alex made history on Estado Crítico (9a), completing the world’s first 9a onsight. Just days later, he climbed La Rambla (9a+), one of Siurana’s most celebrated routes, first ascended by Ramón Julián Puigblanque, on his second attempt.
Over the years, Alex continued returning to Siurana. In 2021, he completed three of the La Capella sector’s hardest routes: King Capella, La Furia de Jabalí, and La Capella. In 2024, Alex made the first repeat of Chris Sharma’s Sleeping Lion (9b), a route later climbed by fellow Tenaya athlete Sachi Amma.
Through years of visits, hard climbs, and memorable ascents, Alex has become part of Siurana’s history. This year, we’re excited to welcome him to the @siuranaclimbingfestival

🏓 As part of the 2025 Biennial, 𝑫𝑬𝑺𝑪𝑶𝑳𝑨 invited six young people from São Miguel to reflect on the importance of living according to logics of abundance. Over the course of a year, their artistic creations travelled across all six municipalities of São Miguel as part of a touring exhibition curated and designed by Diogo Sousa and José Amorim.

With a modular and adaptable structure, the exhibition was reconfigured for each of the spaces that hosted it, travelling through Ponta Delgada (@parque.atlantico), Ribeira Grande (@cmribeiragrande), Nordeste (@municipiodonordeste), Furnas (@ambienteacores), Vila Franca do Campo, and Lagoa (@lagoamunicipioacores).

📍The final opportunity to visit 𝑫𝑬𝑺𝑪𝑶𝑳𝑨 is at Convento dos Franciscanos (Santo António), in Lagoa, until 06.11.

—

A exposição foi reconfigurada para cada um dos espaços que a acolheu, passando por Ponta Delgada (@parque.atlantico), Ribeira Grande (@cmribeiragrande), Nordeste (@municipiodonordeste), Furnas (@ambienteacores), Vila Franca do Campo e Lagoa (@lagoamunicipioacores).

🪁 O 𝑫𝑬𝑺𝑪𝑶𝑳𝑨 inaugurou ontem, no Convento dos Franciscanos (Santo António), na Lagoa, o último município de São Miguel a receber a exposição após quase um ano de itinerância pela ilha. 

Apresentado pela primeira vez durante a Bienal de 2025, o projeto desafiou seis jovens de São Miguel a deslocar-se e a “descolar” criativamente, refletindo sobre a importância de vivermos sob lógicas de abundância. As suas criações passaram pelos seis municípios de São Miguel ao longo de 2025 e 2026, numa exposição com curadoria e museografia de Diogo Sousa e José Amorim.

📍 Convento dos Franciscanos (Santo António)
👀 A exposição pode ser visitada até 06.11.

|

𝑫𝑬𝑺𝑪𝑶𝑳𝑨 opened yesterda, at no Convento dos Franciscanos (Santo António), in Lagoa, the final municipality in São Miguel to host the exhibition, following almost a year of travelling across the island.

First presented as part of the 2025 Biennial, the project brought together six young people from São Miguel, inviting them to move and explore as they reflected on the importance of living under a logic of abundance. Their work has travelled across all six municipalities of São Miguel throughout 2025 and 2026, in an exhibition curated and designed by Diogo Sousa and José Amorim.

—
📸 @marianalidl

#BienalWalkTalk #GestosdeAbundância #GesturesofAbundance

𝐑𝐄𝐕𝐈𝐒𝐈𝐓𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐖&𝐓’25
𝐍𝐮𝐧𝐨 𝐏𝐢𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚 / 𝐄𝐱𝐡𝐢𝐛𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧

Nuno Pimenta designed and developed several of the spaces that housed Gestures of Abundance, including 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐚 𝐝𝐚 𝐁𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐥 — a space for information, resting, and informal encounters with the program.

On the ground floor of an abandoned building in the center of Ponta Delgada, Casa da Bienal was developed in collaboration with @spea_birdlife, an organization dedicated to restoring and preserving native ecosystems in the Azores. A living installation with native plants throughout the space, Casa da Bienal was composed of various spaces divided by curtains made from natural fibers: a multipurpose hall for film screenings, lectures, and gatherings.

𝐍𝐮𝐧𝐨 𝐏𝐢𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚 (@nunopimenta_) develops a transdisciplinary practice at the intersection of art and architecture. Working with a strategy of maximum economy of means, his practice draws on the subversion of traditional construction elements and techniques to create social, political, and ecological narratives.

|

Nuno Pimenta concebeu e desenvolveu vários dos espaços que acolheram Gestos de Abundância, entre eles a 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐚 𝐝𝐚 𝐁𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐥 — um espaço de informação, descanso e encontros informais com o programa.

No rés-do-chão de um edifício devoluto no centro de Ponta Delgada, a Casa da Bienal foi desenvolvida em colaboração com a SPEA – Sociedade Portuguesa para o Estudo das Aves, uma organização dedicada à recuperação e preservação dos ecossistemas nativos dos Açores. Em torno de uma instalação viva com plantas nativas pelo espaço, a Casa da Bienal organizou-se numa rede de espaços divididos por cortinas de fibras naturais: uma sala polivalente para projeções, palestras e encontros.

A Anda&Fala é um projeto em constante construção, feito das relações, das conversas, das colaborações e das amizades que lhe dão forma. Celebramos o caminho percorrido, reconhecendo que este processo permanece aberto.

*
Fundada em 2011, a Anda&Fala tornou-se uma estrutura dedicada à criação, programação, mediação e circulação artísticas, desenvolvendo projetos que visam fortalecer a relação entre cultura, território e comunidade. Mais do que uma organização, é uma plataforma de encontro, onde artistas, públicos, parceiros e colaboradores continuam a imaginar e a construir possibilidades em conjunto.

𝐒𝐈𝐍𝐓𝐎𝐍𝐈𝐙𝐀𝐑 – 𝐏𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐬

“Abundance is not something we acquire, it is something we tune into.”

𝐒𝐈𝐍𝐓𝐎𝐍𝐈𝐙𝐀𝐑 is to tune into something. To do so, two entities need to meet on the same frequency: one transmitting, the other receiving — and vice versa.

Curated by Rita Serra e Silva (@_rita_serraesilva) and Rita Westwood (@west_2_wood), the Public Programs of the Biennial 2025 invited everyone to explore 𝐺𝐸𝑆𝑇𝑈𝑅𝐸𝑆 𝑂𝐹 𝐴𝐵𝑈𝑁𝐷𝐴𝑁𝐶𝐸 over two months, through collective experiences that brought artists, communities, and visitors into closer connection with the island of São Miguel.

Across the Biennial, there were guided visits, creative workshops, a volunteering program, and excursions around the island inspired by the Biennial’s projects and open to the general public and school groups, among other activities.

|

“A abundância não é algo que adquirimos, é algo a que nos sintonizamos.”

Para o fazer, são necessárias duas entidades na mesma frequência: uma transmite, a outra recebe — e vice-versa.

Com curadoria de Rita Serra e Silva (@_rita_serraesilva) e Rita Westwood (@west_2_wood), os Programas Públicos da Bienal Walk&Talk 2025 convidaram a explorar 𝐺𝐸𝑆𝑇𝑂𝑆 𝐷𝐸 𝐴𝐵𝑈𝑁𝐷Â𝑁𝐶𝐼𝐴 durante dois meses através de experiências coletivas que aproximaram artistas, comunidades e visitantes da ilha de São Miguel.

Ao longo da Bienal, o programa desenvolveu-se através de visitas guiadas, oficinas criativas, um programa de voluntariado e excursões pela ilha inspiradas nos projetos da Bienal e abertas ao público em geral e a grupos escolares, entre outras atividades.

_

𝐑𝐄𝐕𝐈𝐒𝐈𝐓𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐖&𝐓’25
𝐉𝐨𝐬𝐞́ 𝐏𝐞𝐝𝐫𝐨 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐬, Ocean Rain (2025) & 𝐉𝐨𝐚𝐧𝐚 𝐀𝐥𝐛𝐮𝐪𝐮𝐞𝐫𝐪𝐮𝐞, Grandes Podões (2024)

Drawing from images collected over time across different Atlantic archipelagos, José Pedro Cortes explored impermanence, immersion, and silent observation. Through photography, he traced bodies and infrastructures in dialogue with a subterranean and volcanic cartography, where documentary recording met the poetic potency of an attentive gaze. His landscapes, portraits, and still lifes became visual maps of contemporary life — open, transitory, and unfinished. Joana Albuquerque’s sculptures extend this relationship between body and territory, evoke the shadows of resting bodies at Pesqueiro de Ponta Delgada, stretched out in the sun and water.

𝐉𝐨𝐬𝐞́ 𝐏𝐞𝐝𝐫𝐨 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐬 (@josepedrocortes) is a visual artist who works mainly with photography. His photographs – landscapes, portraits or still lifes – act as a map of visual possibilities that observe contemporary life. Through a personal, poetic and documentary form, his work mirrors a time of constant doubt in the construction of social relationships: impulse or fabrication, vulnerability or strength, the outer layer or something more.

𝐉𝐨𝐚𝐧𝐚 𝐀𝐥𝐛𝐮𝐪𝐮𝐞𝐫𝐪𝐮𝐞 (@joana___albuquerque) is based between Ponta Delgada and Munich. In her practice, through sculpture, objects and performances, she observes and analyses everyday gestures and social practices of her immediate surroundings. She is interested in the relation and interaction between the body and objects, power dynamics, and in the subversion of functionality. In her work there is an admiration for the pointless and things at rest.

_

𝑃𝑟𝑜𝑔𝑟𝑎𝑚𝑠: @fuso.videoarte

FUSO – International Video Art Festival of Lisbon – was part of the Biennial’s program, presenting a selection inspired by the theme Gestures of Abundance, curated by Claire Shea, Fatima Bintou Rassoul Sy, Jesse James, and Liliana Coutinho.

The program was presented at FUSO Lisboa, at @museu_marioneta, and opened FUSO Insular at Igreja do Colégio in Ponta Delgada, inviting audiences on an audiovisual journey through artistic practices that explore the ecologies of relationships between humans and nonhumans, technology and spirituality, myth and the future.

𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝑩𝒆𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒊𝒏 𝑹𝒆𝒍𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏, ro heinrich, 2022, 10’24’’
The thought of Indigenous Brazilian leader Ailton Krenak and the voices of several interlocutors, including Erin Manning, open a meditative space on being as relation — a film that lingers in the trembling edges of difference, touch, and transformation.

𝑩𝒆𝒂𝒔𝒕𝑸𝒖𝒆𝒔𝒕, Kolbeinn Hugi, 2025, 30’ @animal.internet
Combines humour and science fiction to imagine a digital creature entering the ecological simulation GAIANET to configure a server for the Animal Internet — a techno-shamanic delirium where nature and cyberspace become interdependent.

𝑺𝒐𝒚 𝑴𝒖𝒄𝒉, Soya the Cow, 2021, 4’ @soyathecow
A queer, vegan pop manifesto celebrating freedom and the abundance of dissident bodies — human and non-human alike — through music, irony, and the assertion of difference.

|

O FUSO – Festival Internacional de Videoarte de Lisboa – integrou a programação da Bienal, apresentando uma seleção inspirada no tema Gestos de Abundância, com curadoria de Claire Shea, Fatima Bintou Rassoul Sy, Jesse James e Liliana Coutinho.

Apresentado numa sessão do FUSO Lisboa, no @museu_marioneta, e na abertura do FUSO Insular, na Igreja do Colégio, em Ponta Delgada, o programa convidou o público para uma viagem audiovisual por práticas artísticas que exploram as ecologias das relações entre humanos e não humanos, tecnologia e espiritualidade, mito e futuro.

Imagine growing up thinking this was normal:
Your parents dancing until their feet hurt. 
People actually knowing their neighbours. 
Making a new best mate in about four minutes. 
Running around outside all day while a whole bunch of adults are looking out for you.

We think about that a lot when we’re building Morph.
Obviously we want to create an unreal few days. We want incredible music, beautiful spaces, good food, dancing, workshops, ALL of it ✨

But there’s a bigger reason we want kids here too.
We want them to grow up seeing adults play. 
Seeing people help each other. 
Meeting all kinds of humans. 
Feeling like they belong somewhere bigger than their own little family.
And maybe one day they’ll be the ones creating these spaces for us.

That’s a pretty f*cking beautiful thought 💚
For now though, we’ll keep building it for them, and for all of us.

Together we Morph.

📍 MORPH Festival, 25-28th March 2027, Auckland NZ
#nzfestival #wellnessfestival #festival

The Morph 2026 photo gallery is now live 📸

and honestly, scrolling through it is a bit dangerous because suddenly you’re right back there 😍

so many faces. so many ridiculous little moments. so much going on that we didn’t even see at the time.

these are a few of our favourites.

👉🏽 full gallery is up now via the link in bio.

Workshop applications for Morph 2027 are open 🤍
this is your chance to bring YOUR work into the festival.

your practice. your method. your weird little niche. your thing that gets people out of their heads and into the room with each other.

maybe it’s something you’ve taught a hundred times.
maybe it’s something you’re only just ready to share in a bigger way.

If it creates connection, curiosity, movement, learning, play, reflection or a genuine shift in the room, we want you to consider bringing it to Morph.

Apply via the link in bio. All applications close November 1st.

25-28th March 2027
Auckland, NZ

#togetherwemorph

In a world that seems to move faster every year, creating spaces where kids can feel safe enough to be completely free feels VERY important to us 🤍

to run around, get curious, meet new people, to get muddy.
…to just be kids.

one of the things we loved most about the first Morph was watching the little ones become part of it all, not tucked away on the sidelines, but woven into the whole experience 😍

surrounded by familiar faces, new friends, aunties, uncles and a whole lot of humans looking out for one another 🫶🏽

there’s something really special about seeing that kind of freedom and connection happen naturally.

more of this in March.

Morph Festival 2027
📍 Auckland, NZ
#togetherwemorph

Some of our favourite moments from the first Morph were the ones we could never have planned.

And somehow those are always the stories that stick.

We think that’s part of why we’re so excited to do this again. Not because we know exactly what Morph 2027 is going to look like… we don’t.

We’re building the container.

The rest happens when YOU arrive 🤍

Here’s to more moments we’ll probably struggle to explain afterwards.

See you in March 😍🙌🏽 

#togetherwemorph

The end made us pretty emotional, actually 🥹

Because underneath all the different answers, everyone kept coming back to the same things.

The people.
The whenua.
The friendships.
The crew.
The feeling of being somewhere you can just be yourself.

And yeah, of course we love the music. We love the stages, the dancing, the ridiculous outfits...

But somewhere in between all of that is the reason we really keep coming back.

It’s the person you meet at 2am who somehow feels like an old friend.
The conversations you didn’t plan on having.
The people you came with, and the people you leave with.

👉🏽That’s a huge part of WHY we built Morph in the first place.

Not because the world needed another festival.

Because we still believe we need places to gather like this.

And hearing people say it back to us in their own words... yeah. That got us 🤍

Here’s to doing it all again in 2027!

latestIgtvVideos.title: Step-Up challenge by @mymizu.co
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
#Repost @mymizu.co 
・・・
地球を大切にするのはもちろん、自分を大切にすることも忘れてはいけません😌❤️

先日、mymizuメンバーで 日本国内で昨年自殺で失われた21,081人の命に哀悼の意を表すために、21,081歩歩きました。

この日メンバーでメンタルヘルスについて話し合ったことを少し紹介します🌼

🌿体の健康と違い、メンタルヘルスは目に見えないことが多い。だからこそ自分と向き合い、自分に合ったセルフアを大切にすることが大事。

🌿相手に “元気？”と聞いて、時間をとってその人の返しを聞くだけでも、大きな違いが生まれる。

🌿誰もが周りからのサポートを必要としている！

@telljapan この機会を作っていただきありがとうございます！

To be able to take care of the planet, let’s remember to look after ourselves as well😌❤️

A group of mymizu team members got together to walk 21,081 steps in honour of the 21,081 lives lost to suicide last year in Japan.

As we walked around and took in the fresh air, we discussed how…

​​🌿 Different to physical injuries, mental health issues are often invisible. It’s important to check in with ourselves, and find ways to take care of ourselves

🌿 Just asking ‘how are you?’ and taking time to listen properly can make an enormous difference

🌿 At the end of the day, we all need support from others!

Thank you @telljapan for putting this wonderful initiative together!

Announcing the 2026 #TELL Okinawa Yoga and Wellness Festival! 🧘🏽‍♂️🧘🏻‍♀️🧘🏿

This festival will bring together #yoga, #mindfulness, and family-friendly activities to create a day of connection, slowing down, and prioritizing our well-being. This year, the festival will not only have yoga classes, vendors, and a kids' zone; we have also added a couple of workshops and other types of fitness classes! 

This year, we are excited to announce a free workshop led by one of our TELL clinicians: Open Studio, a TELL Clinician-Led Art Workshop for Children. An opportunity for unstructured creative expression. Participants will be encouraged to reflect on their creative desires and explore them with available materials in a safe manner while being mindful of their choice of media and content. 

This activity supports independent leisure and helps develop self-efficacy, while also practicing modulating thoughts and feelings through nonverbal communication.

**** This is not an art therapy session

**** You must register ahead of time; sign-ups on the day of will not be permitted due to limited supplies and space. To register, please email outreach.okinawa@telljp.com. The registration deadline is November 1st. 

**** Open to children ages 6-17 who do not require extensive supervision for safety

**** A parent or guardian must remain within event grounds for children under 16. Come to Yaeshima Park in Okinawa City between 10:00 and 16:00 on November 15th; entry is free! Stop by the TELL booth to enter the Raffle; our generous instructors and vendors have donated some great prizes.

For the most up-to-date information, please check the TELL Facebook page under the Yoga and Wellness Festival event discussion. If you have any questions, please email outreach.okinawa@telljp.com

If you couldn't join us in person, you can still help TELL make a difference in Japan's #mentalhealth landscape. By raising funds, you help spread awareness and start conversations. 

Your support is invaluable! Donate today at www.donorbox.org/step-up-campaign-2026 and help drive positive change.

A big thank you to our fabulous volunteers, and to everyone who stopped by our booth at @rainbowfesta_kansai this past weekend! It was wonderful to connect and talk with you all 🫶 

🏳️‍🌈 Next stop: Kyushu Rainbow Pride this weekend 🏳️‍⚧️ - come say hi if you're in Fukuoka!

Huge thank you to our #StepUpChallenge community for showing up this year! You truly made a difference in your communities. Thank you again for stepping up for #mentalhealth! We hope to see you at future TELL mental health events 🎉

Check out the TELL website for more mental health resources https://telljp.com/

On October 10th, World Mental Health Day, we came together with members of the community in Okinawa for a sunset walk, as we wrapped up this year's Step Up Challenge. Thank you for joining us in remembering those who died by suicide last year, and in starting the conversation about mental health and suicide prevention. 

To learn more about TELL's service, and our upcoming events, visit our website (link in bio ⬆). 

If you or someone you know is struggling, or needs to talk, please reach out to our Lifeline - you don't have to be alone.

📞0800-300-8355 (toll free phone)
💬telljp.com/lifeline
Last Saturday we held our Tokyo Community Walk - thank you for coming out to walk with us and raise awareness of mental health, suicide prevention, and the support available for anyone struggling 💙

Today is World Mental Health Day 🌍, and it's the last day to buy tickets for this year's #StepUpChallenge. Step by step, we're raising awareness of suicide prevention and sharing a message of hope and support. Sign up by 11:50pm tonight and make a difference. Join us at www.tellevents.org!

Thank you to @staysection_l for the photo from their walk this year!

Ready to challenge yourself for a meaningful cause? The TELL #StepUpChallenge invites you to use the number 19,188 in a creative way. Register by October 10th to join us in remembering those lost and supporting mental health. Register now at www.tellevents.org and let’s #StepUp together!

Contact 02 7813 0420 or gallery@mcontemp.com with any queries, or visit mcontemporary.com for more.

UPCOMING EXHIBITION | Agneta Ekholm 'Equilibrium'

26 September - 24 October
Artist Talk & Opening Event: Saturday, 26 September, 2–4pm

In 'Equilibrium', Agneta holds motion at the edge of stillness. Moving into a deeper tonal register of maroons, muted blues, arctic teals and soft oxide warmth, the new body of work explores the quiet tension between drift and restraint, light and shadow, emergence and dissolution.

Built through Agneta's slow process of layering, dissolving and re-forming, each painting exists in a suspended state, where movement is felt rather than seen and opposing forces coexist without resolution.

Join us at the gallery for Agneta’s artist talk, joined by Malcolm Greenwood, on Saturday, 26 September from 2–4pm. RSVP via DM or email gallery@mcontemp.com

UPCOMING EXHIBITION | Malcolm Greenwood 'Vessels and Faces'

26 September - 24 October
Artist Talk & Opening Event: Saturday, 26 September, 2 - 4pm

‘Vessels and Faces’ brings together two recurring elements in Greenwood's practice, united by an enduring exploration of form, surface, balance and variation.

Drawing on fifty years of making, Greenwood explores how the smallest shifts in proportion, curve and symmetry can transform the presence of a familiar form. Moving between sculptural vessels and a new group of ceramic faces, the exhibition considers repetition and difference, individuality and connection, and the character found within subtle imperfection.

Join us at the gallery for Greenwood's artist talk, joined by Agneta Ekholm, on Saturday, 26 September from 2 - 4pm. RSVP via DM or email gallery@mcontemp.com.

A closer look at 'VF X', featured in Malcolm Greenwood's exhibition 'Vessels and Faces', and 'Driftviel' featured in Agneta Ekholm's exhibition 'Equilibrium', on view at .M Contemporary until 24 October.

UPCOMING EXHIBITION | Laura Kennedy 'My Worst Nightmare Is That My Daughter Ends Up Becoming A Disney Princess'

31 October - 14 November
Artist Talk: Saturday, 7 November, 2 - 4pm

Laura Kennedy's upcoming exhibition explores the complexities of motherhood, mortality and the stories we tell ourselves about love, loss and happily ever after.

Drawing on the familiar narratives of Disney princesses, Kennedy challenges idealised notions of femininity and motherhood, particularly the recurring absence of the maternal figure. Informed by her own experience of illness and becoming a mother, her latest body of work combines humour, vulnerability and irreverence to confront the anxieties, contradictions and unspoken realities of parenthood.

Join us at .M Contemporary for an artist talk with Laura Kennedy on Saturday, 7 November, from 2 - 4pm, as she shares the inspiration and personal stories behind her latest body of work. RSVP via DM or email gallery@mcontemp.com.
