ARTIST IN FOCUS | Jane Guthleben

Reimagining the tradition of still life through a distinctly Australian lens, Jane Guthleben brings native flora and fauna into vivid focus. Drawing on Dutch Golden Age painting, botanical collections and natural history archives, her works celebrate the colour, texture and diversity of the Australian environment while exploring our changing relationship with the natural world.

🌎🧤 Giving back to the outdoors, one bag at a time.

During Flash Foxy's Mini Fest on October 4, participants took a break from their climbing workshop to come together for a community cleanup at Mohonk Preserve, helping care for the trails and landscapes that support recreation, adventure, and connection to nature.

Participants joined Mohonk Preserve staff Andrew Reynolds, Senior Manager of Volunteer Programs; Cheryl Elsinger, Managing Ranger & Trailhead Operations; Justin Key, Associate Director of Facilities & Grounds; and Carmen Acuna, Ranger in removing litter and caring for the lands we all share.

Stewardship takes many forms, and every piece of trash removed helps protect the health and beauty of the landscape for visitors, wildlife, and future generations.

💚 Thank you to Flash Foxy and everyone who participated in this cleanup and demonstrated that caring for the outdoors is part of every adventure.

📸 Photos by Mohonk Preserve Volunteer Photographer Giuseppe Narzisi

#MohonkPreserve #FlashFoxy #VolunteerStewardship #ProtectWhatYouLove #LeaveItBetter.

🍂October is one of the most exciting months of the year for the climbing community in the Gunks.

We're looking forward to welcoming climbers from near and far as both Flash Foxy Mini Fest (October 2-4) and GunksFest x Gunks Climbers' Coalition (October 9-12) bring people together to build new skills, share knowledge, and strengthen connections within the climbing community. From climbing clinics and educational workshops to panel discussions, adventure films, guest speakers, and community gatherings, these events celebrate the many ways people connect through climbing while experiencing the unique landscapes of the Shawangunk Ridge.

As the steward of these climbing landscapes, Mohonk Preserve is proud to support opportunities that inspire connection to nature, stewardship, and community. We know the cliffs, carriage roads, and trails will be busy, vibrant, and full of energy, and we can't wait to see people enjoying this special place together💚

Interested in attending? Visit the event websites or check out the tagged accounts in this post to learn more about schedules, registration, and programming.

If you're visiting the Gunks this month, please help protect the places that make these experiences possible. Stay on designated trails, respect wildlife, pack out everything you bring in, and follow Leave No Trace principles. Small actions make a big difference in protecting the cliffs, forests, and habitats we all love.
Have a great climb, look out for one another, and enjoy an amazing month in the Gunks! ✨

📸 Portraits of the climbing community by Mohonk Preserve Volunteer Photographer A. Jesse Jiryu Davis, including Gunks guide Dustin Portzline

#MohonkPreserve #TheGunks #ClimbingCommunity #LeaveNoTrace #RockClimbing

⚡️Stage One: Alternate Channels Residency⚡️⁠
⁠
Inaugural recipient Mara Schwerdtfeger @mara.mara.mara recently completed Stage One of the Alternate Channels Residency with Brand X at the City of Sydney Creative Studios. ⁠
⁠
Alongside a choir of collaborators, Mara spent five-days at the studios exploring the early stages of her project ‘Tectonics’, a choral work that considers the tensions and resonances created by seismic energy. The team spent time in harmony, and disharmony, playing with auto-tune and vocal arrangements which were created through the mapping of the tectonic plates themselves. ⁠
⁠
The week culminated in an intimate showing as Mara presented her early-stage discoveries, laying the groundwork for Stage Two of her residency which will take place at Soft Centre @soft_centre allowing for further development and future presentation. ⁠
⁠
Collectively, the room was captivated by Mara’s fascinating work, and we can’t wait to watch ‘Tectonics’ continue to develop and evolve all the way to Stage Three of the Alternate Channels Residency which will be hosted by Performance Space @performancespace. ⁠
⁠
Collaborators:⁠
Melisa Bester @headaches.cure⁠
Sophia Carey @sofifififif⁠
Elise Nolte @elisenolte ⁠
⁠
Images by Jones King @joneskingphotography ⁠
⁠
Alternate Channels is supported by the NSW Government through @creatensw in partnership with Soft Centre, Performance Space and Brand X

SOFT CENTRE’s CEO @jemma_amalie is heading to Taipei this week for TMEX 🇹🇼 Catch her speaking alongside SC alum @corin.ileto + @meuko_meuko and GLOWBALL founder @sonia_calico, chatting about Australian arts ecologies and our place in the global electronic music circuit. Drop her a line if you’re in town!

We’re delighted to welcome Mara Schwerdtfeger @mara.mara.mara as the inaugural recipient of the Alternate Channels Residency.

Mara is a composer and curator, working across live performance, film, dance and exhibition contexts, she cultivates an intuitive approach to sound-making, uncovering emotional depth in the details of everyday sound.

Alternate Channels Residency is a new partnership between Brand X, SOFT CENTRE @soft_centre and Performance Space @performancespace that invests in an ambitious experimental live artwork through a multi-stage development pathway.

Mara will develop Tectonics, a new choral work that considers the tensions and resonances caused by seismic energy. Fifteen voices, one for each tectonic plate, slide through intervals and push against Auto-Tune to create constant movement and slipping harmony.

During the Brand X residency, Mara and collaborators will workshop different arrangements for using Auto-Tune in a choir setting and practise different techniques to create specific vocal effects that simulate tectonic movement.	
 
Alternate Channels is supported by the NSW Government through Create NSW, in partnership with Soft Centre, Performance Space and Brand X.

La discapacidad no es el conflicto ni el desenlace en BEAUTY. Es el punto de partida de una historia colectiva sobre deportistas que se mueven, compiten, viajan y construyen comunidad.

Nos entusiasma dar la bienvenida a BEAUTY, dirigida por Eduardo Muñoz y José del Corral, y producida por @toma_cafe_films 

El documental sigue a Alejandro Marín, ingeniero mecánico y referente en ortoprótesis, en su llegada a Vigo para hablar sobre inclusión y deporte adaptado en O Marisquiño, uno de los principales festivales de cultura urbana de Europa.

Durante cuatro días en la playa de Samil, Alejandro se encuentra con skaters y riders de BMX adaptado de todo el mundo. Entre ellos están Marcelo Lusardi, Julián Molina, Dan Butler, Santiago Lozano, Ryusei Ohuchi, Vinicius Sardi, Ítalo Romano y Daniel Amorinha.

Cada uno tiene una relación diferente con la discapacidad y los deportes de acción. Juntas, sus experiencias componen un retrato más amplio de la identidad, el movimiento, la representación y la importancia de encontrar a otras personas que comprendan lo que vives.

En lugar de presentar a sus protagonistas a través de los relatos convencionales de adversidad y superación, BEAUTY se centra en quiénes son, qué hacen y la comunidad que han creado alrededor del skate y el BMX.

We’re peering behind the curtains to meet some of the artists making bold new work for this year’s Junction 👀

Up next is Travis Hennessy, whos show @zoeskillerinstinct opens tonight! 

+ describe what makes a killer thriller: 
Mystery, murder, mayhem, melodies and music and a killer Queen ready to take on the world! 

+ tell us about your practice:
This year has been busy locally with my work at Black Box Theatre Co and as MD for LC’s production of We Will Rock You. I also composed the piano score for Mudlark Theatre’s Enough before heading to Syd for our first season of ZKI. I first started writing songs when I was in my teens so I’ve been a composer now for about 30 years, but this is the first time I have composed for the Cabaret format.

+ what makes creating in lutruwita so special/different? 
Tassie artists take our creative practice very seriously. We have dedicated audiences who appreciate the craft, so when creating works for local audiences it’s important that we really honour that shared love of theatre and really leave no stone unturned as we create a work that’s deserving of people’s time and money. That’s definitely been front-of-mind for us and I can safely say that our lutruwita has never seen anything like this before!! 

+ who is Zoe? [from Zoe’s Killer Instinct]
Zoe is eternal. A superstar – of course – but she is so much more than that. She is the aurora and the eclipse. A force of nature who bestows her light on only those she deems worthy. And if you are unworthy? Then heaven (or anyone) help your black little hearts! 

+ describe your show in 3 emojis
❤️🔪🎹

+ what makes Tasmanian theatre so unique?
I think there is always a level of fearlessness that drives theatre in Tas, especially in the creation of new work. We never take for granted the opportunity to create and share and so I think that allows makers to take more risks and swing a bit wider and push the boundaries. That’s certainly what we’ve done with ZKI and the work is so much better for it!

MXGPU, the collaborative project of Moullinex and GPU Panic, release ‘Live Over Porto’, a full-length live set captured during their stunning performance at Primavera Sound Porto 2026. Performed suspended above the festival dancefloor, ‘Live Over Porto’ expands MXGPU’s distinctive 360º live format into one of their most ambitious performances to date.

the full performance is yours now.

with love, 

mxgpu

Long time friend of Astral People, @joshuaamour 
has just signed to Astral People Recordings and released his debut single and visualiser for ‘Don’t Let Go’ !!

Meanjin/Brisbane-based producer and DJ Joshua Amour has worked closely with the Astral Roster throughout the years, from opening on tour with Genesis Owusu for Cosmo’s Midnight to later working on tracks with the cosmos boys! 🚀

Stuttering to life with a jittery, 2-step inflected beat, bursts of deflated synthetic horns and a shifting waterfall of chopped-and-screwed vocal samples, ‘Don’t Let Go’ is Amour’s love letter to the wistful, subdued syncopation of early 2010’s post-dubstep

🤯 Well that was special...

After two years of setbacks we finally got to celebrate our birthday in the best fashion possible. It always is an absolute privilege to be given the 🔑 keys to possibly the most recognised venue in the world? We've said throughout that these parties were an ode to our city. Nothing says Sydney more than the Opera House (It's quite nice on the eyes too). A HUGE thank you to the @sydneyoperahouse and all of their team who worked tirelessly to help us realise our vision. Thank you for trusting us and allowing us to put what are effectively "outsider" music scenes in your home. 🌏

We humbly think we brought together some of the most cutting edge artists in music and, wow, did they deliver! Two nights that uplifted, inspired and left us in awe. Headlined by some truly mind-boggling internationals, but just as impressively, stacked with homegrown talent proving our scene is well and truly world class. We thank @yussefdayes @hiatuskaiyote @mildlife_ @jitwam @bumpymusic_ @dameeeela @jay1 @s1mbamusic @youngnlipz @barkaa__ @senatorbriggs @arnofaraji @hoodzyy @munasib____ . Thank you for sharing your art with us. Every single act from open to close was brilliant.

Thank you to @darkcinema for further reimagining the special setting with your visuals ✨

Finally let us reiterate - This was AN ODE TO OUR CITY - Thank you to every single person who came through over the two nights. We love all of your beautiful smiles. A further thank you to everyone we've met along the way. Without you we're nothing. It's cheese to say but you really are the key to what makes Astral People so special. We continue to evolve and shapeshift but the memories on this journey is exactly what this is all about. We are humbled by your support over the years. Thank you from the bottom of our hearts. Here's to 11 more years of new friends and memories. We're not going anywhere! 💗

🇦🇺 Things to Do in Hobart This Weekend ❤️
Not sure what to do this weekend? Here’s an easy Hobart day out 👇

🛍️ Start Saturday at Salamanca Market — grab a coffee, try some local food and wander through the stalls.

🏘️ Walk through Battery Point — beautiful old houses, little streets and plenty of photo spots.

🌊 Explore the waterfront — take your time around Constitution Dock and enjoy the harbour views.

⛴️ Catch the ferry to Bellerive — sometimes the journey itself has one of the best views of Hobart.

⛰️ Head up kunanyi / Mount Wellington — if the weather behaves 😂, the views are incredible.

🎨 Visit MONA — because no Hobart weekend list is complete without something a little weird.

🌅 Finish with sunset somewhere by the water — simple, free and one of my favourite ways to enjoy Tasmania.

The best thing about Hobart? You really don’t need a huge plan to have a great weekend. ❤️

📌 Save this for your next weekend in Hobart and send it to someone who needs plans!

DEKEL OPEN TO CLOSE - TICKET LINK IN BIO! 🔥
We’re closing out our 10th anniversary year the only way it could — with DEKEL , open to close, for six and a half hours straight.

There are only a handful of artists who know how to unite a crowd like this — to bring an entire dancefloor together as one, to align a room fully into the moment. Dekel is one of them.

Dekel isn’t just headlining this one. He’s played five Wild Horses festivals, and this November will mark his sixth. His sound has become part of what Wild Horses sounds like — woven into the sonic signature that’s carried this festival through a decade. 
There’s no better way to close our 10th anniversary chapter than with an artist we resonate with this deeply. Now he takes over an entire night, start to finish, no one else on the decks.

This will be the final event of our 10th anniversary year, and one of the biggest city shows Wild Horses has ever staged — inside a room built for sound. Northcote Theatre has hosted some of Melbourne’s most legendary events and artists, with soaring ceilings and acoustics few venues can touch. It’s also the first time a psychedelic production of this scale will take over this stage: full lighting design, immersive projection, and a sound system as clear as it gets.

Expect a night unlike anything Wild Horses has done before — one artist, one journey, six and a half hours, and a production to match the occasion.

THE FULL LINEUP HAS LANDED. ❤️
10 years of Wild Horses… and these are the sounds and artists joining us to celebrate it.

From artists who have been part of our story over the years, to some making their first journey into the wild — internationals, locals, old favourites and plenty we’ve been waiting a long time to bring together.

Across three days, multiple stages and many different corners of psychedelic and electronic music, this is what November is going to sound like.

And yes… there’s still one 10 Year Anniversary Surprise hiding in there 👀
We’re incredibly proud of this one and even more excited to finally share it with you.
Who are you most excited to see in the wild?

As we get closer to celebrating 10 years of Wild Horses, we wanted to share a few words about what has always been at the heart of what we do. ❤️🐎

Wild Horses began in 2016 as a small gathering of just 500 people on a vineyard. What started with a shared love for music, nature and bringing people together has grown organically into one of Australia’s few truly independent festivals of its kind.

Ten years later, we’re still proudly Australian-owned and operated, independently funded and without a single sponsor. We’ve built Wild Horses from the ground up, staying true to our vision and growing alongside the beautiful community that’s supported us.

From the beginning, we’ve followed our own musical direction, supporting artists and sounds that were barely known in Australia at the time and watching them become part of today’s psychedelic music scene.

We’ve welcomed artists from around the world, many returning year after year, becoming friends and part of the Wild Horses family. We’ve always chosen our artists for their music, their character and what they bring to our community.

Beyond the music, we’re proud of our contribution to regional Victoria. Festivals like ours bring thousands of visitors and valuable income to surrounding towns, local businesses, accommodation providers and suppliers. We’re committed to continuing that support for Australian businesses and rural communities.

Wild Horses has always been about leaving everyday life behind for a few days, reconnecting with nature, losing yourself in the music and sharing unforgettable moments with people from all walks of life.

Everyone who comes with an open heart and respects those around them is welcome.

Ten years on, our purpose hasn’t changed.

Music. Art. Freedom. Connection. Respect.

That’s the Wild Horses we’ve always believed in, and the one we’ll continue to build together. ❤️🐎

latestPosts.caption:
Festival week is here!

Taman Baca is being transformed, the shelves are filling, and more than 200 writers and thinkers are converging on Ubud for days of bold conversation, spirited debate and stories that bring us together.

For a first taste of what’s in store, watch our #UWRF26 trailer with Founder and Director Janet DeNeefe. Then head to our website to meet the voices we can’t wait to share with you, explore conversations that will captivate you, and discover performances that will stay with you long after the final bow. You will also find tickets, practical details and everything else you need to plan your visit there too.

See you at the Festival!

Cinematography by Niskala Studio

Pekan festival telah tiba!

Taman Baca sedang bertransformasi, rak-rak buku mulai terisi, dan lebih dari 200 penulis serta pemikir tengah menuju Ubud untuk hari-hari penuh percakapan yang berani, perdebatan yang hidup, dan kisah-kisah yang menyatukan kita.

Untuk mencicipi apa yang menanti, saksikan trailer #UWRF26 bersama Pendiri dan Direktur Janet DeNeefe. Lalu kunjungi situs web kami untuk mengenal para suara yang tak sabar kami perkenalkan kepada Anda, menjelajahi percakapan yang akan memikat Anda, dan menemukan pertunjukan yang akan terus membekas jauh setelah tirai ditutup. Di sana, Anda juga akan menemukan tiket, informasi praktis, dan semua yang Anda perlukan untuk merencanakan kunjungan.

Sampai jumpa di Festival!

Drawn from a Sanskrit philosophy, we are thrilled to announce the theme for our 2026 festival: Samarasā: Awareness. Empathy. Action.

Join us between 21 and 25 October for four days of compelling, challenging, and honest discussions, guided by the theme that emphasises the harmony between Citta (mind), Rasa (heart), and Karsa (action). We will reflect on how thought, feeling, and action can exist in harmony, with awareness bringing clarity, empathy building connection, and action turning insight into purpose.

We are also thrilled to reveal this year’s artwork by emerging Balinese artist Wayan Aris Sarmanta, a young talent whose work originates from his hometown’s famous Batuan painting style. We hope you can become tangled up in the unified image of mythical creatures and landscapes he has created.

Don’t forget to purchase your 4-Day Festival Pass! Head to ubudwritersfestival.com/tickets to secure yours.

—

Terinspirasi dari filsafat Sanskerta, kami dengan antusias mengumumkan tema festival tahun 2026: Samarasā: Awareness. Empathy. Action.

Bergabunglah bersama kami pada 21 hingga 25 Oktober untuk rangkaian diskusi yang menggugah, menantang, dan lugas, yang berpijak pada gagasan tentang harmoni antara Citta (pikiran), Rasa (perasaan), dan Karsa (tindakan). Kita akan merefleksikan bagaimana pikiran, perasaan, dan tindakan dapat berjalan selaras, di mana kesadaran menghadirkan kejernihan, empati membangun keterhubungan, dan aksi mengubah pemahaman menjadi langkah nyata.

Kami juga dengan senang hati memperkenalkan karya seni tahun ini oleh seniman muda Bali, Wayan Aris Sarmanta, talenta muda yang karyanya berakar dari gaya lukisan khas Batuan di kampung halamannya. Semoga Anda dapat turut larut dalam jalinan imaji makhluk mitologis dan lanskap yang ia ciptakan.

Amankan Festival Pass 4 hari Anda! Klik ubudwritersfestival.com/tickets dan dapatkan tiket Anda hari ini.

It’s less than two weeks to the Festival, and the extensive #UWRF26 programme is live, bringing together prize-winning writers at the height of their careers, electrifying debut authors, groundbreaking journalists, commanding poets, and literary masterminds, in a vibrant celebration of reading and writing in all its forms, right here in Ubud.

Get the 4-Day Festival Pass, giving you full access to every session across all four days, or choose a 1-Day Festival Pass for unlimited access to the main programme on the day that suits you best.

Head over to ubudwritersfestival.com/tickets (or link in bio).

—

Kurang dari dua minggu lagi sampai Festival, dan seluruh program #UWRF26 telah tersedia,  menghadirkan para penulis peraih penghargaan di puncak karier mereka, penulis debut yang memukau, jurnalis-jurnalis inovatif, para penyair yang memikat, dan para pemikir sastra terkemuka, dalam sebuah perayaan membaca dan menulis yang penuh semangat, dalam segala bentuknya, di sini, di Ubud.

Dapatkan 4-Day Festival Pass, memberikan Anda akses penuh ke setiap sesi selama empat hari penuh, atau pilih Tiket Festival 1 Hari untuk akses tak terbatas ke program utama pada hari pilihan Anda.

Retret ini ditujukan bagi penulis yang sedang memulai buku baru atau mengembangkan naskah. Anda akan mendapatkan waktu khusus untuk menulis, bimbingan dari ahli, serta masukan pribadi, diiringi suara deburan ombak.

A bold, safe space where every voice shines.

Sebuah panggung dan ruang aman dimana kami merangkul semua suara.

Celebrate the closing night party of the 2026 Festival at Taman Baca, the Main Festival Hub, with an evening of readings, performances and dance, bringing writers, artists and audiences together.

Rayakan malam penutupan Festival 2026 di Taman Baca, pusat Festival utama, dengan malam penuh pembacaan karya, pertunjukan, dan tarian yang mempertemukan penulis, seniman, dan penonton.

Poetry and music are fruits of the same tree. Verse united with voice creates music on the page and is transformed in performance; where there is rhythm and melody, there is poetry. In the grounds of Honeymoon Garden, under the stars and in the shadow of an almighty statue of Shiva, poets and musicians gather as verse takes on rhythm, from song to spoken word to hip-hop, chasing themes of nature, identity and emotion. 

In this magical setting, artists from across the globe collide, with indigenous music meeting contemporary spoken word for a night charged with reflection. Meanwhile, two empires meet in the garden kitchen: Chef Aman Lakhiani’s Lamuri brings the deep spice of South India face to face with the fire of Sumatra, cauldrons steaming as the poets take the stage. Chilled drinks and food are on sale throughout the evening.

📍 Honeymoon Garden
🗓️ Saturday, 24 October
⏰ 8 PM
🎟️ IDR 100,000
➡️ Book Now tinyurl.com/UWRF26AfterDark

Puisi dan musik adalah buah dari pohon yang sama. Larik yang menyatu dengan suara menciptakan musik di atas kertas dan bertransformasi saat dipentaskan; di mana ada irama dan melodi, di situ ada puisi. Di halaman Honeymoon Garden, di bawah langit berbintang dan dalam naungan patung Siwa yang agung, para penyair dan musisi berkumpul saat larik-larik puisi menemukan iramanya, dari lagu hingga spoken word dan hip-hop, menyusuri tema alam, identitas, dan emosi. 

Dalam suasana magis ini, para seniman dari berbagai penjuru dunia saling bertemu, musik tradisi berjumpa dengan spoken word kontemporer, untuk sebuah malam yang sarat perenungan. Sementara itu, dua kekaisaran bertemu di dapur taman: Lamuri karya Chef Aman Lakhiani mempertemukan rempah pekat khas India Selatan dengan api Sumatra, kuali-kuali mengepul saat para penyair naik ke panggung. Minuman dingin dan makanan tersedia untuk dibeli sepanjang malam.

Samarasā: Awareness. Empathy. Action. Two days to go, and we turn to the second: EMPATHY. 

Rooted in Rasa, the heart, empathy is what builds connection. Step into someone else’s world. Listen closely, disagree with care and leave a little changed. Bring a friend, bring your curiosity and join the conversations that connect us.

The countdown is on. The Festival Main Programme begins 22 October.

🎟️ Get your #UWRF26 tickets now: ubudwritersfestival.com/tickets

The annual Poetry Slam is one of the Festival’s most sizzling events. From global poets to local sensations, who will win the crowd? In this event, we unite writers from around the world to slam, spin and interweave their original words in a fiery battle, judged by a glittering array of global poets. 

With one poet to be crowned the Festival’s 2026 Poetry Slam Champion, this celebration of the spoken word is not to be missed.

⏰ 7.30 PM

Poetry Slam tahunan adalah salah satu acara paling membara di Festival. Dari penyair mancanegara hingga bintang lokal, siapa yang akan memikat penonton? Dalam acara ini, kami mempertemukan para penulis dari berbagai penjuru dunia untuk membawakan, merangkai, dan menjalin kata-kata orisinal mereka dalam sebuah pertarungan yang berapi-api, dinilai oleh deretan penyair dunia yang gemilang. 

Dengan satu penyair yang akan dinobatkan sebagai Juara Poetry Slam Festival 2026, perayaan seni kata lisan ini sayang untuk dilewatkan.

The centre of Ubud gathers under the stars, beneath the watchful gaze of Tjokorda Gde Agung Sukawati, as we open the 2026 Festival in an extravaganza of dance, music and spoken word. Free, open to all, and a celebration of everything a story can do.

Samarasā: Awareness. Empathy. Action. Three ideas, three days to go, and we begin with the first: AWARENESS. 

Rooted in Citta, the mind, awareness is where clarity begins. Open your eyes to the stories that shape us and the voices still waiting to be heard. From 21 October, writers, thinkers and readers from across Indonesia and the world gather in Ubud for five days of conversation, debate and discovery. 

Your seat is waiting. The Festival Main Programme begins 22 October.

TÁ NO AR O LINE-UP COMPLETO! 🪩

Mais de 12 horas de festival em 3 palcos e mais de 30 artistas. DÁ PRA TUUU?! 

A 23ª edição do No Ar Coquetel Molotov crava mais um line-up de curadoria afiada, diversidade, sonho e realização.

No dia 28 de novembro, a apoteose do festival acontece descentralizada em cada show, em cada palco, numa grande celebração da cultura e da música independente, brasileira e gringa.

Conectado à própria essência, o Coquetel Molotov segue sem medo de se transformar e de criar possibilidades. Porque a gente é isso: um espaço pra todo tipo de som. Do pop ao rap, do funk ao frevo, do rock experimental à eletrônica.

Esperamos por vocês, vibrando em muitas e deliciosas frequências. 🔥

D’Leesa viralizou nas redes sociais brasileiras este ano, e não foi por acaso. A artista transforma qualidade sonora em arte e, em novembro, desembarca para sua primeira apresentação no Brasil.

De Atlanta, @dreamydleesa conduz o próprio trabalho do começo ao fim. As músicas nascem no GarageBand, instalado no computador do seu quarto. O mesmo espaço também vira cenário para seus clipes e sessions.

Ela define sua sonoridade como soft sapphic soul. O R&B e o soul encontram a produção eletrônica em canções sobre amor, desejo e experiências sáficas. Música de negrona chique, conduzida por uma voz difícil de confundir e melodias que mais parecem beats hipinotizantes.

Foi assim, sem o apoio de uma grande gravadora, que D’Leesa chegou ao público brasileiro. Uma recomendação de @arthurcobat fez seu trabalho circular e criou um burburinho em torno da artista que logo, todo mundo queria descobrir e saber quem era.

Agora, BATEKOO Festival e Coquetel Molotov se unem para trazer D’Leesa ao Brasil.

Dia 14/11, a gente vê a artista de perto no BATEKOO Festival, em São Paulo. No dia 28/11, ela se apresenta no Festival Coquetel Molotov, no Recife.

Público bonito? TÁ NO AR!!! 🚨

A gente sabe que vocês esperam o ano todo por esse momento e que as produções começam muito antes de chegar no festival! Já estamos ansiosos pra ver vocês desfilando pelos nossos palcos e entregando TUDO. 💅💋✨

Em nosso primeiro bate-papo com as atrações confirmadas no No Ar Coquetel Molotov deste ano, o aCena entrevista a banda pernambucana Bruxos de Nadi.

O grupo se prepara para estrear no festival com um show que une o repertório do seu EP de estreia, "A Fruta que Tá Vindo" e seu futuro primeiro álbum de estúdio, "Palavras Garoa".

Formada no Centro de Artes e Comunicação da UFPE em 2022, a banda @bruxosdenadi retorna em novembro ao Campus da universidade pra se apresentar no Coquetel Molotov. 🧚

No primeiro trabalho do grupo, o EP A Fruta Que Tá Vindo (2025), Bruxos de Nadí explora o rock experimental com referências da música nordestina, mistura que pode ser definida como uma psicodelia maranhense-pernambucana, refletindo a essência os integrantes do grupo.

E eles não pararam por aí não, viu? Um novo trabalho tá prometido para o início de 2027.

🔵 Conselho do Molly: a banda lançou agora em setembro a live session Azul Queda Livre, então corre pra assistir no Youtube da banda e sacar como vai ser dia 28.11!

O Festival No Ar Coquetel Molotov manifesta sua solidariedade à Universidade Federal de Pernambuco e a toda a comunidade acadêmica afetada pelos incêndios ocorridos no campus do Recife na última semana.

A UFPE faz parte da nossa história desde o começo. Nascemos como um programa na Rádio Universitária, com a proposta de abrir espaço para artistas da cena pernambucana, que existe até hoje. Nossa primeira edição do festival aconteceu no teatro da UFPE e nossas edições mais recentes também têm o campus como lugar de encontro entre artistas e público.

Essa ligação atravessa nossa trajetória. Sabemos, pela nossa própria história, o quanto uma universidade pública pode abrir caminhos para a cultura, fazer circular ideias e criar oportunidades.

Ver esse espaço sofrer uma perda como essa nos entristece profundamente. Aos estudantes, professores, pesquisadores e trabalhadores que dedicam suas vidas à universidade, nosso respeito e nosso apoio neste momento de reconstrução.

COMUNICADO OFICIAL
Con profundo pesar informamos que la Convención de Tatuajes La Plata queda
suspendida. Esta decisión responde a factores externos y ajenos a nuestra organización.
El municipio desde la intendencia modificó la fecha del evento en más de tres
oportunidades y, posteriormente, intentó adelantarla casi un mes. Finalmente, resolvió de
manera unilateral cancelar todos los eventos privados previstos tanto para este año como
para el próximo.
Hasta último momento trabajamos activamente en la búsqueda de una solución que permitiera sostener esta edición, pero, lamentablemente, no fue posible.
Detrás de cada edición hay meses de trabajo, organización, coordinación con artistas y
proveedores, reservas confirmadas y una importante inversión económica y personal. Nos
duele profundamente no poder concretar, una vez más, una convención del nivel que
nuestro público merece.
Nos pondremos en contacto de manera personal con cada artista y expositor para
coordinar la devolución de las señas correspondientes.
Queremos pedir disculpas sinceras. 
Somos conscientes del esfuerzo que también implicó de parte de ustedes, y comprendemos plenamente la frustración que esta noticia genera.
Esta situación nos afecta especialmente porque esta iba a ser nuestra 15.ª edición: una despedida significativa de una etapa, pensada para dar paso a un nuevo formato.
Sin embargo, no nos rendimos. Ya estamos trabajando en la búsqueda de una nueva
sede para volver a encontrarnos.
Esta situación fue provocada por terceros y resulta completamente ajena a nuestra
voluntad. De nuestra parte, agotamos todas las instancias posibles hasta el último
momento.
Agradecemos profundamente el acompañamiento, la confianza y la participación
sostenida durante tantos años. Porque, si algo aprendimos en todo este tiempo, es que
ustedes fueron, son y seguirán siendo la convención.
Esto no termina acá. Nos volveremos a encontrar con nuevo formato y nueva  locación.

Ongoing industrial action by the Australian Services Union (ASU) is affecting some bin collections in our community. 

If you live north of Bell Street and your bins are not collected, please leave them out and we will collect them as soon as we can. 

The ASU has advised Council that they intend to miss every 5th residential bin as part of this industrial action. 

Kerbside bins to the south of Bell Street will not be affected, as these collections are managed by an external contractor. 

We apologise for any disruption, and we will continue to negotiate in good faith with all unions representing our staff. 

For more information, visit our website at the link in bio.

Happy Dussehra, Dashain, and Vijayadashami!

We celebrate this special festival with Hindu communities across Merri-bek.

Known by different names throughout India, Nepal and South Asia, this festival marks the triumph of good over evil and the victory of righteousness. It's a time for family gatherings, prayer, reflection, blessings and community connection.

May this festive season bring joy, peace and prosperity to all who celebrate.

Our diverse community makes Merri-bek stronger, richer and more vibrant. Wishing everyone a safe and joyful celebration!

Image description: A lit diya (oil lamp) and a decorative plate with rice, leaves, and an orange marigold flower on an orange background. Text reads "Happy Dussehra, Dashain, and Vijayadashami!"

Keep our wildlife safe this spooky season! 🕸️

Halloween decorations can be horror story for birds and other native wildlife, who risk getting tangled or ingesting and choking on decorations in our gardens.

If you’re celebrating Halloween this year, remember to:

✅ Use natural materials like straw, sticks, twigs, leaves and other organic garden waste.
✅ Use cardboard cut-outs or decorate your windows - this will also prevent birds flying into your windows!
❌ Avoid fake spiderwebs.
❌ Avoid using plastics like fishing line, rope, string, cotton wool or balloons.

Visit @birdlifeoz to learn more.

Image description: Halloween decorations, including fake spiders and spider webs, at the front of a house

We are delighted to share that Merri-bek City Council won the Public Sector Diversity and Inclusion Award at the 2026 Victorian Multicultural Awards for Excellence. Our Accessible and Inclusive Communications team, received this award from the Governor of Victoria, her Excellency Professor the Honourable Margaret Gardner AC, on Wednesday night at Government House.

The award recognises Council’s leadership in making Council communications more accessible, inclusive and culturally responsive. Through multilingual campaigns, accessible formats, plain language, practical staff guidance and initiatives such as the Community Connectors Program, the team has strengthened trust, improved participation and empowered more residents to access Council services and opportunities.

We are proud to provide access to services in many community languages spoken across Merri-bek. Contact us via phone, jump onto our website or visit us in-person to connect with Council services in your language.

Image description: three people smiling for a photo with one person holding an award.

Caring for someone can be both rewarding and demanding, and it’s easy to put your own needs last. 

If you look after a family member or friend and need support - our Support for Carers Program can help. 

We can help organise things like a break, wellbeing activities, linking to other supports, or the chance to connect with other carers. 

For local carer Deb, that support has made a real difference. 

“Even an hour or two just to go and have a massage, or a break from the mental load and the physical load, is very much needed a lot of the time,” she says. “And just knowing there was someone who could help when I needed something was really good.”

latestPosts.caption: Acrylic on board. A painting from my nautical series. But it’s not really about boats. Although I am a romantic and do love the aesthetic of the old world. We are all at sea in some ways and the ocean and vessels as a beautiful metaphor.  #sailinglife #seascapespaintings #lovepainting #journeys #seashanties

A painting from an exhibition called the Hidden Path. Acrylic on board. I made a series of these landscapes paintings that formed a loose story. My own mythology. 

#painting #nzlandscapepainting #graphicnovels

Here’s a bunch of my zines. Some of which are hand painted. Acrylic on board , originally created for an exhibition which I then used as a story telling performance. This was done in the kamishibai style. The Japanese story telling tradition on bikes. Disco Alchemy is a modern myth, set in the 1970s. The Dream traveller is Darcy Lamington’s first story that he performed with his magical home made projector. This one is about the colonisation of the imagination and the environment. I’m working on a science communication graphic novel at the moment and bringing some of this magical story telling attributes to this world. At last year’s Scanz conference I told some of Disco alchemy. But left people hanging. Maybe one day I can finish the story. #scanz #graphicnovels #sciencecommunicators #sciencecommunicatorsphilippines #storytelling

Sergio Velcro, inventor of salsa Cricket, Zumba the Arolympics and business thought leader. Sometimes appears to MC festivals and introduce the solid gold dancers. He is often in Bali running a tantric business ashram. Focussing on erogenous profit zones. Circling back around and creating step change inside you. His unique brand of sexy spiritual business takes him around the world spreading love and prosperity. Feeling nice with everyone.  #thoughtleader #businessstrategy #tedtalks #performances
Here’s an Illustration I was asked to make for the fabulous band @tbonetheband. Loved working with these guys. And love their music. #musicart #bandart #tradmusic #folkfestival #americana

These photos from the cheese rave at @splorefestival 2026. Taken by John Williams. Part of the interactive fun and variety that only exists at Lucky star. The Live cheese making workshop, that evolves into an ecstatic cheese rave experience. This is a beautiful collaboration with @luckystar_hq , alleykat.artist, @shadyladyaotearoa and the cheese rave gang. The man in the tracksuit is MC Freek from the Brik a Brak ravers. Improve comedy and real science. Followed by real raving.  You only see this kind of playful comedy and fun at luckystar. #festivalcomedy #interactivecomedy #splore #cheese #oldschoolraver

Not just a cheese raver, lamington maker. But an illustrator and mural painter. An important part of being an artist is listening. Listening with empathy and understanding. Understanding the context and the stories behind the stories. The whole picture.  #artist #listening #murals #interactiveart

Love this photo of Darcy lamington, Mel’s and Daisy Lamington. This was after the lamington making workshop. At Lucky Star festival. I’m so proud to be part of the lucky Star family. Kooky creative and fun. Fun and playfulness is at the heart of everything we do. Also creating a joyful safe place for people to be themselves at festival’s. #festivals #interactive-performance #comedy #nz summer

Here’s my fan art tribute to my friend Nathalie’s extraordinary movie Holy Days. I was lucky enough to have a cameo as the ferry man in this film. Which was an absolute blast. I wanted to create a cartoon version of the characters and story of the film. Who knows it could become a really fun children’s book or graphic novel. Just saying. #filmposter #holydays #cartoon #nzfilm

So excited and happy to see that the Golden Triangle train was a huge success. This is an illustration I made for the event, to help get things moving. The train was full to capacity of happy travellers. People in the luxurious train able to talk, laugh, play music, read books, meditate, what ever you fancy and travel. Beats being stuck in traffic. We need real public transport. And why not make commuting a pleasant experience. Learn a language or write your novel. Anything is possible on the romantic train ride.  #train #trainart #sciencecommunication #nz

This is an Illustration I created for my friend Rowena’s birthday. Atmospheric, energetic and fun. I had a few attempts but landed on this one. It had the balance of colour, and energy. And tells a story.  #posterart #birthday #communication #atmosphere #portrait

Here’s my mural “Mary and the bucket of chicken.”
She’s in Dunedin, suitably dark and moody. I do like work that’s painted with dark blues and greens. Night time scenes allow for fun with lighting.  #murals #Dunedin #Christchurch #kfc

These are for in-person pickup at MADE only! MADE merch can be ordered on the MADE site (link in bio) alongside your show tickets, and picked up at the show. We have also added show posters and special bottles from Bivo. ✨💦✨

#madebikeshow #handmade

Exhibitor Spotlight: We were over the moon to hear from Darren and include Baum Cycles in the Builder Lounge this year, as well as this magnificent build in the Campy booth. 
Hailing from Geelong Australia, Baum is no stranger to MADE having personally attended MADE Australia and one of our earlier Portland shows. 
Huge thanks to Darren and the team for sending bikes, next year we hope to have you in the flesh! 💕🎟️💕
#madebikeshow #handmade
@lamarchebikeco La Marche / "Phat Track" Super Fun Versatile Track Bike with our Mowmow Bar & Rhonda Stem at @made.bike

This bike is a show stopper. One of the most stunning builds we’ve ever been a part of, this custom @forma.bike for @mvdhcx was on display at the Builder’s Lounge at this year’s @made.bike show in Portland. The industrial design is on full display; precision machining everywhere, in-house wound and formed carbon tubes, new road-specific rims from @noblwheels (we hear they’re coming soon 😉) running WT hubs, even the stance, with a geometry that balances a healthy amount of CX agility with all-day comfort, looks fast standing still. Scroll through the gallery for all the juicy details, a real feast for your eyes. 👀

A bike with character, built by a character. As Fall sets in, we’re feeling nostalgic for the hot grindy bike-party that is MADE – our favorite show (weekend?) of the year. The bikes that hold our hearts reflect the friends that build them, and this is no exception. Equal parts precision design and good humor, it personifies so much of what we love about the hand built world.

Bradford Smith of @afterhoursframebuilding knew the protocol from the start and has been helping us at SILCA launch our Protocol tire lineup since the prototyping phase. 

He combined a focus on high-volume speed and comfort with 1970s muscle cars and classic ultra-endurance cycling events, to build the eye-catching After Hours Roadrunner. 

Crafted in Portland by Smith, an industry veteran, this stunning machine was displayed at the most recent @made.bike and blends a classic auto racing aesthetic with the self-sufficiency for events like Paris-Brest-Paris. 

Built from light Columbus steel tubing and featured plenty of modern touches like T47 BB, UDH dropouts, clean internal dynamo routing, and ample tire clearance it’s designed to go fast on fast wide tires.

Want the full breakdown on how Bradford’s endurance racing background shaped this ultimate “grab-it-and-go” tarmac Roadrunner ripper? Head to the link in bio to read the full feature at Marginal Gains Media!

They say the best camera is the one you have with you. What if that's a 58 year old 6x6 SLR full of 20 year old Portra 160, and you're working/living in an 80 year old shipyard building for a week? You bust out the tripod, the handheld meter, and cross your fingers.

Exhibitor Spotlight: Fat Chance! 💕🔥💕
Chris Chance is a legend and wonderful human. It was an honor to have him in the building along side this beautiful Chris Cross. 💕
If you are unfamiliar with the history of domestic bicycle production, Fat City Cycles produced SO many bikes, and started the careers of many builders. 
It was such a pleasure to have Chris return to the show, and we wish him the best as he enters a new chapter in life. Don’t worry, Fat Chance will live on! 👍🏽
#madebikeshow #handmade

Goodbye, Zidell Yards; you were the best. 💕✌🏽💕
As we prepare to bring MADE to the Oregon Convention Center, it’s time to say goodbye to our home for the last 4 years. What a backdrop. Our wild, abandoned shipyard was the perfect home for the show’s first chapter. The raw industrial backdrop helped create the vibe we will bring with us wherever we go. 💕
The decision was “made” for many reasons, but the biggest one was health and safety. A week before this year’s show, Portland had one of the highest AQIs in the world because of the horrible wildfire season. We can’t take that risk for everyone’s well-being. Far too many builders and boutique brands rely on MADE each year, and the thought of canceling the show a few days prior nearly gave us a collective heart attack. 😵‍💫
As the show grows, we will miss our weird venue. At the same time, we are SO excited for AC, flush toilets, and a space built for events at scale. Tons of cool surprises in store for everyone; 2027 will be the biggest MADE to date! 🎟️🔥🎟️
#madebikeshow #handmade

Exhibitor Spotlight: Paladin Bikes AM1 ✨🎉✨
Based in Portland, Oregon, and specializing in multi-axis aluminum CNC machining, Paladin can reach all sides of a frame in a single shot. The front triangle integrates the head tube, seat tube, and bottom bracket into one solid piece. 😵‍💫
Their soon to be released AM1 is stunning, and was on display at MADE 26. Machined in Paladin’s Portland facility, available with elevated suspension, configurable travel, chainstay length, and wheel size. What a ripper! 🔥🛠️🔥

.⁠
Plan your visit to see the exhibition before it closes on Saturday 24 October. The Craft + Design Canberra Gallery is open from Wednesday to Saturday from noon to 4pm.⁠
.⁠
HOW WILL THEY KNOW IT'S ME is a new exhibition by artist Zoe Brand that explores the performative nature of jewellery as a device for communication. Using jewellery archetypes, ready mades and text, Zoe collects mundane and throwaway statements from casual conversation, examining their ambiguity and transforming them into objects to be worn.⁠
.⁠
For this exhibition, Zoe draws on homemade banners, sporting pennants, flags and quilts, considering both their forms and cultural and social contexts. These references inform a new series of SOFT TEXT works, developed through quilting techniques and screen printed text. The large scale works are designed to be worn by multiple people, either as a single piece with multiple points of attachment or as separate pieces worn collectively. ⁠
.⁠
Through these works, Zoe continues to explore the ambiguity and slippages of language, transforming everyday statements into physical, wearable objects. By subverting familiar forms and phrasing, HOW WILL THEY KNOW IT'S ME asks how jewellery can communicate, and what happens to meaning when words move from casual conversation onto the body and into public space. ⁠
.⁠

The Daily Creative Challenge celebrates artistic expression and encourages mindfulness through daily creative practice. This exhibition presents selected works by the award recipients from the 2026 Craft + Design Canberra Daily Creative Challenge.  ABOUT THE CHALLANGE 
The 2026 Craft + Design Canberra Daily Creative Challenge celebrates Canberra as a vibrant centre of creativity while connecting a wider community of makers across Australia and beyond. 
Each July, creatives from around the world respond to a series of daily word prompts, sharing new work via Instagram. Working across ceramics, textiles, photography and mixed media, participants embrace experimentation, process and connection through creativity. 
Now in its fifth year, the 2026 theme Dissent advocates for creativity as a powerful tool for questioning, challenging, and reshaping ourselves and the world around us. 
Over the three week challenge, participants generated thousands of artworks and posts. The result is a diverse and series work that reflects the energy, imagination and collective spirit of the Challenge.

✨ Today we kick off with a workshop led by legendary transhumanist Stelarc!!! 👂

✨ Friday - Our Discourse program at Artspace (tysm @marco.com.au ) curated by the ineffable @eggeplant , featuring a keynote by @lizpelly deconstructing the Spotify-industrial complex and how data-veillance is shaping the music industry. The day is stacked with keynotes, panels, short films, plus Madika Penrith and Sam Miers presenting their Yuin Country Sound compilation.

✨ Friday evening our expanded cinema showcase PARA:Cine with world premieres by @eek_now @_the_longest_hum @kirby_casilli present ‘Hearsay’ and virtual performance icons @team.rolfes The Mustang Speedrun.

FROM THE STREETS OF MULLUMBIMBY TO THE MULLUM ROOTS STAGE.

Last year I met a young busker at Mullum Roots Festival.

We got talking about songwriting. That night he went home and wrote a new song.

The following day he tracked me down at the festival and played it for me. This is the moment I recorded.

I made him a promise: write 10 songs before the next festival and I’ll give you a spot on the lineup.

Well, he did it.

And this July, he’ll be performing at Mullum Roots Festival 2027.

Sometimes the best things happen when you least expect them.

This is what Mullum Roots is all about. ❤️

30+ locations across Aotearoa & Australia 
Book your sauna ↓

latestPosts.caption:
Our partners are at the heart of The Sauna Project, and we’re incredibly grateful for how much the network has grown and every person who has brought sauna to their local community. 🤎⁠
⁠
Now, we’re ready to bring The Sauna Project to more communities across the South Island and Australia, and we’re looking for the right people to help us do it.⁠
⁠
Have you ever thought about owning and running your own sauna? It could become a meaningful local business, whether you’re looking for a second income or something you can grow into your main focus.⁠
⁠
We’re looking for people who love sauna, nature and creating spaces where people can connect. Every new sauna brings the experience to another community while strengthening the wider network.⁠
⁠
If this sounds like you, or someone you know, get in touch + download our partnership information pack through the link in our bio.⁠
⁠
Could your community be next? 🌙⁠
Wellbeing tip #020: when the day feels loud, head for the sauna. 🔥

A different way to build your own sauna business. 🌿⁠
⁠
For Yvonne and Kody, a mobile sauna opened up a way to bring an idea they loved to life, without starting with the overheads of a permanent venue.⁠

We custom-build your traditional wood-fired mobile sauna and provide the turn-key setup, established systems, training and ongoing support. You bring it to life in your community, shaping a business around nature, connection and a lifestyle you genuinely love. 🔥💧⁠
⁠
We’re now looking for our next partners across the South Island + Australia.⁠
⁠
Can you picture this in your own town? Head to the link in our bio to explore becoming a Sauna Project partner.⁠

Some parts of sauna are hard to explain until you’ve felt them. Aufguss is one of them. 🍃⁠
⁠
Originating in German sauna culture, Aufguss is a host-led ritual where essential oil-infused water is poured over hot stones. The rising heat and scent are then moved through the room using a towel.⁠
⁠
Our version happens in complete silence, and that really is the best part of it. No talking. No distractions. A moment to pause. 🙏⁠
⁠
If you’ve felt it, you know. If you haven’t, this is your sign to join us for one. 🔥

Stage two: the work behind the view. 🌿⁠
⁠
A look at the work Will and Megan put in before opening @thesaunaproject_wairarapa_. Clearing the view and getting their place ready for its first sauna guests.⁠
⁠
The doors are now open. Go check out what they’ve been working on. 🤎⁠
Alright, which one are you? Can’t wait to giggle through the comments. 🔥

Still a while away, but @sauna_fest 2027 is already beginning to fill up. 🔥⁠
⁠
For 48 hours, Lake Tikitapu becomes home to wood-fired saunas, cold water, movement, music, good food and plenty of space to slow down.⁠
⁠
It’s all happening again from 14–16 May 2027, and we’re already counting down. A huge thank you to everyone who’s locked it in so far. 🔥⁠
⁠
If it’s been sitting in the back of your mind, autumn plans don’t get much better than this.⁠
⁠
Tickets via the link in bio. ❤️‍🔥🪩⁠

Bringing a vision to life. 🔥

Will and Megan have been putting in the mahi at @thesaunaproject_wairarapa_ slowly turning their piece of land into something pretty special. A place to sauna, slow down and connect, with the whole family part of bringing it to life.

And this is only stage one.

We love seeing what our partners create when they take the idea and make it completely their own. Safe to say, these two have done a bloody good job.

Wairarapa, you’re lucky. 🤎

Northland sauna life is looking pretty hard to beat. 💧 Beautiful views, proper wood-fired heat and quite possibly the cutest sauna dog we’ve ever met.⁠
⁠
Swipe through for a look at @thesaunaproject_paihia in Paihia / Kerikeri. If you needed another reason to head north, this is it. 🔥

Heat is heat, right? Not quite.⁠
⁠
Infrared, electric and wood-fired saunas each create a completely different experience. Here’s why we keep ours wood-fired. >> 🔥

Weekdays off. Sauna weekends on.⁠
⁠
You’ve been loving our partner stories, so here’s another. Meet Meagan and Will, the people behind @thesaunaproject_wairarapa_⁠
⁠
Running their sauna has given them more time outdoors and the freedom to shape their working week around what suits them. For them, that means keeping weekdays open to continue doing what they already do, and welcoming their sauna community through the weekends.⁠
⁠
We’ll let them share what the experience has looked like in their own words. 🤎🔥⁠

Some catch-ups are simply better in the sauna, with phones away and a cold dip in between.⁠
⁠
Send this to the person you’re overdue a sauna with. 🤎🔥

latestPosts.caption:
For @alexandermegos , Siurana is more than just a climbing destination. It’s a place where he has grown as a climber, returning throughout his career to take on some of its most iconic and demanding routes. Over the years, his story has become part of the area’s climbing history and community. 
In 2013, Alex made history on Estado Crítico (9a), completing the world’s first 9a onsight. Just days later, he climbed La Rambla (9a+), one of Siurana’s most celebrated routes, first ascended by Ramón Julián Puigblanque, on his second attempt.
Over the years, Alex continued returning to Siurana. In 2021, he completed three of the La Capella sector’s hardest routes: King Capella, La Furia de Jabalí, and La Capella. In 2024, Alex made the first repeat of Chris Sharma’s Sleeping Lion (9b), a route later climbed by fellow Tenaya athlete Sachi Amma.
Through years of visits, hard climbs, and memorable ascents, Alex has become part of Siurana’s history. This year, we’re excited to welcome him to the @siuranaclimbingfestival

Not long ago, we had the privilege of listening to Wadandi Pibulmun Cultural Custodian Zac Webb, who generously shared stories about Country and some of the Noongar place names in the Margaret River Region. This is Part 2 of that meeting.

In this video, Zac shares more about the Noongar and Wadandi landscape and its place within the 14 Aboriginal language groups of Australia’s South West. Using the sand to help visualise the landscape, he maps out the Cape to Cape region and shows where the Margaret River Region sits - the place where we’re fortunate to live, work and holiday.

Learning about the culture of this place is one seemingly small but meaningful way to deepen our connection to Country, each other and the stories that have existed here for thousands of years.

Some of the Noongar place names and meanings shared in this video are:

👉 Taalinup - Augusta
👉 Bilya - River
👉 Goorbilyup - Blackwood River
👉 Goorbilj - Belly

Don’t miss Part 1, where Zac shares more original Noongar place names from the Margaret River Region and explains the meaning behind the ’-up’.

📍 the Margaret River Region, in @westernaustralia

🎥 @maxzappas @timcampbellphoto @westernaustralia

Over 360 plant species have been recorded here 🤯

Ambergate Reserve is a great spot for a wildflower walk in spring, with an incredible variety of plants and flowers to discover along the flat, 4km trail. 

This 75-hectare reserve protects some of the native bushland that once covered Busselton’s coastal plains, including more than 25 species of orchids. 🌼 Take your time as you wander, and stick to the marked trails to avoid trampling delicate plants that might be hiding beneath the leaves and bush.

There’s a dedicated carpark off Queen Elizabeth Avenue, but no facilities or drinking water, so come prepared.

A couple more things: use the footwear cleaning stations to help prevent the spread of dieback (a fungus that threatens native plant species in the South West), and leave the wildflowers where they are for everyone to enjoy. Picking isn’t allowed. 💚

📍 Ambergate Reserve, near Busselton, @westernaustralia

🎥 @timcampbellphoto

Whale Wednesday 🐋

There are many reasons to love whale season, this is one of them 🌈

Humpback whales have two blowholes that create a distinct heart shaped spray 💙

📍 Margaret River Region, in @westernaustralia 

[This footage was captured from a distance of at least 60 metres, in accordance with applicable WA drone regulations (Shot on DJI Mavic 4 Pro, with up to 6x zoom).]

Beach walks, stunning gardens and a heritage stay in Yallingup? 😍

@caveshouseapartments offers modern, fully self-contained apartments nestled within the grounds of the much-loved heritage property, @caveshousehotel, which has been welcoming guests since 1903.

There’s a range of apartment configurations to choose from, including one- and two-bedroom options, all with outdoor areas overlooking the gardens, as well as accessible layouts. The hotel’s expansive 4.5 hectares of gardens are an experience in themselves, too. And when it’s time to refuel, you can pop over to Caves House for a drink or a bite to eat.

Plus, a 10-minute stroll down the Ghost Trail takes you straight to Yallingup Beach, Yallingup Lagoon and Rabbit Hill, a favourite coastal spot for swimming, surfing and soaking up those ocean views. 🏖️

📍 @caveshouseapartments, Yallingup, in @westernaustralia

🎥/📸 Supplied

#PaidPartnership

How’s this for a great family day out in the Margaret River Region 🙌

Start with a short and sweet guided tour of @capenaturalistelighthouse. It’s an easy climb for all ages, just 59 steps to the top, and 30 minutes is perfect for the kids. The tower sits more than 100 metres above sea level, so the views across Geographe Bay are amazing. There’s plenty of room for the kids to run around, and the museum is full of interactive bits to keep them busy while they learn.

Then it’s a 10-minute drive to lunch at @eaglebaybrewingco, which is set on a working farm looking out over the cape. Cold beers brewed on site for the grown-ups, seriously good food, and a pirate ship playground for the kids.

Finish at Meelup Beach, just a short drive down the road that is generally sheltered, shady and shallow, and about as good as a family swim spot gets. It’s a patrolled beach over summer, but always check conditions with @slswa before heading out. 🏖️

📍 Cape Naturaliste, in @westernaustralia (15 minutes drive from Dunsborough)

It really makes you feel like you’re at the world’s end 😍

This road at Cape Leeuwin in Augusta offers magnificent views of @capeleeuwinlighthouse and the surrounding cape. Skippy Rock Road is accessible by 2WD, but it’s a gravel road, so take it slow and drive carefully. Keep an eye out for wildlife, and be mindful of walkers and cyclists sharing the road.

As you make your way down the ridge, park at Leeuwin Scenic Drive Lookout and take in those incredible views.

Then stop by Cape Leeuwin Lighthouse to see it up close or climb to the top on a tour. It might look small from afar... but it’s a whole different story when you’re standing at its base or taking in the views from the balcony 🤭

📍 Skippy Rock Road (Leeuwin Scenic Drive Lookout), Augusta in @westernaustralia

🎥 @timcampbellphoto

Or did you? 😉

If you thought you knew about all the unique experiences you can have in the Margaret River Region, think again!

Here are some of our favourite, quite unexpected, things to do:

1. Underwater Sculpture Trail: Located at @busseltonjettyinc, you’ll find 13 submerged sculptures that double as an artificial reef. Grab a snorkel pass, or go all out and book a dive with @swandivedunsborough to experience it up close.

2. Wine Chapel at @howardparkwines: The only one of its kind in the region! This private space can be booked for an in-depth wine experience for a minimum of 4 people. Taste back vintages and museum wines, paired with a gourmet platter, vineyard views and stories from Howard Park.

3. Helicopter flight with @scenichelicopters: Soar above  beaches, coastline and vineyards with the doors off (or keep them on if you prefer) 🚁 Choose from a range of tours and flight durations, and why not land land at a winery for lunch?

4. Underwater Observatory: One of only 6 in the world, this is another unforgettable experience at @busseltonjettyinc. See fish, marine life and colourful coral from 8 metres below the surface, without getting wet.

5. Where two oceans meet: Head to the approximate meeting point of the Indian and Southern Oceans at @capeleeuwinlighthouse, Augusta. Explore the Interpretative Centre, take in the views from the lookouts and platforms, and book a tour to climb the lighthouse itself. The views from the balcony are incredible!

6. Megafauna at @mammothcave.mr: Did you know a real zygomaturus jawbone was found embedded in the cave wall? It’s still there for you to see, and much more! The self-guided tour lets you explore at your own pace, with the adventure continuing outside as you climb out of the doline and follow the bushwalk.

7. Electric quad biking with @ecoadventuresmargaretriver: A great way to explore the Boranup Forest. The bikes are silent, making for a different kind of adventure where you can take in the sights and sounds of the forest on a guided tour.

What else would you add? ✍️

🎥 @timcampbellphoto

latestPosts.caption: Mark your calendars, request your PTO and start thinking about tire choice now—the Lost and Found Gravel Festival returns to Portola on Saturday, June 19 in 2027. Keep an eye here for early registration later this year.  More good times with good people in the mountains, all to support trails in the Lost Sierra. What could be better?!

Wow! Thank you to everyone who donated to this year's 5 Bucks a Foot Gravel Fundraiser! Together, we raised almost $26,000 for trail building and maintenance in the Lost Sierra. 5 Bucks a Foot fundraisers are a critical piece of our annual revenue, and we're so grateful for the support. We will call the winner this week (or notify via email if we can't reach you the old-fashioned way), so keep your phone close! Big thank you to our sponsors who supported this year's awesome custom build and full prize package: @evilbicycles, @shimanomtb, @ridefoxbike, @whiteind, @paulcomponent, @wildernesstrailbikes, @astralcycling, @camp.and.go.slow, @loam_equipment, @patagonia_mtb and @patagoniaprovisions—this year's campaign was successful due to their generosity and longtime support of the Stewardship.

We had a great time at @lostandfoundbikeride ! Gravel races sure have changed over the years but they are still a ton of fun.
Check out the full video on the Sklar Bikes YouTube Page.

Hot and a bit dry for June, but @lostandfoundbikeride was pure adventure, as usual.  Riders navigated a blend of dirt, gravel, and pavement through this small and scenic part of the “Lost Sierra” region for 99, 58, or 40 miles, then returned to the small town of Portola, California, which also marked the start of the race.  New this year were sections of single track along Lake Davis built by @sierratrails. 

Complete rider gallery:  https://event.meridianmilephoto.com/galleries/lost-and-found-2026

The new singletrack at @lostandfoundbikeride was absolutely ripping! Massive shoutout to @sierratrails for building it, it was beautiful. If featured in this post, DM @fieldjournal.media for a free copy. And if you’d like to purchase one of 2,000+ shots, click the link in bio.

Can’t think of a better way to kick off the summer than with a weekend of friends, camping and racing in one of my favorite places!

@lostandfoundbikeride truly knows now to put on a top notch event with wonderful, light-hearted community vibes. 

Looking forward to more of these adventures soon! ☀️

And of course, big thanks to @nicophysic for replacing all the parts on my bike after Unbound in time for me to race 🙏 I get a lot of help from my friends to do this bike thing and am so thankful for it.

Lost and Found photos are in! Look for links to shots from the podium, course and festival in your email (sent this morning)—and be sure to also check out the awesome galleries from @seabrightphotography and @dnbphoto, which are also linked in the same email. You’ll also find the post-race survey, where you can pass along your thoughts on the weekend (we read all of these & often incorporate changes based on the feedback), and a link to limited race merch for sale via the @yubaexpeditions website if you missed grabbing it onsite. Thank you racers for an incredible weekend in the mountains—we’ll be doing it again in less than two months at the @downievilleclassic! See you there??
Perhaps the most dramatic finish of @lostandfoundbikeride, plus the pro women and men's starts.

In the lost sierras.. at the Lost & Found gravel fest. Where we question why we live in the city when there’s miles of gravel roads and cutty mountain tracks here. Massive thanks to @sierratrails crew and volunteers for all the hard work bringing the @lostandfoundbikeride every year! Gallery’s are linked 👆in the bio

ONE WEEK until Bike Summer 2026 kicks off!

The Kickoff Ride meets at Alberta Park at 5pm on June 1st.
 Here’s what we have lined up:
- Bike Groups: Hear short speeches from local organizations and ride leaders
- Merch Sales and Pick Up: Get yer hands on merch you’ve already purchased in the first Pre Order, try on shirts to decide what you’d like to order by the end of the 2nd Pre Order (which ends June 8th), or purchase pennants and stickers on site. We’ll have volunteers there to help you affix your pennant to your bike

- Poster Distribution: We’ll have posters on hand for those who want to help us get them all over the city

Did you know there are a handful of rides that happen every week, all year long? 

The Thursday Night Ride (TNR) has been consistently riding every week for TEN YEARS. It is officially the longest standing weekly ride in Portland, Oregon. 

It’s no secret that TNR was removed from the @shift2bikes calendar after a series of Code of Conduct violations, and the ride remained delisted for quite some time, but new TNR organizers stepped up, met with the Shift Code of Conduct (CoC) Committee, and addressed standing concerns. As of this week, the ride is back on the Shift calendar!

It takes a lot of coordination and dedication to host any ride, let alone one that happens every week of every month all year long, no matter the weather. 

We are proud of the TNR leaders for their perseverance and willingness to work with the CoC Committee to make this weekly ride a safer experience for everyone.

Come celebrate TNR number #524 tomorrow. Meet at Salmon Street Springs (1000 SW Naito Pkwy) at 7pm, announcements at 7:30pm.  —
As always, if you ever experience any Code of Conduct violations from any community member, especially ride leaders, please report it to the CoC Committee! Link to the full Code of Conduct and the form to report violations in our bio.   #BikeSummer #Shift2Bikes #WeAreTNR #ThursdayNightRide #TNR

Sea Otter Australia: 22-24 October 2025 @mogotrails in Batemans Bay and the Mogo State Forest on the NSW South Coast!

Well over 150 Australian and international brands have already been secured to exhibit.

As the first industry and consumer event of its kind in the Southern Hemisphere, Sea Otter Australia will be established as one of the country’s premier cycling events. It is set to redefine the cycling landscape in Australia.

The Festival will be held in Batemans Bay, NSW, a renowned tourism destination on the beautiful NSW South Coast and the home of the world-class Mogo Trails. Located in the triangle-heart between Sydney, Melbourne and Canberra, Sea Otter Australia will attract an estimated visitation of 7,000-8,000 industry professionals and cyclists from Australia, New Zealand, and the world.

Inspired by the iconic Sea Otter Festival in North America, this groundbreaking event will offer a comprehensive experience that combines world-class racing on the Mogo Trails.

The activities will also include riding experiences, an industry summit and at the heart will be the industry tradeshow and a comprehensive consumer expo. The event will foster a sense of belonging and shared passion among riders of all ages and skill levels, and provide a platform for showcasing cutting-edge products, technologies, and industry trends.

Sea Otter Australia aims to create an Australian flagship cycling event with a global legacy: Full details on site: https://seaotter.au/sea-otter-australia-a-year-to-go/

Salute to the Sun by Patricia Piccnini @patricia.piccinini

Salute to the Sun continues my long fascination with the boundary we draw between the natural and the artificial — and how readily that line dissolves once you look closely. This new bronze sculpture is a chimera, seamlessly moving between deer, tree, fungus, human and motorcycle. It evolves out of a machine base into an organic form whose arms, or perhaps antlers, unfurl like budding leaves.

The pose comes from the sun salute and from the way plants quietly rotate to face the light. I love that it stands on a beach, an obvious artificial construct, yet entirely at home in that archetypical natural place. Its materiality also reflects this: Bronze is mostly copper, a metal that was laid down in the earth eons ago, but shaped entirely by the manipulation of elemental fire by human activity.

In earlier work I looked at imagining machines with the tenderness, balance and yearning of living things. These machines are the wild creatures of a world where we are all intertwined with technology. ‘Salute to the Sun’ presents a creature of modern mythology: an hybrid chimera drawing its energy from the sun, more vulnerable than threatening, asking us where we fit into this world.

Rota Fortunae by Emily Hastie @emilyrosehastie

Rota Fortunae visualises the role of chance in life's most defining outcome: where on Earth we are born. Fortuna, ancient deity of chance, blindly holds out her hand to reveal a fate on the spinning wheel. Around its edge sits the true distribution of global population, drawn from current United Nations data. Australians are only ~0.34% of that population, yet inherit stewardship of a megadiverse country home to 10% of Earth's known 
species, over 80% found nowhere else on the planet. Such extraordinary fortune begets equal responsibility.

Tidal Orchestra by Lindisfarne Anglican Grammar School @lindisfarnegrammar

Tidal Orchestra is a collaborative ceramic installation created by Creative Industries students and inspired by 
the fluid motion of the ocean. Individually hand-built and glazed in soft pastel sea tones, each fish reflects the 
shifting colours of water and sky. Mounted on slender stainless-steel rods, the fish move gently with the coastal breeze, forming a unified school across the Currumbin dunes. The work symbolises unity, resilience, and interconnection, encouraging viewers to reflect on collaboration, environmental harmony, and the delicate 
balance between human creativity and the marine world.

Reflections by Oliver Mabbutt @_mabart_

Reflections invites participants to move through and around the structure, encountering their own image as it 
fragments and multiplies. The work explores the human need to reflect on the past while remaining oriented 
toward what lies ahead. While reflection is essential for growth, lingering too long can obstruct forward momentum. By framing both the participant and the surrounding landscape, Reflections balances inward 
contemplation with outward projection, encouraging awareness of self, context, and future direction.

Still Room for Sentiment by Wendy Tanner @wentan

In a contemporary world of white walls and grey restraint, this work asks whether nostalgia and sentimentality still belong in our homes. Glass cabinets and ornament collections have given way to flat-packs and single statement pieces. Grandma’s blue-and-white porcelain, once treasured, dusted, and displayed, now drifts to op shops and garage sales as generations pass on. Gathered here, these figurines resist disappearance, asserting the quiet value of memory, care and excess in an age that prefers less.

Littoral Lantern by Brent Grainger & Jai McCartney

Littoral Lantern begins as a distant marker at the festival, a simple form that draws people toward it. As visitors approach, it opens, shifting from an object to a space to be experienced. Framed openings offer moments to pause and view the surrounding coastline from within. As daylight fades, a soft glow emerges, filtering through timber panels and spilling across the ground. The sculpture becomes a lantern—gathering people, light, and movement. Littoral Lantern invites interaction, reflection, and memory, creating an engaging spatial experience.

#BikeSummer #DingDing

There are two Dolly Parton rides on the calendar this week and a skate event, too!   >>> Tonight — Dolly: We will always love you, led by @aye__calypso and friends. Meet at Colonel Summers at 6:30pm 
“Join us tonight for one of the many celebrations of our beloved Dolly - We’ll listen to her music as we travel down greenways and by some spots we think Dolly would have loved in our city.” - Ada  >>> Friday — Secret Roller Disco: Theme Dolly by @secretrollerdisco. Starts at 7pm at Convention Center Plaza. Bring your skates or rent them there. They don’t say it, but… obviously you’ll want to wear your rhinestones.

>>> Sunday — Dolly Parton and Tim Curry Memorial Ride by @c_bozzy3 and @thatsmejustbri. Meet at Salmon Street Springs at noon.
- Homemade Appalachian BBQ — First come, first served!
- 12:30 Dedication Open Mic — Share a memory, a song, a story, or a few words of appreciation.
- 1pm Square Dancing with the Rose Town Ramblers — Get your boots (or bike shoes) moving!
- Then we ride out at 1:45! (This ride is a loop)
- We’ll hit the streets blasting music, spreading joy, and celebrating two absolute icons on a fun loop ride that brings us back around.
- Bring your bike, your friends, and all the Dolly-and-Tim-inspired energy you can muster. Costumes, wigs, sequins, theatrical flair, cowboy glamour, fishnets, or anything else that feels appropriately fabulous are highly encouraged.  —
Photos shared by @aye__calypso showing possible stop locations, plus fliers for all three events.

#BikeSummer #SecretRollerDisco #DollyParton #TimCurry

Tonight’s Keep Brutalism Weird ride will be around 2 hrs and 6-ish miles. It meets on the corner of SW Mill and SW Broadway at 6:30pm. 

@docomomooregon’s ride description reads, “Tour some of the city’s best Brutalist buildings downtown and in NW Portland with a group of architectural historians and other enthusiasts. Everyone’s favorite (or not) postwar architectural style is the star of the show here. We will look at concrete, and more concrete, and even more still. Plus a few examples of significant non-Brutalist buildings thrown in.  Tour leaders will share information at each of our stops—the goal is to be educational, but also fun. Come prepared to listen, learn, and share your opinions about these hulks. We’ll end with an informal hang and refreshments at Portland’s very best Brutalist(-y) site.”

As a teaser, here are some pics of places the tour may stop…

#BikeSummer #Brutalism #ArchitectureTour #IfYourePassionateAboutItItProbablyWillMakeAGoodRide

They browsed, replenished and got a few cool titles from these awesome locations around town. #BikeSummer #Blockbuster #FreeLibrary

The Mosaic Ride brought folks together for a 10-ish mile tour of Portland’s tile and stained glass, followed by a collaborative mosaic made from the colorful bits everyone brought along.

⁠
Made to be part of those moments for years to come, the Pack & Carry Fireplace folds flat for easy transport and sets up wherever camp takes you.

As we venture further into the new season, we’re reminded of autumn’s distinct feeling. It’s a bridge between the height of nature’s energy and its forthcoming hibernal slumber. ⁠
⁠
Read more in the Time Outside Journal.

Big enough for the whole family, with a view worth staying in for. 🏕️⁠
⁠
“What stood out the most is the inner tent! It can fit a family of 5 or 6 people! The double-entry door of the inner tent is a nice feature, as I can leave one side open while having privacy on the other side. The panoramic view from inside the inner tent makes it a perfect solution for those lazy days where I just want to take naps and relax while lying down.” - @sircampalotz

The Art of Return⁠
⁠
Nature moves from its summer crescendo into a quieter note. We come together to notice the subtle shifts in flora and fauna – leaves fading from green to gold, migrating fish rising to meet a fly, sharp cold mornings giving way to fleeting autumn sunshine. ⁠
⁠
Our excursion takes us to the Delaware River, where a group of friends pursues elusive trout. Nature’s slow, yet relentless return to decay surrounds us, and yet, the whish of each cast, hovering mist and tapestry of trees seem to pause time. ⁠
