latestPosts.caption:
Roll up, roll up to experience the spectacle this March! 🎪

The hit of the carnival, @hauteandfreddy move through their music like runaway circus acts, crashing through the veneer of polite society with all the flair of an 18th century escapade. On a meteoric rise as pop’s next big thing, this duo has a penchant for theatre, 80s synth and underground music club culture.

If Lady Gaga spent her birthday listening to them, you can find the time to catch their set when they make their Australian debut. Dress to impress and ready thy bloomers!

Dripping in colourful cloth and star power, when Grammy-nominated artist @fatoumata_diawara__ takes the stage, everyone pays attention 🌟

A major figure in African music, her lush and vibrant albums and collaborations with music industry heavyweights, such as Damon Albarn, Oumou Sangaré and Disclosure, have enabled her to tell the story of the suffering and rediscovered joys of Africa, and the issues of womanhood in her mother tongue, Bambara.

Returning after a spectacular WOMADelaide debut in 2019 – welcome back the queen of contemporary African music.

Is it alien music? Or is it microtonal, prog jazz-rock? Who cares, if it’s this good?! 🫱 🔺🫲

Angine de Poitrine, a Québécois duo, also known as Khn (double-necked guitar/bass) and Klek (drums), have officially been creating music with funky basslines, electronic looping and math-heavy time signatures since 2023. One cult-inspiring album (‘Vol.I’ 2024) and a viral KEXP session later, Angine de Poitrine are the mispronounced name on everyone’s lips.

Brush up on your papier- mâché skills and get out the polka dots; Angine de Poitrine are landing on our little patch of earth this March.

Choose dancing on the grass after sunset. Choose the long weekend over work on Monday. Choose Underworld.

Thirty years ago, the dancefloor changed. At the turn of the decade, acid house opened the door to a new UK rave scene – where indie heads joined the club crowds and transformed empty fields and derelict warehouses into spaces of community and transcendence. And in 1994, Underworld emerged onto the scene with their third album ‘dubnobasswithmyheadman’. 

Their visionary and uninhibited approach to dance music soon caught the attention of director Danny Boyle, landing the group on the soundtrack of the seminal 1996 film Trainspotting with the generation-defining single ‘Born Slippy .NUXX’. Now, Underworld return to the cultural zeitgeist, and to Adelaide for the first time since 2010 for what will be an unmissable set at WOMADelaide on Friday 5 March.

First Release tickets are sold out! 🎟️

Second release tickets on sale now. A reminder, this year you can purchase a 1, 2, 3 or full 4 Day Ticket, and choose whichever mix of days works for you. Explore our first lineup on the website – who are you excited to see? 👀

The moment you’ve been waiting for! The first 36 artists of #WOMADelaide 2027! 🌏

We can’t wait to welcome you for another year of discovery, exploration, and joy, featuring alien prog rock, Afro-emo, ska, modern twists on traditional instruments, and as always mesmerising dance, theatre, and acrobatic performances around the park.

Since first appearing at WOMADelaide in 2004, this GRAMMY-winning collective has earned worldwide acclaim.

A symbol for Tuareg resistance and poetry since 1979, Tinariwen blends blues with Saharan traditions to create a unique output that has turned the heads of artists from Robert Plant to José González. Now on their tenth studio album, Tinariwen are award-winning globetrotters who have left their mark through a marriage of traditional drums with electric guitars and immersive storytelling. 

Performing on Sunday 7 and Monday 8 March at #WOMADelaide.

Madness has entered ‘Our House’! 🏠

‘One Step Beyond’ the rest, Madness have been making hits and mischief for 45 years. A little bit ska, a little bit pop, and whole lotta Camden cheek, these nutty boys have been behind some of the biggest British hits since 1979. From appearances on Top of the Pops to the top of Buckingham Palace (beat that Beatles!), now for their first performance at #WOMADelaide on Sunday 7 March – don’t miss the WOMADness!

A defining voice in modern American R&B, Leon Bridges brings the Texas Sun to #WOMADelaide ☀️

From vintage R&B, to psych-funk, to country, Leon Bridges weaves a thread of magic into everything he does. Presenting his latest album HAPPINESS ANYTIME, expect a dance-filled set to kick-off the 2027 festival on Friday 5 March.

biography: The Unconformity is a nonprofit arts organisation from the West Coast of Lutruwita/Tasmania, Australia.

latestIgtvVideos.caption:
An epic drive-in cinema in the heart of Western lutruwita/Tasmania.

Join us for an outdoor cinema experience, presenting iconic movies and curated content on the big screen from 28–30 October 2022 at the remote Queenstown Aerodrome.

Program and tickets will be available online on Friday 30 September 2022. See link in bio for more information.

Video credit: Nick Maher / Reunion Media

[Video description: A slow-moving shot along the length of a runway. In the distance, the grey rocky peak of Mount Owen towers over the end of the runway. Either side are grasses and shrubs in shades of grey, purple and green.]

Six months ago today, we made the difficult decision to cancel The Unconformity 2021 festival due to COVID-19.

The timing of the cancellation closed the door on many artworks that were ready to engage audiences. Most of these projects were documented and are represented in this video about a festival that started and stopped on its opening day.

We're working hard on our annual program of activities and putting together the building blocks for our next festival in 2023.

Festival dates and other details will be announced later in the year via our social media channels and email newsletter. You can sign up to our newsletter by visiting The Unconformity website.

Video credit: @lusyproductions

[Video description: Quick-cut footage of the Queenstown landscape, various artworks from the festival and audience members engaging with the works. The screen cuts to black then white text says "On Friday 15 October 2021 — the opening day of The Unconformity festival — Southern lutruwita/Tasmania entered a snap three-day lockdown due to COVID-19. To protect the health and safety of the community, the festival was cancelled at 3:13pm that day.", followed by several slow-moving shots of the town in the wake of the festival's cancellation.]

latestPosts.caption:
Your donation can make twice the impact.

This AusArt Day, Creative Australia is providing $5,000 in matched funding to support The Unconformity’s work across the West Coast.

For every $1 donated, Creative Australia will contribute another $1, effectively doubling your contribution until the $5,000 pool has been exhausted. A $50 donation, for example, becomes $100 in support for The Unconformity.

Your donation helps sustain our work in the region, from supporting local creative practices to enabling our three Ongoing Artists to bring new work to the 2027 festival.

Image credit: Stevie Battese, Growling a Pear, 2026

Image description: [A vibrant, symmetrical digital artwork featuring layered neon green, yellow, red, purple and blue patterns against black.]

Artists need more than an idea to bring new work into the world. They need time to experiment, room to explore and support to see where their practice takes them.

Ahead of AusArt Day on Thursday 22 October, an early donation to The Unconformity helps make this possible for our three Ongoing Artists as they work towards the 2027 festival.

By giving today, you’re helping create the conditions for new ideas to take shape on the West Coast.

Image credit: Nancy Mauro-Flude, Bring Your Old Device workshop, 2026, photographed by: Bob Cartledge 

Image description: [A close up photograph of a green circuit board with gold and silver components.]

The Unconformity is participating in AusArt Day on Thursday 22 October, a national initiative supporting Australian artists and arts organisations to raise funds for their creative work.

Our campaign centres on our three Ongoing Artists, supporting them to make work for The Unconformity’s 2027 festival.

Your donation, whatever the size, will provide these artists with the time, space and support they need to develop new work, with the outcomes to be presented on the West Coast in 2027.

This AusArt Day, help us continue to support artists and the work they make in and for this place.

Image Credit: Iris Blazely, Murmuration 1, 2026

Image description: [The Maugean skate moves among the welcome swallows as the sun’s rays appear and disappear.]

Join us this October for our next Open Hall.

This month, we invite veteran screen storyteller, artist and Queenstown resident Nick Maher to present a retrospective of the past two decades of his film and television career and creative practice. Sharing notable works, including UNTV and Long May She Rain, Nick will reflect on the power of screen as an artistic medium to reach hearts and minds.

With our 2027 festival now one year away, it’s also time to share the dates. Join us for an evening of celebration as we launch the dates for our eighth festival edition and begin the countdown to 2027. 

We look forward to seeing you there.

6-8pm, Wednesday 21 October 2026

The Unconformity Hall, 35 Cutten Street, Queenstown

RSVP by email: frankie@theunconformity.com.au 

Image credit: Nick Maher, Discontinuity, 2023, photographed by: Rémi Chauvin

Image description: [An art installation featuring eight vintage television screens in the foyer of the UNTV Station immersive studio experience.]

We are thrilled and look forward to our CEO, Louisa Gordon, speaking at Communicating the Arts in Ottawa-Gatineau, Canada next week.

Louisa will share The Unconformity’s experience of building connection through deep community engagement, and how consistent, open and transparent communication can help strengthen relationships between artists, audiences and place.

We are proud to share the work of the West Coast on an international stage. 

Image credit: Ivett Dodd

Image description: [Louisa stands against a white wall smiling directly at the camera, wearing a yellow scarf and a black jacket.]

Thank you to everyone who joined us for Secret Station.

From Queenstown to Lynchford, Saturday night brought together art, music and people across the West Coast, with each stop offering moments of discovery, connection and surprise along the way.

We’re grateful to the artists, crew and partners who brought the event to life, and to everyone who made the journey with us. 

A memorable night on the West Coast. Thank you for being part of it. 

Artist: Bing/Santospirito Image Credit: Bing/Santospirito, photographed by: Sammie Saltmarsh

Image description: [A person in a white jumpsuit performs inside a railway station, with another musician at a keyboard and a crowd gathered nearby. Warm and purple lighting fills the space.]

We can’t wait to depart with you all for Secret Station.

This Saturday 3 October, we’ll make our way into the West Coast as day turns to night, moving through the landscape and historic stations.

If you’re not on the train or bus, you can still join us at Queenstown Station. The station will come alive from 6pm with free music, art and more for all ages. 

See you in Queenstown.

Image credit: Jesse Hunniford

Image description: [A brown Wilderness Railway Queenstown Station road sign, with golden sunlight peeking through the trees behind it.]

Kayak Orchestra by Dylan Martorell and Lychen Kelp has just concluded a presentation at Cementa, a community-driven regional arts festival in Kandos, NSW on Wiradjuri Country. 

This site-responsive work continues to find new contexts beyond its first festival season at The Unconformity 2023. Congratulations to the entire team for their work bringing this gentle journey to life.

Image credit: Jesse Hunniford

Image description: [Many people in yellow kayaks tow sound making instruments across a lake.]

The Unconformity congratulates our Partnerships & Stakeholder Manager, Jane Longhurst, on receiving a Gallaugher Bequest sponsored Churchill Fellowship. 

Jane will undertake an international study to investigate how audiences and communities can be more meaningfully integrated into the making of theatre, and how this can shape new approaches to creative participation and engagement. 

We look forward to seeing what Jane discovers and how these ideas will inform her practice in Lutruwita/Tasmania on her return.

Image credit: Nick Hanson

Image description [Jane stands on Crib Road with a big smile on her face, clapping along with other people in the background out of focus.]

Join us at our next Open Hall for a conversation about the Art Trail, to celebrate the continued importance of this program and share your thoughts as we work towards The Unconformity 2027.

The Art Trail is a key festival event where artists are invited to sell their work through galleries, studios, and local businesses. We’ll look back at key findings and feedback from 2025, and then look forward to hear your thoughts on what’s next for the Art Trail as we head towards 2027.

We’ll talk through how to prepare to be involved in 2027 – whether you’re an artist or creative, local business, community member, or simply curious about being part of the program. 

Whether you’re experienced or new to the Art Trail, come along to hear what’s happening, share your thoughts and connect with others interested in The Unconformity Art Trail.

6-8pm, Wednesday 23 September 2026

The Unconformity Hall, 35 Cutten Street, Queenstown

RSVP by email: frankie@theunconformity.com.au

Image credit: Mal Gotjes, Suffragette, The Unconformity Art Trail 2025, photographed by: Nick Hanson

Image description: [A visitor in a bright orange jacket explores a gallery filled with sculptural ceramics, displayed across dark shelves. Figurative sculptures and colourful vessels contrast against the gallery’s white walls.]

Applications now open

The Unconformity is seeking applications for their next Chair, Board of Directors.

Applications are sought from executive leaders with strategic arts, cultural, tourism or regional interest or experience, for a three-year term.

The preferred candidate would be a respected leader with senior experience, strong external relationships across government and philanthropy, and the ability to connect artistic ambition with organisational sustainability.

Applicants would have a connection with or interest in the arts, or remote and regional communities, with a preference to the West Coast of Lutruwita/Tasmania.

We believe diversity strengthens our team, and we welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. If you believe you are a strong candidate, we encourage your application, even if you don’t meet all the criteria. 

Enquiries are to be emailed to The Unconformity Deputy Chair, Chloe Tanner deputychair@theunconformity.com.au

To find out more, including the full Position Description and Strategic Plan, visit theunconformity.com.au/work-with-us/.

To apply, please submit your application via the form on our website, together with your CV, by 11:59pm AEDT on Wednesday 23 September 2026. 

A selection panel will assess applications and make recommendations to the Board for consideration. All enquiries and applications will be treated confidentially.

Image credit: Jesse Hunniford - What Water Could Remember by Arif Furqan, The Unconformity 2025.

Image description: [A dark interior with translucent white fabric draped across the floor and suspended in the air. Black-and-white images of a rocky shoreline are projected onto the fabric, creating a layered landscape.]

This week, The Unconformity welcomes artists Kimiya Sato (Japan), Jude Anderson and Kirri Buchler (Victoria) to Queenstown as part of their ongoing project, Strong Heart of the Jade Road. 

The artists have spent the week in Queenstown exploring the musical properties of jade and the connection between place, people, music and story. Building on research across the Philippines, Taiwan, and Australia, they’ll share traditional and experimental instruments and forms of music making in this informal sharing session.

5–6pm, Saturday 29 August 2026

The Unconformity Hall, 35 Cutten Street, Queenstown

Tea and coffee provided

This residency is a partnership between The Unconformity, Punctum (Castlemaine), and San Fes (Japan), supported through Regional // Regional, an initiative of Asialink Arts and the University of Melbourne.

Image Credit: Loren Kronemyer

Join us in Napier, Hawke’s Bay for New Zealand’s largest heritage festival!

Enjoy four immersive days filled with classic cars, vintage planes, speakeasy bars, live music and all the style and spirit of the Jazz Age 🎷✨

View the full event line-up or download the Art Deco Festival Napier 2026 programme: 👉 www.artdeconapier.com

Start your engines! The Vintage Car Parade is back for Art Deco Festival 2025!

Sponsored by Progressive Meats, this grand parade showcases a dazzling line-up of vintage cars, with Bugatti as the feature marque. Watch as these stunning vehicles cruise from Clive Square to Marine Parade, then get an up-close view at the Show and Shine!

Own a pre-1946 vintage car? Don’t miss your chance to be part of the action – register now and join the parade!
👉www.artdecofestival.co.nz/events/vintage-car-parade-2/

When: Saturday, 15 Feb 2025 Time: Parade starts 1PM Where: Clive Square to Marine Parade 
Cost: Free to watch. Free to enter.

🏆 Ready, set, race! The Soap Box Derby is back in 2025! 🏆

With summer holidays just around the corner, it’s the perfect time to get those creative gears turning and start building your ultimate cart for the Art Deco Festival Soap Box Derby!

Generously sponsored by Conroy Removals & Brebner Print, this fan-favourite event brings families together for a thrilling race down Tennyson Street, cheered on by thousands!

When: Sunday, 16 February 2025
Time: Scrutineering at 9 AM, first race at 10 AM
Where: Tennyson Street,
Cost: Free to view. Free to enter.

Great prizes are up for grabs, so don’t miss out! Check out the race rules and cart specs on our website and register today!

👉 www.artdecofestival.co.nz/events/soap-box-derby-2

2025 marks 100 years since the 1925 Paris World Fair, where the world celebrated a new and emerging aesthetic: Art Deco!

After the 1931 earthquake, Napier was rebuilt in this new style.

In 2025, we’re celebrating the centenary of the Paris exhibition in Art Deco style with a Fête Champêtre at Mission Estate! 

Join us for live music, lawn games, French canapés, and a touch of summer joie de vivre. Don your best garden party attire, grab a parasol, and enjoy the stunning grounds.

For details and tickets, visit the Festival website: 
www.artdecofestival.co.nz

Tickets now on sale!

Join us for an unforgettable, immersive festival celebration, brimming with energy, classic cars, speakeasy bars, vintage planes, and all the jazz of the Art Deco era!

Art Deco Festival Napier 2025 
13-16 February 2025

View the full programme of events here: 
www.artdecofestival.co.nz

Registrations are now open for the Winter Deco Fashion Flaunt!

This Year’s Categories:

Best Dressed Child
Calling all young fashionistas aged 14 and under! Flaunt your flair for style with an Art Deco-inspired ensemble. Don’t forget to accessorize to complete your look. Open to both original creations and recreations.

Most Dapper
From waterfront strolls to formal receptions, we’re looking for the ultimate in tailoring, tone, and accessories—complete outfits from tip to toe. Open to both original creations and recreations.

Most Chic
Show off your impeccable Art Deco style. Winter is your chance to dress and impress. Open to both original creations and recreations.
Best Original Ensemble
A platform for the best original outfits that capture the Art Deco aesthetic. Open to original creations only, allowing participants to showcase their unique collections.

Register now at: 
www.artdecofestival.co.nz

We look forward to meeting you at our Volunteer Open Day happening tomorrow! 🎉

Indulge in some delightful Devonshire Tea, enjoy a scone or two, and mingle with our fantastic Volunteers, Staff and Board Members. It's the perfect opportunity to discover how you can truly make a difference in our Art Deco city! 

🗓️ When: Saturday, March 23, 2024
🕘 Time: 9:00 am to 12:00 pm
📍 Where: 7 Tennyson Street, Napier

Can't swing by on Saturday? No worries! We have a second Open Day on Monday, March 25, 2024, also from 9:00 am to 12:00 pm. 

We're always on the lookout for new recruits! If you can't make it to either of the Open Days but still want to explore joining our team, just give us a shout, and we'll arrange a time to chat that suits you best. 

Whether your passion lies in guiding visitors through our city's architectural wonders, spreading warmth as a greeter, or serving as a proud ambassador of Art Deco Napier, we'd be thrilled to welcome you aboard!

Before you head to Soundsplash, do yourself a favour and practise putting your tent up AND packing it down.

Know which poles go where, make sure you’ve got all the pegs and figure out how that thing gets back into the tiny bag it came in.

For Te Wiki o te Reo Māori, we’re sharing the kupu behind our Māori name, Paratī Oro - Soundsplash.
 
Paratī - to splash up
Oro - sound, echo or resonance

Together, the name evokes a splash of sound... bringing to mind both the ocean waves and music flowing through the air here at Whāingaroa and resonating back out from the hills.

Celebrate Māori Language Week with us by learning these kupu and giving them a go. 💛

We kicked off the Māoriland Rangatahi Film Festival on Thursday. Congrats to all participants of the @etuwhanaunz Rangatahi Film Awards! Head over to @ngapakiaka to find out who our winners are!

Civic Theatre was packed out for the ‘He Waiora’ premiere of the NPIP films! 🤩

Māoriland: The Origin Story - Episode 1 - Libby Hakaraia ✨

Te Tumu Whakarae o Māoriland, Libby Hakaraia, shares the story of the inception of the Māoriland Film Festival.

Passionate to include her whānau and hapori in the filmmaking world, Libby made the 2012 short film 'The Lawnmower Men of Kapu' in her hometown of Ōtaki, starring many of her own whānau members.

The film was adored and swept up by film festivals worldwide. At the @imaginenative Film Festival in Toronto, she put the call out, inviting the Indigenous world to Ōtaki. Thus, the first Māoriland Film Festival was born.

Nine years on, and success of the Māoriland Film Festival speaks for itself. This month, #MFF2022 begins, where 107 films from 132 Indigenous nations will be showcased across five days.

Ōtaki welcomes the world to the Māoriland Film Festival, June 29 - July 3.

With the Māoriland Film Festival now in it's ninth year, the driving forces behind the festival sat down to share their stories of how it all began. From a small caravan on the side of the road, to now being the largest Indigenous film festival in the Southern Hemisphere... there is a lot to be told.

Over the next few weeks, we'll be posting kōrero from Libby Hakaraia, Tainui Stephens, Tania Hakaraia, Madeleine Hakaraia de Young, and Matilda Poasa -- sharing how the Māoriland Film Festival came to be what it is today, and what it means to us as Indigenous creatives.

Don’t forget, #MFF2022 is happening on June 29 - July 3!

Today Māoriland announces our ninth MFF programme! 🌟

MFF2022 will present 106 films from 132 Indigenous nations over five days during Matariki (June 29 - July 3) with over 60 film screenings, industry and arts events.

The theme for this year’s festival is “He pitomata he pito ora” - the potential of life.

“We have all felt the effects of the Covid 19 pandemic and for filmmakers it has been a hugely disruptive time. Working through lockdowns the creative output from Indigenous filmmakers has resulted in the strongest MFF programme we’ve ever had. The potential has been released,” said Festival director Libby Hakaraia.
We’re excited to welcome you all to Ōtaki as we celebrate the return of international filmmakers to Aotearoa to present their films at the largest international Indigenous film festival in the world!

For nine years, ʻOhina Labs has helped Hawaiʻi-based filmmakers turn scripts into films, and many of those films have screened at Māoriland in Ōtaki, Aotearoa.  For over a decade, Māoriland has built one of the world’s most celebrated homes for Indigenous cinema, creating opportunities and a creative hub for emerging Indigenous voices, stories, and community.  This November, at Shangri La, Center for Cultures & Ideas and Museum of Islamic Art, we are building a Pacific pathway where stories travel from the Lab to the screen, reaching the global audiences who need them.

“The beloved Oscar® -winning classic Spirited Away from the legendary Japanese studio, Studio Ghibli, is to be dubbed into te reo Māori. 

For over 40 years, Studio Ghibli’s films have enthralled fans around the world, including generations of New Zealanders. And now, in a deal by Māoriland Films and supported by Māori language funding agency Te Māngai Pahō, global anime brand Crunchyroll and Sony Pictures Entertainment, new generations will be captivated by the beautifully hand-drawn, detail-rich animations of iconic classic Spirited Away.

Directed by Hayao Miyazaki, Spirited Away will premiere in te reo Māori across Whakaata Māori and MĀORI+, New Zealand’s national Indigenous broadcaster and streaming platform for catch-up, before screening at Māoriland, the world’s largest Indigenous film festival. 

Together, these platforms will ensure a te reo Māori version of this iconic film is accessible to audiences across Aotearoa and beyond.

‘When we’re young, we learn the stories of others. When we’re adults, we create our own story. When we’re old, we tell our story.’

Please join us for a BWB Talk to celebrate the publication of Kua Tau: A Life in Stories by Tainui Stephens.
Tainui Stephens (Te Rarawa) is one of Aotearoa’s most prominent Māori storytellers. Across five decades he has been finding stories, in people, in place, and in the shifting shape of Māori life in Aotearoa. And alongside a career in filmmaking, broadcasting and cultural advocacy, he has been finding himself. Kua Tau gathers up a kete of his best writing on these subjects, drawing from his much-loved essays for the online magazine E-Tangata.
. Copies of the book will be available for sale and signing by the author.

Final days of solo exhibition by senior Pitjantjatjara artist and lawman Frank Young, bringing together six dynamic paintings and an installation of kuḻaṯa (spears).

The sixth Canberra Art Biennial unfolds across Canberra’s designed landscape, bringing contemporary art into gardens, car parks, hotels, civic spaces and unexpected corners of the city.

Across more than 20 locations, the Biennial considers how art might shift our relationship to place - and how a city can become both exhibition space and subject.

Presented in partnership with Canberra Art Biennal, don’t miss Jason Phu’s solo exhibition at ANCA Gallery ‘Dreams of a Cicada, Waking in the Summer Heat’. Part play, part storytelling, part dreamscape, Phu reimagines folk tales blurring dreams and reality.

Snippit from an interview with @ninenbn newswhile facilitating at @starlightfestival_byron earlier in the year.

We spoke about the power of breathwork and why more and more people are turning to these practices for emotional regulation, stress relief and deeper connection with themselves.

Breathwork is rapidly becoming recognised as a powerful tool for:

- Stress and anxiety regulation
- Emotional release and processing
- Nervous system reset
- Greater clarity and presence
- Deeper mind–body connection
- Safe way to access altered states of consciousness 
- Reducing pain and so much more!

The breath is one of the few systems in the body that is both automatic and consciously controllable, making it a powerful gateway to influencing your physiology, emotions and state of mind.

Simple practices can create profound shifts.

This is why I’m so passionate about sharing this work with leaders, coaches, facilitators and everyday humans who want to live with more presence, power, fulfilment and alignment.

Not every breathwork journey is intense or results in big shifts or releases, but I do find Conscious Connected Breathing with large groups of people definitely gets the energy moving!

Breath is life.

And when you learn to work with it consciously… everything changes.

Let's Get It.

🌲 Lake Tahoe Wellness Festival 
🌱August 6-9, 2026
⛺️Meeks Bay Resort & Campground 
📣 Registration is officially open with our SUPER early bird special discount tickets link in bio. 

Join us for another magical weekend on this beautiful sacred land with Yoga, AcroYoga, Nature Hikes, Meditation, Dance, Slackline, lakeside camping, Educational Talks with incredibly talented wellness practitioners from our local and extended community!

More good vibes from the Lake Tahoe Wellness Festival 💕💕. Love my community! Thanks to everyone that made it a success! @wellnessplaygroundretreats @greenearthlover @mountainlotusprovisions @newmoonnaturalfoods #wellnessplayground

I’m still feeling the glow from all the wonderful experiences I enjoyed at the Lake Tahoe Wellness Festival at Meeks Bay. So many great conversations and dances with old friends along side meeting wonderful new friends. I’m honored to have been one of the teachers invited to share my gifts. We are blessed to have so many amazing people in this Truckee Tahoe community. Celebrating playfulness and the beauty of the Tahoe waters and land. Thanks @greenearthlover and @wellnessplaygroundretreats for all your hard work to create this time and space to engage in conscious community. 💕🕺🏔️

Still vibrating with pure gratitude after an unforgettable 4 days at the Wellness Playground Retreat.🌀✨️ 

We started our days with sunrise yoga 🧘‍♀️ paddleboarding and Qigong, learned transformative breathwork, journeyed within 👁 and pushed past fears. We grooved, laughed and danced like no one was watching💃🏼. We watched the stars 🌌 and jumped into the clear waters of Tahoe 🌊

This experieence reminded me of the incredible healing power of human connection and kindness 🫂 Every interaction was a beautiful reminder of how good it feels to be seen, supported, and loved just as you are. I left with full heart and a quiet soul 🤍

Huge love to Laura, Anastasia, and every beautiful soul who shared their magic with me this weekend. You are my people. 🫶✨

#WellnessPlayground

A little glimpse into Lake Tahoe Wellness Festival with @wellnessplaygroundretreats 
I reallllly wish I took more photos / vids, was way too busy being fully in the moment! 

It was an incredible honor and pleasure to have facilitated and participated in this amazing weekend experience. We were tucked away in our own paradise at Meeks Bay on the West Shore of Lake Tahoe, with our own private beach, food truck @mountainlotusprovisions, yoga, dance and wellness classes all day, live music and DJ sets, beautiful mermaids, swimming, paddle boarding, camping, and most importantly a beautiful community of incredible people that felt like family even though many of them I had just met for the first time. I’m continually reminded of how important it is to gather and be in community, connecting, playing, being, sharing. This is the medicine of our times. Keep showing up, we need you! 

Thank you @coopdaloopthedj for co-creating ALCHEMIZE with me, for everyone who showed up courageously to this class to co-create the magical experience we had. It’s not everyday that you’re guided into a rage ritual. ALCHEMIZE asks those who show up to step out of their comfort zone and face uncomfortable parts of ourselves, so I’m truly grateful to everyone who shows up and is willing and open 😊🔥

It was such a treat being on the water on a paddling adventure with @thatmountaingirl on Friday and @powerrestoremethod and @inspiredlifeayurveda on Sunday, taking an amazing yoga class with @shari.w.beard, chilling the F out in @wildharmonyhealth sound bath next to my dear sister @marissa.mignone.doula , reconnecting with old friends, making new connections, dancing in the water with a crew of badass babes, and finishing with a sweet closing circle that felt like a big warm hug. 

A huge shout out to @greenearthlover and @atouchofjoy for the vision and creation of this incredible event and all the hearts and hands that played a role in making it come alive. It truly takes a village. 

My heart is full & my soul is lit!
🫶 ❤️‍🔥✨🌊 🧜‍♀️ 🧘🏻‍♀️🌮🌅 🎶👙💃🏻⛰️🦎🐿️ 🩵

I had the pleasure to facilitate community activity during the Chinny Charge run #mullumbimby.
It was so much fun to work with the kids, have interesting conversations and get our hands dirty with clay!!!

#northcoastceramics #mullumbimby #chinnyrun #k eramika

This beautiful exhibition finishes today, 20 September 2026 at 5pm - you don’t want to miss it.  Mullumbimby Civic Memorial Hall,  55 Dalley Street. Mullumbimby. #ceramics #australianceramics #ceramicsculpture

We’re open all day until 5pm!  Come and check out the incredible ceramics by @northcoastceramics members. 
We’re open from 10 am until 5 pm tomorrow as well 🙌

#Ceramics #sculpture #artshow #comeandsee

A busy hive of activity getting the art space ready for opening night!  Artists, husbands of artists, and curatorial team 🙌. So wonderful and very exciting!  I hope to see you there tonight or over the next couple of days to celebrate local ceramic artists and their many talents. 🩷🌸🙏🏻

#sculpture #ceramicsculpture #localartists #comeandcelebratewithus

Congratulations  @venessa_stella_skye @middle_pocket_pottery on your selection for the Chinny Charge Sculpture Exhibition.

Drawing on her Maltese heritage, Venessa  creates large vessels, with an amphoric influence rooted in tradition. The intention is for each piece to carry its own voice, unique story, character and timelessness with soul and connection to the ancient.

Join us for the opening, Thursday 17 September, 5–7pm, then explore the exhibition Friday 18 and Saturday 19 September, 10am–5pm both days.

Come and experience the diverse and thoughtful sculptures our ceramic artists have been creating, and meet the artists behind the work.

It was genuinely such a delight documenting this year’s @northcoastceramics Mud Trail. This is an event in which over 30 incredible ceramic artists open their studios to visitors across the Northern Rivers over 4 days. While there was plenty of shopping to be had, the event is really about bringing people together around clay — presentations, demos, workshops, artists answering questions and sharing their craft. I absolutely loved seeing the spectrum of art, meeting so many lovely and talented artists and getting a behind-the-scenes look into their studios and inspiration. Photographing artists and their art is always such a joy and couldn’t more highly recommend this event in the Northern Rivers for anyone with a passion for ceramics.

Congratulations @suelfraser on your selection for the Chinny Charge Sculpture Exhibition. 

Sue’s work has a relationship with history and clay, horses and women, strength and fragility where surface tensions and treatments leave records not only of the maker hand but also the earth and firing that made it. 

Join us for the opening, Thursday 17 September, 5–7pm, then explore the exhibition Friday 18 and Saturday 19 September, 10am–5pm both days.

Come and experience the diverse and thoughtful sculptures our ceramic artists have been creating, and meet the artists behind the work.

Civic Art Space, Mullumbimby Civic Memorial Hall.

55 Dalley Street, Mullumbimby

NCC exists to champion ceramics as a vibrant art form - connecting makers, collectors, and community across the Northern Rivers. This spirit drives tje upcoming Chinny Charge Sculpture Exhibition at the Civic Art Space, Mullumbimby Civic Memorial Hall.

Join us for the opening, Thursday 17 September, 5–7pm, then explore the exhibition Friday 18 and Saturday 19 September, 10am–5pm both days.

Come and experience the diverse and thoughtful sculptures our ceramic artists have been creating, and meet the artists behind the work.

What happens after a ceramic kiln burns continuously for 100 hours? 🔥🏺 

Participants witnessed the reveal last month at an anagama kiln opening during the celebrated North Coast Mud Trail. Jo Norton, ceramic artist and Technical Assistant at TAFE NSW Murwillumbah, supported the event, having assisted with the construction of the anagama kiln. 

Hosted at Middle Pocket Pottery by acclaimed ceramic artist and TAFE NSW Lismore graduate Venessa Stella Skye, the hands-on experience offered visitors a unique opportunity to explore traditional wood-firing techniques and connect with the thriving ceramics community of the Northern Rivers. 🤎🧑‍🎨🪵

For Jo, woodfiring is a key part of her own ceramic practice and a rewarding opportunity to share her knowledge of this unique firing process.

It's just one of the many ways TAFE NSW staff stay connected with industry and bring contemporary practices and insights back to the classroom, helping students develop skills that work. 📚

👉 Follow your creativity and find out more about TAFE NSW Art & Design courses via the link in our bio.

@northcoastceramics, @thrownbyjo, @middle_pocket_pottery, @venessa_stella_skye

#TAFENSW #NorthCoastMudTrail #Ceramics #ArtAndDesign #CreativeIndustries #NorthernRivers RTO 90003

Carving binary into clay.

A language of our time, recorded like an ancient text.

Technology feels permanent — but what happens when the machines, systems and intelligence shaping our lives become history?

Perhaps one day, these too will be archaeological artefacts.

A glimpse of INTERFACE.

Opening night: Thursday 8 October 2026, 5.30pm - 7.30pm @ Byron CoLab on Arakwal (Byron Bay’s first of hospital)

#interfaceexhibition #ceramicart #contemporaryceramics #artandtechnology #future

Introducing INTERFACE. 

We’re Jay Richardson and Jennifer Muller, two artists bringing our work together for a collaborative exhibition exploring the space where nature, technology and humanity converge. 

At the heart of INTERFACE is a question. 

As our world evolves, what does it mean to remain human?

Set in the former Byron Bay Hospital, now Byron CoLab on Arakwal, the exhibition brings together ceramics and wall-art that explores our changing relationship with the world  around us. 

INTERFACE 
Opening Thursday 8 October
Byron CoLab on Arakwal 
2 Wordsworth St
Byron Bay
NSW 2481

We’d love you to join us.  #ceramics #byronbay #ceramicart #artexhibition #northernnsw

latestPosts.caption:
‘La era de los gusanos’ 2026, acrylic on exterior wall, 4 x 10 m

Part of @polinizados 
Universidad Politécnica de Valencia

From May 11 to 15, 2026, The Universitat Politècnica de València, through the Cultural Action Area of the Vice-Rectorate for Art, Science, Society and Technology, presented the 21st edition of the PolinizaDOS 2026 Urban Art Encounter. This year, the event proposed a reflection on spatiality, aiming to go beyond the mural as a pictorial format and contribute to the construction of a spatial and architectural sense. To this end, it proposed an expanded approach based on artistic research, understood as a tool for configuring unique spatiality’s imbued with discursive meaning.

Retrat Hada: Clara Peeters 

Fuimos invitadas a participar de @polinizados en la UPV Universidad Politécnica de Valencia 💫

Clara se escondía en los reflejos de las escenas que pintaba en un tiempo donde las mujeres pintoras eran muy pocas y estaban destinadas a pintar únicamente bodegas. 
“Mesa con mantel, salero, taza dorada, pastel, jarra, plato de porcelana con aceitunas y aves asadas” (c. 1611) se encuentra en el Museo del Prado en Madrid y es una de las 60 pinturas realizadas mujeres entre las aproximadas 8000 obras que se encuentran en el Museo. 

Un homenaje a las hadas que logran aparecer la historia del arte 

gracias a todo el equipo de la universidad por confiar en nuestro trabajo y gracias a todos los artistas que formaron parte la experiencia.

Every wall is made of sand, acrylics, oil pastels, sand on concrete, 4x10m, 2026

for @polinizados

Transcendence now! 
Behind the wall, the beach! 
1,9km behind the wall lies the beach.
The wall is made of bricks.
The bricks are made of clay or concrete,  and infinite grains of sand. 
The wall is made of sand.

Who makes the brick, when, how, and why?
Who builts the wall, when, how,  and why? 
How does the wall go up, stay still, or fall down? 
What is on one side and what on the other? 
What was before it and what will be after it?

Tot mur e fet d'arena.
Detras del muro la playa.
Sous les paves, la plage.
Sota l'asfalt.
Aguantamos.
Nadie gana.
Mirar a los drones.
Paz por todo.
Cafeteria suenos.
La horta.

latestPosts.caption:
We are excited to announce our penultimate artist!
This young aspiring creative is still in year 13 in college here locally in Taupō, and has been a big fan of Graffiato, volunteering her time last year.  Her name is Taylor Tefono!

We gave her the chance to paint one of Town Centre Taupō's Christmas trees last year and now it's time for a wall of her own.  She'll be right next to our other local emerging artist, Magali Moreau, so they can support each other for the entire weekend. 

We can't wait to see what our local ladies have dreamed up for the festival.

We weren't lying when we said we had internationals coming for the event! 
Please give a warm welcome to @stephaniecartledge, who is coming across the ditch from Victoria just to paint at Graffiato. 

Stephanie is inspired by native flora and fauna, which comes out in her collaborations with Art Aid and BirdLife Australia. 

She reached out to us back in early 2025 looking for a chance to paint and have a great reason to visit NZ again, and we count ourselves lucky she was happy to wait until 2026.

Practically a local, our next artist intro is for @razortaserlaser, who is coming all the way down SH5 from Roto-vegas to see us!  Razor cut his teeth with stencil art in Bristol, UK, before returning to NZ, and has been making his mark on home soil ever since. 

His art does sneakily appear around Taupō already, but this will be his first official Graffiato festival.  Razor has also been working hard with other Rotorua artists to establish their street art scene, and we're excited to see what's coming soon just up the road. 

In the meantime, we're lucky to have Razor for our big weekend.  He has such a variety of skill sets to draw upon, so we're looking forward to seeing what he pulls out of the bag!

🗺️Since our 2026 Graffiato walking map is ready to go, let's share it!
🚶For those hoping to get their steps up, this is not your year. 😅

We are all going to be in one single laneway, marking the first time that has ever happened at our festival.  As organisers, we're not going to lie, this is very exciting.

For this year, bring down a chair and a picnic and stay awhile.  The art will unfold before your eyes.

🌋Our next artist is one of our locals, and she has a very unique background. Magali Moreau's official title is "National Groundwater Monitoring Programme Manager" working for GNS Science. 

🎨When she isn't studying our geothermal landscape, she's being artistic.  What a great combo!

Magali has volunteered at Graffiato many times and even painted Town Centre Taupō's Christmas Trees.  This will be her first ever wall and we know she's going to knock it out of the park.  Come on by to give her some of your support!

If you've been keeping score at home, you may have seen us mention that @mrcinzah will be paired up on a wall with another returning artist. 

That artist is one of our all time favourites...@ginakiel_! 
This is such a cool collaboration of amazing talent on one wall.  We can't wait to see what they dream up together.

Gina painted in 2024, but it wasn't quite the experience she was gunning for that year.  She had to miss the actual festival and then swung by a couple weeks later to paint her amazing mural.  This time, she'll be fully part of it all and we can't wait to welcome her back!

Graffiato: Taupō Street Art Festival returns this Labour Weekend, and 2026 is bringing something new 🎨
 
For the first time in its history, this vibrant annual event will see every artist complete their mural within the same laneway, maximising their impact.
 
This year will feature 11 incredibly talented artists, including two internationals, two emerging locals and seven artists from around New Zealand whose backgrounds span the globe.
 
The artists will transform this single laneway into a living canvas, showcasing live the incredible effort and unbelievable skill that is required to paint at scale. With 10 murals being painted over this coming Labour Weekend, Taupō’s 85+ existing works will be joined by several more in their ever-growing expansion.   
 
Save this for Labour Weekend and come watch Graffiato 2026 unfold.
 
📍 Taupō town centre
📅 Saturday 24 to Monday 26 October 2026
🎨 Graffiato: Taupō Street Art Festival @graffiato_taupo_street_art 
🎟 Free and family-friendly

We are up to artist announcement #4!  Try to keep up, people!
Hailing from where the world's greatest musical and performing arts festival takes place, it should be no surprise this Glastonbury-born artist is brimming with creative talent!  It must be in the water up there.

After the making the big move from the UK to Taranaki, we are really privileged to welcome @fayesuzannah  into the Graffiato family of artists. 

This is shaping up to be a crazy good lineup of artists and we're just getting started!

✈️The award for longest travel time to get to Graffiato goes to this guy.... @codoartni!

Hailing all the way from Bangor in Northern Ireland, Codo has gone the extra mile to make it to Graffiato, and we are honoured to have him join us. 

We don't often have internationals come all the way down to our neck of the woods, so if you make it to the festival, please let this very talented man know how much it means to us kiwis. 
His art will be a joy to watch come together, so do come out for a look.

And speaking of internationals....we actually have another one coming that we'll announce shortly...

It's been a hot minute since this artist graced our streets, but we are absolutely fizzing to welcome him back to Taupō.  He has had an incredible career painting in countless countries around the world and displaying an unbelievable range of styles. 

Looking back through the archives, I believe this will be his 4th or even 5th Graffiato mural, and to see his evolution as an artist from his first mural in Taupō to this one will be quite a trip. 

Ladies and gentlemen, I give you..... @mrcinzah!!

Cinzah will be paired up with another returning artist....all to be revealed in the coming days.

It is time to announce our Graffiato artists for 2026!!! Aaaahhhhh!! 
If social media had a confetti cannon, we'd be launching it. 🎉

Please put your hands together for our first artist off the blocks, @bean_wang_! 

Bean got in touch with us last year and we're so excited we could give him an opportunity this time around.  He is a bit of a renaissance man with a whole slew of skill sets beyond mural painting.  His evolving style will be such a unique addition to our street art gallery, and we can't wait to see what he has in store for Taupō.

Location information for all artists coming soon...

¿Cómo participar?

Dale me gusta a esta publicación.

Comenta etiquetando a esa persona con la que compartirías unas cervezas y una buena lectura.

¡Y listo! Ya estás participando.

📅 💗

Un último paseo por Feria Aparte 2026 antes de empezar a pensar en todo lo que viene 🍡.

Celebramos tres días de cientos de obras, encuentros entre artistas, agentes del arte y diversos públicos, conversaciones, música, actividades y más de 7.500 personas recorriendo la Ex Cervecería Ebner en el @mallbarrioindepe 🏭

Ahora queremos saber de ustedes: 
¿Con qué te quedaste de esta edición? 🧸

ᴄᴇʀʀᴀᴍᴏꜱ ᴜɴᴀ ɴᴜᴇᴠᴀ ᴇᴅɪᴄɪóɴ ᴅᴇ ꜰᴇʀɪᴀ ᴀᴘᴀʀᴛᴇ 🐬🪄🧸

Esta quinta edición no fue fácil de levantar. Hubo momentos durante el año en que incluso nos preguntamos si iba a ser posible hacerla. Feria Aparte sigue siendo un proyecto independiente y autogestionado, que cada año tiene que volver a buscar los recursos y las personas necesarias para existir. Nada está asegurado de una edición a otra.
Por eso, ver la Ex Cervecería Ebner llena durante tres días tuvo un valor muy especial.

Más de 𝟳.𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻𝗮𝘀 🔮 pasaron por la feria este fin de semana, recorrieron, preguntaron, conversaron con artistas, participaron, compraron obras o simplemente entraron a mirar.

Hace cinco años comenzamos este proyecto justamente con esa idea: hacer del arte contemporáneo un espacio más cercano, donde distintas formas de producir y circular pudieran encontrarse y donde no fuera necesario saber de arte o tener intención de comprar para sentirse parte.

Cinco ediciones después, seguimos intentando defender esa misma idea.

Gracias a las galerías, talleres, colectivos, artistas y proyectos que confiaron en esta edición. A las instituciones, colaboradores y aliados que decidieron apoyarla. A quienes aportaron recursos, tiempo, trabajo, ideas y energía para que pudiéramos volver a abrir las puertas nuevamente. Y especialmente a todo el equipo que estuvo detrás y delante de la feria haciendo posible algo que durante meses solo existió en planillas, reuniones, correos y muchas conversaciones.

Y gracias a quienes llegaron este fin de semana. A quienes vienen desde la primera edición y a quienes entraron por primera vez. Que más de 7.000 personas hayan decidido dedicar parte de su fin de semana a encontrarse con el trabajo de más de 200 artistas es algo que no damos por sentado.

Feria Aparte cumplió cinco años. Y después de esta edición, quizás la respuesta a la pregunta de por qué seguir haciendo todo esto está un poco más clara.
Gracias por estar acá ❤️‍🔥.

latestPosts.caption: Don’t miss the 2026 Nightcliff Seabreeze Festival - where memories are made 🪼 🌴 🌊 🐚 💜

📣 IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT📣
The Nightcliff Arts, Music & Culture Committee are saddened to announce that the Nightcliff Seabreeze Festival will be a biennial festival. This means we will have a break in 2027, and come back in 2028 with a bang! 

This has not been an easy decision for us, however with the rising pressure, increasing costs, decreasing funding and the amount of work involved for a small committee - we have decided that we need more time for planning and ensuring that we deliver the best festival possible. 

If you have any queries, or concerns please contact namcisecretary@gmail.com

We will continue to work on improving the Festival throughout 2027, if you are interested in joining the committee or becoming involved, please contact namcisecretary@gmail.com

Golden hour hit different at @nightcliffseabreezefestival 

The sunset view from Nightcliff Jetty never gets old and it was a dream to sit on the beach and film these scenes during the festival. As the day went on, the light just kept getting better and better. I ticked off each shot from my shot list and then had the chance to get some additional creative pieces. 

Can’t wait for next year 🙌🏼

Art Jakarta
2–4 October 2026
JIExpo Kemayoran

#ArtJakarta #AJ2026

Check out TACO’s collaboration with Aji Fajar (Palette Studio)!

The work, titled “The Curiosity Engine”, depicts how curiosity opens a path towards a new horizon. Here, Aji invites audiences to experience how familiar mechanisms can break free from their usual functions and awaken an innate sense of curiosity.

Music: “Orang Orang di Kerumunan” by FSTVLST @fstvlst

#ArtJakarta #AJ2026

Join Januar Rianto, founder and operator of Further Reading, as he shares more about the activation and reading club at Aesop Women’s Library.

The library takes over Art Jakarta with a selection of books by female authors, spanning diverse subjects and genres, available to collect as literary gifts.

Experience Aesop Women’s Library and join its activation in person at Art Jakarta 2026.

Music: “Orang Orang di Kerumunan” by FSTVLST @fstvlst

#ArtJakarta #AJ2026

Check out a glimpse of the first public day of #ArtJakarta2026.

Join us for an art-filled weekend featuring gallery presentations, curated solo presentations, a series of talks, and special sections.

Get your tickets at artjakarta.com and join us for the Fair’s final day tomorrow!

Art Jakarta
2–4 October 2026
JIExpo Kemayoran

#ArtJakarta #AJ2026

EDISII returns to Art Jakarta for its second year. Join Lio Adrian, co-founder of EDISII, at their booth, where he will elaborate on the concept of fine art printing and how it differs from other forms of art reproduction.

Discover more about the artists EDISII is bringing to this year’s edition.

Music: “Orang Orang di Kerumunan” by FSTVLST @fstvlst

#ArtJakarta #AJ2026

Check out the artworks by the 19 awardees of the MR.D.I.Y. Regional Art Competition 2026. Hailing from Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, these artists explore the theme of “Strength & Resilience”, with their individual voices becoming part of a broader regional conversation.

Discover more at the MR.D.I.Y. booth.

Music: “Orang Orang di Kerumunan” by FSTVLST @fstvlst

#ArtJakarta #AJ2026

Check out ALCHEMIST and ALCHEMIST Brew Lab’s collaboration with artist Mai Yokoyama in person! 

Artist Mai Yokoyama (横山 麻衣)  is a contemporary Japanese painter born in Kanagawa in 1989 that explores the shifting idea of authenticity in the digital age. For the collaboration, she is featuring the Sphinx, as a symbol of intellect and imagination, perfectly capturing the spirit of meaningful gifting for oneself and loved ones.

Music: “Orang Orang di Kerumunan” by FSTVLST @fstvlst

#ArtJakarta #AJ2026

Every change begins with curiosity ✨

In this interview, Aji Fajar, Founder of Palette Studio, shares the story behind The Curiosity Engine — a collaborative artwork with TACO at Art Jakarta 2026.

From HPL waste to TACO PVC Sheet, Drawer Slide, and PVC Board, familiar materials are reimagined through new compositions, colors, textures, and possibilities.

A reminder that sometimes, a different perspective opens new possibilities to Explore New Horizons.

biography: Showcasing the core of the surf industry. Oct. 10 & 11, 2026 Del Mar -

latestPosts.caption: Gary Linden’s half century and Alrik Yuill’s decades in the shaping room, gives these Master’s intuition that only comes with time. The gravity that pulls them together is Dick’s Brewer. Alrik recreated the 6’7” Winged 74’, a single fin (blue board over Gary’s shoulder) and Gary shaped a modern 10’0” Buzzy quad as our entry in the “BEST IN SHOW”. The Boardroom Show causes us to pause and revere the craftsmen who build our boards and especially our “Shapers! #garylindensurfboards #spacetimesurfboards #boardroomshow

What a weekend. We were in San Diego for The @boardroomshow, and what a success it was.

Seeing so much excitement around sustainable surfboard manufacturing, sugarcane cores, and a new way of designing and building boards is exactly why we do this.

We were humbled by the legends who stopped by our booth, and grateful for every conversation, old friends, new friends, and new connections we can’t wait to build with.

Thank you for your presence and your stoke.

If you stopped by and have a project in mind, reach out, we’d love to make something together.

See you next year! 🤙

Post Mavericks surf session 2006 Randy Cone @randy_cone_surfboards breaking down the green machine he made for himself that @granttwigbaker won the @titansofmavericks contest on. Grant Washburn was riding some magic Cones at this point as was @alexmblau @rseelbach and @benandrewssurf most still do. I was lucky enough to hang around the shop and pick their brains and surf OB and Mavs with these two mentors. This board featured a swallowtail 2+1 Randy fin set up and heavy glass. Very inspiring design.
Breaking down @randy_cone_surfboards Super El Niño Best in Show Winner 🏆
Big shout out to Kelly Slater “The G.O.A.T” for taking so much time for endless photos with the kids @boardroomshow @kellyslater @outerknown @slaterdesigns

I’ve been working on the Skil 100 Timeline for about 15 years. Here’s where we’re at in 2026.  My aim is to continue add depth and dimension to the exhibit. Check the YouTube link in my bio for a detailed view.

Thank you to all involved and tremendous appreciation to everyone who came out to make another wonderful @boardroomshow 🙏🏽 @mcsurfboards brought some incredibly challenging and progressive boards to replicate. Some of the Icons Of Foam replicas captured the essence, others nailed the numbers, and it was Matt Calvani’s 3 shapes that Maurice deemed the sharpest reflection. We were all winners. And we’re grateful to help supply the core of surfing. Thanks all! We’ll see you soon. 🙏🏽
Best in Show 1st place 🥇 @randy_cone_surfboards
Best in show 2026 @randy_cone_surfboards !!!

Demystifying Twinzers at @boardroomshow with Stu Kenson  @sk_shape and @nakedvikingsurf

Helpful info below! Excited to see everyone for our 25th annual fest this Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026 at the Hibernia (1 Jones St, SF) 🥹

1) Masks required the whole event! Free KN95 mask provided to everyone to put on before entering. Keeping events accessible for our immunocompromised community members!
2) Our SFZF 2026 venue doesn’t have a water fountain onsite, so fill up a bottle before you head over! 
3)  What’s for lunch? SF Zine Fest is a long day for exhibitors, volunteers, organizers AND attendees, so remember to eat!
4) Need anything? Visit our welcome table/info booth just inside the doors at either entrance. 
5) Our Accessible Entrance is on Jones St and the Stairs Entrance is on the corner of Jones & McAllister. An outdoor lift on the side of the building is currently broken but the indoor elevator accesses every floor / every part of the event.
6) We’ll have first aid available onsite all day. 
7) Organizers will be at the Organizers Zines table in the Guest of Honor’s room (off the southwest side of the lobby near the elevator), near the entrances, and floating all day wearing ORANGE safety vests. 🦺 Or catch any of our 2026 interns and 50+ volunteers wearing neon YELLOW safety vests. 
8) We’ll do our best to answer social media messages during the day but we’re getting a ton! Thanks for understanding if there’s a delay.
9) Tag us! #sfzf2026

More info at www.sfzinefest.org 🖤

Cultivating Community provided time to connect, reflect and create as part of Nature Festival.

Karl Winda Telfer told stories of Country and the six cultural seasons, represented in his 'Kuri Kurru' (Turning Circle) digital art exhibition. Karl and Claire from @Kanyanyapilla shared their native grass restoration project on Mullawirra Patpa Yerta (Southern Dry Forest Country). Highlighting how every contribution can help regenerate Country.

Tatiana from @arvoflora.adl shared her passion for creating seed paper with a hands on workshop using edible garden and native flower seeds from The Diggers Club. We're all looking forward to planting our papers and bringing more seasonal colour to spring!

This event was generously funded by Inspiring SA.

#Sientelainspiracion en #IFEMADRID

IFEMA MADRID lidera el inicio de la temporada 2026-2027 de la Comisión de Sostenibilidad de la Asociación de Ferias Españolas (@afe_asocferiasesp). 🌱
 
Un espacio de colaboración e intercambio de conocimiento entre profesionales del sector ferial, orientado a impulsar la sostenibilidad en la industria de ferias, eventos y congresos.
 
A través de sus sesiones de trabajo, la Comisión aborda los principales retos y oportunidades del sector en materia de sostenibilidad, profundizando en cuestiones como la huella de carbono, la gestión de residuos, la comunicación y el reporte de información sobre sostenibilidad.
 
Desde IFEMA MADRID, seguimos contribuyendo activamente a este espacio de diálogo, compartiendo nuestra experiencia y conocimiento para avanzar hacia un sector cada vez más sostenible, responsable y comprometido con el futuro.

🏗️ La construcción del futuro se encuentra en IFEMA MADRID.

Hoy hemos celebrado la presentación de la Semana Internacional de la Construcción 2026, una cita que reunirá del 10 al 13 de noviembre a más de 500 empresas y 43.000 m² de exposición para impulsar la innovación, la sostenibilidad y la industrialización del sector.

@feria_construtec, @veteco_feria, @smartdoors_ifema y @feriapiscimad conformarán una plataforma común de negocio y conocimiento, con Colombia como País Invitado, Navarra como Comunidad Autónoma Invitada y Barcelona como Ciudad Invitada.

Además, el II Congreso de la Semana Internacional de la Construcción abordará los principales retos de la industria y su transformación. 

#Sientelainspiracion en #IFEMADRID

Durante el recorrido inaugural, le han acompañado Daniel Martínez, vicepresidente ejecutivo de IFEMA MADRID; Rafael Olmos, presidente del Comité Organizador de GUEXT y de FELAC; y María Valcarce, directora de la feria.

La comitiva ha visitado varios stands para conocer de primera mano las últimas propuestas, soluciones e innovaciones que las empresas expositoras presentan para impulsar la transformación y el crecimiento del sector.

✨ Arranca una nueva edición de GUEXT, punto de encuentro clave para los profesionales del hospitality y un espacio de negocio, inspiración y oportunidades para toda la industria.

🚘 Los amantes del motor clásico tienen una nueva cita en IFEMA MADRID.

Del 11 al 13 de diciembre, #RetromóvilMadrid2026 (@eventosmotor) reunirá vehículos clásicos, coleccionismo, restauración y recambios, con una programación que incluye una exposición especial por el 75 aniversario del Pegaso Z-102 y un homenaje a su creador, Wifredo Ricart.

Una oportunidad para descubrir la historia del automóvil y algunos de sus modelos más emblemáticos.

latestPosts.caption:
📅ExCom meets every month to plan the event and to discuss anything of note that’s happening within the various departments.

Here’s the latest update from this month’s meeting.

Noteworthy topics/updates from the recent ExCom meeting

🪑We have a new Chair! Keri, our acting chair applied and was voted in as full Chairperson
🚦All the usual event planning and tasks are underway e.g. wristband designs, stickers etc
🐝The Working Bee is currently taking place in Hunterville. A number of volunteers on the Paddock, getting things ready for the 2027 event
Open Facilitator roles:
🧯Site Safety Facilitator role is now open, due to Keri switching to Chairperson
👷🏾Infrastructure Facilitator
🎪Theme Camps Facilitator
🎨Arts Facilitator
All other roles are full at this time
📸Photo credit: Nabulen

If you haven’t had your head in the sand, you’ll have known that Kiwiburn was looking for a new Chairperson.
Well we’re happy to report that we have now filled this role! 🧡🩵
Keri, Kiwiburn’s (until now) acting Chair is now full time Chair, after being voted in at the last ExCom meeting.
When asked if they applied because they were tired of playing musical chairs (since they were also our Site Safety Facilitator), Keri responded ‘This Chair has no musical talent’.
While they were the only applicant, ExCom also felt that Keri had done a great job as acting Chair (and possessing musical talent isn’t a requirement of the role), so they were happy to vote Keri in.
So, a big thank you to Keri for stepping up to be Kiwiburn’s Chair! We’re sure they’ll do a fantastic job in the role.
📸Image Credit: @fra.gmentz

🪜A special notice from this year’s Temple Team!
The Temple team (“The Capsule”) is looking for a Pallet Lead for one of the most critical logistics jobs in our build: sourcing the reclaimed pallets that will form a large part of the Temple structure.🪵
The job:
Source ~200 pallets (reclaimed/free where possible – think supermarkets, distribution centres, hardware stores, industrial estates)
Arrange storage for them in the lead-up to the burn
Arrange transport of all pallets to the Hunterville paddock, delivered by 15 January 2027

You’ll be sorting the pallets and coordinating directly with the build leads – this is a job for someone who’s organised, resourceful, and good on the phone/email chasing down free stuff.
Note: while we won’t ask for cost estimates at application stage, the Pallet Lead will be responsible for estimating and organising costs (storage, transport/fuel, etc.) once appointed, in coordination with the build budget holder.
This role comes with a crew ticket and at least one standard Kiwiburn ticket. Details on our website! 

📸Image Credit; Please Help
🤎Temple Credit; Kym S and David Y

❤️‍🔥Got a big, beautiful, paddock-worthy piece of art in the works? Large Art Logistics Grants and Art Registrations are now open! 🎨
Whether you need a hand getting your creation out to the Paddock or you’re ready to officially register your masterpiece, head to the links below to find out more and get amongst it.
Art registrations close on 15 November 2026, so don’t leave it until Paddock time! Details on our website. 

📸Image Credit; John Williams
🔥Creation credit; Lumos

🎟️The ticketing machine is warming up! Here’s what you need to know for KB27:
🏷️General sale via STEP — from 27 November, 2026
Our first batch of 100 general tickets will hit STEP on 27 November. More tickets will be released as we fill the volunteer roles needed to increase our event capacity. So if you’re volunteering, your mahi could literally help someone get through the gate!
Volunteer, Theme Camp & Art tickets — 1 November, 2026
Department leads will have tickets loaded into the Leads Portal from 1 November, ready to allocate to their teams. EE and PL requests are in the final stages of being sorted and will be communicated to the relevant Team Leads soon.
💵Ticket price — $260
We’re increasing the general ticket price by $10 for KB27, bringing it to $260. The good news? We can confirm this won’t increase again for KB28. Two years of ticket price certainty — look at us, getting organised!
✂️Ticketing cut-off — 26 January, 2027
General ticket sales and ticket transfers close on 26 January. After that, the ticketing gates come down, so don’t leave it until the last minute!
Keep an eye on the EFP and official Kiwiburn channels for further ticketing updates.
📸Image credit; Ignacio Nabulen

We need another design witch! 🧙🏿‍♀️

We have one Graphic Designer. ONE. 👨🏻‍🎨And while they are extremely talented and definitely not being held together by caffeine and sheer force of will, we reckon they could use a mate. ☕️
Enter: YOU, potentially. 🫵
We’re looking for a Graphic Designer to help turn the beautiful chaos of Kiwiburn into beautiful visual chaos. Posters! Stickers! Wristbands! Volunteer patches! Tickets! Socials! Event Guides! Survival Guides! EFP! Department merch! Probably approximately 47 other things we’ve forgotten!
You’ll need InDesign & Illustrator skills, Adobe Creative Suite access, print + digital design experience, and enough organisation to stop our Google Drive from becoming an archaeological site. You’ll work alongside the Communications crew and other delightful humans to make Kiwiburn look bloody good, with roughly 1–3 hours a month year-round, plus some bigger bursts of designy goodness around June/July and December–January.
Come wield the pixels. Befriend the vectors. Tame the PDFs. Make things pretty.
We have one designer. We need two. And maybe it’s you? Check our website for more details and to apply!
Image credit 📸 Jane Davies

Do you like burner art? Do you like music? Do you like burn events? ❤️‍🔥

Well, have we got the fundraiser for you! InflammARTory is crashing into Nightmare on Bones Street in association with @aucklandburners bringing artists and the community together to help fund the next wave of glorious burn art. Artists will pitch their projects, you get to wander, chat, ask questions and check out what’s cooking, then YOU choose where the money goes. 🤑
Your ticket includes $15 worth of donation chips to distribute between your favourite projects, with the fundraising totals climbing in real time throughout the night. Part street party, part science fair, part art showcase, and 100% community-powered chaos — come see what’s headed to Kiwiburn and other regional burns, support some artists, and maybe find your next project to get involved with.
For all of the info, check out their profile!

Image credit 📸 Auckland Burners

🪑Kiwiburn is looking for its next ExCom Chairperson! Want to help steer the ship, wrangle the chaos, support our teams and have a real say in where Kiwiburn heads next? This could be your moment. 🫵
A huge thank you to Keri for the awesome mahi they’ve put in so far as Acting Chair – keeping things moving, navigating the big conversations and stepping up when Kiwiburn needed it. 🧡
Now we’re looking for someone to take the reins. Got good communication skills, a knack for bringing people together, and a desire to serve the Burner community? Come get amongst it!
Check out the link in our bio for the full job description!
Image credit📸 fra.gmentz

📌It’s that time of year again! Kiwiburn’s 2026 AGM is happening on 25 August! More details will be landing in your emails soon, so keep an eye on your inbox and get ready to join the conversation, have your say, and help shape the future of our wonderfully weird community.
📸Image Credit; Please Help
Kiwiburn Screen Print by; Inky Fingers

❤️‍🔥The call is going out again! Earlier this year we opened applications for the Kiwiburn Temple, but with too few expressions of interest, we hit pause. Since then, we’ve heard from members of the community who are feeling inspired, so we’re re-opening applications and inviting fresh ideas to the table.
✏️If you’ve been quietly sketching concepts, waiting for the right moment, or have only recently found the time and inspiration, this is your chance. We’d love to hear your vision for this year’s Temple, no matter how polished or rough around the edges. The Temple is one of the most meaningful spaces at Kiwiburn, and it begins with someone brave enough to share an idea. If that’s you, we’d love to see what you’ve been dreaming up and how we can help make it a reality!
For more information and specifics or to send us your application, visit our website for more details. 
♥️Heart and Home Temple; Kym and David
📸Image Credit; John Williams

🏕️Who is the biggest Type A on the paddock? Get your registration in first to win this hotly contested title!
Registrations opened on 15 July and close 11.59pm 23 August for camps desiring reserved tickets, and 11.59pm 31 August for everyone else.
Don’t be a dilly-dallier!
📸Photo credit: Paul Chaffe

📋Are you passionate about project management, community building and organized chaos? As we get closer to our Kiwiburn 2027 event it’s time for our Event Management Team to grow! As 2IC, you’ll spend the year supporting our Event Manager (Lauren/Loz) in event logistics, management coordination, emergency response protocol and assisting our wider Kiwiburn teams in developing their departments and resources.
🌿As a part of the Event Management Team you are expected to have a broad understanding of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and be interested in upskilling your project management and community development abilities.
If you are interested in learning more about Event Management but are not ready to commit to a 2IC role we suggest you apply for the General Event Management Team (applications opening mid August, or reach out directly to express your interest at eventmanager@kiwiburn.com) to get a good feel for the responsibilities of the Event Manager. Additionally it is up to the discretion of the ExCom and Event Manager to determine if they will take on multiple 2ICs and who shall be the successor.
📸Image Credit; Jane Davies
Temple Credit; Kym S and David Y

latestPosts.caption:
descEND. 
Been trying to post this one since last year but the words just won’t come gang. After a decade of doing a thing you never saw coming it’s time to say aloha. I think ole Dave summed it up best, the dopamine hits just can’t outweigh the realities anymore. I keep coming back to this photo @vanagonlife took so long ago and know that my favorite shot is a direct reflection of our favorite times sitting around fires in the Outback with a couple handfuls of friends who’d become family. Thank you all for celebrating being human with us, I hope to God you’ve all found the people at your small fire that we have through this wild ride. Massive thanks to the Molloy family for trusting us with your family farm to host our last gathering. My absolute favorite Descend was 2020 when the government told us we couldn’t gather so we did anyway. Perhaps that’s a good way to wrap this up, please feel free to send me back to being the last human on earth without email or social media by leaving your favorite memory in the comments for the bots. Here’s to the hearts and the hands of the men who come with the dust and are gone with the wind. Adios and Aloha.

I got to take my son to one of my favorite Vanlife gatherings - Descend on Bend!

This year Descend was in a new location.  And I was super loving the new vibe!  We had such a great time! 

We were blessed with one of the most epic sunsets I’ve ever seen.  And I took Tyler up to the roof of a van to howl at the sunset in true Vanlife fashion!

The weekend capped off with an 80s dance party.  My son got totally into it with the glam rocker vibe, complete with a full face of makeup!

And we danced the night away to @driftalongdjaaron ‘s last nomadic show!  We’re sooo gonna miss you Aaron!! (The end of an era! 🥲) Thank you for making all of our get togethers rock these past few years!  I’m going to miss seeing your amazing always happy smile in camp!

I think I almost have my son convinced to give up houselife and buy a van.  Almost.  Haha

Thank you @descendonbend and everyone involved for another epic event!! Already cannot wait for the next one!

For those wondering… no, we weren’t hiding in a dark room recovering after Tanglewood pack-down 😅🌿

A bunch of our crew rolled straight into Rainbow Spirit Festival to collaborate on the build and design of the Homestead Stage alongside the legends at Home Bass Crew. It was a real privilege to bring a little slice of the Tanglewood vibe to a Rainbow dancefloor — bamboo, earthy textures, immersive lighting and deep bass in the bush 🌙🔊🪵

Rainbow has long been one of the grandmothers of transformational festivals in Australia, so it felt pretty special to be involved in its long-awaited return after six years away. Even in a more intimate form, the same beautiful Rainbow energy was alive and well, and we’re feeling very grateful to have been a part of it 💜

Huge love to everybody involved:

🌱 Build / Rigging / Design — Leigh, Spyda, Tim, Tony & Sean
🌱 Art Decor — Ben Lopez Art
🌱 Curation / Overall Management — Home Bass Crew & Cory Kodiak
🌱 Lighting — Bad Idea Factory (Andrew, Albie & Dylan)

Big thanks to the entire Rainbow crew for having us ✨

O Terra Incógnita em São Miguel juntou Artur Carvalho à Filarmónica Minerva de Ginetes e o dia de apresentação foi uma festa que se prolongou com Rubén Monfort e a Despensa Amigos de São Sebastião, e piquenique Terra Fogo.

Terra Incógnita in São Miguel brought Artur Carvalho together with Filarmónica Minerva de Ginetes, and the presentation day was a celebration that continued with Rubén Monfort and Despensa Amigos de São Sebastião, and a Terra Fogo picnic.

Últimos dias para te inscreveres na Rave açoriana do Ciclo 2026! 

Esta edição tem o acompanhamento e coordenação artística de Inês Coutinho aka @violetakaviolet. 

O programa decorre entre outubro de 2026 e março de 2027, e está dividido em três componentes:
- Quatro módulos de formação (Direção Artística, Luz, Vídeo e Cenografia, Comunicação & Comunidade e Direção Técnica & Implementação);
- Sessões de acompanhamento com a coordenadora artística;
- Residência de implementação e apresentação final de projeto no Festival Tremor 2027.

O resultado final? Uma celebração da cultura Rave nos Açores.

Toda a informação e inscrições gratuitas em tremor-pdl.com, arquipelagocentrodeartes.azores.gov.pt ou através do link na bio.

#tremoréamor

O Arquipélago - Centro de Artes Contemporâneas e o festival Tremor  desenvolvem, desde 2021, acções regulares de formação, direcionadas a profissionais e curiosos das áreas artísticas. O objetivo do Ciclo é a capacitação de novos agentes culturais locais, dando continuidade ao trabalho que ambas as entidades têm desenvolvido na abertura de novas oportunidades de empoderamento para o território.

A edição 2026/27 do Ciclo pretende criar contexto para a celebração da cultura Rave nos Açores, proporcionando a criação de um coletivo que crie e implemente uma nova festa, que tomará forma durante o presente ano, sendo apresentada durante o Tremor 2027.

Toda a informação e inscrições em tremor-pdl.com ou diretamente através do link na bio.

¿Qué hace que un festival sea realmente inolvidable?

Durante mucho tiempo la respuesta parecía estar en el cartel. Hoy, algunos proyectos están demostrando que el verdadero protagonista también puede ser el territorio.

En BIME PRO conversaremos con quienes están impulsando esta visión:
🎙️ Marcio Laranjeira, director artístico de Tremor. 🎙️ Jaime Torrego, co-director de Observatorio.

Una conversación para repensar el papel del territorio en la creación de experiencias culturales.
